(ἀ- neg., πιστός) [in LXX: Pro.17:6 28:25, Isa.17:10 * ;]
__(a) of things, incredible: Act.26:8;
__(b) of persons, without faith or trust, unbelieving: Mat.17:17, Mrk.9:19, Luk.9:41 12:46, Jhn.20:27, Tit.1:15, Rev.21:8; specif., of unbelievers as opposite to Christians: 1Co.6:6 7:12-15 10:27 14:22-24, 2Co.4:4 6:14-15, 1Ti.5:8 (cf. Lft., Notes, 265; Cremer, 491).†
(AS)
G0571.s: (actively) disbelieving, i.e. without Christian faith (specially, a heathen); (passively) untrustworthy (person), or incredible (thing)
G0571.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4103 (πιστός);
G0571.k: that believeth not, faithless, incredible thing, infidel, unbeliever(-ing)

G0572.d:
ἀπλότης, -ητος, ή
(ἁπλοῦς), [in LXX: 4Ki.15:11 (תֹּם), 1Ch.29:17 (לֵבָב יֹשֶׁר, ἁ. τῆς καρδίας, cf. Col.3:22, where see Lft.), Wis.1:1, al. ;]
simplicity, sincerity: Rom.12:8, 2Co.11:3, Eph.6:5, Col.3:22; as manifested in generous, unselfish giving, liberality, graciousness: 2Co.8:2 9:11 9:13 (see ICC, Rom.12:8; Hort, Jas.1:5, and see: ἁπλῶς).†
(AS)
G0572.s: singleness, i.e. (subjectively) sincerity (without dissimulation or self-seeking), or (objectively) generosity (copious bestowal)

G0573.d:
ἁπλοῦς, -ῆ, -οῦν
(contr. fr. -όος; ἁ.- cop., πλόος), [in LXX: Pro.11:25 * ;]
simple, single: in a moral sense (DCG, ii, 628 f.), ἀφθαλμός, Mat.6:22, Luk.11:34. (In π. of a marriage dowry, see MM, see word).†
ἁπλόος, see: ἁπλοῦς
SYN.: ἄδολος, ἄκακος, ἀκέραιος (Tr., Syn., § lvi; Cremer, 107, 639) (AS)
G0573.s: properly, folded together, i.e. single (figuratively, clear)
G0573.o: probably from G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) and the base of G4120 (πλέκω);

G0574.d:
ἁπλῶς
adv. (ἁπλοῦς), [in LXX: Pro.10:9 (תֹּם), Wis.16:27, 2Ma.6:6 * ;]
simply, sincerely, graciously: Jas.1:5. ("Later writers comprehend under the one word the whole magnanimous and honour­able type of character in which ... singleness of mind is the central feature "-Hort, Ja., l.with)†
(AS)
G0574.o: adverb from G573 (ἁπλοῦς) (in the objective sense of G572 (ἁπλότης));

G0575.d:
ἀπό (on the frequently neglect of elision bef. vowels, see Tdf., Pr., 94, WH, App., 146),
prep. with genitive (WM, 462ff.; on its relation to ἐκ, παρά, ὑπό, ib. 456f.), [in LXX for לְ ,בְּ ,מִן ;]
from (i.e. from the exterior).
__1. Of separation and cessation;
__(1) of motion from a place: Mat.5:29, 30 7:23, Luk.5:2 22:41, al.;
__(2) in partitive sense (M, Pr., 72, 102, 245; MM, see word; Bl., §40, 2), Mat.9:16 27:21, Jhn.21:10, Act.5:2, al.; also after verbs of eating, etc.;
__(3) of alienation (cl. genitive of separation), after such verbs as λούω (Deiss., BS, 227), λύω, σώζω, παύω, etc.;…
G0575.s: "off," i.e. away (from something near), in various senses (of place, time, or relation; literal or figurative)
G0575.k: (X here-)after, ago, at, because of, before, by (the space of), for(-th), from, in, (out) of, off, (up-)on(-ce), since, with

G0576.d:
ἀπο-βαίνω
[in LXX for הָיָה, etc. ;]
to step off, disembark: Luk.5:2, Jhn.21:9; metaphorically, of events, to issue, turn out (Field, Notes, 74): Luk.21:13, Php.1:19 (MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0576.s: literally, to disembark; figuratively, to eventuate
G0576.o: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G939 (βάσις);

G0577.d:
ἀπο-βάλλω
[in LXX: Isa.1:30 (נָבֵל) and elsew. without Heb. equiv. ;]
to throw off: Mrk.10:50; metaphorically, to lose, let go (Field, Notes, 231 f.; MM, see word): Heb.10:35.†
(AS)
G0577.s: to throw off; figuratively, to lose

G0578.d:
ἀπο-βλέπω
[in LXX for פָּנָה, etc. ;]
to look away from all else at one object; hence, to look steadfastly: Heb.11:26 (cf. ἀφοράω).†
(AS)
G0578.s: to look away from everything else, i.e. (figuratively) intently regard

G0579.d:
ἀπό-βλητος, -ον
(ἀποβάλλω), [in Aq.: Lev.7:18, al.; Sm.: Hos.9:3 (טָמֵא) ;]
to be thrown away, rejected: 1Ti.4:4 (Hom., Plut.).†
(AS)
G0579.s: cast off, i.e. (figuratively) such as to be rejected

G0580.d:
ἀπο-βολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ἀποβάλλω);
__1. a throwing away, rejection: opposite to πρόσλημψις, Rom.11:15.
__2. a losing, loss: Act.27:22.†
(AS)

G0581.d:
ἀπο-γίνομαι (cl. -γίγν-)
[in LXX: Da TH Dan.2:1 * ;]
__1. to be away, removed from.
__2. to depart life, to die (MM, see word): τ. ἀμαρτίαις, i.e. with ref. to sins, 1Pe.2:24 (Cremer, 149, 668).†
(AS)
G0581.o: past participle of a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G1096 (γίνομαι);

G0582.d:
ἀπο-γραφή, -ῆς, ἡ (ἀπογράφω)
[in LXX: Dan.10:21 (כָּתָב), I Est.8:30, AB, 2Ma.2:1, 3Ma.2:32 3Mac 4:15 3Mac 4:17 3Mac 7:22 * ;]
__1. a written copy.
__2. As law term, a deposition (Demos.).
__3. In late writers, a register, enrolment, census (MM, see word; Deiss., LAE, 160, 268 f.): Luk.2:2, Act.5:37.†
(AS)
G0582.s: an enrollment; by implication, an assessment

G0583.d:
ἀπο-γράφω
[in LXX: Jdg.8:14, Pro.22:20 (כָּתַב), I Est.8:30, 3Ma.2:29 3Mac 4:14 3Mac 6:34 3Mac 6:38 * ;]
__1. to write out, copy.
__2. to enrol; mid., to enrol oneself: Luk.2:1 (M, Pr., 162; but. see ICC, in l), Luk.2:3, 5; pass., Heb.12:23 (see reff, see word ἀπογραφή ).†
(AS)
G0583.s: to write off (a copy or list), i.e. enrol

G0584.d:
ἀπο-δείκνυμι
[in LXX: Est.2:9 (רָאָה), al. ;]
__1. to bring out, show forth, exhibit (Lft., Notes, 200; ICC, in l): 1Co.4:9.
__2. to declare, show: Act.2:22
__3. to prove: Act.25:7.
__4. As frequently in late Gk., to proclaim to an office: before ὅτι, 2Th.2:4 (Milligan, in l; MM, see word; Lft., Notes. 113.)†
(AS)
G0584.s: to show off, i.e. exhibit; figuratively, to demonstrate, i.e. accredit

G0585.d:
ἀπό-δειξις, -εως, ἡ
(ἀποδείκνυμι) [in LXX: 3Ma.4:20, 4Ma.3:19 4Mac 13:10 * ;]
__1. a showing off.
__2. As used by Gk. philosophers, demonstration, certain proof: 1Co.2:4 (see ICC, in l; MM, see word; Lft., Notes, 173).†
(AS)

G0586.d:
ἀπο-δεκατοω,
[in LXX for עָשַׂר in both senses foll., e.g. (1) Gen.28:22 (2) 1Ki.8:15 ;]
__1. with accusative of thing(s), to tithe, pay a tenth of: Mat.23:23, Luk.11:42.
__2. C. accusative of person(s), to exact tithes from: Heb.7:5.
__3. to decimate (Socr., HE, 573 A; see Kennedy, Sources, 117).†
(AS)

G0588.d:
ἀπο-δέχομαι
[in LXX: Tob.7:17, Jdth.13:13; Jdt.13.1, 4Mac.10:1-21 * ;]
to accept gladly, welcome, receive: Luk.8:40 9:11, Act.18:27 21:17 28:30; metaphorically, with accusative of thing(s), Act.2:41 24:3 (MM, see word; Cremer, 688).†
(AS)
G0588.s: to take fully, i.e. welcome (persons), approve (things)

G0589.d:
ἀπο-δημέω, -ῶ
(ἀπόδημος), [in LXX: Eze.19:3 A * ;]
to be or go abroad (M, Pr., 130, 2): Mat.21:33 25:14-15, Mrk.12:1, Luk.15:13 20:9.†
(AS)
G0589.s: to go abroad, i.e. visit a foreign land
G0589.k: go (travel) into a far country, journey

G0590.d:
ἀπό-δημος, -ον
gone abroad (RV, sojourning in another country): Mrk.13:34.†
(AS)
G0590.s: absent from one's own people, i.e. a foreign traveller

G0591.d:
ἀπο-δίδωμι
[in LXX for מָכַר, שׁוּב hi., נָתַן, שָׁלֵם pi., etc. ;]
to give up or back, restore, return: Mat.27:58, Luk.4:20 9:42 19:8; esp. of wages, debts, oaths, etc. (MM, see word), to render what is due, to pay (Deiss., LAE, 334 f.): absol., Mat.18:25, 28, Luk.7:42. with accusative, Mat.5:26 18:29-30, 34 20:8 21:41 22:21, Mrk.12:17, Luk.10:35 12:59 20:25, Rom.13:7, Heb.12:11, Rev.22:2; ὅρκους, Mat.5:33 (cf. Num.30:3, Deu.23:21 al.); of conjugal duty, τ. ὀφειλήν, 1Co.7:3; ἀμοιβάς, 1Ti.5:4; μαρτύριον, to give (as in duty bound) testimony, Act.4:33; λόγον, to render account, Mat.12:36, Luk.16:2, Act.19:40, Heb.13:17, 1Pe.4:5; hence of requital,…
G0591.s: to give away, i.e. up, over, back, etc. (in various applications)
G0591.k: deliver (again), give (again), (re-)pay(-ment be made), perform, recompense, render, requite, restore, reward, sell, yield

G0592.d:
ἀπο-δι-ορίζω
(διορίζω, ἅρος, a limit),
to mark off, hence metaphorically to make separations: Ju 19 (Cremer, 806).†
(AS)
G0592.s: to disjoin (by a boundary, figuratively, a party)
G0592.o: from G575 (ἀπό) and a compound of G223 (Ἀλέξανδρος) and G3724 (ὁρίζω);

G0593.d:
ἀπο-δοκιμάζω
[in LXX: Psa.118:22, al. (מָאַס) ;]
to reject: Mat.21:42 (LXX), Mrk.8:31 12:10" (LXX) Luk.9:22 17:25 20:17" (LXX), Heb.12:17, 1Pe.2:4 2:7" (LXX) (Cremer, 701; MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0593.s: to disapprove, i.e. (by implication) to repudiate

G0596.d:
ἀπο-θήκη, -ης, ἡ
(ἀποτίθημι), [in LXX for אוֹצָר, טֶנֶא, etc. ;]
a storehouse, granary: Mat.3:12 6:26 13:30, Luk.3:17 12:18, 24.†
(AS)

G0597.d:
ἀπο-θησαυρίζω
[in LXX: Sir.3:4 * ;]
to treasure up, store away: 1Ti.6:19.†
(AS)

G0598.d:
ἀπο-θλίβω
[in LXX for לָחַץ, Num.22:25 * ;]
to press hard: Luk.8:45.†
(AS)

G0599.d:
ἀπο-θνῄσκω,
[in LXX chiefly for מוּת ;]
to die: of natural death, Mrk.5:35, al.; of violent death (pass. of ἀποκτείνω), esp. of Christ, Mat.26:35, Jhn.12:33, Heb.10:28, al.; of spiritual death, Jhn.6:50, Rom.8:13, al.; with dative ref., Rom.6:2, 10 14:7, 8, Gal.2:19; accusative, ὅ, Rom.6:10; before ἐν, Mat.8:32, Jhn.8:21, 24 1Co.15:22, Heb.11:37, Rev.14:13; before ὑπέρ, περί, Jhn.11:50, 51 18:14, Rom.5:6-8 14:15, 1Co.15:3, 2Co.5:15, 1Th.5:10, 1Pe.3:18; ἀπό, Col.2:20; ἐκ, Rev.8:11; figuratively, 1Co.15:31 (cf. συν-αποθνήσκω, and V. Milligan, NTD, 258f.; DCG, i, 791b; Cremer, 286; MM, see word; on the perfective force of this verb, M, Pr., 112,…
G0599.k: be dead, death, die, lie a-dying, be slain (X with)

G0600.d:
ἀπο-καθ-ίστημι (ἀποκαθιστάω, Mrk.9:12, Rec., -ιστάνω, LTTr.; cf. Act.1:6; -κατιστάνω, WH),
[in LXX chiefly for שׁוּב ;]
__1. to restore, i.e. to a former condition: of health, Mat.12:13, Mrk.3:5 8:25, Luk.6:10; of social or political affairs, Mat.17:11, Mrk.9:12, Act.1:6.
__2. to give back, bring back: Heb.13:19 (so in π., MM, see word; cf. also Cremer, 312).†
(AS)
G0600.s: to reconstitute (in health, home or organization)

G0601.d:
ἀπο-καλύπτω
[in LXX chiefly for גָּלָה ]
__1. in general sense (cl.), to reveal, uncover, disclose,
__(a) of things: Mat.10:26, Luk.2:35 12:2, 1Co.3:13;
__(b) of persons: pass., Christ, Luk.17:30; Antichrist, 2Th.2:3 2:6 2:8
__2. In LXX and NT, in special sense of divine revelation: Mat.11:25 (on the tense, see M, Pr., 136), ib. Mat.11:27 16:17, Luk.10:21-22, Jhn.12:38, Rom.1:17-18 8:18, 1Co.2:10 14:30, Gal.1:16 3:23, Eph.3:5, Php.3:15, 1Pe.1:5-12 5:1 (Westc., Eph., 178 f.; M, Th., 149 f.).†
SYN.: φανερόω (see Thayer, 62; Cremer, 342).† (AS)
G0601.s: to take off the cover, i.e. disclose

G0602.d:
ἀπο-κάλυψις, -εως, ἡ
(ἀποκαλύπτω), [in LXX: 1Ki.20:30 (עֶרְוָה), Sir.11:27 22:22 42:1 * ;]
an uncovering, laying bare (Plut.). Metaphorical, a reveal­ing, revelation: a disclosure of divine truth, or a manifestion from God: Luk.2:32 Rom.2:5 8:19 16:25, 1Co.1:7 14:6 14:26, 2Co.12:1 12:7, Gal.1:12 2:2, Eph.1:17 3:3 2Th.1:7 1Pe.1:7 1:13 4:13, Rev.1:1.†
SYN.: ἐπιφάνεια, παρουσία, φανέρωσις (see Tr., Syn., xciv; Lft., Notes, 102, 178; Westc, Eph., 178 f.; M, Th., 145 ff.; Cremer, 343) (AS)
G0602.k: appearing, coming, lighten, manifestation, be revealed, revelation

G0603.d:
ἀπο-καραδοκία, -ας, ἡ
(ἀποκαραδοκέω, used by Aq. in Psa.37:7 for חוּל; ἀπό, κάρα the head, δοκέω, in Ion., to watch),
to watch with outstretched head, watch anxiously (Polyb., π.; see Deiss., LAE, 374.5, 377 f.), Rom.8:19, Php.1:20 (Lft., in l; Cremer, 177).†
(AS)
G0603.o: from a comparative of G575 (ἀπό) and a compound of (the head) and G1380 (δοκέω) (in the sense of watching);

G0604.d:
ἀπο-κατ-αλλάσσω
(cf. καταλλάσσω: ἀπό here signifies completely, see Lft., Col., l.with; Ellic., Eph., l.with; but also Mey., Eph., l.with),
to reconcile completely: Eph.2:16, Col.1:20-21.†
(AS)

G0605.d:
ἀπο-κατά-στασις, -εως, ἡ
(ἀποκαθίστημι),
restoration: Act.3:21 (in τ. of repairs and restorations of temples, see MM, see word).†
(AS)

G0606.d:
ἀπό-κειμαι
[in LXX: Gen.49:10 (שִׁילֹה), Job.38:23 (חָשַׂךְ), 2Ma.12:45, 4Ma.8:11 * ;]
to be laid up, in store, laid away: Luk.19:20. Metaphorical, C. dative of person(s), to be reserved (Dem., Plat.; and see MM, see word): Col.1:5, 2Ti.4:8, Heb.9:27.†
(AS)
G0606.s: to be reserved; figuratively, to await

G0607.d:
ἀπο-κεφαλίζω
(ἀπό, κεφαλή), [in LXX: Psa.151:7 * ;]
to behead: Mat.14:10, Mrk.6:16, 28 Luk.9:9.†
(AS)

G0608.d:
ἀπο-κλείω
[in LXX chiefly for סָגַר ;]
to shut fast: Luk.13:25.†
(AS)

G0609.d:
ἀπο-κόπτω
[in LXX for קָצַץ, כָּרַת, etc. ;]
to cut off: Mrk.9:43, 45, Jhn.18:10, 26 Act.27:32. Mid., to mutilate oneself, have oneself mutilated: Gal.5:12 (cf. Deu.23:1 LXX; and see Cremer, 751; MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0609.s: to amputate; reflexively (by irony) to mutilate (the privy parts)

G0610.d:
ἀπό-κριμα, -τος, τό
(ἀποκρίνω);
__1. prop., a judicial sentence: 2Co.1:9, R, mg.
__2. an answer (see Thayer, see word): 2Co.1:9, R, txt. (In FlJ, Ant., xiv, 10, 6, of a rescript of the Senate; in Inscr. of an official decision, Deiss., BS, 257; a reply to a deputation, MM, see word: cf. also Cremer, 3'75).†
(AS)
G0610.o: from G611 (ἀποκρίνομαι) (in its original sense of judging);

G0611.d:
ἀποκρίνω, ἀποκρίνομαι,
[in LXX chiefly for ענה ;]
in cl.,
__1. to separate, distinguish.
__2. to choose.
Mid., to answer: Mat.27:12, Mrk.14:61, Luk.3:16 23:9, Jhn.5:17, 19 Act.3:12. In late Gk. the pass, also is used in this sense, and pass. forms are the more frequently in NT (M, Pr., 39, 161; MM, see word);
__(a) in general sense: absol., Mrk.12:34; with accusative of thing(s), Mat.22:46; with dative of person(s), Mat.12:38; before πρός, Act.25:16;
__(b) Hebraistically
__(i) like ענה, to begin to speak, take up the conversation (Kennedy, Sources, 124f.): Mat.11:25, al.,
__(ii)…
G0611.s: to conclude for oneself, i.e. (by implication) to respond; by Hebraism (compare H06030) to begin to speak (where an address is expected)

G0612.d:
ἀπό-κρισις, -εως, ἡ
(ἀποκρίνομαι), [in LXX for דָּבָר, etc. ;]
an answering, an answer: Luk.2:47 20:26, Jhn.1:22 19:9.†
(AS)

G0613.d:
ἀπο-κρύπτω
[in LXX chiefly for סָתַר ;]
to hide, conceal, keep secret: with accusative, Luk.10:21; pass., 1Co.2:7, Eph.3:9, Col.1:26 (MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0613.s: to conceal away (i.e. fully); figuratively, to keep secret

G0614.d:
ἀπόκρυφος, -ον
(ἀποκρύπτω), [in LXX Chiefly for סֵתֶר ;]
hidden: Mrk.4:22, Luk.8:17, Col.2:3 (see Lft., in l; MM, see word).†
(AS)

G0615.d:
ἀπο-κτείνω
(also in late forms -κτέννω, Mat.10:28, a1., LTTr., -κτεννύω, Mrk.12:5, WH), [in LXX for הָרַג, מוּת ;]
to kill: Mat.14:5, al.; before instr. ἐν (which see), Eph.2:16, Rev.2:23, al. Metaphorical: Rom.7:11; τ. ἔχθραν, Eph.2:16; τὸ γράμμα ἀποκτείνει 2Co.3:6 (on the perfective force of this verb, see M, Pr., 114)
(AS)
G0615.s: to kill outright; figuratively, to destroy

G0616.d:
ἀπο-κυέω
(Rec. -κύω), -ῶ (ἀπό, κυέω or κύω, to be pregnant), [in LXX: 4Ma.15:17 * ;]
prop., "the medical word for birth as the close of pregnancy" (Hort, Ja., 26 f.). In κοιν, "an ordinary syn. of τίκτω, but definitely 'perfectivised' (M, Pr., 111 ff.; MM, see word) by the
ἀπό, and so implying safe delivery," to bring forth, give birth to: Jas.1:15, 18.†
(AS)
G0616.s: to breed forth, i.e. (by transference) to generate (figuratively)
G0616.o: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G2949 (κῦμα);

G0617.d:
ἀπο-κυλίω
(see: κυλίω), [in LXX: Gen.29:3, 8 29:10 (גָּלַל) Jdth.13:9 * ;]
to roll away: Mat.28:2, Mrk.16:3, Luk.24:2.†
(AS)

G0618.d:
ἀπο-λαμβάνω
[in LXX: Num.34:14 (לָקַח (Deu.25:5 A, Isa.5:17, 2Ma.4:46 2Mac 6:21 2Mac 8:6, 4Ma.18:23 * ;]
__1. to receive from another; absol., to receive as one's due: Luk.16:25 18:30 (seel. λάβῃ) Luk.23:41, Rom.1:27, Gal.4:5, Col.3:24, 2Jn.8.
__2. to receive back: Luk.6:34 15:27.
__3. to take apart or aside: Mrk.7:33 (cf. use in π. of the recluses of the Serapeum; MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0618.s: to receive (specially, in full, or as a host); also to take aside

G0619.d:
ἀπόλαυσις, -εως, ἡ
(ἀπολαύω, to take of, enjoy a thing) [in LXX: 3Ma.7:16 * ;]
enjoyment: 1Ti.6:17, Heb.11:26 (for late exx., see MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0619.o: from a comparative of G575 (ἀπό) and (to enjoy);

G0620.d:
ἀπο-λείπω
[in LXX for H2308 יָתַר, etc. ;]
__1. to leave, leave behind (in π. a term. techn. in wills; see MM, see word): 2Ti.4:13 4:20, Tit.1:5; pass., to be reserved, remain: Heb.4:6, 9 10:26.
__2. to desert, abandon: Ju 6.†
(AS)
G0620.s: to leave behind (passively, remain); by implication, to forsake

G0621.d:
ἀπο-λείχω
(for ἐπιλ-, which see),
to lick up: Luk.16:21, Rec.†
(AS)

G0622.d:
ἀπ-όλλυμι and ἀπολλύω
[in LXX for אָבַד, etc. (38 words in all)].
__1. Act.,
__1 to destroy utterly, destroy, kill: Mk 124, 922, al.; τ. ψνχήν, Mat.10:28, al.;
__2 to lose utterly: Mat.10:42, al.; metaphorically, of failing to save, Jhn.6:39 18:9.
__2. Mid.,
__1 to perish;
__(a) of things: Mat.5:29, Jhn.6:12, Heb.1:11 (LXX, al.;
__(b) of persons: Mat.8:26, al. Metaphorical, of loss of eternal life, Jhn.3:15-16 10:28 17:12, Rom.2:12, 1Co.8:11 15:18, 2Pe.3:9. In οἱ ἀπολλὺμενοι, the perishing, contrasted in 1Co.1:18, al., with οἱ σωζόμενοι, the "perfective" force of the verb, WH. " implies the completion of the…
G0622.s: to destroy fully (reflexively, to perish, or lose), literally or figuratively
G0622.o: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G3639 (ὄλεθρος);

G0623.d:
Ἀπολλύων, -οντος, ὁ
(present ptcp. of ἀπολλύω),
Apollyon, i.e. the Destroyer: Rev.9:11 (cf. Ἀβάδδων). (Cremer, 453; DB, i, 125, 172.) †
(AS)

G0624.d:
Ἀπολλωνία, -ας, ἡ
Apollonia, a city of Macedonia: Act.17:1.†
(AS)
G0624.s: from G622 (ἀπόλλυμι)); Apollonia, a place in Macedonia
G0624.o: from the pagan deity (i.e. the sun;

G0625.d:
Ἀπολλώς, -ώ, ὁ
(perh. contr. from Ἀπολλώνιος, Act.18:24 D)
Apollos: Act.18:24 19:1, 1Co.1:12 3:4-6 3:22 4:6 16:12, Tit.3:13.†
(AS)
G0625.o: probably from the same as G624 (Ἀπολλωνία);

G0626.d:
ἀπολογέομαι, -οῦμαι
(ἀπό, λόγος), [in LXX: Jer.12:1 (רִיב) Jer.31:6, 2Ma.13:26 * ;]
__1. to defend: with accusative, Rom.2:15.
__2. to defend one's self: absol., Luk.21:14, Act.26:1; before ὅτι, Act.25:8; τί, to adduce something in one's defence, Luk.12:11, Act.26:24 (ταῦτα) Act.24:10 (τὰ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ); περί, with genitive of thing(s), and ἐπί, with genitive of person(s), Act.26:2; with dative of person(s), Act.19:33, 2Co.12:19.†
(AS)
G0626.s: to give an account (legal plea) of oneself, i.e. exculpate (self)
G0626.o: middle voice from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G3056 (λόγος);
G0626.k: answer (for self), make defence, excuse (self), speak for self

G0627.d:
ἀπολογία, -ας, ἡ
(ἀπολογέομαι), [in LXX: Wis.6:10 * ;]
a speech in defence: Act.25:16, 2Co.7:11, Php.1:7, 16, 2Ti.4:16; with dative of person(s), 1Co.9:3, 1Pe.3:15; before πρός, Act.22:1.†
(AS)
G0627.k: answer (for self), clearing of self, defence

G0628.d:
ἀπο-λούω
[in LXX: Job.9:30 (רָחַץ)* ;]
to wash off, wash away; mid., metaphorically, with accusative of thing(s), to wash off oneself: ἀμαρτίας, Act.22:16; absol., ἀπελούσασθε, ye washed yourselves clean (cf. Cremer, 406), 1Co.6:11.†
(AS)
G0628.s: to wash fully, i.e. (figuratively) have remitted (reflexively)

G0629.d:
ἀπο-λύτρωσις, -εως, ἡ
(ἀπολυτρόω, to release on payment of ransom, cf. λύτρον), [in LXX: Da (LXX) Dan.4:30 with * ;]
release effected by pay­ment of ransom, redemption, deliverance; metaphorically, Heb.11:35; of deliverance thr. Christ from evil and the consequences of sin: Luk.21:28, Rom.3:24 (Vau., in l) 8:23, 1Co.1:30, Eph.1:7, 14 4:30, Col.1:14, Heb.9:15. (On the extent to WH. the word retains the sense of ransom, see ICC, Rom.3:24, Westc., He., 297 ff.; see also ICC, Eph., 11; DCG, ii, 605; Cremer, 410; Deiss., LAE, 331; Lft., Notes, 271, 316; Tr., Syn., § 77.)†
(AS)
G0629.s: (the act) ransom in full, i.e. (figuratively) riddance, or (specially) Christian salvation
G0629.o: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G3083 (λύτρον);

G0630G.d:
ἀπο-λύω
[in LXX for שׁוּב, etc., frequently in 1-4 Mac ;]
__1. to set free, release: Luk.13:12, Jhn.19:10, al.; a debtor, Mat.18:27; metaphorically, of forgive­ness, Luk.6:37.
__2. to let go, dismiss (Field, Notes, 9 f.): Mat.15:23, Luk.2:29 9:12, Act.19:41, al.; of divorce, τ. γυναῖκα: Mat.1:19 5:31-32 19:3, 8 19:10 Mrk.10:2, 4 10:11, Luk.16:18; with ref. to Gk. and Rom. (net Jewish) custom, τ. ἄνδρα: Mrk.10:12. Mid., to depart: Act.28:25 (MM, see word)
(AS)
G0630G.s: to free fully, i.e. (literally) relieve, release, dismiss (reflexively, depart), or (figuratively) let die, pardon or (specially) divorce
G0630G.k: (let) depart, dismiss, divorce, forgive, let go, loose, put (send) away, release, set at liberty

G0630H.d:
ἀπο-λύω
[in LXX for שׁוּב, etc., frequently in 1-4 Mac ;]
__1. to set free, release: Luk.13:12, Jhn.19:10, al.; a debtor, Mat.18:27; metaphorically, of forgive­ness, Luk.6:37.
__2. to let go, dismiss (Field, Notes, 9 f.): Mat.15:23, Luk.2:29 9:12, Act.19:41, al.; of divorce, τ. γυναῖκα: Mat.1:19 5:31-32 19:3, 8 19:10 Mrk.10:2, 4 10:11, Luk.16:18; with ref. to Gk. and Rom. (net Jewish) custom, τ. ἄνδρα: Mrk.10:12. Mid., to depart: Act.28:25 (MM, see word)
(AS)
G0630H.s: to free fully, i.e. (literally) relieve, release, dismiss (reflexively, depart), or (figuratively) let die, pardon or (specially) divorce
G0630H.k: (let) depart, dismiss, divorce, forgive, let go, loose, put (send) away, release, set at liberty

G0631.d:
απο-μάσσω
(μάσσω, Att... -ττω, to touch, handle), [in LXX: Tob.7:17 * ;]
to wipe off, wire clean: mid., Luk.10:11.†
(AS)
G0631.o: middle voice from G575 (ἀπό) and (to squeeze, knead, smear);

G0632.d:
ἀπο-νέμω
(νέμω, to distribute), [in LXX: Deu.4:19 (חָלַק), 3Ma.1:7 3Mac 3:16 * ;]
to assign, apportion: 1Pe.3:7. (In π. of a Prefect who renders to all their dues; see MM, see word)†
(AS)
G0632.o: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G3551 (νόμος);

G0633.d:
ἀπο-νίπτω
[in LXX for שָׁטַף, רָחַץ, מָחָה ;]
to wash off: mid. (reflex.), τ. χεῖρας, Mat.27:24.†
(AS)
G0633.s: to wash off (reflexively, one's own hands symbolically)

G0634.d:
ἀπο-πίπτω
[in LXX for מָלַל, נָפַל, etc. ;]
to fall off: Act.9:18.†
(AS)

G0635.d:
ἀπο-πλανάω, -ῶ
[in LXX for נָדַח hi., נָטָה hi., שׁוּב pi. ;]
to cause to go astray; metaphorically, of leading into error: Mrk.13:22; pass., to be led astray: 1Ti.6:10.†
(AS)
G0635.s: to lead astray (figuratively); passively, to stray (from truth)

G0637.d:
ἀπο-πλύνω
[in LXX chiefly for כָּבַס pi. ;]
to wash off: seel. for πλύνω, Luk.5:2, Rec.†
(AS)

G0638.d:
ἀπο-πνίγω
[in LXX: Nam.2:13 (חָנַק pi.), Tob.3:8 * ;]
to choke: Mat.13:7, Luk.8:7; pass., of drowning (= καταποντίζομαι), Luk.8:33.†
(AS)

G0639.d:
ἀπορέω, -ῶ
(ἄπορος, ἀ- neg., πόρος, a way, resource), [in LXX for צָרַר, מוּךְ, etc. ;]
to be at a loss, be perplexed: absol., Mrk.6:20 (ἐποίει, R, mg.); mid., be in doubt: absol., 2Co.4:8; with accusative, Act.25:20; before περί, Luk.24:4; ἐν, Gal.4:20; περὶ τίνος λέγει, Jhn.13:22.†
SYN.: διαπορέω, διακρίνομαι, διστάζω, μετεωρίζομαι (see DCG, i, 491) (AS)
G0639.s: to have no way out, i.e. be at a loss (mentally)
G0639.o: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G4198 (πορεύομαι);

G0640.d:
ἀπορία, -ας, ἡ
(ἀπορέω), [in LXX for בֶּהָלָה, etc. ;]
perplexity: Luk.21:25 (MM, see word; on the construction, see Field, Notes, 74 f.).†
(AS)

G0641.d:
ἀπο-ρίπτω
(Rec. -ρρίπτω, c1.), [in LXX for שָׁלַךְ hi., etc. ;]
to throw away, cast forth: reflexively, Act.27:43 (BV, cast themselves overboard; see MM, see word).†
(AS)

G0642.d:
ἀπ-ορφανίζω
(ἀπό, ὀρφανός),
to be bereaved (prop., of a parent, Lft., Notes, 36); metaphorically, 1Th.2:17 (where Field thinks it = χωρισθέντες, Notes, 199).†
(AS)
G0642.s: to bereave wholly, i.e. (figuratively) separate (from intercourse)
G0642.o: from G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G3737 (ὀρφανός);

G0643.d:
ἀπο-σκευάζω
[in LXX: Lev.14:36 (פָּנָה pi.) * ;]
to pack and carry off; mid., to pack and remove one's goods: Act.21:15, Rec. (see ἐπισ-).†
ἐπι-σκευάζω,
[in LXX for pm pi., etc. ;]
to equip, make ready; mid., to make one's preparations: Act.21:15.†
(AS)
G0643.o: from G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G4632 (σκεῦος);

G0644.d:
ἀπο-σκίασμα, -τος, τό
(ἀποσκιάζω, to cast a shadow; v,s. σκία)
a shadow: Jas.1:17 (MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0644.o: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G4639 (σκιά);

G0645.d:
ἀπο-σπάω, -ῶ
[in LXX for נָתַק: ni., hi., etc. ;]
to draw off or away, tear away (MM, see word): Act.20:30; μάχαιραν, draw a sword, Mat.26:51; pass., to be parted or withdrawn (Field, Notes, 134; but see Thayer, see word), Luk.22:41, Act.21:1.†
(AS)
G0645.s: to drag forth, i.e. (literally) unsheathe (a sword), or relatively (with a degree of force implied) retire (personally or factiously)

G0646.d:
άποστασία, -ας, ἡ
(ἀφίστημι), [in LXX for מַעַל, etc. ;]
defection, apostasy, revolt; in late Gk. (MM, Exp., viii; Lft., Notes, 111; Cremer, 308) for cl. ἀπόστασις, frequently in sense of political revolt, in LXX (e.g. Jos.22:22, 2Ch.29:19, Jer.2:19) and NT always of religious apostasy: Act.21:21, 2Th.2:3.†
(AS)
G0646.o: feminine of the same as G647 (ἀποστάσιον);

G0647.d:
ἀποστάσιον, -ου, τό
(ἀφίστημι), [in LXX; Deu.24:1, 3, Jer.3:8, Isa.50:1 (כְּרִיתוּת) * ;]
__1. in cl., only in phrase ἀποστασίου δίκη, an action against a freedman for forsaking his προστάτης (Dem.).
__2. In LXX, βιβλίον ἀποστασίου, a bill of divorce: Mat.19:7, Mrk.10:4; in same sense ἀ. alone (MM, see word), Mat.5:31 (for other late exx., see MM, l.with; Kennedy, Sources, 121).†
(AS)
G0647.o: neuter of a (presumed) adjective from a derivative of G868 (ἀφίστημι);

G0648.o: from G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G4721 (στέγη);

G0649.d:
ἀπο-στέλλω,
[in LXX very freq., almost always for שׁלח ;]
prop., to send away, to dispatch on service;
__1. to send with a commission, or on service;
__(a) of persons: Christ, Mat.10:40; the apostles, 10:16; servants, Mrk.12:2; angels, 13:27;
__(b) of things: ὄνος, Mat.21:3; τὸ δρέπανον, Mrk.4:29; τ. λόγον, Act.10:36; τ. ἐπαγγελίαν (i.e. the promised Holy Spirit), Luk.24:49, Rec.; before εἰς, Mat.20:2, Luk.11:49, Jhn.3:17; ὀπίσω, Luk.19:14; ἔμπροσθεν, Jhn.3:28; πρὸ προσώπου, Mat.11:10; πρός, Mat.21:34; with ref. to sender or place of departure: ἀπό, Luk.1:26 (Rec. ὑπό); παρά, Jhn.1:6; ἐκ, ib. 1:19; ὑπό, Act.10:17 (Rec. ἀπό); before…
G0649.s: set apart, i.e. (by implication) to send out (properly, on a mission) literally or figuratively
G0649.k: put in, send (away, forth, out), set (at liberty)

G0650.d:
ἀπο-στερέω, -ῶ
(στερέω, to rob), [in LXX: Exo.21:10 (גָּרַע), Deu.24:14 (עָשַׁק), Mal.3:5, Sir.4:1 29:6-7 31:21-22 * ;]
to defraud, deprive of, despoil (in cl. chiefly of the misappropriation of trust funds, Field, Notes, 33; cf. MM, see word): absol., Mrk.10:19, 1Co.6:8; with accusative of person(s), 1Co.7:5. Mid., endure deprivation: 1Co.6:7 (WM, § 38, 3; but see Bl., § 54, 5; M, Pr., 162); pass., ἀπεστερημένοι, bereft of: 1Ti.6:5.†
(AS)
G0650.k: defraud, destitute, kept back by fraud

G0651.d:
ἀπο-στολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ἀποστέλλω), [in LXX: Deu.22:7, 3Ki.4:34 9:16 Psa.78:49, Ecc.8:8, Sng.4:13 (for שָׁלַח and its cognates), 1Es.9:51 Est.9:54, Jer.32:36, Bar.2:25, 1Ma.2:18, 2Ma.3:2 *.]
__1. In cl., a sending away (MM, see word), as, an expedition (Hdt.).
__2. In LXX
__(a) discharge, dis­missal (Ecc.8:8);
__(b) a gift (3Ki.9:16, 1Ma.2:13).
__3. In NT, the office of an Apostle of Christ, apostleship: Act.1:25, Rom.1:5, 1Co.9:2, Gal.2:8 (Cremer, 530).†
(AS)

G0652.d:
ἀπόστολος, -ου, ὁ
(ἀοστέλλω), [in LXX; 3Ki.14:6 A (שָׁלַח) * ;]
__1. a fleet, an expedition (Dem.).
__2. a messenger, one sent on a mission (Hdt., LXX, l.with, and π.; see M, Pr., 37 f.; MM, see word; M, Th., i, 2:7 and reff.): Jhn.13:16, 2Co.8:23 Php.2:25.
__3. In NT, an Apostle of Christ
__(a) with special ref. to the Twelve: Mat.10:2, Mrk.3:14, Luk.11:49, Eph.3:5, Rev.18:20, al., equality with whom is claimed by St. Paul, Gal.1:1, 11 ff, 1Ti.2:7, a1.;
__(b) in a wider sense of prominent Christian teachers, as Barnabas, Act.14:14, apparently also Silvanus and Timothy, 1Th.2:6, and perhaps Andronicus and Junias (Junia?), Rom.16:7 (see…
G0652.s: a delegate; specially, an ambassador of the Gospel; officially a commissioner of Christ ("apostle") (with miraculous powers)
G0652.k: apostle, messenger, he that is sent

G0653.d:
ἀποστοματίζω
(στόμα),
__1. In cl., to speak from memory, to dic­tate to a pupil (Plat.).
__2. In late Gk., to catechize, question: Luk.11:53 (MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0653.s: to speak off-hand (properly, dictate), i.e. to catechize (in an invidious manner)
G0653.o: from G575 (ἀπό) and a (presumed) derivative of G4750 (στόμα);

G0654.d:
ἀπο-στρέφω
[in LXX chiefly for שׁוּב ;]
trans., with accusative,
__(a) to turn away, remove: Rom.11:26, 2Ti.4:4; metaphorically, to turn away from allegiance, pervert: Luk.23:14;
__(b) to turn back, return: μάχαιραν, Mat.26:52. Pass., reflex., to turn oneself away from: with accusative, Mat.5:42, 2Ti.1:15, Tit.1:14, Heb.12:25; so act., absol., Act.3:26 (cf. Sir.8:5; Bl., § 53, 1; Cremer, 880).†
(AS)
G0654.s: to turn away or back (literally or figuratively)

G0655.o: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G4767 (στυγνητός);

G0657.d:
ἀπο-τάσσω
[in LXX: Ecc.2:20 (יָאַשׁ pi.), I Est.6:27, Jer.20:2, 1-18; 1Ma.4:1-61 * ;]
to set apart. Mid., in late Gk. (El., § 37, 1; Swete, Mk., 136 f.; MM, e. dative,
__(a) to take leave of: Mrk.6:46, Luk.9:61, Act.18:18, 21, 2Co.2:13;
__(b) to forsake: Luk.14:33.†
(AS)
G0657.s: literally, to say adieu (by departing or dismissing); figuratively, to renounce
G0657.o: middle voice from G575 (ἀπό) and G5021 (τάσσω);
G0657.k: bid farewell, forsake, take leave, send away

G0658.d:
ἀπο-τελέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: I Est.5:73, 1Ma.15:39 * ;]
to bring to an end, complete, accomplish (cf. MM, see word): Luk.13:32, Jas.1:15.†
(AS)

G0659.d:
ἀπο-τίθημι
[in LXX chiefly for נוּחַ hi. ;]
to put off or aside; in NT always mid.,
__(a) to put of from oneself as a garment: τ. ἱμάτια, Act.7:58; metaphorically, in ethical sense, to put of, lay aside: Rom.13:12, Eph.4:22, 25, Col.3:8, Heb.12:1, Jas.1:21, 1Pe.2:1;
__(b) to stow away, put: ἐν τ. φυλακῇ (MM, see word), Mat.14:3.†
(AS)
G0659.k: cast off, lay apart (aside, down), put away (off)

G0660.d:
ἀπο-τινάσσω
[in LXX: Jdg.16:20 A (נָעַר ni.), 1Ki.10:2 (נָטַשׁ), La 2:7 (נָאַר pi.) * ;]
to shake of: Luk.9:5, Act.28:5.†
(AS)

G0661.d:
ἀπο-τίνω (or -τίω)
[in LXX chiefly for שׂוּם pi. ;]
to pay off, repay: Phm 19 (MM, see word).†
(AS)

G0662.d:
ἀπο-τολμάω, -ῶ
to be quite bold, make a bold venture: Rom.10:20.†
(AS)

G0663.d:
ἀποτομία, -ας, ἡ
(ἀποτέμνω, to cut of), [in Sm.: Jer.51:35, Nam.3:1 * ;]
steepness, sharpness; metaphorically, severity (MM, see word): Rom.11:22.†
(AS)

G0664.d:
ἀποτόμως
adv., [in LXX: Wis.5:22 * ;]
abruptly, curtly, hence sharply, severely: 2Co.13:10, Tit.1:13 (MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0664.o: adverb from a derivative of a comparative of G575 (ἀπό) and (to cut);

G0665.d:
ἀπο-τρέπω
[in LXX: Sir.20:29 48:18, 3Ma.1:23, 4Ma.1:33 4Mac 16:12 * ;]
to turn away; mid., to turn oneself away from: with accusative, 2Ti.3:5.†
(AS)
G0665.o: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G5157 (τροπή);

G0666.d:
ἀπουσία, -ας, ἡ
(ἄπειμι);
__1. absence (Æsch., Thuc.): Php.2:12,
__2. deficiency, waste (MM, s.v).†
(AS)

G0667.d:
ἀπο-φέρω
[in LXX for הָלַךְ, etc. ;]
to carry off, bear, or lead away: with accusative, Mrk.15:1, 1Co.16:3, Rev.17:3 21:10. Pass., Luk.16:22, Act.19:12.†
(AS)

G0668.d:
ἀπο-φεύγω
[in LXX: Sir.22:22 * ;]
to flee from, escape: with accusative, 2Pe.2:18 2:20; with genitive, 2Pe.1:4.†
(AS)

G0669.d:
ἀπο-φθέγγομαι
[in LXX for נָבָא, etc. ;]
to speak forth, give utterance: Act.2:4, 14 26:25 (MM, s. see).†
(AS)

G0670.d:
ἀπο-φορτίζομαι
(φορτίζω, to load),
to discharge a cargo (Field, Notes, 134), to unlade: with accusative, τ. γόμον, Act.21:3.†
(AS)
G0670.o: from G575 (ἀπό) and the middle voice of G5412 (φορτίζω);

G0671.d:
ἀπό-χρησις, -εως, ἡ
(ἀποχράομαι, to use to the full, abuse)
abuse, misuse: Col.2:22 (MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0671.s: the act of using up, i.e. consumption
G0671.o: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G5530 (χράομαι);

G0672.d:
ἀπο-χωρέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Jer.46:5 (סוּג), 2Ma.4:33, 3Ma.2:33 * ;]
to go away, depart, withdraw: before ἀπό, Mat.7:23, Luk.9:39, Act.13:13 (absol., Luk.20:20, Tr., mg.).†
(AS)

G0673.d:
ἀπο-χωρίζω
[in LXX: Eze.43:21 (מִפְקָד)* ;]
to separate, part asunder: pass., Rev.6:14; reflexively, to separate oneself: Act.15:39.†
(AS)
G0673.s: to rend apart; reflexively, to separate

G0674.d:
ἀπο-ψύχω
[in LXX: 4Ma.15:18 * ;]
__1. to breathe out life, expire (Thue.; LXX, l.with).
__2. to leave off breathing, faint (Hom., Od., xxiv, 348): before ἀπό, Luk.21:26.†
(AS)

G0675.d:
Ἀππιος, -ου, ὁ
Appius; Ἀππίου Φόρον, Appii Forum (Market of Appius), a town in Italy: Act.28:15.†
(AS)
G0675.s: (in the genitive, i.e. possessive case) of Appius, the name of a Roman

G0676.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a comparative of G4314 (πρός) and (to go);

G0677.d:
ἀπρόσκοπος, -ον
(προσκόπτω), [in LXX: Sir.32:21, 3Ma.3:8 * ;]
__1. act., not causing to stumble: metaphorically, of not leading others into sin, 1Co.10:32.
__2. Pass., not stumbling, without offence, blameless: Act.24:16, Php.1:10 (for exx., see MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0677.s: actively, inoffensive, i.e. not leading into sin; passively, faultless, i.e. not led into sin
G0677.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4350 (προσκόπτω);

G0678.d:
ἀπροσωπολήμπτως (Rec. -λήπτως, cl.), adv.
(α- neg., προσωπολήμπτης),
without respect of persons, impartially: 1Pe.1:17.†
(AS)
G0678.s: in a way not accepting the person, i.e. impartially
G0678.o: adverb from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a presumed compound of G4383 (πρόσωπον) and G2983 (λαμβάνω) (compare G4381 (προσωπολήπτης));

G0679.d:
ἄ-πταιστος, -ον
(πταίω), [in LXX: 3Ma.6:39 * ;]
without stumbling, sure-footed: metaphorically (MM, see word), Ju 24.†
(AS)
G0679.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4417 (πταίω);

G0680.d:
to touch, hold, handle; (act.) to start a fire; "to touch a woman" means "to get married"
primarily to bring in contact, fit, fasten; to light, kindle, Mk. 4:21; Lk. 8:16; to touch, Mt. 8:3; to meddle, venture to partake, Col. 2:21; to have intercourse with, to know carnally, 1Cor. 7:1; by implication to harm, 1Jn. 5:18
G0680.s: properly, to attach oneself to, i.e. to touch (in many implied relations)

G0681.d:
ἅπτω
[in LXX chiefly for נָגַע ;]
prop., to fasten to; hence, of fire, to kindle, light: Luk.8:16 11:33 15:8, Act.28:2. Mid., with genitive, to fasten oneself to, cling to, lay hold of (so in π.; MM, see word): Mat.8:3, 15, Jhn.20:17, al.; of carnal intercourse, 1Co.7:1; with reference to levitical and ceremonial prohibitions, 2Co.6:17, Col.2:21; of hostile action, 1Jn.5:18 (cf. ἀν-, καθ-, περι- άπτω)
SYN.: θιγγάνω, ψηλαφάω. ἅ. is the stronger, θ., to touch, the lighter term. ψ. is to feel, as in search of something (Tr., Syn., § xvii; Lft., Col., 201 f.) (AS)
G0681.s: properly, to fasten to, i.e. (specially) to set on fire

G0683.d:
ἀπ-ωθέω, -ῶ
[in LXX for זָנַח, מָאַס, etc. ;]
to thrust away. Mid., to thrust away from oneself, refuse, reject: with accusative of person(s) (MM, see word), Act.7:27, 39 13:46, Rom.11:1-2, 1Ti.1:19.†
(AS)
G0683.s: to push off, figuratively, to reject
G0683.o: from G575 (ἀπό) and the middle voice of or (to shove);
G0683.k: cast away, put away (from), thrust away (from)

G0684.d:
ἀπώλεια, -ας, ἡ
(ἀπόλλυμι), [in LXX (Cremer, 797) for אָבַד, אֵיד, etc. ;]
destruction, waste, loss, perishing (in π., of money, see MM, see word): Mat.26:8, Mrk.14:4, Act.8:20, Rom.9:22, 1Ti.6:9, 2Pe.2:1; in special sense of the loss of eternal life, perdition, the antithesis of σωτηρία: Mat.7:13, Jhn.17:12, Php.1:28 3:19, 2Th.2:3, Heb.10:39, 2Pe.2:3 3:7 3:16, Rev.17:8, 11 (DB, iii, 744).†
(AS)
G0684.s: ruin or loss (physical, spiritual or eternal)
G0684.o: from a presumed derivative of G622 (ἀπόλλυμι);
G0684.k: damnable(-nation), destruction, die, perdition, X perish, pernicious ways, waste

G0685.d:
ἀρά, -ᾶς, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for אָלָה ];
__1. a prayer (MM, see word).
__2. (as in Homer) a curse, malediction: Rom.3:14 (LXX),†
(AS)
G0685.s: properly, prayer (as lifted to Heaven), i.e. (by implication) imprecation

G0686.d:
ἄρα,
illative particle, expressing a more subjective or informal inference than οὖν,
then: prop. (as in cl.), the second word in the sentence, Rom.7:21 8:1, Gal.3:7; ἐπεὶ ἄρα, 1Co.7:14 (with another word between) 5:10; as the first word, Luk.11:48, Act.11:18, Rom.10:17, 1Co.15:18, 2Co.5:15 7:12, Heb.4:9; so prop. in apodosis after protasis with εἰ, Mat.12:28, Luk.11:20, Gal.2:21 3:29 5:11, Heb.12:8 (κενὸν ἄρα), 1Co.15:14; often in interrogations, direct and indirect, τίς (τί) ἄρα, Mat.18:1 19:25, 27 24:45, Mrk.4:41, Luk.1:66 8:25 12:42 22:23, Act.12:18; εἰ ἄρα, Mrk.11:13, Act.8:22; εἴπερ ἄρα, 1Co.15:15; οὐκ ἄρα, Act.21:38; μήτι ἄρα, 2Co.1:17; in strengthened…
G0686.s: a particle denoting an inference more or less decisive (as follows)
G0686.o: probably from G142 (αἴρω) (through the idea of drawing a conclusion);
G0686.k: haply, (what) manner (of man), no doubt, perhaps, so be, then, therefore, truly, wherefore

G0687.d:
ἆρα,
interrog. particle,
implying anxiety or impatience, "quite rare and only in Luke and Paul, therefore a literary word" (Bl., §77, 2).
__1. (num igitur) expecting a neg. reply, Luk.18:8; ἆρά γε, Act.8:30.
__2. (ergone) in apodosis, expecting an affirm. reply, Gal.2:17 (Bl., l.with; Lft., Ga., in l.; MM, see word).
† (AS)
G0687.o: a form of G686 (ἄρα), denoting an interrogation to which a negative answer is presumed

G0689.d:
Ἀράμ indec. (Heb. רָם),
Aram: Mat.1:3-4, Luk.3:33 (R, txt., WH, Ἀρνεί).†
(AS)

G0690.s: an Arab or native of Arabia

G0691.d:
ἀργέω, -ῶ
(ἀργός), [in LXX: Est.4:24, Ecc.12:3 (בָּטֵל), I Est.2:30, Sir.33:27), 2Ma.5:25 * ;]
to be idle; τὸ κρίμα . . . ἀ., lingers (cf. MGr. ἀργά, late: MM, see word): 2Pe.2:3.†
(AS)
G0691.s: to be idle, i.e. (figuratively) to delay

G0692.d:
ἀργός, -όν
(in late Gk., incl. NT, -ή, -όν; ἀ- neg., ἔργον) [in LXX: 3Ki.6:7 (מַסָּע), Wis.14:5 15:15, Sir.37:11 38:28 * ;]
inactive, idle: Mat.20:3, 6, 1Ti.5:13, Tit.1:12, 2Pe.1:8. Metaphorical, of things, inactive, ineffective, worthless: ῥῆμα, Mat.12:36; πίστις, Jas.2:20 (see Cremer, 259 f.).†
SYN.: βραδύς, slow; νωθρός, sluggish (Tr., Syn., § civ) (AS)
G0692.s: inactive, i.e. unemployed; (by implication) lazy, useless
G0692.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2041 (ἔργον);

G0693.d:
ἀργύρεος (see MM, see word), -οῦς, -ᾶ, -οῦν
(ἄργυρος), [in LXX for כֶּסֶף ;]
of silver: Act.19:24 (WH, br.), 2Ti.2:20, Rev.9:20.†
(AS)

G0694.d:
ἀργύριον, -ου, τό
(ἄργυρος), [in LXX for כֶּסֶף (Gen.13:2, al.), exc. La 4:1 (כֶּתֶם) ;]
prop., a piece of silver (Lft., Notes, 191); in NT,
__(a) silver: Act.3:6 7:16 19:19 20:33, 1Co.3:12, 1Pe.1:18;
__(b) money: Mat.25:18, 27, Mrk.14:11, Luk.9:3 19:15, 23 22:5, Act.8:20;
__(with) a silver coin: p1., Mat.26:15 27:3-6, 9 28:12, 15, where the value is that of a shekel or tetradrachm; ἀργυρίου μυριάδες πέντε (prob. drachmas; MM, see word), Act.19:19.†
(AS)
G0694.s: silvery, i.e. (by implication) cash; specially, a silverling (i.e. drachma or shekel)
G0694.o: neuter of a presumed derivative of G696 (ἄργυρος);

G0695.d:
ἀργυροκόπος, -ου, ὁ
(ἄργυρος, κόπτω, to beat) [in LXX: Jdg.17:4, Jer.6:29 (צָרַף) * ;]
a silversmith: Act.19:24 (Plut.; 77., see MM, see word).†
(AS)

G0696.d:
ἄργυρος, -ου, ὁ
(ἀργός, shining), [in LXX for כֶּסֶף ;]
silver (on its relation to ἀργύριον, see MM, see word): Mat.10:9, Act.17:29, Jas.5:5, Rev.18:12.†
(AS)
G0696.s: silver (the metal, in the articles or coin)

G0697.d:
Ἄρειος Πάυος (T, Ἄριος Π.), -ου, ὁ
Hill of Pres or Mars, Areopagus; also, the Court of Areopagus, the highest tribunal of Athens: Act.17:19, 22.†
(AS)
G0697.s: rock of Ares, a place in Athens
G0697.o: from (the name of the Greek deity of war) and a derivative of G4078 (πήγνυμι);

G0698.d:
Ἀρεοπαγίτης (T, -είτης), -ου, ὁ (see supr.),
a judge of the Court of Areopagus: Act.17:34.†
(AS)
G0698.s: an Areopagite or member of the court held on Mars' Hill

G0699.d:
ἀρεσκία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ
(ἀρέσκω), [in LXX (-εία): Pro.31:30 (חֵן) * ;]
pleasing, desire to please: Col.1:19 In Gk. writers (Arist., Polyb.), most frequently in bad sense, but in π., Inscr., and in Philo, as above (see Deiss., BS, 224; MM, see word; Cremer, 642).†
(AS)

G0700.d:
ἀρέσκω
[in LXX chiefly for טוֹב ;]
__1. to please (Hom., Hdt., al.): with dative of person(s), Mat.14:6, Mrk.6:22, Rom.8:8 15:2, 1Th.2:15 4:1, 1Co.7:32-34 Gal.1:10, 2Ti.2:4; before ἐνώπισν (= Heb. בּעֵנֵי, Bl., § 37, 1; 40, 7), Ac 65.
__2. In late Gk., esp. in Inscr., to render service to (see M, Th., ICC, 1 Co., ll with; Cremer, 640 f.); Rom.15:1, 3, 1Co.10:33, 1Th.2:4.†
(AS)
G0700.s: to be agreeable (or by implication, to seek to be so)
G0700.o: probably from G142 (αἴρω) (through the idea of exciting emotion);

G0701.d:
ἀρεστός, -ή, -όν
(ἀρέσκω), [in LXX for יָשָׁר, etc. ;]
pleasing, agreeable (Hdt., Xen., and later writers; see Cremer, 641 f; MM, see word): with dative of person(s), Jhn.8:29, Act.12:3; before ἐνώπιον, with genitive (Bl., § 37, 1; 40, 7), 1Jn.3:22; ἀρεστόν ἐστιν, with accusative and inf (El., § 69, 5; 72, 5), Act.6:2.†
(AS)

G0702.d:
Ἀρέτας (WH, Ἀρ.; Intr., 313), -α, ὁ,
Aretas, an Arabian king: 2Co.11:32 (Deiss., BS, 183 f., thinks the proper spelling Ἀρέθας was changed, as Schürer suggests, "by desire to Hellenise a barbaric name by assimilation to ἀρετή").†
(AS)

G0703.d:
ἀρετή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX, in sing.: Hab.3:3, Zec.6:13 (הוֹד), in pl.: Isa.42:8, 12 43:21 63:7 (תְּהִלָּה), Wis.4:1 5:13 8:7 2:1-24; 4Mac.2.2 * ;]
prop., whatever procures pre-eminent estimation for a person or thing, in Hom. any kind of conspicuous advantage. Later confined by philos. writers to intrinsic eminence-moral goodness, virtue;
__(a) of God: 2Pe.1:3;
__(b) of men: Php.4:8, 2Pe.1:5; pl. (Isa, Es, ll. with), excellencies: 1Pe.2:9 (the usage appears to be a survival of an early comprehensive sense in which the original idea is blended with the impression which it makes on others, i.e. praise, renown; see Hort, 1 Pe., 129. Deiss., BS, 95…
G0703.s: properly, manliness (valor), i.e. excellence (intrinsic or attributed)

G0704.d:
ἀρήν, ἀρνός, ὁ
(nom, not in use, exc. in early times: see MM, see word), [in LXX for מְרִיא, כֶּבֶשׂ, etc. ;]
a lamb: Luk.10:3.†
(AS)

G0705.d:
ἀριθμέω, -ῶ
[in LXX for סָפַר pi., פָּקַד pi., etc. ;]
to number (esp. for payment, MM, see word): Mat.10:30, Luk.12:7, Rev.7:9.†
(AS)

G0706.d:
ἀριθμός, -οῦ, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for מִסְפָּר ;]
number, a number: Luk.22:3, Jhn.6:10, Act.4:4 5:36 6:7 11:21 16:5, Rom.9:27, Rev.5:11 7:4 9:16 13:17-18 15:2 20:8 (for exx. of mystical use in π., see MM, see word).†
(AS)

G0707.d:
Ἁριμαθεία
(WH, Ἁρ.), -ας, ἡ [in LXX: Ἁριμαθάιμ, 1Ki.1:1, al. (רָמָה) ;]
Arimathæa: Mat.27:57, Mrk.15:43, Luk.23:51, Jhn.19:38.†
(AS)
G0707.s: Arimathæa (or Ramah), a place in Palestine

G0708.d:
Ἀρίσταρχος, -ου, ὁ
(ἄριστος, ἀρχός; i.e. best-ruling)
Aristarchus: Act.19:29 20:4 27:2, Col.4:10, Phm 24
(AS)
G0708.o: from the same as G712 (ἄριστον) and G757 (ἄρχω);

G0709.d:
ἀριστάω, -ῶ
(ἄριστον), [in LXX: Gen.43:25 (לֶחֶם אָכַל), 1Ki.14:24 (לֶחֶם), 3Ki.13:7 (סָעַד), Tob.2:1 * ;]
__1. prop., to breakfast: Jhn.21:12, 15
__2. In late Gk., to take a meal, dine: Luk.11:37.†
(AS)

G0710.d:
ἀριστερός, -ά, -όν
[in LXX for שְׂמֹאול ;]
left, on the left: ὅπλα, 2Co.6:7; ἡ ἀ.. (sc. χείρ), Mat.6:3; ἐξ ἀριστερῶν, on the left (MM, see word ): Mrk.10:37, Luk.23:33.†
(AS)
G0710.o: apparently a comparative of the same as G712 (ἄριστον);

G0711.d:
Ἀριστόβουλος, -ου, ὁ
(ἄριστος, βουλή, i.e. best-counselling)
Aristobulus, a Christian: Rom.16:10.†
(AS)
G0711.o: from the same as G712 (ἄριστον) and G1012 (βουλή);

G0712.d:
ἄριστον, -ου, τό
[in LXX: 3Ki.3:1 (לֶחֶם), Tob.2:1, 4, al. ;]
__1 1, prop., breakfast.
__2. In late Gk. = cl. δεῖτνον, dinner: Mat.22:4, Luk.11:38 14:12.†
(AS)
G0712.s: the best meal (or breakfast; perhaps from ("early")), i.e. luncheon
G0712.o: apparently neuter of a superlative from the same as G730 (ἄῤῥην);

G0713.d:
ἀρκετός, -ή, -όν
(ἀρκέω), [in Aq.: Deu.25:2 * ;]
sufficient: Mat.6:34 (on the neut., see B1., § 31, 2); before ἵνα (M, Pr., 210), Mat.10:25; with inf., 1Pe.4:3 (for exx., see Deiss., BS, 257; MM, see word).†
(AS)

G0714.d:
ἀρκέω, -ῶ
[in LXX for הוֹן, etc. ;]
__1. to keep off; with dative, to assist.
__2. to suffice: with dative of person(s), Jo 67, 2Co.12:9; impers., Mat.25:9, Jhn.14:8 (MM, see word). Pass., to be satisfied: with dative of thing(s), Luk.3:14, 1Ti.6:8, Heb.13:5; before ἐπί, III Jn 10.†
(AS)
G0714.s: properly, to ward off, i.e. (by implication) to avail (figuratively, be satisfactory)
G0714.o: apparently a primary verb (but probably akin to G142 (αἴρω) through the idea of raising a barrier);
G0714.k: be content, be enough, suffice, be sufficient

G0715.d:
ἅρκος
(Rec. (cl.) ἅρκιος), [in LXX for דֹּב ;] -ου, ὁ, ἡ,
a bear: Rev.13:2. (This form is also found in late Inscr.; MM, see word)†
(AS)

G0716.d:
ἅρμα, -τος, τό
(ἀραρίσκω, to join), [in LXX רָכַב ;]
a chariot: Act.8:28-29, 38, Rev.9:9.†
(AS)
G0716.s: a chariot (as raised or fitted together (compare G719 (ἁρμός)))
G0716.o: probably from G142 (αἴρω) (perhaps with G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) prefixed);

G0717.d:
Ἁρμαγεδών (WH, Ἃρ Μαγεδών; Rec. Ἀρμαγεδδών, prop. = הַר מְגִדּוֹן), cf. LXX, Μαγεδών, 2Ch.35:22, Μαγεδώ, Jdg.1:27; Har-Magedon (AV, Armageddon): Rev.16:16 (see Swete, in l, but also Thayer, see word).†
Ἅρ,
indecl., Rev.16:16, see, Ἁρμαγεδών
Μαγεδών,
Magedon: Rev.16:16 (WH, Ἅρ M. for Ἁρμαγεδών, which see).†
(AS)

G0718.d:
ἁρμόζω
(ἁρμός), [in LXX for אמן, etc. ;]
__1. to fit, join.
__2. of marriage, to betroth. Mid.,
__(a) to join to oneself, marry, take to wife; (b) to give in marriage: 2Co.11:2 (for this there is no direct parallel. But see M, Pr., 160; MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0718.s: to joint, i.e. (figuratively) to woo (reflexively, to betroth)

G0719.d:
ἁρμός, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Sir.27:2, 4Ma.10:5 * ;]
a joining, joint: Heb.4:12.†
(AS)

G0720.d:
ἀρνέομαι -οῦμαι, depon.,
[in LXX: Gen.18:15 (כָּחַשׁ pi.), Wis.12:27 16:16 17:10, 4Ma.8:7 4Mac 10:15 * ;]
__1. to deny, say no, opposite to είπεῖν: absol., Mat.26:70, Luk.8:45; before ἅτι, 1Jn.2:22; with inf., Heb.11:24
__2. In late Gk. (MM, see word), with accusative of person(s), to deny, refuse to acknowledge, disown: Act.3:14 7:35; Ἰησοῦν, Mat.10:33, 2Ti.2:12, 1Jn.2:22, Ju 4; ἑαυτόν, Luk.9:23, 2Ti.2:13 (prove false to)
__3. C. accusative of thing(s) (in cl. to refuse), to deny, abjure: 1Ti.5:8, Tit.2:12, 2Ti.3:5 (cf. ἀπαρνέομαι)
(AS)
G0720.s: to contradict, i.e. disavow, reject, abnegate
G0720.o: perhaps from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the middle voice of G4483 (ῥέω);

G0721.d:
ἀρνίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of ἀρήν; see MM, see word), [in LXX: Psa.114:4, 6 (pl., צֹאן בֵּן), Jer.11:19 (כֶּבֶשׂ), Jer.50:45 (צָעִיר)* ;]
a little lamb, a lamb: Jhn.21:15, Rev.2:7.†
(AS)

G0722.d:
ἀροτριάω, -ῶ
(ἄροτρον), [in LXX: Deu.22:10, al. (חָרַשׁ), Isa.7:25 (עֲדַר) ;]
later form of ἀρόω, to plough (MM, see word): Luk.17:7, 1Co.9:10.†
(AS)

G0723.d:
ἄροτρον, -ου, τό
(ἀρόω, to plough), [in LXX chiefly for אֵת ;]
a plough: Luk.9:62.†
(AS)

G0724.d:
ἁρπαγή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ἁρπάζω), [in LXX (as also ἅρπαγμα) for גָּזֵל, etc. ;]
pillage, plundering, robbery: Mat.23:25, Luk.11:39, Heb.10:34.†
(AS)

G0725.d:
ἁρπαγμός, οῦ, ὁ
(ἁρπάζω);
__1. prop., accusative, to the rule of its formation (Bl., § 27, 2), actively, the act of seizing, robbery (Plut., Deu Puer. Educ., p. 12A), Php.2:6, AV (Waterland, Works, II, 108; Cremer, 649 f.; Meyer, in l; cf. also JThS, July, 1909, April, 1911; MM, see word).
__2. Passively = ἅρπαγμα (Eze.22:25, of a lion's prey, ), a thing seized, hence, a prize: Phi, l.with, RV (Lft., Ellic., ICC, in l; Donaldson, NCrat., 450 ff.; and esp. Gifford, The Incarnation, 59-71, and reff. in DB, ii, 835 B). The lexical data favour the active meaning, but as they also admit the possibility of the alternative, most modern expositors have…

G0726.d:
ἁρπάζω
[in LXX chiefly for גָּזַל, טָרַף ;]
to seize, catch up, snatch away, carry off by force: with accusative of thing(s), Mat.12:29 13:19, Jhn.10:12, 28-29; τ. βασιλείαν τ. θεοῦ, Mat.11:12; with accusative of person(s), Jhn.6:15, Act.8:39 23:10, Ju 23; pass., before ἕως, 2Co.12:2; εἰς, 2Co.12:4, 1Th.4:17; πρός, Rev.12:5 (cf. δι-, συν-αρπάζω, and see MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0726.k: catch (away, up), pluck, pull, take (by force)

G0727.d:
ἅρπαξ, -αγος, ὁ, ἡ
(ἁρπάζω), [in LXX: Gen.49:27 (טָרַף) * ;]
rapacious: Mat.7:15, Luk.18:11; as subst., a swindler, an extortioner (MM, see word), 1Co.5:10-11 6:10.†
(AS)

G0728.d:
ἀρραβών
(T, ἀραβ-: 2Co, ll. with), -ώνος, ὁ, [in LXX: Gen.38:17-20 (עֲרָבוֹן)* ;]
an earnest, part payment in advance for security, a first instalment: 2Co.1:22 5:5, Eph.1:14. (The word is found in cl. and was prob. brought to Greece by the Phænicians (AR, Eph., l.with). It is found in π. with both spellings (see Milligan, NTD, 73). In MGr. ἀρραβῶνα is an engagement ring; see MM, see word)†
(AS)
G0728.s: a pledge, i.e. part of the purchase-money or property given in advance as security for the rest

G0729.s: unsewed, i.e. of a single piece
G0729.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of the same as G4476 (ῥαφίς);

G0730.d:
ἄρσην (ἄρρην, T, in Rom.1:27; Rec. in Rev.12:5, 13) -ενος, ὁ, ἡ, ἄρσεν, τό
(old Attic for ἄρρην, see supr.; both forms are found in π.; MM, see word), [in LXX chiefly for זָכָר ;]
male: Mat.19:4, Mrk.10:6, Luk.2:23, Rom.1:27, Gal.3:28, Rev.12:5, 13.†
(AS)

G0731.d:
ἄρρητος, -ον
(ἀ- neg., ῥητός, ῥέω), [in Sm.: Lev.18:23 * ;]
__1. unspoken (Hom., al.).
__2. unspeakable (Hat., al.; frequently in Inscr.; MM, see word): 2Co.12:4.†
(AS)
G0731.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the same as G4490 (ῥητῶς);

G0732.d:
ἄρρωστος, -ον
(ἀ- neg., ῥώννυμι), [in LXX: 3Ki.14:5Α, Mal.1:8 (חָלָה), Sir.7:35 * ;]
feeble, sickly: Mat.14:14, Mrk.6:5, 13 16:18, 1Co.11:30.†
(AS)
G0732.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4517 (ῥώννυμι);

G0733.k: abuser of (that defile) self with mankind

G0734.s: gift of Artemis; Artemas (or Artemidorus), a Christian
G0734.o: contracted from a compound of G735 (Ἄρτεμις) and G1435 (δῶρον);

G0735.d:
Ἄρτεμις, -ιδος, ἡ
Artemis, an Asiatic goddess, to be disting. from the Gk. goddess of the same name: Act.19:24, 27-28
(AS)
G0735.s: prompt; Artemis, the name of a Grecian goddess borrowed by the Asiatics for one of their deities
G0735.o: probably from the same as G736 (ἀρτέμων);

G0736.d:
ἀρτέμων, -ωνος (Rec. -ονος), ὁ
(ἀρτάω, to fasten to),
a fore-sail or top-sail: Act.27:40 (see DB, ext., 366b, 399a; MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0736.s: properly, something ready (or else more remotely from G142 (αἴρω) (compare G740 (ἄρτος)); something hung up), i.e. (specially) the topsail (rather foresail or jib) of a vessel

G0737.d:
ἄρτι
adv., [in LXX: Dan LXX 9:22 10:11 (עַתָּה), al. ;]
adv.,
of coincidence, denoting strictly present time, as contrasted with past or future, just, just now, this moment: Mat.3:15 9:18 26:53, Jhn.13:7, Gal.4:20, 1Th.3:6 (see Lft., Notes, 44; Milligan, in l), Rev.12:10; opposite to past time, Jhn.9:19, 25 13:33, 1Co.16:7, Gal.1:9-10; to future, Jhn.13:37 16:12, 31, 1Co.13:12, 2Th.2:7, 1Pe.1:6 1:8; ἄχρι τῆς ἅ. ὥρας, 1Co.4:11; ἕως ἄ., Mat.11:12, Jhn.2:10 5:17 16:24, 1Co.4:13 8:7 15:6, 1Jn.2:9; ἀπ᾽ ἄ., see: ἀπάρτι (see Rutherford, NPhr., 70 f; MM, see word).†
SYN.: νῦν, now, "the objective, immediate present; ἤδη, now,…
G0737.o: adverb from a derivative of G142 (αἴρω) (compare G740 (ἄρτος)) through the idea of suspension;
G0737.k: this day (hour), hence(-forth), here(-after), hither(-to), (even) now, (this) present

G0738.s: just born, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert

G0740.d:
ἄρτος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for לֶחֶם ;]
bread, a loaf: Mat.4:3, 4 Mrk.3:20, al.; ἄρτοι τ. προθέσεως, bread of the setting forth, i.e. the shewbread. Metaphorical, ὁ ἄ. τ. θεοῦ, τ. ζωῆς, ref. to Christ, Jhn.6:33, 35; in general, food: Mat.6:11, al.; ἄ. φαγεῖν (Heb. אֲכֹל לֶחֶם), to eat (MM, see word), Lu 14:1, al.
(AS)

G0741.d:
ἀρτύω
[in Sm.: Sng.8:2 * ;]
__1. to arrange, make ready (Hom.).
__2. Of food (as in comic writers), to season (MM, see word): Mrk.9:50, Luk.14:34, Col.4:6.†
(AS)
G0741.s: to prepare, i.e. spice (with stimulating condiments)
G0741.o: from a presumed derivative of G142 (αἴρω);

G0743.d:
ἀρχ-άγγελος, -ου, ὁ
(ἄρχι-, ἄγγελος),
archangel, a chief angel: 1Th.4:16, Ju 9 (Cremer, 24; MM, see word).†
(AS)

G0744.d:
ἀρχαῖος, -αία, -αῖον
(ἀρχή), [in LXX chiefly for קֶדֶם ;]
original, ancient: Mat.5:21, 33, Luk.9:8, 19, Act.15:7, 21 21:16, 2Co.5:17, 2Pe.2:5, Rev.12:9 20:2.†
SYN.: παλαιός, old, without the reference to beginning and origin contained in ἀ. The distinction is observed in π. (MM, see word). ἀ. is the antithesis to καινός: παλ. to vέος (see Westc., He., 223; Cremer, 116) (AS)

G0745.d:
Ἀρχέλαος, -ου, ὁ
Archelaus, son of Herod the Great, King of Judma, Samaria and Idumæa: Mat.2:22.†
(AS)

G0746.d:
ἀρχή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX for קֶדֶם, רֹאשׁ, רֹאשׁ, etc. ;]
__1. beginning, origin;
__(a) absol., of the beginning of all things: of God as the Eternal, the First Cause, Rev.21:6 (cf. 18); similarly, of Christ, Rev.22:13; of Christ as the uncreated principle, the active cause of creation, Rev.3:14; in his relation to the Church, Col.1:18; ἐν ἀ., Jhn.1:1-2; ἀπ᾽ ἀ. (and ἀπ᾽ ἀ. κτισεως), Mat.19:4, 8 24:21, Mrk.10:6 13:19, Jhn.8:44, 2Th.2:13, 2Pe.3:4, 1Jn.1:1 Jn 2:13-14 Jn 2:24; κατ ἀρχἀς, Heb.1:10;
__(b) relatively: Heb.7:3; ἀ. ὠδίνων, Mat.24:8, Mrk.13:9; τ. σημείων, Jhn.2:11; τ. ὑποστάσεως, Heb.3:14; τ. λογίων, Heb.5:12; ὁ τ. ἀρχῆς τ. Χριστοῦ λόγος, the…
G0746.s: (properly abstract) a commencement, or (concretely) chief (in various applications of order, time, place, or rank)
G0746.k: beginning, corner, (at the, the) first (estate), magistrate, power, principality, principle, rule

G0747.d:
ἀρχηγός, -όν
[in LXX for רֹאשׁ, נָשִׂיא etc. ;]
beginning, originating: more freq., as subst.;
__1. founder, author (Lat. auchor; so some­times in π., see MM, see word; Milligan, NTD, 75): Act.3:15 (R, mg.), Heb.2:10 (R, txt.; but see Westc., in l, and Page, Ac., l.with).
__2. prince, leader (so in MGr., see Kennedy, Sources, 153): Act.3:15 (R, txt.) Act.5:31, Heb.2:10 (cf. R, mg.) 122 (Cremer, 117).†
(AS)

G0748.o: from G746 (ἀρχή) and a derivative of G2413 (ἱερός);

G0749.d:
ἀρχιερεύς, -έως, ὁ,
[in LXX for כּ'' הָרֹאשׁ,כּ'' הַגָּדוֹל ,כּהֵן ;]
__1. high-priest: Mrk.2:26 14:47, al.; of Christ: Heb.2:17 3:1, al.
__2. In pl., chief priests, including ex-high-priests and members of high-priestly families: Mat.2:4, Mrk.8:31, al. (Cremer, 294; DCG, i, 297f.; MM, see word).
(AS)
G0749.s: the high-priest (literally, of the Jews, typically, Christ); by extension a chief priest
G0749.k: chief (high) priest, chief of the priests

G0750.d:
ἀρχι-ποίμην, -ενος, ὁ
[in Sm.: 4Ki.3:4 * ;]
found on an Egyptian mummy label (Deiss., LAE, 97 ff.; cf. MM, see word); used by modem Greeks of tribal chiefs; chief shepherd. of Christ, 1Pe.5:4.†
(AS)

G0752.d:
ἀρχισυνάγωγος, -ου, ὁ
(συναγωγή),
ruler of a synagogue, an administrative officer, supervising the worship (הַכְּנֵםֶת רֹאשׁ): Mrk.5:22, 35-36 5:38 Luk.8:49 13:14, Act.13:15 18:8, 17 (Inscr., see MM, see word; cf. also DB, ext., 101).†
(AS)

G0753.d:
ἀρχι-τέκτων, -ονος, ὁ
(τέκτων), [in LXX: Isa.3:3 (חָרָשׁ) Sir.38:27. 2Ma.2:29 * ;]
a master-builder, architect: 1Co.3:10 (in π. of building contractors, MM, see word).†
(AS)

G0754.d:
ἀρχι-τελώνης, -ου, ὁ
a chief tax-collector, chief publican: Luk.19:2.†
(AS)

G0755.d:
ἀρχι-τρίκλινος, -ου, ὁ
(τρί-κλινος or -ον, a room with three couches)
the superintendent of a banquet, whose duty it was to arrange the tables and food (DB, ii, 253): Jhn.2:8-9.†
(AS)
G0755.o: from G746 (ἀρχή) and a compound of G5140 (τρεῖς) and G2827 (κλίνω) (a dinner-bed, because composed of three couches);

G0756.d:
ἄρχω
[in LXX for חָלַל, מָשַׁל, etc. ;]
__1. to begin.
__2. to rule (see DCG, ii, 538b.): with genitive, Mrk.10:42, Rom.15:12. Mid., to begin: before ἀπό, Mat.16:21 20:8, Luk.14:18 23:5 24:27, 47, Jhn.8:9, Act.1:22 8:35 10:37, 1Pe.4:17; with inf., an Aramaic pleonasm, Mrk.1:45 2:23 5:17, Luk.3:8, al. (see M, Pro.14:1-35 f.; Dalman, Words, 27; MM, see word)
(AS)
G0756.o: middle voice of G757 (ἄρχω) (through the implication, of precedence);

G0757.d:
ἄρχω
[in LXX for חָלַל, מָשַׁל, etc. ;]
__1. to begin.
__2. to rule (see DCG, ii, 538b.): with genitive, Mrk.10:42, Rom.15:12. Mid., to begin: before ἀπό, Mat.16:21 20:8, Luk.14:18 23:5 24:27, 47, Jhn.8:9, Act.1:22 8:35 10:37, 1Pe.4:17; with inf., an Aramaic pleonasm, Mrk.1:45 2:23 5:17, Luk.3:8, al. (see M, Pro.14:1-35 f.; Dalman, Words, 27; MM, see word)
(AS)
G0757.s: to be first (in political rank or power)

G0758.d:
ἄρχων, -οντος, ὁ
(present ptcp. of ἄρχω), [in LXX for נָשִׂיא., רֹאשׁ, שַׂר, etc. ;]
a ruler, chief: Jesus, Rev.1:5; rulers of nations, Mat.20:25, Act.4:26 7:35; magistrates, Act.23:5, Rom.13:3; judges, Luk.12:58, Act.7:27, 35 16:19; members of the Sanhedrin, Luk.14:1 23:13, 35 24:20, Jhn.3:1 7:26, 48 12:42, Act.3:17 4:5, 8 13:27 14:5; rulers of synagogues, Mat.9:18, 23, Luk.8:41 18:18; οἱ ἄ. τ. αἰῶνος τούτου, 1Co.2:6-8; of the devil: ἄ. τῶν δαιμονίων, Mat.9:34 12:24, Mrk.3:22, Luk.11:15; ὁ ἄ. τοῦ κόσμου, Jhn.12:31 14:30 16:11; ἄ. τ. ἐξουσίας τ. ἀέρος, Eph.2:2 (MM, see word; DB, iii, 838; Ext., 99 f; DCG, ii, 419; DCG, see word Archon).†
(AS)

G0759.d:
ἄρωμα, -τος, τό
[in LXX for בֶּשֶׂם ;]
spice: Mrk.16:1, Luk.23:56 24:1, Jhn.19:40.†
(AS)
G0759.o: from G142 (αἴρω) (in the sense of sending off scent);

G0760.d:
Ἀσάφ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. אָסַף), [H609]
Asaph, an obvious error for Ἀσά, found in the best texts, and adopted by LTTr. and WH, R, mg.: Mat.1:7-8.†
(AS)

G0761.d:
ἀ-σάλευτος, -ον
(σαλεύω), [in LXX: Exo.13:16, Deu.6:8 11:18 (טוֹפָפָה)* ;]
unmoved, immovable: Act.27:41; metaphorically, Heb.12:28.†
(AS)
G0761.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4531 (σαλεύω);

G0762.d:
ἄ-σβεστος, -ον
(σβέννυμι), [in LXX for נָפַח לֹא, Job.20:26 א3 A (ἄκαυστον, א2 B)* ;]
unquenched, unquenchable: πῦρ, Mat.3:12, Mrk.9:43, Luk.3:17.†
(AS)
G0762.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4570 (σβέννυμι);

G0763.d:
ἀσέβεια, -ας, ἡ
(ἀσεβής), [in LXX for פֶּשַׁע, רֶשַׁע, etc. ;]
ungodliness, impiety: Rom.1:18 11:26, 2Ti.2:16, Tit.2:12; ἔργα ἀσεβείας, ungodly deeds, Ju 15; ἐπιθυηίαι τ. ἀσεβειῶν, desires for ungodly things or deeds, Ju 18 (DB, iv, 532; Cremer, 523; MM, see word).†
(AS)

G0764.d:
ἀσεβέω, -ῶ
(ἀσεβής), [in LXX for פָּשַׁע, רָשַׁע ;]
to be ungodly, act profanely: 2Pe.2:6; with cogn. accusative (MM, see word), Ju 15.†
(AS)
G0764.s: to be (by implied act) impious or wicked
G0764.k: commit (live, that after should live) ungodly

G0765.d:
ἀσεβής, -ές
(σέβω, to reverence), [in LXX chiefly for רָשַׁע ;]
un­godly, impious: Rom.4:5 5:6, 1Ti.1:9, 1Pe.4:18, 2Pe.2:5-6 3:7, Ju 4 15.†
(AS)
G0765.s: irreverent, i.e. (by extension) impious or wicked
G0765.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4576 (σέβομαι);

G0766.d:
ἀσέλγεια, -ας, ἡ
(ἀσελγής, licentious; see MM, see word), [in LXX: Wis.14:26, 3Ma.2:26 * ;]
licentiousness, wantonness, excess: Mrk.7:22, Rom.13:13, 2Co.12:21, Gal.5:19 (Lft., in l), Eph.4:19, 1Pe.4:3, 2Pe.2:2 2:7 2:18, Ju 4.†
SYN.: ἀσωτία, profligacy, prodigality (see Tr., Syn., § xvi; DB, iii, 46). (AS)
G0766.o: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed (of uncertain derivation, but apparently meaning continent);

G0767.d:
ἄσημος, -ον
(σῆμα, a mark), [in LXX: Gen.30:42 (עָטַף), Job.42:11, 3Ma.1:3 * ;]
without mark (in π. of an uncircumcised boy: Deiss., BS, 153; MM, see word). Metaphorical (MM, see word), unknown, obscure: litotes, οὐκ ἄ (Eur., al.), πόλις, Act.21:39.†
(AS)
G0767.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G4591 (σημαίνω);

G0769G.d:
ἀσθένεια, -ας, ἡ
(ἀσθενής), [in LXX for כָּשַׁל, etc. ;]
weakness, frailty, sickness: Luk.13:11-12, Jhn.11:4, Act.28:9, Rom.6:19 8:26, 2Co.11:30 13:4, Gal.4:13 (MM, see word), Heb.5:2 7:28 11:34; ἐν ἀ., Jhn.5:5, 1Co.2:3 15:43, 2Co.12:9; pl., Mat.8:17, Luk.5:15 8:2, 2Co.12:5 12:9-10, 1Ti.5:23, Heb.4:15.†
SYN.: μαλακία, νόσος (see DB, iii, 323a) (AS)
G0769G.s: feebleness (of mind or body); by implication, malady; morally, frailty

G0769H.d:
ἀσθένεια, -ας, ἡ
(ἀσθενής), [in LXX for כָּשַׁל, etc. ;]
weakness, frailty, sickness: Luk.13:11-12, Jhn.11:4, Act.28:9, Rom.6:19 8:26, 2Co.11:30 13:4, Gal.4:13 (MM, see word), Heb.5:2 7:28 11:34; ἐν ἀ., Jhn.5:5, 1Co.2:3 15:43, 2Co.12:9; pl., Mat.8:17, Luk.5:15 8:2, 2Co.12:5 12:9-10, 1Ti.5:23, Heb.4:15.†
SYN.: μαλακία, νόσος (see DB, iii, 323a) (AS)
G0769H.s: feebleness (of mind or body); by implication, malady; morally, frailty

G0770G.d:
ἀσθενέω, -ῶ
( ἀσθενής) [in LXX chiefly for כָּשַׁל ;]
to be weak, feeble: Act.20:35, Rom.8:3, 2Co.11:21 12:10 13:4 13:9; with dative, πίστει (Cremer, 527), Rom.4:19 14:1; same implied, Rom.14:2, 21, 1Co.8:11-12, 2Co.11:29; εἰς, 2Co.13:3. Specif., of bodily debility, to be sick: Mat.25:36, 39, Luk.4:40, Jhn.4:46 5:3, 7 5:13 11:1-3, 6 Act.9:37, Php.2:26-27, 2Ti.4:20, Jas.5:14; οἱ ἀσθενοῦντες, the sick: Mat.10:8 (MM, see word), Mrk.6:56, Luk.9:2, Act.19:12.†
(AS)
G0770G.k: be diseased, impotent folk (man), (be) sick, (be, be made) weak

G0770H.d:
ἀσθενέω, -ῶ
( ἀσθενής) [in LXX chiefly for כָּשַׁל ;]
to be weak, feeble: Act.20:35, Rom.8:3, 2Co.11:21 12:10 13:4 13:9; with dative, πίστει (Cremer, 527), Rom.4:19 14:1; same implied, Rom.14:2, 21, 1Co.8:11-12, 2Co.11:29; εἰς, 2Co.13:3. Specif., of bodily debility, to be sick: Mat.25:36, 39, Luk.4:40, Jhn.4:46 5:3, 7 5:13 11:1-3, 6 Act.9:37, Php.2:26-27, 2Ti.4:20, Jas.5:14; οἱ ἀσθενοῦντες, the sick: Mat.10:8 (MM, see word), Mrk.6:56, Luk.9:2, Act.19:12.†
(AS)
G0770H.k: be diseased, impotent folk (man), (be) sick, (be, be made) weak

G0772G.d:
ἀσθενής -ές
(ἀ- neg., σθένος, strength), [in LXX for עָנִי, etc. ;]
without strength, weak, feeble: 1Co.1:27 4:10 12:22, 2Co.10:10, Gal.4:9, 1Th.5:14, Heb.7:18, 1Pe.3:7. Rhetorically, τό ἀ. τ. θεοῦ, God's action of apparent weakness: 1Co.1:25; of bodily debility, sick, sickly: Mat.25:39 (Rec.) Mat.25:43-44, Luk.9:2 (Rec.) Luk.10:9, Act.4:9 5:15-16 In moral and spiritual sense (MM, see word; Cremer, 526), Mat.26:41, Mrk.14:38, Rom.5:6, 1Co.8:7 8:9-10 9:22 11:30.†
(AS)
G0772G.s: strengthless (in various applications, literal, figurative and moral)
G0772G.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G4599 (σθενόω);
G0772G.k: more feeble, impotent, sick, without strength, weak(-er, -ness, thing)

G0772H.d:
ἀσθενής -ές
(ἀ- neg., σθένος, strength), [in LXX for עָנִי, etc. ;]
without strength, weak, feeble: 1Co.1:27 4:10 12:22, 2Co.10:10, Gal.4:9, 1Th.5:14, Heb.7:18, 1Pe.3:7. Rhetorically, τό ἀ. τ. θεοῦ, God's action of apparent weakness: 1Co.1:25; of bodily debility, sick, sickly: Mat.25:39 (Rec.) Mat.25:43-44, Luk.9:2 (Rec.) Luk.10:9, Act.4:9 5:15-16 In moral and spiritual sense (MM, see word; Cremer, 526), Mat.26:41, Mrk.14:38, Rom.5:6, 1Co.8:7 8:9-10 9:22 11:30.†
(AS)
G0772H.s: strengthless (in various applications, literal, figurative and moral)
G0772H.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G4599 (σθενόω);
G0772H.k: more feeble, impotent, sick, without strength, weak(-er, -ness, thing)

G0773.s: Asia, i.e. Asia Minor, or (usually) only its western shore

G0774.d:
Ἀσιαός, -ή, -όν
Asian, of Asia, Asiatic; as subst., ὁ (οἱ) Ἀ.: Act.20:4.†
(AS)
G0774.s: an Asian (i.e. Asiatic) or an inhabitant of Asia

G0775.d:
Ἀσιάρχης, -ου, ὁ
an Asiarch, one of ten officers elected by the various cities in the province of Asia whose duty it was to celebrate at their own charges the public games and festivals: Act.19:31 (Strab., Inscr.; DB, see word).†
(AS)
G0775.s: an Asiarch or president of the public festivities in a city of Asia Minor

G0776.d:
ἀσιτία, -ας, ἡ
(ἄσιτος),
fasting, abstinence from food: Act.27:21.†
SYN.: νηστεία (MM, ut infr.) (AS)

G0777.d:
ἄσιτος, -ον
(ἀ- neg., σῖτος)
fasting, without eating (cf. MM, see word): Act.27:33.†
(AS)
G0777.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4621 (σῖτος);

G0778.d:
ἀσκέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: 2Ma.15:4 * ;]
__1. to adorn (poët.).
__2. to practise, exercise (Hdt., Xen.).
__3. to endeavour (Xen., al.): with inf., Act.24:16.†
(AS)
G0778.s: to elaborate, i.e. (figuratively) train (by implication, strive)
G0778.o: probably from the same as G4632 (σκεῦος);

G0779.d:
ἀσκός, -οῦ, ὁ
[in LXX for חֵמֶת, נֹאד, נֶבֶל ;]
a leather bottle, wine-skin: Mat.9:17, Mrk.2:22, Luk.5:37-38.†
(AS)
G0779.s: a leathern (or skin) bag used as a bottle

G0780.o: adverb from a derivative of the base of G2237 (ἡδονή);

G0781.d:
ἄ-σοθος, -ον
[in LXX: Pro.9:8 א2 Α * ;]
unwise, foolish: Eph.5:15.†
(AS)
G0781.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4680 (σοφός);

G0782.d:
ἀσπάζομαι depon.,
[in LXX: Eze.18:7, Jdg.18:15 (שָׁלוֹם שָׁאַל), Est.5:2, 1Ma.7:29, al. ;]
to welcome, greet, salute: with accusative of person(s), Mat.5:47, Mrk.9:15, Act.21:7, al.; id. before ἐν φιλήματι, Rom.16:16, 1Co.16:20, 2Co.13:12, 1Th.5:26, 1Pe.5:14; τ. ἐκκλησίαν (Deiss., BS, 257), Act.18:22; as term. tech. for conveying greetings at the end of a letter (MM, see word), used by an amanuensis (Milligan, NTD, 23), Rom.16:22 (on the aoristic Pres., here and elsewhere, see M, Pr., 119; Bl., § 56, 4); κατήντησαν . . . ἀσπασάμενοι (on this constr., see El., § 58, 4; M, Pr., 132, 238), Act.25:13 (cf. ἀπ-ἀπ-ασπάζομαι).†
(AS)
G0782.s: to enfold in the arms, i.e. (by implication) to salute, (figuratively) to welcome
G0782.o: from G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) and a presumed form of G4685 (σπάω);

G0783.d:
ἀσπασμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(ἀσπάζομαι),
a salutation (so always in RV), greeting: oral, Mat.23:7, Mrk.12:38, Luk.1:29, 41 1:44 11:43 20:46; written, 1Co.16:21, Col.4:18, 2Th.3:17.†
(AS)
G0783.s: a greeting (in person or by letter)

G0784.d:
ἄ-σπιλος, -ον
(ἀ- neg., σπῖλος) [in Sm.: Job.15:15 (LXX, καθαρός)* ;]
spotless, unstained: 1Pe.1:19; metaphorically, 1Ti.6:14, Jas.1:27, 2Pe.3:14 (for exx., see MM, see word).†
SYN.: ἀμίαντος, ἄμωμος (AS)
G0784.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4695 (σπιλόω);

G0785.d:
ἀσπίς, -ίδος, ἡ
[in LXX for פֶּתֶן, etc. ;]
an asp: Rom.3:13.†
(AS)
G0785.s: a buckler (or round shield); used of a serpent (as coiling itself), probably the "asp"

G0786.d:
ἄσπονδος, -ον
(σπονδή, a libation);
__1. without truce (Thuc.).
__2. admitting of no truce, implacable (Dem., al.): 2Ti.3:3.†
(AS)
G0786.s: literally, without libation (which usually accompanied a treaty), i.e. (by implication) truceless
G0786.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4689 (σπένδω);

G0787.d:
ἀσσάριον, -ον, τό
(diminutive of Lat. as),
an assarion, a farthing, one-tenth of a drachma: Mat.10:29, Luk.12:6 (MM, see word; DB, iii, 428; DCG, ii, 200).†
(AS)
G0787.s: an assarius or as, a Roman coin

G0788.d:
ἆσσον (Rec., after Vg., Ἄσσον),
adv. (compar. of ἄγχι, near),
nearer: Act.27:13 (RV, close in shore; see B1., § 11, 3; 44, 3; poets, Ion, and late prose).†
(AS)
G0788.o: neuter comparative of the base of G1451 (ἐγγύς);

G0789.d:
Ἄσσος, -ου
(also Ἀσσός, -οῦ), ή
Assos, a city on the E. coast of Asia Minor: Act.20:13-14 (see: ἆσσον).†
(AS)
G0789.s: Assus, a city of Asia MInor

G0790.d:
ἀστατέω, -ῶ
(ἄστατος, unstable), [in Aq.: Isa.58:7 (LXX, ἄστεγος)* ;]
to be unsettled, be homeless, lead a vagabond life (Cremer, 738 MM, see word): 1Co.4:11 †
(AS)
G0790.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2476 (ἵστημι);

G0791.d:
ἀστεῖος, -ον
(ἄστυ, a city), [in LXX: Exo.2:2 (טוֹב), Num.22:32 (οὐκ ἀ. יָרַט), Jdg.3:17 (בָּרִיא), Jdth.11:23, Dan LXX, Sus 1:7, 2Ma.6:23 * ;]
__1. of the town.
__2. (Like Lat. urbanus),
__(a) courteous,
__(b) elegant (in π., of clothing, MM, see word), comely, fair (as in Ex, l.with), Heb.11:23, Act.7:20.†
(AS)

G0792.d:
ἀστήρ, -έρος, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for כּוֹכָב ;]
a star: Mat.2:2, 7-10 :, Mrk.13:25, 1Co.15:41, Rev.6:13 8:10-12 9:1 12:1, 4; metaphorically, ὁ ἀ. ὁ πρωϊνός Rev.2:28 22:16; ἀ. πλαῆται, Ju 13; ἀ. ἑπτά, symbolizing the angels of the seven churches, Rev.1:16, 20 2:1 3:1 (cf. ἄστρον, and see DCG, ii, 674 f.; MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0792.s: a star (as strown over the sky), literally or figuratively
G0792.o: probably from the base of G4766 (στρώννυμι);

G0793.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4741 (στηρίζω);

G0794.d:
ἄστοργος, -ον
(στοργή, family affection, love of kindred, see: ἀγάπη)
without natural affection: Rom.1:31, 2Ti.3:3 (MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0794.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of (to cherish affectionately);

G0795.d:
ἀστοχέω, -ῶ
(στόχος, a mark), [in LXX: Sir.7:19 8:9 * ;]
to miss the mark, fail: with genitive, 1Ti.1:6 (so in π., MM, see word); before περί, 1Ti.6:21, 2Ti.2:18.†
(AS)
G0795.s: to miss the mark, i.e. (figuratively) deviate from truth
G0795.o: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and (an aim);

G0796.d:
ἀστραπή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX for בָּרָק ;]
lightning: Mat.24:27 28:3, Luk.10:18 17:24; pl., Rev.4:5 8:5 11:19 16:18; of a lamp, shining brightness, Luk.11:36.†
(AS)

G0797.d:
ἀστράπτω
[in LXX for בָּרָק ;]
to lighten, flash forth: Luk.17:24 24:4 (MM, see word).†
(AS)

G0798.d:
ἄστρον, -ου, τό
[in LXX chiefly for כּוֹכָב ;]
__(a) mostly in pl. (as in cl.), the stars: Luk.21:25, Act.27:20, Heb.11:12;
__(b) in sing. (Xen., al.), only of some noted star; the symbol or image of a star, Act.7:43 (cf. ἀστήρ, and see MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0798.s: properly, a constellation; put for a single star (natural or artificial)

G0799.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4793 (συγκρίνω);

G0800.d:
ἀ-σύμφωνος, -ον
[in LXX: Wis.18:10, Da, LXX, Bel 1:15 * ;]
dissonant, discordant; metaphorically, at variance: πρὸς ἀλλήλους, Act.28:25.†
(AS)
G0800.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4859 (σύμφωνος);

G0801.d:
ἀ-σύνετος, -ον
[in LXX: Deu.32:21 (נָבָל). Job.13:2 (נָפַל), Psa.92:6 (כְּסִיל), Psa.76:5, Wis.2:1-24, Sir.6:1-37 * ;]
without understanding or discernment: Mat.15:16, Mrk.7:18 (Swete, in l), Rom.1:21, 31 10:19 (for an ex. of its use in the moral sense, see MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0801.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4908 (συνετός);

G0802.d:
ἀ-σύν-θετος, -ον
(συντίθεμαι ν. M, Pr., 222; MM, see word), [in LXX: Jer.3:7-11 (בָּגַד)* ;]
false to engagements, not keeping covenant, faithless (MM, see word): Rom.1:31.†
(AS)
G0802.s: properly, not agreed, i.e. treacherous to compacts
G0802.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4934 (συντίθεμαι);

G0803.d:
ἀσφάλεια, -ας, ἡ
(ἀσφαλής), [in LXX for בָּטַח, etc. ;]
__1. firmness.
__2. certainty: Luk.1:4.
__3. security: Act.5:23, 1Th.5:3.
(In π. it is used as a law-term, proof, security; see MM, see word; M, Th., l.with)†
(AS)

G0804.d:
ἀσφαλής, -ές
(ἀ- neg., σφάλλω, to trip up), [in LXX for אָשַׁר pu., etc. ;]
certain, secure, safe: Act.21:34 22:30 25:26, Php.3:1, Heb.6:19 (MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0804.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and sphallo (to "fail");

G0805.d:
ἀσφαλίζω
(ἀσφαλής), [in LXX: Neh.3:15 (חָזַק hi.), Isa.41:10 (תָּמַךְ), Wis.4:17 10:12 13:15 * ;]
to make firm, secure: mid., Mat.27:65-66, Act.16:24; pass., Mat.27:64 (MM, see word).†
(AS)

G0806.d:
ἀσφαλῶς
adv., [in LXX: Gen.34:25 (בֶּטַח), Tob.6:4, Wis.18:6, Bar.5:7, 1Ma.6:40, 3Ma.7:6 * ;]
__(a) safely: Mrk.14:44, Act.16:23;
__(b) assuredly: Act.2:36.†
(AS)

G0807.d:
ἀσχημονέω, -ῶ
(ἀσχήμαων), [in LXX: Eze.16:7, 22 16:39 23:29 (עֶרְיָה); Deu.25:3 (קָלָה ni.)* ;]
to act unbecomingly, behave dishonourably: 1Co.13:5; before ἐπί, ib. 1Co.7:36 (MM, see word).†
(AS)

G0808.d:
ἀσχημοσύνη, -ης, ή
(ἀσχήμων), [in LXX chiefly for עֶרְוָה ;]
unseemliness: Rom.1:27 (MM, see word); euphemism for ἡ αἰσχύνη, as frequently in LXX, shame, nakedness: Rev.16:15.†
(AS)
G0808.s: an indecency; by implication, the pudenda

G0809.d:
ἀσχήμων, -ον
(ἀ- neg., σχῆμα) [in LXX: Gen.34:7 (נְבָלָה), Deu.24:1 (עֶרְוָה), Wis.2:20, Da TH Sus 1:63, 2Ma.9:2 * ;]
__1. shapeless.
__2. uncomely, unseemly: 1Co.12:23.†
(AS)
G0809.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G2192 (ἔχω) (in the sense of its congener G4976 (σχῆμα));

G0810.d:
ἀσωτία, -ας, ή
(ἀ- neg., σώζω), [in LXX: Pro.28:7 (זָלַל), 2Ma.6:4 * ;]
prodigality, wastefulness, profligacy: Eph.5:18, Tit.1:6, 1Pe.4:4 (MM, see word).†
SYN.: ἀσέλγεια, q.v (AS)
G0810.o: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4982 (σώζω);

G0811.d:
ἀσώτως
adv. (ἄσωτος, prodigal, wasteful), [in LXX for סָרַר, Pro.7:11 * ;]
wastefully: Luk.15:13
(EV, in riotous living; but not necessarily dissolute; cf. MM, ut supr.; Milligan, NTD, 79).† (AS)
G0811.o: adverb from the same as G810 (ἀσωτία);

G0812.d:
ἀτακτέω -ῶ
(ἄτακτος),
primarily, of soldiers marching, to be out of order, to quit the ranks; hence, metaphorically, to be remiss, fail in the performance of duty (in π., of truancy on the part of an apprentice): 2Th.3:7 (on ἀ. and its cognates, see M, Th., 152 ff.; MM, s.vv.).†
(AS)

G0813.d:
ἀ-τακτος, -ον
(τάσσω), [in LXX: 3Ma.1:19 * ;]
out of order, out of place (Lat. inordinatus), frequently of soldiers not keeping the ranks, or an army in disarray (cf. 3Ma.1:19); hence, metaphorically, irregular, disorderly (see previous word): 1Th.5:14.†
(AS)
G0813.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5021 (τάσσω);

G0815.d:
ἄτεκνος, -ον
(τέκνον), [in LXX: Gen.15:2, Lev.20:20-21 (עֲרִירִי), Isa.49:21, Jer.18:21 (שָׁכֹל), Sir.16:3 * ;]
childless: Luk.20:28-29.†
(AS)
G0815.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5043 (τέκνον);

G0816.d:
ἀτενίζω
(ἀτενής, strained, intent; τείνω), [in LXX: I Est.6:28, 3Ma.2:26 * ;]
to look fixedly, gaze (MM, see word): with dative of person(s), gaze upon: Luk.4:20 22:56, Act.3:12 10:4 14:9 23:1; before εἰς, with accusative of person(s), Act.3:4 6:15 13:9; metaphorically, Act.1:10 7:55 11:6, 2Co.3:7 3:13.†
(AS)
G0816.o: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) and (to stretch);
G0816.k: behold earnestly (stedfastly), fasten (eyes), look (earnestly, stedfastly, up stedfastly), set eyes

G0817.d:
ἄτερ
prep., [in LXX: 2Ma.12:15 * ;]
in cl. most frequently in poets; without, apart from: with genitive, Luk.22:6, 35 (for exx. from π., see MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0817.s: aloof, i.e. apart from (literally or figuratively)
G0817.o: a particle probably akin to G427 (ἄνευ);

G0818.d:
ἀτιμάζω
(ἄτιμος), [in LXX for בּוּז, קָלָה, etc. ;]
to dishonour, insult: Mrk.12:4, TTr., mg., WH, Luk.20:11, Jhn.8:49, Rom.2:23, Jas.2:6; pass.: Act.5:41, Rom.1:24 (cf ἀτιμάω).†
(AS)
G0818.s: to render infamous, i.e. (by implication) contemn or maltreat
G0818.k: despise, dishonour, suffer shame, entreat shamefully

G0819.d:
ἀτιμία, -ας, ἡ
(ἄτιμος) [in LXX for כְּלִמָּה, קָלוֹן, etc. ;]
dishonour, disgrace: 1Co.11:14, 2Co.6:8; εἰς ἀ., Rom.9:21, 2Ti.2:20; ἐν ἀ., 1Co.15:43; κατ᾽ ἀ., 2Co.11:21; πάθη ἀτιμίας, base passions, Rom.1:26.†
(AS)

G0820.d:
ἄτιμος, -ον
(τιμή), [in LXX: Isa.3:5 (קָלָה ni.), Isa.53:3 (בָּזָה), Job.30:4, 8 (שֵׁם בְּלִי), שֵׁם בְּלִי), Wis.5:1-23, Sir.1:1-30 * ;]
without honour, dishonoured, despised: Mat.13:57, Mrk.6:4, 1Co.4:10; comp., 1Co.12:23.†
(AS)
G0820.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5092 (τιμή);
G0820.k: despised, without honour, less honourable (comparative degree)

G0821.d:
ἀτιμόω, -ῶ
(ἄτιμος), [in LXX chiefly for בָּזָה ;]
= ἀτιμάζω, to dishonour, treat with indignity: Mrk.12:4, Rec.†
(AS)

G0822.d:
ἀτμίς, -ίδος, ἡ
[in LXX for עָנַן, תִּמֹּר, etc. ;]
vapour: Jas.4:14; ἀ. καπνοῦ, Act.2:19 (LXX).†
(AS)

G0823.d:
ἄ-τομος, -ον
(τέμνω), [in Sm.: Isa.54:8 (MM, see word) * ;]
indivisible; of time, ἄτομον, a moment: ἐν ἄ., 1Co.15:52.†
(AS)
G0823.s: uncut, i.e. (by implication) indivisible (an "atom" of time)
G0823.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G5114 (τομώτερος);

G0824.d:
ἄ-τοπος, -ον
(τόπος), [in LXX: Job.4:8 11:11, Pro.30:20, al., for אָוֶן, etc. ;]
__1. out of place, not befitting.
__2. marvellous, strange (of symptoms, Hipp.): Act.28:6; hence, in late Greek, with ethical sense,
__3. improper, unrighteous (so in LXX, and for exx. from π., see M, Th., l.with; MM, see word): Luk.23:41, Act.25:5, 2Th.3:2.†
(AS)
G0824.s: out of place, i.e. (figuratively) improper, injurious, wicked
G0824.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5117 (τόπος);

G0825.d:
Ἀτταλία (Rec. -άλεια), -υς, ἡ
Attalia, a city of Pamphylia: Act.14:25.†
(AS)

G0826.d:
αὐγάζω
(αὐγή), [in LXX: Lev.13:24-28, 38 14:56 (בֹּהֶרֶת) Lev.13:39 (כֵּהֶה)* ;]
__1. Trans. (cl.), to irradiate.
__2. Intrans.
__(a) (poët.), to see clearly (so perh. 2 Co, l.with; MM, see word)
__(b) as in LXX, to shine forth: 2Co.4:4 (cf. δι-, κατ-αυγάζω).†
(AS)

G0827.d:
αὐγή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX: Isa.59:9 (נְגֹהָה), 2Ma.12:9 * ;]
__1. brightness
__2. Later (as in MGr.; MM, see word), daylight, dawn: Act.20:11 (Cremer, 118).†
SYN.: φέγγος (see Thayer, s. φ.; DB, iii, 44a; Tr., Syn., § xlvi). (AS)
G0827.s: a ray of light, i.e. (by implication) radiance, dawn

G0828.d:
Αὔγουστος, -ου, ὁ
(Lat.), Augustus, the Roman Emperor: Luk.2:1 (cf. Σεβαστός; and see MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0828.s: Augustus, a title of the Roman emperor

G0829.d:
αὐθάδης, -ες
(αὐτος, ἥδομαι), [in LXX: Gen.49:3, 7 (עַז), Pro.21:24 (יָהִיר)* ;]
self-pleasing, arrogant: Tit.1:7, 2Pe.2:10 (Cremer, 654).†
SYN.: φίλαυτος (see Tr., Syn., § xciii) (AS)
G0829.o: from G846 (αὐτός) and the base of G2237 (ἡδονή);

G0830.d:
αὐθαίρετος, -ον
(αὐτός, αἱρέομαι), [in Sm.: Exo.35:5, 22 * ;]
__1. self-chosen.
__2. of one's own accord: 2Co.8:3 8:17.†
(AS)
G0830.o: from G846 (αὐτός) and the same as G140 (αἱρετίζω);
G0830.k: of own accord, willing of self

G0831.d:
αὐθεντέω, -ῶ
(αὐθέντης, i.e. αὐτο- ἕντης, one who acts on his own authority, in π., an autocrat; cf. Wis.12:6; cf. -ία, 3Ma.2:29; -ικος is frequently in vernacular, MM, see word)
to govern, exercise authority over: 1Ti.2:12.†
(AS)
G0831.s: to act of oneself, i.e. (figuratively) dominate
G0831.o: from a compound of G846 (αὐτός) and an obsolete (a worker);

G0832.d:
αὐλέω, -ῶ
(αὐλός), [in Al.: 3Ki.1:40 * ;]
to play on a flute, to pipe: mid., Mat.11:17, Luk.7:32, 1Co.14:7.†
(AS)

G0833.d:
αὐλή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for חָצֵר ;]
__1. in Hom., an open courtyard before a house, hence, an enclosure in the open, a sheepfold: Jhn.10:1, 16
__2. the court, courtyard, round which a house is built: Mat.26:3, 58 26:69, Mrk.14:54, 66 15:16 Luk.11:21 22:55, Jhn.18:15; τ. ναοῦ, Rev.11:2. a dwelling, a palace (so, accusative to Grimm-Th., see word): Mat.26:3, 58, Mrk.14:54 15:16, Luk.11:21, Jhn.18:15 (but see MM, see word; cf. also DB, ii, 25, 287).†
(AS)
G0833.s: a yard (as open to the wind); by implication, a mansion

G0834.d:
αὐλητής, -οῦ, ὁ
(αὐλέω),
a flute-player: Mat.9:23, Rev.18:22 (MM, see word).†
(AS)

G0835.d:
αὐλίζομαι
(αὐλή), [in LXX chiefly for לוּן ;]
__1. prop., to lodge in a courtyard.
__2. to lodge in the open.
__3. to pass the night, lodge (LXX; MM, see word): Mat.21:17, Luk.21:37.†
(AS)
G0835.s: to pass the night (properly, in the open air)

G0836.d:
αὐλός, -οῦ, ὁ
(ἄω, to blow), [in LXX chiefly for חָלִיל ;]
a pipe: 1Co.14:7.†
(AS)

G0837.d:
αὐξάνω
(and the earlier form αὔξω, Eph.2:21, Col.2:19; MM, see word), [in LXX chiefly for פָּרָה ;]
__1. trans., to make to grow: 1Co.3:6-7, 2Co.9:10. Pass., to grow, increase, become greater: Mat.13:32, Mrk.4:8, 2Co.10:15, Col.1:6; τῇ ἐπιγνώσει τ. θεοῦ, Col.1:10; εἰς σωτηρίαν, 1Pe.2:2.
__2. In later Gk. (but nowhere in LXX), intrans., to grow, increase: of plants, Mat.6:28, Luk.12:27 13:19; of infants, Luk.1:80 2:40; of a multitude, Act.7:17; of the increase of the Gospel: ὁ λόγος ηὔξανε, Act.6:7 12:24 19:20; of Christ as a leader, Jhn.3:30; of Christian character: εἰς Χριοτόν, Eph.4:15; εἰς ναόν, Eph.2:21; ἐν χάριτι, 2Pe.3:18; τὴν αὔξησιν τ. θεσῦ,…
G0837.s: to grow ("wax"), i.e. enlarge (literal or figurative, active or passive)
G0837.o: a prolonged form of a primary verb;

G0839.d:
αὔριον
adv., [in LXX for מָחָר ;]
to-morrow: Mat.6:30, Luk.12:28, Act.23:20 25:22, 1Co.15:32, Luk.13:32-33, Jas.4:13; ἡ αὔ. (sc. ἡμέρα, MM, see word), Mat.6:34, Act.4:3; ἐπὶ τὴν αὔ., Luk.10:35, Act.4:5; τὸ (WH om.) τῆς Jas.4:14.†
(AS)
G0839.s: properly, fresh, i.e. (adverb with ellipsis of G2250 (ἡμέρα)) to-morrow
G0839.o: from a derivative of the same as G109 (ἀήρ) (meaning a breeze, i.e. the morning air);

G0840.d:
αὐστηρός, -ά, -όν
(αἄω, to dry up) [in LXX: 2Ma.14:30 * ;]
prop., stringent, harsh to the taste. Metaphorical, in Inscr., of a rough country; of disposition and manners, strict, severe (as in π., of an inspector; MM, s v): Luk.19:21-22.†
