SYN.: σκληρός (Tr., § xiv) (AS)
G0840.s: rough (properly as a gale), i.e. (figuratively) severe
G0840.o: from a (presumed) derivative of the same as G109 (ἀήρ) (meaning blown);

G0841.d:
αὐτάρκεια, -ας, ἡ
(αὐτάρκης, which see),
__(a) sufficiency (MM, see word): in subjective sense (see Milligan, NTD, 57), 2Co.9:8;
__(b) contentment: 1Ti.6:6.†
(AS)
G0841.s: self-satisfaction, i.e. (abstractly) contentedness, or (concretely) a competence

G0842.d:
αὐτάρκης, -ες
(αὐτός, ἀρκέω), [in LXX: Pro.30:8 (חֹק), Sir.5:1 11:24 31:28 40:18, 4Ma.9:9 * ;]
as in cl., in philosophical sense, self-­sufficient, independent; subjectively, contented: Php.4:11 (in non-lit. π., the word means simply enough, sufficient; MM, see word).†
(AS)

G0843.d:
αὐτο-κατά-κριτος, -ον
(αὐτός, κατακρίνω),
self-condemned: Tit.3:11 (Eccl., Cremer, 377; MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0843.o: from G846 (αὐτός) and a derivative or G2632 (κατακρίνω);

G0844.d:
αὐτόματος -ον, and -η, -ον
(etym. doubtful; see Boisacq, Prellwitz, see word), [in LXX, Lev.25:5, 11, 4Ki.19:29 (סָפִיחַ), Jos.6:5, Job.24:24, Wis.17:6 * ;]
__1. of persons, acting of one's own will.
__2. Of inanimate things and natural agencies, of itself, of its own accord: γῆ Mrk.4:28 (MM, see word); πύλη, Act.12:10.†
(AS)
G0844.o: from G846 (αὐτός) and the same as G3155 (μάτην);

G0846.d:
αὐτός, -ή, -ό,
determinative pron., in late Gk. much more frequently than in cl. (WM, 178f.; Jannaris, HGG, §1399).
__1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., see infr., iii);
__(1) self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, Luk.5:37; αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, Jhn.2:25; αὐ.ὑμεῖς, Jhn.3:28; καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, Rom.15:14; αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, Jhn.2:24; αὐ. καὶ οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ, Mrk.2:25; ὑμεῖς αὐ., Mrk.6:31; esp. (as freq in cl.) αὐ. ὁ, Mat.3:4, Mrk.6:17, Jhn.16:27, 1Th.3:11, al.; in late Gk., sometimes weakened, ἐν αὐτῇ τ. ὥρᾳ, in that hour, Luk.10:21 (M, Pr., 91; MM, see word);
__(2) emphatic,…
G0846.s: the reflexive pronoun self, used (alone or in the comparative G1438 (ἑαυτοῦ)) of the third person , and (with the proper personal pronoun) of the other persons
G0846.o: from the particle (perhaps akin to the base of G109 (ἀήρ) through the idea of a baffling wind) (backward);
G0846.k: her, it(-self), one, the other, (mine) own, said, (self-), the) same, ((him-, my-, thy- )self, (your-)selves, she, that, their(-s), them(-selves), there(-at, - by, -in, -into, -of, -on, -with), they, (these) things, this (man), those, together, very, which

G0847.d:
αὐτοῦ
adv., prop. neut. genitive of αὐτός, [in LXX for פֹּה, בָּזֶה ;]
there: Mat.26:36, Mrk.6:33, WH, mg., Luk.9:27, Act.15:34, WH, mg., R, mg., Act.18:19 21:4 .†
(AS)
G0847.s: properly, belonging to the same spot, i.e. in this (or that) place
G0847.o: genitive (i.e. possessive) of G846 (αὐτός), used as an adverb of location;

G0848.d:
αὑτοῦ, -ῆς, -οῦ
= ἑαυτοῦ (which see), Mat.6:34, Luk.12:17, al. (MM, see word)
(AS)
G0848.s: self (in some oblique case or reflexively, relation)
G0848.k: her (own), (of) him(-self), his (own), of it, thee, their (own), them(-selves), they

G0849.d:
αὐτό-χειρ, -ρος, ὁ, ἡ
(αὐτός, χείρ),
with one's own hand: Act.27:19.†
(AS)

G0850.o: from (probably from a base akin to that of G109 (ἀήρ)) (dust, as dried by wind);

G0851.d:
ἀφ-αιρέω, -ῶ
[in LXX (Cremer, 615 f.) for סוּר, עָבַר, H7311 כָּרַת, etc. (35 words in all) ;]
to take from, take away, take off: with accusative, τὸ ὠτίον, Mat.26:51, Mrk.14:47 (ὠτάριον, WH), Luk.22:50 (οὖς); ὄνειδος, Luk.1:25; before ἀπό, Rev.22:19, Luk.16:3 (mid.); pass., C. genitive, Luk.10:42; ἀ. ἁμαρτίος, Heb.10:4, Rom.11:27 (mid.) (MM, see word).†
(AS)

G0852.d:
ἀφανής, -ές
(φαίνω), [in LXX: Neh.4:8(2), Job.24:20, Sir.20:30 41:14, 2Ma.3:34 * ;]
unseen, hidden: Heb.4:13.†
(AS)
G0852.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5316 (φαίνω);

G0853.d:
ἀφανίζω
(ἀφανής), [in LXX for שָׁמֵם ni., שָׁמַד hi., etc. ;]
__1. to make unseen, hide from sight (Xen., a1.).
__2. Later (MM, see word)
__(a) to destroy: Mat.6:19-20;
__(b) to disfigure: Mat.6:16. Pass., to vanish: Jas.4:14; to perish: Act.13:41(LXX).†
(AS)
G0853.s: to render unapparent, i.e. (actively) consume (becloud), or (passively) disappear (be destroyed)

G0854.d:
ἀφανισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(ἀφανίζω), [in LXX chiefly for שַׁמָּה, שְׁמָמָה ;]
vanishing: Heb.8:13.†
(AS)

G0855.d:
ἄφαντος, -ον
(φαίνομαι), poët. and late prose (MM, see word)
invisible, hidden: Luk.24:31.†
(AS)
G0855.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5316 (φαίνω);

G0856.d:
ἀφεδρών, -ῶνος, ὁ
(cf. ἄφεδρος, Lev.12:5) = cl. ἄφοδος (MM, see word),
a privy, drain: Mat.15:17, Mrk.7:19 (ὀχετόν, WH, mg.).†
**ὀχετός, -οῦ, ὁ
(ὀχέω, to carry) [in Sm.: Job.22:24, Psa.65:10 al. ;]
__1. a water-pipe, channel.
__2. the intestinal canal: Mrk.7:19, WH, mg. (for ἀφεδρών).†
(AS)
G0856.s: a place of sitting apart, i.e. a privy
G0856.o: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G1476 (ἑδραῖος);

G0857.d:
ἀφειδία (L, -εία), -ας, ἡ
(ἀφειδής, unsparing);
__1. extravagance.
__2. unsparing treatment, severity: Col.2:23.†
(AS)
G0857.o: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5339 (φείδομαι);

G0858.d:
ἀφελότης, -ητος, ἡ
= cl. ἀφέλεια (see MM, see word),
simplicity: Act.2:46†
(AS)
G0858.o: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and (in the sense of a stone as stubbing the foot);

G0859.d:
ἄφεσις, -εως, ἡ
(ἀφίημι), [in LXX for יוֹבֵל, דְּרוֹר, etc. (see Deiss., BS, 98 ff.; MM, see word) ;]
__1. dismissal, release: Luk.4:18.
__2. Metaphorical, of sins (never in LXX), pardon, remission of penalty: ἁμαρτιῶν, Mat.26:28, Mrk.1:4, Luk.1:77 3:3 24:47, Act.2:38 5:31 10:43 13:38 26:18, Col.1:14; παραπτωμάτων, Eph.1:7; absol., Mrk.3:29, Heb.9:22 10:18 (cf. DB, ii, 56; DCG, i, 437, ii, 605; Cremer, 297 f.).†
SYN.: πάρεσις, which see (and cf. Tr., § xxxiii) (AS)

G0860.d:
ἁφή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ἅπτω, to fasten, fit), [in LXX for נֶגַע, frequently in Le ;]
a joint (MM, see word): Eph.4:16, Col.2:19 (Lft., in l).†
(AS)

G0861.d:
ἀφθαρσία, -ας, ἡ
(ἄφθαρτος), [in LXX: Wis.2:23 6:19, 4Ma.9:22 4Mac 17:12 * ;]
incorruptibility, immortality: Rom.2:7, 1Co.15:42 15:50 15:53-54, 2Ti.1:10; ἀγαπώντων . . . ἐν ἀ., Eph.6:24 (see AR, in l).†
ἀ-φθορία, -ας, ἡ
(φθείρω), [in LXX: Hag.2:17 (שְׁדֵפָה)* ;]
uncorruptness: Tit.2:7 (Rec. ἀφθορία).†
(AS)

G0862.d:
ἄ-φθαρτος, -ον
(φθείρω), [in LXX: Wis.12:1 18:4 * ;]
imperishable, immortal;
__(a) of things: 1Co.9:25, 1Pe.1:4 1:23 3:4;
__(b) of persons: of men, 1Co.15:52; of God, Rom.1:23, 1Ti.1:17 (MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0862.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5351 (φθείρω);

G0863G.d:
ἀφ-ίημι,
[in LXX for נשׂא, נוח hi., נתן, סלח ni., עזב, etc. ;]
__1. to send forth, send away, let go: of divorce (DB, iii, 274a), τ. γυναῖκα (Hdt.), 1Co.7:11-13; of death, τ. πνεῦμα (Gen.35:18, Hdt., al.), Mat.27:50; (φωνήν, to utter a cry, Mrk.15:37; of debts, to remit, forgive (cl.), τ. δανεῖον, Mat.18:27; τ. ὀφειλήν, Mat.18:32; esp. of sins (Cremer 296f.), τ. ἁμαρτίας, ἁμαρτήματα, ἀνομίας, Mat.9:2, Rom.4:7" (LXX), 1Jn.1:9, al.; punctiliar and iterative present (M, Pr., 119), Mrk.2:5, Luk.11:4; Ion. pf., ἀφέωνται (M, Pr., 38), Luk.5:23.
__2. to leave alone, leave, neglect: Mat.4:11 5:24 15:14, Mrk.1:20, 31 Jhn.4:3, 28…
G0863G.s: an intensive form of , to go); to send forth, in various applications (as follow)

ἀφ-ίημι,

G0864.d:
ἀφ-ικνέομαι, -οῦμαι
[in LXX for בּוֹא, etc. ;]
perfective of ἱκνέομαι, to come (M, Pr., 247), to arrive at, come to, reach: metaphorically (MM, see word), Rom.16:19.†
(AS)
G0864.o: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G2425 (ἱκανός);

G0865.d:
ἀ-φιλ-άγαθος, -ον
without love of good: 2Ti.3:3 (not elsewhere in Gk. lit., but see MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0865.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5358 (φιλάγαθος);
G0865.k: despiser of those that are good

G0866.d:
ἀ-φιλ-άργυρος, -ον
without love of money, not avaricious; 1Ti.3:3, Heb.13:5. (For other instances, see MM, see word)†
(AS)
G0866.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5366 (φιλάργυρος);
G0866.k: without covetousness, not greedy of filthy lucre

G0867.d:
ἄφ-ιξις, -εως, ἡ
(ἀφικνέομαι), [in LXX: 3Ma.7:18 * ;]
in cl. usually, arrival; rarely, departure: Act.20:29 (so in π., cf. MM, see word; M, Pro.26:1-28, n.).†
(AS)

G0868.d:
ἀφ-ίστημι
[in LXX for סוּר, מָעַל, etc. (41 words in all) ;]
__1. trans. in pres., impf., fut., 1 aor., to put away, lead away; metaphorically, to move to revolt: Act.5:37.
__2. Intrans. in pf., plpf., 2 aor., to stand off, depart from, withdraw from: with genitive, Luk.2:37; before ἀπό, Luk.4:13 13:27, Act.5:38 12:10 15:38 19:9 22:29, 2Co.12:8; metaphorically, ἀπὸ ἀδικίας, 2Ti.2:19; ἀπὸ θεοῦ, (fall away, apostatize), Heb.3:12 Mid. (exc. 1 aor., WH. is trans.), to withdraw oneself from, absent oneself from: Luk.2:37; metaphorically, fall away, apostatize: absol., Luk.8:13; with genitive, 1Ti.4:1 (MM, see word; Cremer, 308).†
(AS)
G0868.s: to remove, i.e. (actively) instigate to revolt; usually (reflexively) to desist, desert, etc.
G0868.k: depart, draw (fall) away, refrain, withdraw self

G0870.d:
ἀφόβως
adv. (φόβος), [in LXX: Pro.1:33 (פַּחַד), Wis.17:4 * ;]
without fear: Luk.1:74, Php.1:14, 1Co.16:10, Ju 12.†
(AS)
G0870.o: adverb from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5401 (φόβος);

G0871.d:
ἀφ-ομοιόω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Wis.13:14, Ep. Jer 1:5, 63, 71* ;]
to make like: pass., Heb.7:3.†
(AS)

G0872.d:
ἀφ-οράω, -ῶ
[in LXX: 4Ma.17:10 (είς θεόν)* ;]
__(a) to look away from all else at, fix one's gaze upon: metaphorically (MM, see word), Heb.12:2;
__(b) simply, to see: ἀφίδω (see: ἀπεῖδον, and Lft., Phi., in l; MM, see word), Php.2:23 (see Ellic., in l).†
(AS)

G0873.d:
ἀφ-ορίζω
[in LXX (Cremer, 805 f.) for בָּדַל hi., סָגַר hi., נוּף hi., רוּם hi etc. ;]
__(a) to mark off by boundaries from, separate from: with accusative, Act.19:9, Gal.2:12; id. before ἐκ (ἀπό), Mat.13:49 25:32 (MM, see word); of excom­munication, Luk.6:22. Pass., absol., 2Co.6:17;
__(b) to set apart, devote to a special purpose (before εἰς): with accusative, Gal.1:15. Mid., Act.13:2, Rom.1:1 (DB, iii 588).†
(AS)
G0873.s: to set off by boundary, i.e. (figuratively) limit, exclude, appoint, etc.

G0874.d:
ἀφ-ορμή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX: Eze.5:7 (הָמוֹן), Pro.9:9, 3Ma.3:2 * ;]
prop., a starting point; in war, a base of operations; metaphorically, an occasion, incentive, opportunity (MM, see word): 2Co.11:12, Gal.5:13; ἀφ. λαμβάνειν, Luk.11:24, WH, mg., Rom.7:8, 11; ἀφ. διδόναι, 2Co.5:12, 1Ti.5:14.*
(AS)
G0874.o: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G3729 (ὁρμάω);

G0875.s: to froth at the mouth (in epilepsy)

G0876.d: foam , of the sea, (Iliad by Homer): of an angry lion, foam, froth , (Iliad by Homer); ἀπ᾽ ἀνθρώπων ἀφρόν frothy blood , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G0877.d:
ἀφροσύνη, -ης, ἡ
(ἄφρων), [in LXX for אִוֶּלֶת, נְבָלָה, etc. ;]
foolishness: Mrk.7:22, 2Co.11:1 11:17 11:21.†
(AS)

G0878.d:
ἄφρων, -ον genitive -ονος
(φρήν), [in LXX for כְּסִיל, נָבָל, etc. ;]
without reason, senseless, foolish, expressing "want of mental sanity and sobriety, a reckless and inconsiderate habit of mind" (Hort; cf. MM, see word): Luk.11:40 12:20, Rom.2:20, 1Co.15:36, 2Co.11:16 12:6 12:11, 1Pe.2:15; opposite to φρόνιμος, 2Co.11:19; to συνιέντες, Eph.2:17.†
(AS)
G0878.s: properly, mindless, i.e. stupid, (by implication) ignorant, (specially) egotistic, (practically) rash, or (morally) unbelieving
G0878.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5424 (φρήν);

G0879.d:
ἀφ-υπιόω, -ῶ
(ὑπνόω, to put to sleep), [in Al.: Gen.28:11 * ;]
__1. to awake from sleep (Anth.).
__2. = cl. καθυπνόω (MM, see word), to fall asleep: Luk.8:23.†
(AS)
G0879.s: properly, to become awake, i.e. (by implication) to drop (off) in slumber
G0879.o: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G5258 (ὕπνος);

G0880.d:
ἀφωνος, -ον
(φωνή) [in LXX: Isa.53:7 (עָלַם ni.), Wis.4:19, 2Ma.3:29 * ;]
dumb, speechless: Act.8:32 (LXX); of idols (MM, see word), 1Co.12:2; of beasts, 2Pe.2:19; τοσαῦτα γένη φωνῶν καὶ οὐδὲν ἄ.—so many kinds of voices and none voiceless, i.e. without signification, unintelligible: 1Co.14:10.†
(AS)
G0880.s: voiceless, i.e. mute (by nature or choice); figuratively, unmeaning
G0880.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5456 (φωνή);

G0882.d:
Ἀχαία (T, Ἀχαΐα), -ας, ἡ (Bl., § 46, 11)
Achaia, the Roman province: Act.18:12, 27 19:21 Rom.15:26, 1Co.16:15, 2Co.1:1 9:2 11:10, 1Th.1:7-8.†
(AS)
G0882.s: Achaia (i.e. Greece), a country of Europe

G0884.d:
ἀχάριστος, -ον
(χαρίζομαι), [in LXX: Wis.16:29, Sir.29:17, 25, 4Ma.9:10 * ;]
__(a) ungracious, unpleasing;
__(b) ungrateful, thankless: Luk.6:35, 2Ti.3:2.†
(AS)
G0884.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G5483 (χαρίζομαι);

G0886.d:
ἀ-χειρο-ποίητος, -ον
(χειροποίητος)
not made by hands: Mrk.14:58, 2Co.5:1; metaphorically, περιτομή ἀ. (i.e. spiritual ), Col.2:11 (MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0886.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5499 (χειροποίητος);

G0887.d:
ἀχλύς, -ύος, ἡ
[in Aq.: Eze.12:7; Sm.: Job.3:5 * ;]
a mist, esp. a dimness of the eyes: Act.13:11 (see Tr., Syn., § with).†
(AS)
G0887.s: dimness of sight, i.e. (probably) a cataract

G0888.d:
ἀ-χρεῖος, -ον
(χρεῖος, useful), [in LXX: 2Ki.6:22 (שָׁפָל), Ep. Jer.17:1-27 * ;]
useless, unprofitable: Mat.25:30, Luk.17:10 (MM, see word).†
(AS)
G0888.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5534 (χρή) (compare G5532 (χρεία));

G0889.d:
ἀχρεόω (Rec. -ειόω, Polyb., LXX), -ῶ
(ἄχρεος = ἀχρεῖος) [in LXX (-ειόω) for אָלַח ni., etc. ;]
to make useless, unprofitable: pass., Rom.3:12 (LXX).†
(AS)

G0890.d:
ά-χρηατος, -ον
[in LXX: Hos.8:8 (חֵפֶץ אַיִן), Wis.2:11, Sir.16:1, al. ;]
useless; unserviceable: opposite to εὔχρηστος, Phm 11.†
(AS)
G0890.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5543 (χρηστός);

G0891.d:
ἄχρι
(and Epic ἄχρις, bef. vowel (see MM, see word), Rom.11:25 T, Gal.3:19 T, WH, mg., Heb.3:13);
__1. adv., utterly (Hom.).
__2. Prep. with genitive, until, unto, as far as;
__(a) of time Act.3:21 22:22, Rom.1:13 5:13, 1Co.4:11, 2Co.3:14, Gal.4:2, Php.1:6; ἄ. καιροῦ, Luk.4:13, Act.13:11; ἄ. ἧς ἡμέρας, Mat.24:38, Luk.1:20 17:27, Act.1:2 (τῆς ἡ. ἧς), Act.1:22; ἄ. ταύτης τ. ἡμέρας (τ. ἡ. ταύτης), Act.2:29 23:1 26:22; ἄ. ἡμερων πέντε, Act.20:6; ἄ. αὐγῆς, Act.20:11; ἄ. τοῦ νῦν, Rom.8:22, Php.1:5; ἄ. τέλους, Heb.6:11, Rev.2:26;
__(b) of space: Act.11:5 13:6 20:4 (R, txt., WH, mg.) Act.28:15, 2Co.10:13-14, Heb.4:12, Rev.14:20 18:5;
__(with) of measure…
G0891.s: (of time) until or (of place) up to
G0891.o: akin to G206 (ἄκρον) (through the idea of a terminus);
G0891.k: as far as, for, in(-to), till, (even, un-)to, until, while

G0892.d:
ἄχυρον, -ον, τό
[in LXX chiefly for תֶּבֶן ;]
chaff: Mat.3:12, Luk.3:17.†
(AS)

G0893.d:
ἀ-ψευδής, -ές
(ψεῦδος), [in LXX: Wis.7:17 * ;]
free from false-hood, truthful: Tit.1:2.†
(AS)
G0893.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5579 (ψεῦδος);

G0894.d:
ἄψινθος, -ου, ἡ
(also ἀψίνθιον, τό; ἀψινθία, ἡ),
wormwood: as a proper name, Rev.8:11.†
(AS)
G0894.s: wormwood (as a type of bitterness, i.e. (figuratively) calamity)

G0895.o: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5590 (ψυχή);

G0896.d:
Βάαλ (Rec. βαάλ), ὁ, ἡ, indecl. (Heb. בַּעַל, lord),
Baal: Rom.11:4 (LXX). The fem. art. here agrees with the usage of LXX, where, following a similar Hebrew practice (בֹּשֶׁת for בַּעַל), αἰσχύνη appears to have been substituted in reading for the written Βάαλ (cf. 3Ki.18:19), and to account for the frequently use of the fem. art. bef. Β. The usage, however, is not general, and in the passage cited in Ro (3Ki.19:18), LXX reads τῷ Β. †
(AS)
G0896.s: Baal, a Phœnician deity (used as a symbol of idolatry)

G0897.d:
Βαβυλών, -ῶνος, ἡ (בָּבֶל, Heb. form of Assyr. Bab-ili, Gate of God),
Babylon: Mat.1:11, 12 17, Act.7:43" (LXX) ; symbolically, of Rome: Rev.14:8 16:19 17:5 18:2, 10, 21, and prob. also 1Pe.5:13.†
(AS)
G0897.s: Babylon, the capitol of Chaldæa (literally or figuratively (as a type of tyranny))

βαθμός, -οῦ, ὁ, Ion. form of βασμός
(βαίνω, to step), [in LXX 1Ki.5:5 (מִפְתָּן), 4Ki.20:9, 10 11 (מַעֲלָה), Sir.6:36 * ;]
a step (4Ki, l.with, of degrees of a dial); metaphorically, a degree, standing: 1Ti.3:13.†
(AS)

βάθος, -εος (-ους), τό,
[in LXX for מְצוּלָה ,תַּחְתִּי, etc. ;]
depth: Mat.13:5, Mrk.4:5, Rom.8:39, Eph.3:18; τὸ β., the deep sea: Luk.5:4; metaphorically, β. πλούτου . . . Θεοῦ, Rom.11:33; τὰ β. τ. Θεοῦ (the Divine counsels), 1Co.2:10; ἡ κατὰ βάθους πτωχεία, deep poverty, 2Co.8:2.†
(AS)

G0900.d:
βαθύνω
(βαθύς), [in LXX for עמד: Psa.91 (92):5, Jer.29 (49):8 30(49)30 * ;]
to deepen: Luk.6:48.†
(AS)

G0901.d:
βαθύς (genitive -έως, vernac., Lk, l.with; Bl., §8, 5), -εῖα, -ύ,
[in LXX chiefly for עמק ;]
deep; Jhn.4:11; metaphorically, ὄρθρου βαθέως (see supr.), early dawn, Luk.24:1; ὕπνος, Act.20:9; τὰ β. τοῦ Σατανᾶ, Rev.2:24.†
(AS)
G0901.s: profound (as going down), literally or figuratively

G0902.d:
βαΐον, ου, τό
(also βὰϊον, another form of βὰϊς, from the Egyptian), [in LXX: 1Ma.13:51 * ;] (frequently in Egyptian π., see MM, Exp., x)
a palm-branch: Jhn.12:13 (DB, i, 314).†
(AS)
G0902.s: a palm twig (as going out far)
G0902.o: a diminutive of a derivative probably of the base of G939 (βάσις);

G0903.d:
Βαλαάμ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בִּלְעָם), as in LXX (FlJ has ὁ βάλαμος);
Balaam (Num.22-24): 2Pe.2:15, Ju 11, Rev.2:14.†
(AS)
G0903.s: Balaam, a Mesopotamian (symbolic of a false teacher)

G0905.d:
βαλλάντιον (Rec. βαλά-), -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX: Job.14:17 (צְרוֹר), Pro.1:14 (כִּיס), Tob.1:14 8:2, Sir.18:33 א 2 * ;]
a purse: Luk.10:4 12:33 22:35, 36.†
(AS)
G0905.o: probably remotely from G906 (βάλλω) (as a depository);

to dip, immerse, sink;

G0907.s: to immerse, submerge; to make whelmed (i.e. fully wet); used only (in the New Testament) of ceremonial ablution, especially (technically) of the ordinance of Christian baptism

G0908.d:
βάπτισμα, -τος, τό (βαπτίζω), prop., the result of the act, τὸ βαπτίζειν, as distinct from βαπτισμός, the act itself,
immersion, baptism;
__1. metaphorically, of affliction: Mrk.10:38, 39 Luk.12:50.
__2. Of the religious rite of baptism;
__(a) of John's baptism: Mat.3:7 21:25, Mrk.11:30, Luk.7:29 20:4, Act.1:22 10:37 18:25 19:3; β. μετανοίας, Mrk.1:4, Luk.3:3, Act.13:24 19:4;
__(b) of Christian baptism; Rom.6:4, Eph.4:5, Col.2:12 (Tr., -μῷ, which see), 1Pe.3:21 (cf. Cremer, 130; Tr., Syn. §xcix).
† (AS)

G0909.d:
βαπτισμός, -οῦ, ὁ (βαπτίζω), prop., the act of which βάπτισμα is the result;
__1. a dipping, washing, lustration: Mrk.7:4; of Jewish ceremonial. Heb.9:10; in Heb.6:2, βαπτισμῶν διδαχήν (-ῆς), "the pl. and the peculiar form seem to be used to include Christian baptism with other lustral rites" (Westc, in l.).
__2. baptism: FlJ, Ant., 18, 5, 2 (of John's baptism), and some Fathers (see Soph., see word). Not so in NT, unless ἐν τ. βαπτισμῷ, in the act of baptism, Col.2:12, be read with Tr. (Rec., WH, R, -ματι).
† (AS)

G0910.d:
βαπτιστής, -ου, ὁ (βαπτίζω),
a baptizer: of John the Baptist, Mat.3:1 11:11, 12 14:2, 8 16:14 17:13, Mrk.6:25 8:28, Luk.7:20, 33 9:19.†
(AS)
G0910.s: a baptizer, as an epithet of Christ's forerunner

G0911.d:
βάπτω,
[in LXX chiefly for טבל ;]
__(a) to dip: Luk.16:24, Jhn.13:26 (ἐμβ-, L);
__(b) to dip in dye, to dye: Rev.19:13 (Rec.; ῥεραντισμένον, WH; περιρεραμμένον, T; ῥεραμμένον, Swete, in l., which see).
† (AS)
G0911.s: to whelm, i.e. cover wholly with a fluid; in the New Testament only in a qualified or special sense, i.e. (literally) to moisten (a part of one's person), or (by implication) to stain (as with dye)

G0912.d:
Βαραββᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ (Aram. בַּר־אַבָּא, lit., son of a father, i.e. accusative to Jerome, filius magistri),
Barabbas: Mat.27:16, 17 20, 21, 26, Mrk.15:7, 11 15, Luk.23:18, Jhn.18:40. (In Mat.27:16, some MSS. read Ἰησοῦν Β.; see WH, App., 19f.).†
(AS)
G0912.s: son of Abba; Bar-abbas, an Israelite

G0915.d:
βάρβαρος, -ον (prob. onomatop., descriptive of unintelligible sounds),
[in LXX: Ps 113 (114):1 (לעז), Eze.21:31 (36) (בּער), 2Ma.2:21 4:25 10:4, 3Ma.3:24 * ;]
barbarous, barbarian, strange to Greek language and culture (and also, after the Persian war, with the added sense of brutal, rude): Act.28:2, 4 Rom.1:14, 1Co.14:11, Col.3:11 (see Lft., in l., and Notes, 249).†
(AS)

G0916.d:
βαρέω, -ῶ (later form of βαρύνω, which see),
[in LXX: Exo.7:14 (כָּבֵד), 2Ma.13:9 * ;]
to depress, weigh down. In NT, in pass. only: Mat.26:43, Luk.9:32 21:34, 2Co.1:8 5:4, 1Ti.5:16.†
(AS)

G0917.d:
βαρέως, adv.
(βαρύς), [in LXX: β. φέρειν, Gen.31:35 (חרה בעיני); β. ἀκούειν, Isa.6:10 (כּבד hi.)* ;]
heavily, with difficulty: Mat.13:15, Act.28:27" (LXX) .†
(AS)

G0918.d:
Βαρθολομαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Aram. בַּר־תָּלְמַי, son of Tolmai),
Bartholomew, the Apostle (see: Ναθαναήλ): Mat.10:3, Mrk.3:18, Luk.6:14, Act.1:13.†
(AS)
G0918.s: son of Tolmai; Bar-tholomæus, a Christian apostle

G0919.d:
Βαρι-ησοῦς, -οῦ, ὁ (Aram. בַּר־יֵשׁוּעַ, son of Joshua),
Bar-Jesus: Act.13:6 (see: Ἐλύμας).†
(AS)
G0919.s: son of Jesus (or Joshua); Bar-jesus, an Israelite

G0920.d:
Βαριωνᾶς, Βαριωνᾶ, -ᾶ, ὁ (Aram. בַּר־יוֹנָה, son of Jonah),
Bar-Jonah, a surname of Peter: Mat.16:17.†
(AS)
G0920.s: son of Jonas (or Jonah); Bar-jonas, an Israelite

G0921G.d:
Βαρναβᾶς, -α, ὁ (Aram. בַּר, son, as prefix to another word interpreted in Act.4:36, τῆς παρακλήσεως, perh. נְבוּאָה, wh., however, should be rendered by προφητεία as in II Est.6:14, LXX. Deiss., BS, 309f., thinks Β. may be a variant of the name Βαρνεβοῦς, son of Nebo, found in a Syrian Inscr., altered with a view to disguising its origin; see also Milligan, NTD, iii; Dalman, Gr., 142),
Barnabas: Act.4:36 9:27 11:22, 30 12:25 13-15, 1Co.9:6, Gal.2:1, 9 13, Col.4:10.†
(AS)
G0921G.s: son of Nabas (i.e. prophecy); Barnabas, an Israelite

G0922.d:
βάρος, -εος, τό,
[in LXX: Jdg.18:21 (כּבד), Jdth.7:4, Sir.13:2, 2Ma.9:10, 3Ma.5:47 * ;]
weight;
__(a) a weight, burden, lit. and metaphorically: Mat.20:12, Act.15:28, 2Co.4:17, Rev.2:24; ἀλλήλων τὰ β., one another's faults, Gal.6:2; ἐν β., burdensome: 1Th.2:6, R, txt., but see infr.;
__(b) in late Gk. (Soph., Lex., see word), dignity, authority: ἐν βάρει, 1Th.2:6 (R, mg.; see Milligan, ICG, in l.).†
SYN.: ὄγκος, an encumbrance; φορτίον, a burden, that which is borne. (AS)
G0922.s: compare G899 (βάθος)); weight; in the New Testament only, figuratively, a load, abundance, authority
G0922.o: probably from the same as G939 (βάσις) (through the notion of going down;

G0923G.d:
Βαρσαββᾶς (Rec. -αβᾶς), -ᾶ (Aram., son of Sabba),
Barsabbas:
__1. the surname of one Joseph: Act.1:23.
__2. The surname of one Judas: Act.15:22.
† (AS)
G0923G.s: son of Sabas (or Tsaba); Bar-sabas, the name of two Israelites
G0923G.o: of Chaldee origin (H01247 and probably H06634);

G0923H.d:
Βαρσαββᾶς (Rec. -αβᾶς), -ᾶ (Aram., son of Sabba),
Barsabbas:
__1. the surname of one Joseph: Act.1:23.
__2. The surname of one Judas: Act.15:22.
† (AS)
G0923H.s: son of Sabas (or Tsaba); Bar-sabas, the name of two Israelites
G0923H.o: of Chaldee origin (H01247 and probably H06634);

G0924.d:
Βαρτίμαιος, -ου, ὁ (-μαῖος, T; perh. Aram. בַּר־טִמְאַי, see DB, iv, p. 762),
Bartimæus: Mrk.10:46.†
(AS)
G0924.s: son of Timæus (or the unclean); Bar-timæus, an Israelite

G0925.d:
βαρύνω,
to weigh down = βαρέω (which see): Luk.21:34, Rec.†
(AS)

G0926.d:
βαρύς, -εῖα, ύ,
[in LXX chiefly for כָּבֵד ;]
heavy: Mat.23:4. Metaphorical, burdensome: ἐντολή, 1Jn.5:3; severe (perh. impressive): ἐπιστολή, 2Co.10:10; weighty: τὰ βαρύτερα τ. νόμου, Mat.23:23; αἰτιώματα, Act.25:7; violent, cruel (EV, grievous): λύκος, Act.20:29.†
(AS)

G0927.d:
βαρύτιμος, -ον
(βαρύς, τιμή),
of great value, very costly: Mat.26:7 (T, πολυτίμου) .†
(AS)

G0928G.d:
βασανίζω
(βάσανος), [in LXX: 1Ki.5:3, Sir.4:17, and frequently in Wi, II, 4Mac ;]
__1. prop., to rub on the touchstone, put to the test.
__2. to examine by torture, hence, generally, to torture, torment, distress: Mat.8:6, 29 14:24, Mrk.5:7 6:48, Luk.8:28, 2Pe.2:8, Rev.9:5 11:10 12:2 14:10 20:10.
† (AS)

G0928H.d:
βασανίζω
(βάσανος), [in LXX: 1Ki.5:3, Sir.4:17, and frequently in Wi, II, 4Mac ;]
__1. prop., to rub on the touchstone, put to the test.
__2. to examine by torture, hence, generally, to torture, torment, distress: Mat.8:6, 29 14:24, Mrk.5:7 6:48, Luk.8:28, 2Pe.2:8, Rev.9:5 11:10 12:2 14:10 20:10.
† (AS)

G0930.d:
βασανιστής, -οῦ, ὁ (βασανίζω),
prop., a torturer; used of a gaoler, Mat.18:34.†
(AS)

G0931.d:
βάσανος, -ου, ὁ (of Oriental origin),
[in LXX chiefly for כְּלִמָּה ,אָשָׁם, and frequently in 4Mac ;]
__1. prop., touchstone, a dark stone used in testing metals.
__2. examination by torture.
__3. torment, torture: Mat.4:24, Luk.15:23, 28.
† (AS)
G0931.o: perhaps remotely from the same as G939 (βάσις) (through the notion of going to the bottom);

G0932.d:
βασιλεία, -ας, ἡ
(βασιλεύω), [in LXX chiefly for מַמְלָכָה ,מַלְכוּת ;]
__1. prop. abstract, sovereignty, royal power, dominion: Luk.1:33 22:29, Jhn.18:36, Act.1:6, Heb.1:8, 1Co.15:24; λαβεῖν β., Luk.19:12, 15 Rev.17:12; δοῦναι τὴν, ib. 17; ἔχειν β., ib. 18; ἔρχεσθαι ἐν τ. (εἰς τὴν) β., Mat.16:28, Luk.23:42; β. τ. θεοῦ, Rev.12:10.
__2. By meton., concrete (MM, Exp., x),
__(a) a kingdom, the territory or people over whom the king rules (Est.5:3, al.): Mat.4:8 12:25, 26 24:7, Mrk.3:24 6:23, Luk.4:5, Heb.11:33, al.;
__(b) the royal majesty (cf. our phrase His Majesty), the king himself (τ. σπέρμα τῆς β., 4Ki.11:1).
…
G0932.s: properly, royalty, i.e. (abstractly) rule, or (concretely) a realm (literally or figuratively)

G0933.d:
βασίλειον, -ου, τό
(βασίλειος, which see), [in LXX for הֵיכָל ( Nam.2:6, Dan.6:18*), מַמְלָכָה ( 3Ki.3:1 14:8, 4Ki.15:19*), etc. ;]
__1. a capital city.
__2. Freq. in pl., τὰ β., a palace: Luk.7:25.
† (AS)

G0934.d:
βασίλειος, -ον (also -α, -ον; βασιλεύς),
[in LXX; Exo.19:6, Deu.3:10 (מַמְלָכָה), Exo.23:22, Wis.18:15, 3Ma.3:28, 4Ma.3:8 * ;]
royal: 1Pe.2:9 (LXX) (see Hort, in l.).†

royal, regal, kingly;, metaphorically possessed of high prerogatives and distinction, 1Pet. 2:9; (AS)

G0935.d:
βασιλεύς, -έως, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for מֶלֶךְ ;]
a king: Mat.1:6 2:1; used by courtesy of Herod the Tetrarch, Mat.14:9; of the Roman Emperor, as frequently in κοινή (Deiss., LAE, p. 367), 1Pe.2:13, 17; of the Christ, in the phrase ὁ β. τ. Ἰουδαίων, Mat.2:2, al.; τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, Mrk.15:32, Jhn.1:50 12:13; of God, Mat.5:35, 1Ti.1:17, Rev.15:3; β. βασιλέων, Rev.17:14 19:16; β. τ. βασιλευόντων, 1Ti.6:15 (on the associations of the word to Jewish Hellenists, see Cl. Rev., i, 7).†
(AS)
G0935.o: probably from G939 (βάσις) (through the notion of a foundation of power);

G0936.d:
βασιλεύω, (βασιλεύς),
[in LXX for מלךְ, its parts and derivatives, exc. 4Ki.15:5 (ישׁב) ;]
to be king, to reign, rule: 1Ti.6:15; with genitive (cl.), Mat.2:22; before ἐπί, with accusative (= Heb. מלךְ על; Bl., §36, 8), Luk.1:33 19:14, 27 Rom.5:14; ἐπὶ τ. γῆς, on earth, Rev.5:10; of God, Rev.11:15, 17 19:6; of Christ, Luk.1:33, 1Co.15:25, Rev.11:15; of Christians, Rev.5:10 20:4 (constative aor., M, Pr., 130), ib. 6 22:5. Metaphorical, Christians, Rom.5:17, 1Co.4:8; θάνατος, Rom.5:14, 17; ἁμαρτία, Rom.5:21 6:12. Ingressive aor. (M, Pr., 109), to begin to reign: 1Co.4:8, Rev.11:17 19:6 (Cremer, 137).†
(AS)

G0937.d:
βασιλικός, -ή, -όν (βασιλεύς),
[in LXX for מֶלֶךְ and its cognates ;]
royal, belonging to a king: χώρα, Act 12:20; ἐσθής, Act.12:21; νόμος β., a supreme law, "a law which governs other laws and so has a specially regal character" (Hort), or because made by a king (LAE, p. 3673), Jas.2:8; τις, one in the service of a king, a courtier, Jhn.4:46, 49 (WH, mg., βασιλίσκος).†
(AS)
G0937.s: regal (in relation), i.e. (literally) belonging to (or befitting) the sovereign (as land, dress, or a courtier), or (figuratively) preeminent

G0938G.d:
βασίλισσα, -ης, ἡ (in Attic, βασιλεία, βασιλίς),
[in LXX chiefly for מַלְכָּה ;]
a queen: Mat.12:42, Luk.11:31, Act.8:27, Rev.18:7.†
(AS)

G0938H.d:
βασίλισσα, -ης, ἡ (in Attic, βασιλεία, βασιλίς),
[in LXX chiefly for מַלְכָּה ;]
a queen: Mat.12:42, Luk.11:31, Act.8:27, Rev.18:7.†
(AS)

G0939.d:
βάσις, ־εως, ἡ
(βαίνω), [in LXX chiefly for אֶדֶן ;]
__1. a step (Æsch., al.).
__2. Hence, a foot (Plat.; Wis.13:18): Act.3:7.
† (AS)
G0939.s: a pace ("base"), i.e. (by implication) the foot

G0940.d:
βασκαίνω,
[in LXX: Deu.28:54, 56 (רעע), Sir.14:6, 8*.]
__1. to slander (Dem.).
__2. to blight by the evil eye, to fascinate, bewitch: Gal.3:1.
† (AS)
G0940.s: to malign, i.e. (by extension) to fascinate (by false representations)

G0941.d:
βαστάζω,
[in LXX: Jdg.16:30 (נטה), Rut.2:16, 2Ki.23:5, 4Ki.18:14 and Job.21:3 (נשׂא), Sir.6:25, Da TH Bel 36 * ;]
__1. to take up with the hands, to lift: λίθους, Jhn.10:31.
__2. to bear, to carry, as a burden, and metaphorically, to endure; Mat.3:11 20:12, Mrk.14:13, Luk.7:14 10:7 11:27 14:27 22:10, Jhn.16:12 19:17, Act.3:2 9:15 15:1 21:35, Rom.11:18 15:1, Gal.5:10 6:2, 5 17, Rev.2:2, 3 17:7.
__3. In late writers (MM, Exp., ii, iii, x),
__(a) to take away; Mat.8:17 (Isa.53:4, Heb.);
__(b) to carry off, steal: Jhn.12:6 20:15.
† (AS)
G0941.s: to lift, literally or figuratively (endure, declare, sustain, receive, etc.)
G0941.o: perhaps remotely derived from the base of G939 (βάσις) (through the idea of removal);

G0942.d:
βάτος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ,
[in LXX (always masc, as in Attic): Exo.3:2-4, Deu.33:16 (סְנֶה), Job.31:40 (בָּאְשָׁה)* ;]
a bramble-bush: Luk.6:44, Act.7:30, 35; ἐπὶ τοῦ (τῆς) β., in the place concerning the bush: Mrk.12:26, Luk.20:37.†
(AS)

G0943.d:
βάτος, -ου, ὁ (Heb. בַּת),
[in LXX (also βαίθ, βάδος): II Est.7:22 * ;]
bath, a Jewish liquid measure, = μετρητής (which see), or about 8 3/4 gals.: Luk.16:6.†
(AS)
G0943.s: a bath, or measure for liquids

G0945.d:
βατταλογέω, -ῶ (Rec. βαττολ-, D, βλαττ- = βατταρίζω, prob. onomatop.; see MM, see word; DCG, ii, 499b, 790a);
to stammer, repeat idly: Mat.6:7 (Cremer, 765).†
(AS)
G0945.s: to stutter, i.e. (by implication) to prate tediously

G0946.d:
βδέλυγμα, -τος, τό
(βδελύσσω), [in LXX chiefly for שֶׁקֶץ ,תּוֹעֵבָה ;]
an abomination, a detestable thing: Luk.16:15, Rev.17:4, 5 21:27; τὸ β. τ. ἐρημώσεως (Dan LXX 12:11, cf . 1Ma.1:54; DB, i, 12f.; DCG, i, 6f.), Mrk.13:14, Mat.24:15 (Cremer, 138).†
(AS)

G0947.d:
βδελυκτός, ή, -όν
(βδελύσσω), [in LXX: Pro.17:15 (תּוֹעֵבָה), Sir.41:5, 2Ma.1:27 * ;]
abominable, detestable: Tit.1:16 (Cremer, 137).†
(AS)

G0948.d:
βδελύσσω, βδελύσσομαι
(βδέω, to stink), [in LXX chiefly for שׁקץ ,תּעב ;]
in cl., mid. only (Attic, -ττομαι); to make foul; pass., Rev.21:8; mid., to turn away in disgust from, to detest: Rom.2:22 (Cremer, 137).†
(AS)
G0948.s: to be disgusted, i.e. (by implication) detest (especially of idolatry)

G0949.d:
βέβαιος, -ον (also -α, -ον; βαίνω),
[in LXX: Est.3:13, Wis.7:23, 3Ma.5:31 7:7, 4Ma.17:4 * ;]
firm, secure: ἄγκυρα, Heb.6:19; metaphorically, sure (esp. "in the sense of legally guaranteed security," Deiss., BS, 109; cf . two foll. words): ἐπαγγελία, Rom.4:16; ἐλπίς, 2Co.1:6; λόγος, Heb.2:2; παρρησία, Heb.3:6; ἀρχή (τ. ὑποστάσεως), Heb.3:14; διαθήκη, Heb.9:17; κλῆσις κ. ἐκλογή, 2Pe.1:10; comp. (-ότερος), προφητικὸς λόγος, 2Pe.1:19.†
(AS)
G0949.o: from the base of G939 (βάσις) (through the idea of basality);

G0950.d:
βεβαιόω, -ῶ
(βέβαιος), [in LXX: Ps 40 (41)12 (נצב hi.), 118 (119)28 (קוּם pi.), 3Ma.5:42 * ;]
to confirm, establish, secure, of things (cl.): λόγον, Mk 16:[20]; ἐπαγγελίας, Rom.15:8; of persons (DCG, ii, 605): 1Co.1:8, 2Co.1:21. Pass., 1Co.1:6, Col.2:7, Heb.2:3 13:9 (as an Attic legal term, to guarantee the validity of a purchase, establish or confirm a title; see next word, Cremer, 139; cf. δια-β.).†
(AS)

G0951.d:
βεβαίωσις, -εως, ἡ
(βεβαιόω, which see), [in LXX: Lev.25:23 (צְמִיתֻת), Wis.6:19 * ;]
confirmation: τ. εὐαγγελίου, Php.1:7; εἰς β., Heb.6:16, a phrase frequently in π. of guarantee in a business transaction (Deiss., BS, 104ff.; Cremer, 140).†
(AS)

G0952.d:
βέβηλος, -ον
(βαίνω, whence βηλός, a threshold), [in LXX chiefly for חֹל ;]
__1. permitted to be trodden, accessible (see DCG, ii, 422b); hence,
__2. (opposite to ἱερός) unhallowed, profane: of things, 1Ti.4:7 6:20, 2Ti.2:16; of men, 1Ti.1:9, Heb.12:16 (cf. κοινός; Cremer, 140).
† (AS)
G0952.s: accessible (as by crossing the door-way), i.e. (by implication, of Jewish notions) heathenish, wicked
G0952.o: from the base of G939 (βάσις) and (a threshold);

G0953.d:
βεβηλόω, -ῶ
(βέβηλος), [in LXX chiefly for חלל ;]
to profane: τ. σάββατον, Mat.12:5; τ. ἱερόν, Act.24:6 (Cremer, 141).†
SYN.: κοινόω, which see (AS)

G0954.d:
Βεελζεβούλ (WH, App., 159, Rec., βεελζεβούλ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בַּעַל, lord, and the Talmudic זִבּוּל, from זֶבֶל, dung (Dalman, Gr., 137.n), or perh. זִבֻל, habitation, but, see DB, iv, 409f.; DCG, i, 181). The AV, RV, Beelzebub, comes through Vg. from 4Ki.1:2, בַּעַל זִבוּב, lord of flies (LXX, βάαλ μυῖα, Sm., βεελζεβούβ),
Beelzebul, Beelzebub, a name of Satan: Mat.10:25 12:24, 27 Mrk.3:22, Luk.11:15, 18 19.†
(AS)
G0954.s: dung-god; Beelzebul, a name of Satan
G0954.o: of Chaldee origin (by parody on H01176);

G0955.d:
Βελίαλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בְּלִיַּעַל, worthlessness, but see DB, i, 268),
Belial, a name of Satan: 2Co.6:15, Rec. See next word.†
Βελιάρ, ὁ, indecl. (another form of previous word, "due to harsh Syriac pronunciation," or else Heb. בֵּל יַעַר, lord of the forest),
Beliar, a name of Satan: 2Co.6:15 (see DB, i, 269).†
(AS)
G0955.s: worthlessness; Belial, as an epithet of Satan

G0956.d:
βέλος, -εος, τό
(βάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for חֵץ ;]
a missile, a dart: Eph.6:16.†
(AS)
G0956.s: a missile, i.e. spear or arrow

G0957.d:
βελτίων, -ον (genitive -ονος), comp. of ἀγαθός,
[in LXX chiefly for טוֹב ;]
neut. as adv., better, very well: 2Ti.1:18 (also Act.10:28 D). On elative use in these passages, see M, Pr., 78, 236.†
(AS)
G0957.o: neuter of a compound of a derivative of G906 (βάλλω) (used for the comparative of G18 (ἀγαθός));

G0958.d:
Βενιαμίν, (Rec. -μίν), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בֶּנְיָמִין),
Benjamin: Act.13:21, Rom.11:1, Php.3:5, Rev.7:8.†
(AS)

G0959.d:
Βερνίκη (elsewhere Βερενίκη), Macedonian form of Φερενίκη, cf. Veronica, Victoria), -ης, ἡ,
Bernice, Berenice, dau. of Herod Agrippa I: Act.25:13, 23 26:3o.†
(AS)
G0959.s: victorious; Bernice, a member of the Herodian family
G0959.o: from a provincial form of G5342 (φέρω) and G3529 (νίκη);

G0960.d:
Βέροια, -ας, ἡ,
Berœa, a city of Macedonia: Act.17:10, 13.†
(AS)
G0960.o: perhaps a provincial from a derivative of G4008 (πέραν) (Perœa, i.e. the region beyond the coast-line);

G0961.s: a Berœoean or native of Berœa

G0962.d:
Βηθαβαρά, -ας (Rec. -ρᾶ, indecl.; Heb. בֵּית עֲבָרָה, place of crossing; -αραβᾷ, R, mg.),
Bethabara: Jhn.1:28, Rec. (WH, R, βηθανία).†
(AS)
G0962.s: ferry-house; Bethabara (i.e. Bethabarah), a place on the Jordan

G0963.d:
Βηθανία, -ας (also -ιά, indecl., Luk.19:29 and in B*, Mrk.11:1), ἡ, (Heb. בֵּית עֲנִיָּה, house of affliction, accusative to Jerome, or perh., house of dates, cf. Bethphage),
Bethany;
__1. a village fifteen furlongs from Jerusalem, the modern El Azerîyeh: Mat.21:17 26:6, Mrk.8:22 (WH, mg.) 11:1, 11, 12 14:3 Luk.19:29 24:50, Jhn.11:1, 18 12:1.
__2. A place on E. bank of Jordan: Jhn.1:28 (R, mg., Βηθαβαρά, which see).
† (AS)
G0963.s: date-house; Beth-any, a place in Palestine

G0964.d:
Βηθεσδά, ἡ, indecl. (deriv. uncertain, see Westc. on Jhn.5:2, and DB, i, 279),
Bethesda, a pool in Jerusalem: Jhn.5:2, Rec. (Βηθζαθά, WH, Βηθσαϊδά, WH, mg.).†
(AS)
G0964.s: house of kindness; Beth-esda, a pool in Jerusalem
G0964.o: of Chaldee origin (compare H01004 and H02617);

G0965.d:
Βηθλέεμ, ἡ, indecl. (Heb. בֵּית לֶחֶם, house of bread),
Bethlehem, a town 6 m. S. of Jerusalem: Mat.2:1, 5 6, 8, 16, Luk.2:4, 15 Jhn.7:42.†
(AS)
G0965.s: Bethleem (i.e. Beth-lechem), a place in Palestine

G0966.d:
Βηθσαιδά (Rec. -σαϊδά), and -δάν (Mt, Mk, ll. with), ἡ, indecl. (Syr., house of fish),
Bethsaida, a town on NE. shore of the Sea of Galilee: Luk.9:10. It is generally supposed that a second B. on the W. shore is referred to in Mat.11:21, Mrk.6:45 8:22, Luk.10:13, Jhn.1:45 12:21 (DB, i, 282f.; but see Swete on Mrk.6:45).
__2. 2. Βηθζαθά, ἡ, indecl. (perh. Aram. בֵּית זַיְתָה, house of olives) Jhn.5:2..†
(AS)
G0966.s: fishing-house; Bethsaida, a place in Palestine
G0966.o: of Chaldee origin (compare H01004 and H06719);

G0967.d:
Βηθφαγή (L, -γῆ), ἡ, indecl. (Aram. בֵּית־פַּגֵּי, house of unripe figs; Dalman, Gr., 191),
Bethphage: Mat.21:1, Mrk.11:1, Luk.19:29.†
(AS)
G0967.s: fig-house; Beth-phage, a place in Palestine
G0967.o: of Chaldee origin (compare H01004 and H06291);

G0968.d:
βῆμα, -τος, τό
(βαίνω), [in LXX: Deu.2:5 (מִדְרָךְ), Neh.8:4 (מִגְדָּל), I Est.9:42, Sir.19:30 45:9, 2Ma.13:26 * ;]
__1. a step, stride, pace: Act.7:5.
__2. a raised place, a platform reached by steps, originally that in the Pnyx at Athens from which orations were made; frequently of the tribune or tribunal of a Roman magistrate or ruler: Mat.27:19, Jhn.19:13, Act.12:21, 18:12, 16, 17 25:6, 10, 17; β. τοῦ θεοῦ, Rom.14:10; τ. Χριστοῦ, 2Co.5:10.
† (AS)
G0968.s: a step, i.e. foot-breath; by implication, a rostrum, i.e. a tribunal

G0969.d:
βήρυλλος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ,
[in LXX: Tob.13:17 (-ύλλιον in Exo.28:20, שֹׁהַם * ;])
beryl, a jewel of sea-green colour: Rev.21:20.†
(AS)

G0970.d:
βία, -ας, ἡ,
[in LXX for פֶּרֶךְ, etc. ;]
strength, force, violence: Act.5:26 21:35 24:7 27:41.†
(AS)
G0970.o: probably akin to G979 (βίος) (through the idea of vital activity);

G0971.d:
βιάζω (βία), and depon. -ομαι,
[in LXX for פּרץ, פּצר, etc. ;]
to force, constrain, rare in active (poet, and late prose), but found in cl. in pass., and so perh. βιάζεται, suffereth violence, Mat.11:12, EV (but see infr.), whether
__(a) in good sense, of disciples (Thayer, al.), or
__(b) in bad sense, of the enemies of the kingdom (Meyer, in l.; Dalman, Words, 139ff.; Cremer, 141ff.). Mid., advanceth violently, Mt, l.with (Deiss., BS., 258; Banks, see ref. in DCG, ii, 803f.); before εἰς, to press violently, or force one's way into, Luk.16:16 (see ICC, in l., and in Mt, l.with; cf. παραβιάζομαι and see MM, see…
G0971.s: to force, i.e. (reflexively) to crowd oneself (into), or (passively) to be seized

G0972.d:
βίαιος, -α, -ον
(βία), [in LXX for אָנַשׁ, עַז, צַר, etc. ;]
violent: Act.2:2.†
(AS)

G0973.d:
βιαστής, -οῦ, ὁ (βιάζω), late form of βιατάς;
__1. strong, forceful.
__2. violent (Philo): Mat.11:12 (see: βιάζω).
† (AS)

G0974.d:
βιβλαρίδιον, -ου, τό (diminutive of βιβλάριον, diminutive of βίβλος),
a little book: Rev.10:2, 8 (WH, βιβλιόν, T2, 7 βιβλιδάριον) 9, 10. Not hitherto found elsewhere.†
(AS)

G0975.d:
βιβλίον, -ου, τό (diminutive of βίβλος, which see),
[in LXX also in the alternat. form βυβ-, chiefly for סֶפֶר and the most frequently of the cognate forms ;]
__1. a paper, letter, written document: β. ἀποστασίου, bill of divorce, Mat.19:7, Mrk.10:4.
__2. a book, a roll: Luk.4:17, 20 Jhn.20:30 21:25, Gal.3:10, 2Ti.4:13, Heb.9:19 10:7, Rev.1:11 5:1-9 6:14 10:8 20:12 22:7-19; β. τ. ζωῆς, Rev.13:8 17:8 20:12 21:27.
† (AS)

G0976.d:
βίβλος, -ου, ἡ (variant form of βύβλος, the Egyptian papyrus, paper made from its fibrous coat),
[in LXX for סֶפֶר, the form βύβ- being sometimes used ;]
a book, a roll, used much less frequently than βιβλίον, and with a "connotation of sacredness and veneration" (MM, Exp., x), Mat.1:1 Mrk.12:26, Luk.3:4 20:42 Act.1:20 7:42 19:19; β. τ. ζωῆς, Php.4:3, Rev.3:5 20:15.†
(AS)
G0976.o: properly, the inner bark of the papyrus plant, i.e. (by implication) a sheet or scroll of writing

G0977.d:
βιβρώσκω, poët, and late prose,
[in LXX for אכל ;]
to eat: Jhn.6:13.†
(AS)
G0977.o: a reduplicated and prolonged form of an obsolete primary verb (perhaps causative of G1006 (βόσκω));

G0979.d:
βίος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for יָמִים ;]
__1. period or course of life, life: Luk.8:14, 1Ti.2:2, 2Ti.2:4, 1Jn.2:16.
__2. living, livelihood, means (in Pro.31:14 for לֶחֶם; see DCG, ii, 39a): Mrk.12:44, Luk.8:43 15:12, 30 21:4, 1Jn.3:17.†
SYN.: ζωή, is life intensive, "vita quâ, vivimus," the vital principle; βίος, life extensive, "vita quam vivimus," (1) the period of life, (2) the means by which it is sustained. Hence, in cl., ζ., being confined to the physical life common to men and animals, is the inferior word (cf. zoology, biography). In NT, ζωή is elevated into the ethical and spiritual sphere (cf.…
G0979.s: life, i.e. (literally) the present state of existence; by implication, the means of livelihood

G0980.d:
βιόω, -ῶ
(βίος), [in LXX: Pro.7:2 9:6 (חיה), Job.29:18, Wis.4:4 א 1, 12:23, Sir.40:28, 4Ma.5:22 17:18 * ;]
to spend life, to live: τ. χρόνον βιῶσαι (cl., more frequently 2 aor., -ναι), 1Pe.4:2 (cf. Jb, l.with).†
SYN.: ζάω (which see). (AS)

G0981.d:
βίωσις, -εως, ἡ
(βιόω), [in LXX: Si prol. 12 * ;]
manner of life: Act.26:4.†
(AS)
G0981.s: living (properly, the act, by implication, the mode)

G0982.k: of (pertaining to, things that pertain to) this life

G0984.d:
βλάπτω,
[in LXX: Pro.25:20, Tob.12:2, Wis.10:8 18:2, 2Ma.12:22, 4Ma.9:7 * ;]
to hurt, injure: with accusative, Mrk.16:[18], Luk.4:35.†
(AS)
G0984.s: properly, to hinder, i.e. (by implication) to injure

G0985.d:
βλαστάνω,
[in LXX for צמח, etc. ;]
__1. to sprout: Mat.13:26, Mrk.4:27, Heb.9:4.
__2. In late Gk., causal, to make to grow, produce: with accusative, Jas.5:18.
† (AS)
G0985.s: to germinate; by implication, to yield fruit

G0986.s: Blastus, an officer of Herod Agrippa
G0986.o: perhaps the same as the base of G985 (βλαστάνω);

G0987.d:
βλασφημέω, -ῶ
(βλάσφημος), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:4 (יכח hi.) ib. 6, 22 (גּדף pi.), Isa.52:5 (נאץ hith.), Dan LXX 3:29 (96) (אמר שׁלח), Tob.1:18, Da TH Bel 9, 2Ma.2 * ;]
__1. to speak lightly or profanely of sacred things (in cl., opp. of εὐφημέω), esp. to speak impiously of God, to blaspheme, speak blasphemously: absol., Mat.9:3 26:65, Mrk.2:7, Jhn.10:36, Act.26:11, 1Ti.1:20, 2Pe.2:12; τ. θεόν, Act.19:37, Rev.16:11, 21; τὸ ὄνομα τ. θεοῦ, Rev.13:6 16:9; δόξας, Ju 3, 2Pe.2:10; εἰς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, Mrk.3:29, Luk.12:10.
__2. to revile, rail at, slander: absol., Luk.22:65, Act.13:45 18:6, 1Pe.4:4; with accusative, Mat.27:39, Mrk.3:28 15:29,…
G0987.s: to vilify; specially, to speak impiously
G0987.k: (speak) blaspheme(-er, -mously, -my), defame, rail on, revile, speak evil

G0988.d:
βλασφημία, -ας, ἡ
(βλάσφημος), [in LXX: Eze.35:12 (נֶאָצָה), Da TH 3:29 (96) (שׁלה), Tob.1:18, 1Ma.2:6, 2Ma.8:4 10:35 15:24 * ;]
__(a) railing slander: Mat.12:31 15:19, Mrk.3:28 7:22, Eph.4:31, Col.3:8, 1Ti.6:4, Ju 9, Rev.2:9
__(b) spec., impious speech against God, blasphemy: Mat.26:65, Mrk.14:64, Luk.5:21, Jhn.10:33, Rev.13:5; ὄνομα βλασφημίας, Rev.13:1 17:3; with genitive obj. Mat.12:31; πρὸς τ. θεόν, Rev.13:6 (Cremer, 570; DB, i, 305; DCG ii, 423).†
(AS)

G0989.d:
βλάσφημος, -ον
(βλασ-, of uncertain deriv., see Thayer, Boisacq; + φήμη, speech), [in LXX: Isa.66:3 (מְבָרֵךְ אָוֶן), Wis.1:6, Sir.3:16, 2Ma.9:28 10:4, 36 * ;]
__(a) evil-speaking, slanderous, blasphemous: Act.6:11, 2Ti.3:2, 2Pe.2:11 (cf. Ju 9);
__(b) as subst. a blasphemer: 1Ti.1:13 (Cremer, 570).
† (AS)
G0989.s: scurrilious, i.e. calumnious (against men), or (specially) impious (against God)
G0989.o: from a derivative of G984 (βλάπτω) and G5345 (φήμη);

G0990.d:
βλέμμα, -τος, τό
(βλέπω),
a look, a glance: βλέμματι καὶ ἀκοῇ, 2Pe.2:8, sight and hearing, a sense not found for β. in Gk. lit., but perh. recognized in the vernacular (ICC, in l.)†
(AS)

G0991.d:
βλέπω,
[in LXX chiefly for ראה, also for פּנה, etc. ;]
__1. of bodily sight;
__(a) to see, have sight (opposite to τυφλὸς): Mat.12:22, Jhn.9:7, Act.9:9, Rom.11:8, Rev.3:18, al.;
__(b) to perceive, look (at), see: absol., Act.1:9; with accusative, Mat.7:3, Mrk.5:31, Luk.6:41, Jhn.1:29, al.; ὅραμα, Act.12:9; γυναῖκα, Mat.5:28; βιβλίον, Rev.5:3, 4; τ. βλεπόμενα, 2Co.4:18.
__2. Metaphorical, of mental vision;
__(a) to see, perceive, discern: absol., Mat.13:13, Luk.8:10; δι ̓ ἐσόπτρου, 1Co.13:12; with accusative, Heb.2:9 10:25; before ὅτι, Heb.3:19, Jas.2:22;
__(b) to consider, look to, take heed: absol., Mrk.13:23, 33;…
G0991.k: behold, beware, lie, look (on, to), perceive, regard, see, sight, take heed

G0992.d:
βλητέος, -α, -ον (gerundive of βάλλω),
(that which) one must put: Luk.5:38.†
(AS)

G0993.d:
Βοανηργές, indecl. (on the derivation, see Dalman, Gr., 144; Words, 42; Swete, Mk., l.with; DCG, i, 216),
Boanerges: Mrk.3:17.†
(AS)
G0993.s: sons of commotion; Boanerges, an epithet of two of the apostles

G0994.d:
βοάω, -ῶ
(βοή), [in LXX chiefly for זעק, צעק, קרא ;]
__1. absol., to cry, call out: Mat.3:3, 27:46, Mrk.1:3 15:34, Luk.3:4 9:38 18:38, Jhn.1:23, Act.8:7 17:6 25:24, Gal.4:27.
__2. C. dative, to call on for help (Heb. זעק על, Hos.7:14, al.), Luk.18:7.†
SYN.: καλέω, to call, invite, summon; κράζω, to cry, harshly or inarticulately, as animals; κραυγάζω, intensive of κράζω. βοάω expresses emotion, whether joy, fear, etc. (AS)
G0994.s: to halloo, i.e. shout (for help or in a tumultuous way)
G0994.o: apparently a prolonged form of a primary verb;

G0995.d:
βοή, -ῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX for זְעָקָה, etc. ;]
a cry: Jas.5:4.†
(AS)
G0995.s: a halloo, i.e. call (for aid, etc.)

G0996.d:
βοήθεια, -ας, ἡ (see: βοηθέω),
[in LXX for עֵזֶר, etc. ;]
help: Heb.4:16; pl., helps, "frapping," a technical nautical term (MM, Exp., x; DB, ext., 367): Act.27:17.†
(AS)
G0996.s: aid; specially, a rope or chain for frapping a vessel

G0997.d:
βοηθέω, -ῶ
(βοή + θέω, to run), [in LXX chiefly for עזר ;]
to come to aid, to help, succour: absol., Act.21:28; with dative, Mat.15:25, Mrk.9:22, 24 Act.16:9, 2Co.6:2" (LXX), Heb.2:18, Rev.12:16.†
(AS)

G0998.d:
βοηθός, -ον (see: βοηθέω),
[in LXX chiefly for עזר ;]
__1. (poët. -όος), hasting to the war-cry (Hom.).
__2. helping, auxiliary; as subst. (Hdt.), a helper: Heb.13:6 (LXX).
† (AS)

G0999.d:
βόθυνος, -ου, ὁ (= βόθρος, more frequently in cl.),
[in LXX chiefly for פַּחַת ;]
a pit: Mat.12:11 15:14, Luk.6:39 (cf. DB, iii, 885; DCG, ii, 367).†
(AS)
G0999.s: a hole (in the ground); specially, a cistern

G1000.d:
βολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(βάλλω), [in LXX: Gen.21:16 (טחה), 2Ma.5:3, 3Ma.5:26 * ;]
a throw; λίθου β. (Thuc., v, 65, 2), a stone's throw: Luk.22:41.†
(AS)
G1000.s: a throw (as a measure of distance)

G1001.d:
βολίζω
(βολίς, in sense of sounding-lead),
to heave the lead, take soundings: Act.27:28.†
(AS)

G1002.d:
βολίς, -ίδος, ἡ
(βάλλω), [in LXX for חֵץ, יָרָה, etc. ;]
a dart, javelin: Heb.12:20, Rec. (LXX).†
(AS)

G1003.d:
Βοός and Βοές (RV, Βοάζ, Rec. Βοόζ), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בֹּעַז),
Boaz (Rut.2:1): Mat.1:5, Luk.3:32.†
(AS)

G1005.d:
βορρᾶς, -ᾶ (Attic contr. of Βορέας, the North wind personified),
[in LXX for צָפוֹן ;]
__1. Boreas, the North wind.
__2. the north: Luk.13:29, Rev.21:13.
† (AS)

G1006.d:
βόσκω,
[in LXX for רעה ;]
prop., of a herdsman, to feed: Mat.8:33, Mrk.5:14, Luk.8:34 15:15; metaphorically, of Christian pastoral care, Jhn.21:15, 17. Pass., of cattle, to feed, graze: Mat.8:30, Mrk.5:11, Luk.8:32.†
SYN.: ποιμαίνειν, to tend, shepherd, a wider term, including oversight as well as feeding (see Tr., Syn., §xxv). (AS)
G1006.s: to pasture; by extension to, fodder; reflexively, to graze
G1006.o: a prolonged form of a primary verb (compare G977 (βιβρώσκω), G1016 (βοῦς));

G1007.d:
Βοσόρ see Βεώρ - ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בְּעוֹר),
Beor, father of Balaam: 2Pe.2:15 (Rec. Βοσόρ).†
(AS)

G1008.d:
βοτάνη, -ῆς, ἡ
(βόσκω), [in LXX for עֵשֶׂב, דֶשֶׁא, חָצִיר ;]
__1. grass, fodder.
__2. green herb: Heb.6:7.†
SYN.: λάχανον, a garden herb, a vegetable. (AS)

G1009.d:
βότρυς, -οῦ, ὁ,
[in LXX for אֶשְׁכֹּל ;]
a cluster of grapes: Rev.14:18 (cf. στραφυλή) .†
(AS)

G1010.d:
βουλευτής, -οῦ, ὁ
(βουλεύω), [in LXX: Job.3:14 12:17 (יעץ)* ;]
a councillor, a senator; of a member of the Sanhedrin: Mrk.15:34, Luk.23:50.†
(AS)
G1010.s: an adviser, i.e. (specially) a councillor or member of the Jewish Sanhedrin

G1011.d:
βουλεύω
(βουλή), [in LXX chiefly for יעץ ;]
to take counsel, deliberate, resolve. In mid.,
__1. to take counsel with oneself, consider: before εἰ, Luk.14:31.
__2. to determine with oneself, resolve: with inf., Act.5:33 27:39; with accusative, 2Co.1:17; before ἵνα, Jhn.11:53 12:10 (cf. παρα-, συμ-).
† (AS)
G1011.s: to advise, i.e. (reflexively) deliberate, or (by implication) resolve
G1011.k: consult, take counsel, determine, be minded, purpose

G1012.d:
βουλή, -ῆς, ἡ
(βούλομαι), [in LXX frequently for עֵצָה ;]
counsel, purpose (in cl., esp. of the gods): Luk.23:51, Act.4:28 5:38 19:1 27:12, 42; pl., 1Co.4:5; of the Divine purpose, Heb.6:17; τ. βουλὴν τ. θελήματος αὐτοῦ, Eph.1:11; β. τ. Θεοῦ, Luk.7:30, Act.2:23 13:36 20:27.†
(AS)
G1012.s: volition, i.e. (objectively) advice, or (by implication) purpose

G1013.d:
βούλημα, -τος, τό
(βούλομαι), [in LXX: Pro.9:10 (דַּעַת), 2Ma.15:5, 4Ma.8:18 * ;]
purpose, will: Act.27:43, Rom.9:19, 1Pe.4:3.†
SYN.: θέλημα. (AS)

G1014.d:
βούλομαι,
[in LXX for חפץ, אבה, יעץ, etc. ;]
to will, wish, desire, purpose, be minded, implying more strongly than θέλω (which see), the deliberate exercise of volition (see Hort on Jas.1:18): with inf. (M, Pr., 205; Bl., §69, 4), Mrk.15:15, Act.5:28, 33 12:4 15:37 17:20 18:15, 27 19:30 22:30 23:28 27:43 28:18, 2Co.1:15, 1Ti.6:9, Heb.6:17, II Jhn.12, 3Jo.10, Ju 5; with accusative, 2Co.1:17; with accusative and inf., Php.1:12, 1Ti.2:8 5:14, Tit.3:8, 2Pe.3:9; of the will making choice between alternatives, Mat.1:19 11:27, Luk.10:22, Act.25:20, 1Co.12:11, Jas.3:4 4:4; εἰ βούλει (cl., a courteous phrase = θέλεις, colloq.; Bl., §21, 8; LS, see word), Luk.22:42;…
G1014.o: middle voice of a primary verb;
G1014.k: be disposed, minded, intend, list, (be, of own) will (-ing)

G1015.d:
βουνός, -οῦ, ὁ (a Cyrenaїc word, Hdt., iv, 199),
[in LXX chiefly for גִּבְעָה ;]
a hill: Luk.3:5 (LXX) 23:30.†
(AS)

G1016.d:
βοῦς, βοός, ὁ, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for בָּקָר ;]
an ox, a cow: Luk.13:15 14:5, 19 Jhn.2:14, 15 1Co.9:9" (LXX), 1Ti.5:18.†
(AS)
G1016.s: an ox (as grazing), i.e. an animal of that species ("beef")
G1016.o: probably from the base of G1006 (βόσκω);

G1017.d:
βραβεῖον, -ου, τό
(βραβεύς, an umpire),
a prize in the games: 1Co.9:24; metaphorically, of the Christian's reward, Php.3:14.†
(AS)
G1017.s: an award (of arbitration), i.e. (specially) a prize in the public games

G1018.d:
βραβεύω
(βραβεύς, an umpire), [in LXX: Wis.10:12 * ;]
__(a) prop., to act as umpire; hence,
__(b) generally, to arbitrate, decide (Isocr., Dem.; Lft., Col., l.with; MM, see word): Col.3:15;
__(with) in some late writers, to direct, rule, control (so in Col., l.with, accusative to Thayer, see word, Meyer, in l.), (cf. κατα-βραβεύω).
† (AS)
G1018.s: to arbitrate, i.e. (genitive case) to govern (figuratively, prevail)

G1019.d:
βραδύνω
(βραδύς), [in LXX: Gen.43:10 (מההּ hith.), Deu.7:10, Isa.46:13 (אחר pi.), Si 32 (35):18 * ;]
__1. trans., to retard (Soph., Is, l.with).
__2. More frequently intrans., to be slow, to tarry: 1Ti.3:15, 2Pe.3:9.
† (AS)

G1020.o: from G1021 (βραδύς) and a prolonged form of G4126 (πλέω);

G1021.d:
βραδύς, -εῖα, -ύ,
slow: εἰς τὸ λαλῆσαι, Jas.1:19; metaphorically, of the understanding: β. τ. καρδίᾳ, assoc. with ἀνόητος, Luk.24:25.†
(AS)

G1022.d:
1. slowness , (Iliad by Homer), attic
2. of the mind, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G1023.d:
βραχίων, -ὀνος, ὁ,
[in LXX, β. Κυρίου, frequently for זְרוֹעַ יהוָֹה ;]
the arm; as in OT, β. Κυρίου, metaphorically, for the Divine power: Luk.1:51, Jhn.12:38" (LXX), Act.13:17.†
(AS)
G1023.o: properly, comparative of G1024 (βραχύς), but apparently in the sense of (to wield);

G1024.d:
βραχύς, -εῖα, -ύ,
[in LXX chiefly for מְעַט ;]
short;
__(a) of time; short, little: βραχύ, Act.5:34; μετὰ β., Luk.22:58; β. τι, a short time, Heb.2:7, 9 RV, mg.;
__(b) of distance: Act.27:28;
__(with) of quantity or value, little, few: Jhn.6:7, Heb.2:7, 9 RV, txt.; pl., διὰ βραχέων, in few words, Heb.13:22.
† (AS)
G1024.s: short (of time, place, quantity, or number)

G1025.d:
βρέφος, -ους, τό,
[in LXX: Sir.19:11, 1Ma.1:61, 2Ma.6:10, 3Ma.5:49, 4Ma.4:25 * ;]
__1. an unborn child: Luk.1:41, 44.
__2. a newborn child, a babe: Luk.2:12, 16 18:15, Act.7:19, 1Pe.2:2; ἀπὸ βρέφους, from infancy, 2Ti.3:15.
† (AS)
G1025.s: an infant (properly, unborn) literally or figuratively

G1026.d:
βρέχω,
[in LXX chiefly for מטר ;]
__1. to wet: Luk.7:38, 44.
__2. In late Gk. writers and vernac. = ὕειν, to send rain, to rain (Kennedy, Sources, 39, 155): Mat.5:45; trop., β. πῦρ κ. θεῖον, Luk.17:29; impers., βρέχει, it rains: Jas.5:17; with ὐετός as subj., Rev.11:6.
† (AS)

G1028.d:
βροχή, -ῆς, ἡ
(βρέχω), [in LXX: Psa.67 (68):9, 104 (105):32 (גֶּשֶׁם)* ;]
__1. = βροχετός, a wetting (in π., of irrigation in Egypt; Deiss., LAE, 77).
__2. As in MGr. (Kennedy, Sources, 153), = ὑετός, rain: Mat.7:25, 27.
† (AS)

G1029.d:
βρόχος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX: Pro.6:5 (יָד) 7:21 (חֵלֶק) 22:25 (מוֹקֵשׁ), 3Ma.4:8 * ;]
a noose, a slip-knot, a halter: metaphorically, a restraint (not, as AV, R, txt., a snare): 1Co.7:35.†
(AS)

G1030.d:
βρυγμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(βρύχω), [in LXX: Pro.19:12 (נַהַם), Sir.51:3 * ;]
a biting, a gnashing of teeth: Mat.8:12 13:42, 50 22:13 24:51 25:30, Luk.13:28.†
(AS)

G1031.d:
βρύχω (Attic, βρύκω),
[in LXX: Job.16:10(9), Psa.34 (35):16 36 (37):12 111 (112):10, La 2:16 (חרק)* ;]
__1. to bite or eat greedily.
__2. to gnash, grind, with the teeth: Act.7:54.
† (AS)
G1031.s: to grate the teeth (in pain or rage)

G1032.d:
βρύω, poët., late prose and vernac.,
to be full to bursting;
__1. of the earth producing vegetation.
__2. Of plants putting forth buds.
__3. Of springs, to gush with water: Jas.3:11.
† (AS)
G1032.s: to swell out, i.e. (by implication) to gush

G1033.d:
βρῶμα, -τος, τό (cf. βιβρώσκω),
[in LXX chiefly for אֹכֶל ;]
food: Rom.14:15, 20 1Co.8:8, 13 10:3; pl., Mat.14:15, Mrk.7:19, Luk.3:11 9:13, 1Co.6:13, 1Ti.4:3, Heb.9:10 13:9; trop., of spiritual food, Jhn.4:34, 1Co.3:2 (cf. βρῶσις).†
(AS)
G1033.s: food (literally or figuratively), especially (ceremonially) articles allowed or forbidden by the Jewish law

G1035.d:
βρῶσις, -εως, ἡ (cf. βιβρώσκω),
[in LXX chiefly for parts and derivatives of אכל ;]
__1. eating: β. καὶ πόσις, Rom.14:17, Col.2:16 (see Lft., ICC, in l.); with genitive obj., 1Co.8:4; metaphorically, corrosion, rust: Mat.6:19, 20.
__2. As also in cl. (Hom., al.) = βρῶμα, food: Jhn.6:27a, 2Co.9:10, Col.2:16 (EV, but see supr.). Heb.12:16; metaphorically, of spiritual nourishment, Jhn.4:32 6:27b, 55.†
(AS)
G1035.s: (abstractly) eating (literally or figuratively); by extension (concretely) food (literally or figuratively)

G1036.d:
βυθίζω
(βυθός), [in LXX: 2Ma.12:4 * ;]
trans., to cause to sink, to sink: metaphorically, εἰς ὄλεθρον, 1Ti.6:9; pass., to sink, intrans.: Luk.5:7.†
(AS)
G1036.s: to sink; by implication, to drown

G1037.d:
βυθός, -οῦ, ὁ,
[in LXX: Exo.15:5, Neh.9:11 (מְצוֹלָה), Psa.67 (68):22 68 (69):2, 15 106 (107):24 (מְצוּלָה)* ;]
__1. the bottom.
__2. the depth of the sea, the deep sea: 2Co.11:25.
† (AS)

G1038.d:
βυρσεύς, -έως, ὁ (βύρσα, a hide), late form for βυρσοδέψης,
a tanner: Act.9:43 10:6, 32.†
(AS)

G1039.d:
βύσσινος, -η, -ον
(βύσσος), [in LXX chiefly for שֵׁשׁ, בּוּץ, etc. ;]
made of βύσσος, fine linen: Rev.18:12, 16 19:8, 14.†
(AS)
G1039.s: made of linen (neuter a linen cloth)

G1040.d:
βύσσος, -οῦ, ἡ (cf. Heb. בּוּץ),
[in LXX chiefly for שֵׁשׁ, בּוּץ ;]
byssus, a fine species of flax, also the linen made from it: Luk.16:19.†
(AS)

G1041.d:
βωμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(βαίνω), [in LXX (Hex.) for מִזְבֵּחַ, in Proph., chiefly for בָּמָה ;]
__1. any raised place, a platform.
__2. an altar: Act.17:23 (cf. θυσιαστήριον and see DB, i, 75).
† (AS)
G1041.s: properly, a stand, i.e. (specially) an altar

G1042.d:
Γαββαθα (Rec. -θᾶ), ἡ, indecl.,
Gabbatha, the Greek transliteration of an uncertain Aramaic word (DB, see word; Dalman, Words, 7), used as the equivalent of λιθόστρωτον, stone pavement: Jhn.19:13.†
(AS)
G1042.s: the knoll; gabbatha, a vernacular term for the Roman tribunal in Jerusalem

G1043.d:
Γαβριήλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. גַּבְרִיאֵל, hero of God),
the archangel Gabriel: Luk.1:19, 26.†
(AS)

G1044.d:
γάγγραινα, -ης, ἡ,
a gangrene, an eating sore, which leads to mortification: 2Ti.2:17.†
(AS)

G1045.d:
Γάδ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. גָּד),
Gad (Gen.30:11 49:13, al.): Rev.7:5.†
(AS)

G1046.d:
Γαδαρηνός, -ή, -όν
(Γαδαρά, Gadara, the capital of Peræa),
Gadarene, of Gadara: Mat.8:28 (Rec. Γεργεσηνῶν), Mrk.5:1, Rec. (Edd., Γερασηνῶν), Luk.8:26, 37 Rec. (Edd., Γερασηνῶν).†
(AS)
G1046.s: a Gadarene or inhabitant of Gadara
G1046.o: from (a town east of the Jordan);

G1047.d:
γάζα, -ης, ἡ (a Persian word),
[in LXX for גִּנְזִין, II Est.5:17 6:1 7:20, 21, Est.4:7; גִּזְבָּר, II Est.7:21; Isa.39:2 * ;]
treasure: Act.8:27.†
(AS)

G1048.d:
Γάζα -ης, ἡ (Heb. עַזָּה),
Gaza, in OT, one of the five chief cities of the Philistines: Act.8:26.†
(AS)
G1048.s: Gazah (i.e. Azzah), a place in Palestine

G1049.d:
γαζο-φυλάκιον, -ου, τό
(γάζα, φυλακή), [in LXX chiefly for לִשְׁכָּה, נִשְׁכָּה (4Ki.23:11, al.), once for גְּנָזִים (Est.3:9); το͂ γ., τᾶ γ., of a temple treasury, Neh.10:37, 2Ma.3:6, al. ;]
treasury: also, apparently, the trumpet-shaped chests into which the peoples' temple-offerings were thrown (DB, iv, 96; DCG, ii, 748): Mrk.12:41, 43 Luk.21:1, Jhn.8:20.†
(AS)
G1049.s: a treasure-house, i.e. a court in the temple for the collection-boxes

G1050G.d:
Γαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Γάϊος, Rec.),
Gaius, the name of a Christian;
__1. of Macedonia: Act.19:29.
__2. Of Derbe: Act.20:4.
__3. Of Corinth: Rom.16:23, 1Co.1:14.
__4. The one to whom in Ep. Jo is addressed: III Jo 1.
† (AS)

G1050H.d:
Γαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Γάϊος, Rec.),
Gaius, the name of a Christian;
__1. of Macedonia: Act.19:29.
__2. Of Derbe: Act.20:4.
__3. Of Corinth: Rom.16:23, 1Co.1:14.
__4. The one to whom in Ep. Jo is addressed: III Jo 1.
† (AS)

G1050I.d:
Γαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Γάϊος, Rec.),
Gaius, the name of a Christian;
__1. of Macedonia: Act.19:29.
__2. Of Derbe: Act.20:4.
__3. Of Corinth: Rom.16:23, 1Co.1:14.
__4. The one to whom in Ep. Jo is addressed: III Jo 1.
† (AS)

G1050J.d:
Γαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Γάϊος, Rec.),
Gaius, the name of a Christian;
__1. of Macedonia: Act.19:29.
__2. Of Derbe: Act.20:4.
__3. Of Corinth: Rom.16:23, 1Co.1:14.
__4. The one to whom in Ep. Jo is addressed: III Jo 1.
† (AS)

G1051.d:
γάλα, -ακτος, τό
[in LXX for חלב ;]
milk: 1Co.9:7. Metaphorical, of elementary Christian teaching: 1Co.3:2, Heb.5:12, 13; τὸ λογικὸν ἄδολον γ., the rational (spiritual) genuine milk (see Hort, in l.), 1Pe.2:2 (in support of AV, milk of the word, see ICC, in l.).†
(AS)

G1052.d:
Γαλάτης, -ου, ὁ (originally syn. with cl. Κέλτης; cf. 1Ma.8:2, and see next word),
a Galatian: Gal.3:1.†
(AS)
G1052.s: a Galatian or inhabitant of Galatia

G1053.d:
Γαλατία, -ας, ἡ,
Galatia;
__1. a gentilic region in Asia Minor, settled by Gauls (iii/B.C).
__2. A Roman Province which included this region (DB, ii, 85ff.): 1Co.16:1, Gal.1:2, 2Ti.4:10 (T, Tr., mg., Γαλλίαν), 1Pe.1:1.
† (AS)

G1056G.d:
Γαλιλαία, -ας, ἡ (Heb. הַגָּלִיל, the circle, district),
Galilee, the name of the northern region of Palestine in NT times: Γ. τῶν ἐθνῶν, Mat.4:15 (LXX); θάλασσα τῆς Γ., Mat.15:29 (cf. Jhn.6:1).
(AS)
G1056G.s: Galilæa (i.e. the heathen circle), a region of Palestine

G1056H.d:
Γαλιλαία, -ας, ἡ (Heb. הַגָּלִיל, the circle, district),
Galilee, the name of the northern region of Palestine in NT times: Γ. τῶν ἐθνῶν, Mat.4:15 (LXX); θάλασσα τῆς Γ., Mat.15:29 (cf. Jhn.6:1).
(AS)
G1056H.s: Galilæa (i.e. the heathen circle), a region of Palestine

G1059.d:
Γαμαλιήλ, ὁ (Heb. גַּמְלִיאֵל),
Gamaliel the elder, a Pharisee and Doctor of the Law: Act.5:34 22:3.†
(AS)

G1060.d:
γαμέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: Est.10:3, 2Ma.14:25, 4Ma.16:9 * ;]
to marry;
__1. of the man, to marry, take to wife (ducere): absol., Mat.19:10 22:25, 30 24:38, Mrk.12:25, Luk.17:27, 20:34, 35, 1Co.7:28, 33; with accusative: Mat.5:32 19:9, Mrk.6:17 10:11, Luk.14:20 16:18.
__2. Of the woman,
__(a) mid. (and in late writers, pass.), to give oneself in marriage, marry (nubere): 1Co.7:39;
__(b) in Hellenistic (M, Pr., 159), act. (as of the man), to marry: absol., 1Co.7:28, 34 1Ti.5:11, 14. with accusative, Mrk.10:12.
__3. Of both sexes: absol., 1Ti.4:3, 1Co.7:9, 10 36.
† (AS)

G1061.d:
γαμίζω
(γάμος),
to give in marriage, a daughter: 1Co.7:38. Pass., Mat.22:30 24:38, Mrk.12:25, Luk.17:27 20:35 (WH, mg., γαμίσκονται; cf. γαμίζω).†
(AS)
G1061.s: to espouse (a daughter to a husband)

G1062.d:
γάμος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX for מִשְׁתֶּה ;]
__1. a wedding, esp. a wedding-feast: Mat.22:8, 10 11, 12, Jhn.2:1-3, Rev.19:7, 9; pl. (Field, Notes, 16), Mat.22:2-4, 9 25:10, Luk.12:36 14:8.
__2. marriage: Heb.13:4 (Cremer, 666).
† (AS)

G1063.d:
γάρ,
co-ordinating particle, contr. of γε ἄρα,
verily then, hence, in truth, indeed, yea, then, why, and when giving a reason or explanation, for, the usage in NT being in general accord with that of cl.;
__1. explicative and epexegetic: Mat.4:18 19:12, Mrk.1:16 5:42 16:4, Luk.11:3o, Rom.7:1, 1Co.16:5, al.
__2. Conclusive, in questions, answers and exclamations: Mat.9:5 27:23, Luk.9:25 22:27, Jhn.9:30, Act.8:31 16:37 19:35, Rom.15:26, 1Co.9:10, Php.1:18 (Ellic., in l.), 1Th.2:20, al.
__3. Causal: Mat.1:21 2:2, 5, 6, 3:23, Mrk.1:22, 9:6, Luk.1:15, 18, Jhn.2:25, Act.2:25, Rom.1:9, 11, 1Co.11:5, Rev.1:3, al.;…
G1063.s: properly, assigning a reason (used in argument, explanation or intensification; often with other particles)
G1063.k: and, as, because (that), but, even, for, indeed, no doubt, seeing, then, therefore, verily, what, why, yet

G1064.d:
γαστήρͅ, -τρός, ἡ,
[in LXX for בֶּטֶן, ἐν γ. ἔχειν for הרה, ἐν γ. λαμβάνειν for חרה ;]
__1. the belly: metaphorically, a glutton, Tit.1:12.
__2. the womb: ἐν γ. ἔχειν, to be with child, Mat.1:18, 23" (LXX) 24:19, Mrk.13:17, Luk.21:23, 1Th.5:3, Rev.12:2; εν γ. συλλαμβ., to conceive, Luk.1:31.
† (AS)
G1064.s: the stomach; by analogy, the matrix; figuratively, a gourmand

G1065.d:
γε, enclitic postpositive particle, rarer in κοινή than in cl., giving special prominence to the word to which it is attached, distinguishing it as the least or the most important (Thayer, see word),
indeed, at least, even (but not always translatable into English);
__1. used alone: Luk.11:8 18:5 Rom.8:32.
__2. More frequently with other particles: αλλά γε, Luk.24:21, 1Co.9:2; ἄρα γε, Mat.7:20 17:26, Act.17:27; ἆρά γε, Act.8:30; εἴ γε (Rec. εἴγε), 2Co.5:3, Gal.3:4, Eph.3:2 4:21, Col.1:23 (see Meyer, Ellic., on Ga, Eph, ll. with; Lft., on Ga, Col, ll. with); εἰ δὲ μήγε, following an affirmation, Mat.6:1, Luk.10:6 13:9; a negation, Mat.9:17,…
G1065.o: a primary particle of emphasis or qualification (often used with other particles prefixed)
G1065.k: and besides, doubtless, at least, yet

G1066.d:
Γεδεών, ὁ, indecl. in LXX and NT, in FlJ, Ant., see 6, 3 and 4 -ῶνος (Heb. גִּדְעוֹן),
Gideon (Jdg.6-8): Heb.11:32.†
(AS)

G1067.d:
γέεννα (γέενα, Mrk.9:45, Rec.), -ης, ἡ (perh. through Aram. גֵּיהִנָּם, from Heb. גֵּי הִנֹּם, Neh.11:30; גֵּי בֶּן־הִנֹּם, Jhn.18:16; גֵּי בּנֵי־הִנֹּם, 4Ki.23:10; valley of (the son, sons of) lamentation);
[in LXX the nearest approach to γ. is γαίεννα, Jos.18:16 (Γαὶ Ὀννόμ, A), elsewhere φάραγξ Ὀνόμ (Jos.15:8, al.), V. Swete on Mrk.9:43 ;]
Gehenna, a valley W. and S. of Jerusalem, which as the site of fire-worship from the time of Ahaz, was desecrated by Josiah and became a dumping-place for the offal of the city. Later, the name was used as a symbol of the place of future punishment, as in NT: Mat.5:29, ; 10:28, Mrk.9:43, 45 47, Luk.12:5, Jas.3:6; γ. τ.…
G1067.s: valley of (the son of) Hinnom; ge-henna (or Ge-Hinnom), a valley of Jerusalem, used (figuratively) as a name for the place (or state) of everlasting punishment

G1068.d:
Γεθσημασεί (Rec. -νῆ, LTr. -νεῖ) indecl. (Heb. גֵּת שְׁמָנִי, oil-press),
Gethsemane: called in Jhn.18:1 a κῆπος, but named only in Mat.26:36, Mrk.14:32.†
(AS)
G1068.s: oil-press; Gethsemane, a garden near Jerusalem
G1068.o: of Chaldee origin (compare H01660 and H08081);

G1069.d:
γείτων, -ονος, ὁ, ἡ
(γῆ), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁכֵן ;]
a neighbour: Luk.14:12 15:6, 9 Jhn.9:8.†
(AS)
G1069.s: a neighbour (as adjoining one's ground); by implication, a friend

G1070.d:
γελάω, -ῶ,
[in LXX chiefly for צחק, שׂחק ;]
to laugh: Luk.6:25; fut., γελάσω) (M, Pr., 154), ib. 21 (cf. κατα-γελάω).†
(AS)
G1070.s: to laugh (as a sign of joy or satisfaction)

G1071.d:
γέλως, -ωτος, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for שְׂחוֹק ;]
laughter: Jas.4:9.†
(AS)

G1072.d:
γεμίζω
(γέμω), [in LXX: Gen.45:17 (טען), 3Ma.5:47, 4Ma.3:14 * ;]
to fill;
__1. properly, of a ship (Thuc, al.): Mrk.4:37 (pass.).
__2. In late writers, generally (MGr., see Kennedy, Sources, 155), with accusative, before genitive, Mrk.15:36, Jhn.2:7 6:13, Rev.15:8; ἀπό, Luk.15:16, Rec. WH, mg.; ἐκ, Luk.15:16, WH, Rev.8:5. Pass., absol.: Luk.14:23.
† (AS)

G1073.d:
γέμω (used only in present and impf.),
[in LXX for מלא, נשׂא ;]
to be full;
__1. properly, of a ship (Xen.).
__2. Generally (Plat., al.),
__(a) with genitive of thing(s): Mat.23:27, Luk.11:39, Rom.3:14" (LXX), Rev.4:6, 8 5:8 15:7 17:3 (Rec.) 4 21:9
__(b) before ἐκ: Mat.23:25;
__(with) with accusative of thing(s) (called a solecism in WM, 251; Bl., §36, 4), as in later Gk. from Byz. to Mod. times (Jannaris, Gr., 1319): Rev.17:3.
† (AS)
G1073.s: to swell out, i.e. be full

G1074.d:
γενεά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(γίγνομαι), [in LXX chiefly for דּוֹר, דֹּר (Cremer, 148) ;]
__1. race, stock, family (in NT, γέννημα, which see).
__2. generation;
__(a) of the contemporary members of a family: pl., Mat.1:17 (cf. Gen.31:3, מוֹלֶדֶת); metaphorically, of those alike in character, in bad sense, Mat.17:17, Mrk.9:19, Luk.9:41 16:8, Act.2:40;
__(b) of all the people of a given period: Mat.24:34, Mrk.13:30, Luk.21:32, Php.2:15; pl., Luk.1:48; esp. of the Jewish people, Mat.11:16 12:39, 41 42, 45 16:4 23:36, Mrk.8:12, 38 Luk.7:31 11:29, 30-32, 50, 51 17:25, Act.13:36, Heb.3:10" (LXX) ; τὴν γ. αὐτοῦ τίς διηγήσεται, Act.8:33 (LXX);
…
G1074.s: a generation; by implication, an age (the period or the persons)

G1075.d:
γενεαλογέω, -ῶ
(γενεά, λέγω), [in LXX: 1Ch.5:1 (יחשׁ)* ;]
to trace ancestry, reckon genealogy; pass., before ἐκ: Heb.7:6.†
(AS)
G1075.s: to reckon by generations, i.e. trace in genealogy

G1076.d:
γενεαλογία, -ας, ἡ (see previous word);
__1. the making of a pedigree.
__2. a genealogy: pl., 1Ti.1:4, Tit.3:9 (see CGT, in l., and ib. Intr., xlix ff.; DB, ii, p. 141).
† (AS)

G1077.d:
γενέσια, -ων, τά, neut. pl. of adj. -ιος, -ον, relating to birth (γένεσις);
__1. in Attic Gk., a commemoration of the dead.
__2. In late Gk., a birthday feast (= cl. γενέθλια; so in π., see MM, Exp., x; cf. also Ῥutherford, NPhr., 184): Mat.14:6, Mrk.6:21.
† (AS)
G1077.o: neuter plural of a derivative of G1078 (γένεσις);

G1078.d:
γένεσις, -εως, ἡ
(γίγνομαι), [in LXX chiefly for תּוֹלֵדֹת ;]
__1. origin, lineage: βίβλος γενέσεως (as in Gen.2:4a 5:1), Mat.1:1.
__2. birth: Mat.1:18, Luk.1:14 (Rec. γέννησις); πρόσωπον τῆς γ., face of his birth ("what God made him to be," Hort., in l.), Jas.1:23; ὁ τροχὸς τῆς γ., the wheel (course) of birth or creation ("the wheel of man's nature according to its original Divine purpose," Hort), Jas.3:6.
† (AS)

G1079.d:
γενετή, -ῆς, ἡ = γενεή, Ion. for γενεά,
[in LXX: Lev.25:47 (עֵקֶר מִשְׁפָּחָו), Est.4:17 * ;]
birth: ἐκ γ., Jhn.9:1.†
(AS)
G1079.o: feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of G1074 (γενεά);

G1080.d:
γεννάω, -ῶ
(γέννα, poët. for γένος), [in LXX chiefly for ילד ;]
__1. of the father, to beget: with accusative, Mat.1:1-16, Act.7:8, 29; before ἐκ, Mat.1:3, 5, 6.
__2. Of the mother, to bring forth, bear: Luk.1:13, 57 23:29, Jhn.16:21; εἰς δουλείαν, Gal.4:24. Pass.
__(1) to be begotten: Mat.1:20;
__(2) to be born: Mat.2:1, 4 19:12 26:24, Mrk.14:21, Luk.1:35, Jhn.3:4, Act.7:20, Rom.9:11, Heb.11:23; before εἰς, Jhn.16:21 18:37, 2Pe.2:12; ἐν, Act.2:8 22:3, (ἁμαρτίαις), Jhn.9:34; ἀπό, Heb.11:12 (WH, mg., ἐγεν-); ἐκ, Jhn.1:13 3:6 8:41; with adj., τυφλὸς γ., Jhn.9:2; [Ῥωμαῖος ], Act.22:28; κατὰ σάρκα: κ. πνεῦμα: Gal.4:29. Metaphorical;…
G1080.s: to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother); figuratively, to regenerate
G1080.k: bear, beget, be born, bring forth, conceive, be delivered of, gender, make, spring

G1081G.d:
γέννημα, -τος, τό
(γεννάω), [in LXX chiefly for תְּבוּאָה ;]
offspring of men or animals: ἐχιδνῶν, Mat.3:7 12:34 23:33, Luk.3:7 (and elsewhere in Rec. for γένημα, which see).†
(AS)
G1081G.s: offspring; by analogy, produce (literally or figuratively)

G1082.d:
Γεννησαρέτ (Rec. Γενησ-, Mk, l.with; Targ. גְּנֵיסַר),
[in LXX: Γεννησάρ (as in some MSS. Mt, Mk), 1Ma.11:67 * ;]
Gennesaret, a fertile plain on W. shore of the Sea of Galilee; ἡ γῆ, Mat.14:34, Mrk.6:53; ἡ λίμνη (יָם כִּנֶּרֶת, Num.34:11, elsewhere ἡ θάλασσα τ. Γαλιλαίας, Mrk.1:16; ἡ θ. τ. Τιβεριάδος, Jhn.6:1), Luk.5:1.†
(AS)
G1082.s: Gennesaret (i.e. Kinnereth), a lake and plain in Palestine

G1083.d:
γέννησις, -εως, ἡ,
[in LXX: 1Ch.4:8 (מִשְׁפָּחָה), Ecc.7:2 (ילד ni.; γένεσις, Aא), Wis.3:13 א 1 (γένεσις, ABא 2), Sir.22:3 * ;]
__1. begetting.
__2. birth: Mat.1:18, Luk.1:14, Rec.
† (AS)

G1084.d:
γεννητός, -ή -όν
(γεννάω), [in LXX: Job.11:2, 12 14:1 15:14 25:4 (ילד)* ;]
begotten, born: pl., γ. γυναικῶν (cf. יְלוּד אִשָּׁה, Job.14:1), periphrasis for mankind, Mat.11:11, Luk.7:28 (Cremer, 147).
(AS)

G1085G.d:
γένος, -ους, τό
(γίγνομαι), [in LXX for עַם, מִין, זֶרַע, etc. ;]
__1. family: Act.4:6 7:13 13:26.
__2. offspring: Act.17:28, 29 Rev.22:16.
__3. race, nation; Mrk.7:28, Act.4:36 7:19 18:2, 24, 2Co.11:26, Php.3:5, Gal.1:14, 1Pe.2:9.
__4. kind, sort, class: Mat.13:47 17:21, Rec., Mrk.9:29, 1Co.12:10, 28 14:10.
† (AS)
G1085G.s: "kin" (abstract or concrete, literal or figurative, individual or collective)
G1085G.k: born, country(-man), diversity, generation, kind(-red), nation, offspring, stock

G1085H.d:
γένος, -ους, τό
(γίγνομαι), [in LXX for עַם, מִין, זֶרַע, etc. ;]
__1. family: Act.4:6 7:13 13:26.
__2. offspring: Act.17:28, 29 Rev.22:16.
__3. race, nation; Mrk.7:28, Act.4:36 7:19 18:2, 24, 2Co.11:26, Php.3:5, Gal.1:14, 1Pe.2:9.
__4. kind, sort, class: Mat.13:47 17:21, Rec., Mrk.9:29, 1Co.12:10, 28 14:10.
† (AS)
G1085H.s: "kin" (abstract or concrete, literal or figurative, individual or collective)
G1085H.k: born, country(-man), diversity, generation, kind(-red), nation, offspring, stock

G1086G.d:
Γεργασηνός, -ή, -όν,
Gerasene, of Gerasa, not the G. of Decapolis, 30 m. S.E. of the Lake, but a Gerasa or Gergesa (perh. the mod. Kersa) on E. shore; as subst., pl. οἱ Γ., Mrk.5:1, Luk.8:26, 37 (Γεργεσηνῶν, RV, mg. 1; Γαδαρηνῶν, RV, mg. 2).†
(AS)
G1086G.s: a Gergesene (i.e. Girgashite) or one of the aborigines of Palestine

G1087.d:
γερουσία, -ας, ἡ
(γέρων), [in LXX (Hex. only in OT) for זָקֵן ;]
a council of elders, senate; in NT, of the Sanhedrin (Cl. Rev., i, 43f.; DB, ext., 99): Act.5:21.†
(AS)
G1087.s: the eldership, i.e. (collectively) the Jewish Sanhedrin

G1088.d:
γέρων, -οντος, ὁ,
[in LXX for זָקֵן ;]
an old man: Jhn.3:4.†
(AS)

G1089.d:
γεύω, γεύομαι,
[in LXX chiefly for טעם ;]
to make to taste. Mid., to taste eat: absol., Act.10:10 20:11, Col.2:21; with genitive, Mat.27:34, Luk.14:24, Act.23:14; with accusative (not cl., but see Westc, Heb., l.with; M, Pr., 66, 245), Jhn.2:9. Metaphorical, Heb.6:4; ῥῆμα θεοῦ, Heb.6:5 (on case, see supr., and cf. Milligan, NTD, 68) θανάτου (cf. Talmudic טַעַם מִיתָה), Mat.16:28, Mrk.9:1, Luk.9:27, Jhn.8:52, Heb.2:9; before ὅτι, 1Pe.2:3 (Cremer, 148).†
(AS)
G1089.s: to taste; by implication, to eat; figuratively, to experience (good or ill)

G1090.d:
γεωργέω, -ῶ
(γεωργός), [in LXX: 1Ch.27:26 (עָשָׂה מְלֶאכֶת הַשָּׂדֶה), I Est.4:6, 1Ma.14:8 * ;]
to till the ground: pass., Heb.6:7.
(AS)

G1091.d:
γεώργιον, -ου, τό
(γεωργός), [in LXX, frequently in Pr., for שָׂדֶה, etc. ;]
__1. a field (Pro.24:5, 30, Strabo).
__2. cultivation, husbandry, tillage (Pro.6:7 9:12, Jer.28:23, Sir.27:6): 1Co.3:9.
† (AS)
G1091.o: neuter of a (presumed) derivative of G1092 (γεωργός);

G1092.d:
γεωργός, -οῦ, ὁ
(γῆ, ἔργω = ἔρδω, to do), [in LXX for אִכָּר, etc. ;]
__1. a husbandman: 2Ti.2:6, Jas.5:7.
__2. a vine-dresser (cf. ἀμπελουργός, Luk.13:7): Mat.21:33-35, 38, 40, 41, Mrk.12:1, 2 7, 9, Luk.20:9, 10 14, 16, Jhn.15:1.
† (AS)
G1092.o: from G1093 (γῆ) and the base of G2041 (ἔργον);

G1093G.d:
γῆ, γῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX for אֲדָמָה ,אֶרֶץ, etc. ;]
__1. the earth, world: Luk.21:35, Act.1:8, Heb.11:13, Rev.3:10, al.; opposite to οὐρανός, Mat.5:18 11:25, Mrk.13:27, al.
__2. land;
__(a) opposite to sea or water: Mrk.4:1, Luk.5:3, Jhn.6:21, al.;
__(b) as subject to cultivation: Mat.13:5, Mrk.4:8, Luk.13:7, Heb.6:7, al.;
__(with) the ground: Mat.10:29, Mrk.8:6, Luk.24:5, Jhn.8:6, al.;
__(d) a region, country: Luk.4:25, Rom.9:28, Jas.5:17; γῆ Ἰσραήλ, Mat.2:20, 21; Χαλδαίων, Act.7:4; ἡ Ἰουδαία γῆ, Jhn.3:22; with genitive of person(s), Act.7:3.
(AS)
G1093G.s: soil; by extension a region, or the solid part or the whole of the terrene globe (including the occupants in each application)

G1093H.d:
γῆ, γῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX for אֲדָמָה ,אֶרֶץ, etc. ;]
__1. the earth, world: Luk.21:35, Act.1:8, Heb.11:13, Rev.3:10, al.; opposite to οὐρανός, Mat.5:18 11:25, Mrk.13:27, al.
__2. land;
__(a) opposite to sea or water: Mrk.4:1, Luk.5:3, Jhn.6:21, al.;
__(b) as subject to cultivation: Mat.13:5, Mrk.4:8, Luk.13:7, Heb.6:7, al.;
__(with) the ground: Mat.10:29, Mrk.8:6, Luk.24:5, Jhn.8:6, al.;
__(d) a region, country: Luk.4:25, Rom.9:28, Jas.5:17; γῆ Ἰσραήλ, Mat.2:20, 21; Χαλδαίων, Act.7:4; ἡ Ἰουδαία γῆ, Jhn.3:22; with genitive of person(s), Act.7:3.
(AS)
G1093H.s: soil; by extension a region, or the solid part or the whole of the terrene globe (including the occupants in each application)

G1093I.d:
γῆ, γῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX for אֲדָמָה ,אֶרֶץ, etc. ;]
__1. the earth, world: Luk.21:35, Act.1:8, Heb.11:13, Rev.3:10, al.; opposite to οὐρανός, Mat.5:18 11:25, Mrk.13:27, al.
__2. land;
__(a) opposite to sea or water: Mrk.4:1, Luk.5:3, Jhn.6:21, al.;
__(b) as subject to cultivation: Mat.13:5, Mrk.4:8, Luk.13:7, Heb.6:7, al.;
__(with) the ground: Mat.10:29, Mrk.8:6, Luk.24:5, Jhn.8:6, al.;
__(d) a region, country: Luk.4:25, Rom.9:28, Jas.5:17; γῆ Ἰσραήλ, Mat.2:20, 21; Χαλδαίων, Act.7:4; ἡ Ἰουδαία γῆ, Jhn.3:22; with genitive of person(s), Act.7:3.
(AS)
G1093I.s: soil; by extension a region, or the solid part or the whole of the terrene globe (including the occupants in each application)

G1094.d:
γῆρας, Attic, genitive (-αος) -ως, dative ᾳ; Ion. and κοινή, -εος (-ους), dative -ει, τό,
[in LXX for שֵׂיבָה, etc. ;]
old age: ἐν γήρει, Luk.1:36.†
(AS)

G1095.d:
γηράσκω (also γηράω; γῆρας),
[in LXX chiefly for זקן ;]
to grow old: Jhn.21:18, Heb.8:13.†
SYN.: παλαιοῦμαι. (AS)

G1096.d:
γίνομαι, Ion. and κοινή for Att. γίγν- (M. Pr., 47; Bl., §6, 8 Mayser, 166 f.),
[in LXX chiefly for היה ;]
__1. of persons, things occurrences, to come into being, be born, arise, come on: Jhn.1:15 8:58, 1Co.15:37; a first appearance in public, Mrk.1:4, Jhn.1:6, al.; before ἐκ (of birth), Rom.1:3, Gal.4:4; διά, Jhn.1:3; βροντή, Jhn.12:29; σεισμός, Rev.6:12; γογγυσμός, Act.6:1; χαρά, Act.8:8, many other similar exx.; ἡμέρα, Luk.22:66, al.; ὀψέ, Mrk.11:19; πρωΐα, Mat.27:1; νύξ, Act.27:27.
__2. Of events, to come to pass, take place, happen: Mat.5:18, Mrk.5:14, Luk.1:20 2:15, Act.4:21, 2Ti.2:18, al.; μὴ γένοιτο [LXX for חָלִילָה, Jhn.22:29, al.],…
G1096.s: to cause to be ("gen"-erate), i.e. (reflexively) to become (come into being), used with great latitude (literal, figurative, intensive, etc.)
G1096.o: a prolongation and middle voice form of a primary verb;
G1096.k: arise, be assembled, be(-come, -fall, -have self), be brought (to pass), (be) come (to pass), continue, be divided, draw, be ended, fall, be finished, follow, be found, be fulfilled, + God forbid, grow, happen, have, be kept, be made, be married, be ordained to be, partake, pass, be performed, be published, require, seem, be showed, X soon as it was, sound, be taken, be turned, use, wax, will, would, be wrought

G1097.d:
γινώσκω (= γιγν-: see previous word. So also vulgar Attic, in Inscr., see Thumb, MGV, 207),
[in LXX chiefly for ידע ;]
to be taking in knowledge, come to know, recognize, perceive, understand; in past tenses to know, realize; pass., to become known: with accusative, Mat.22:18, Mrk.5:43, Col.4:8, 1Th.3:5, al. Pass., Mat.10:26, Php.4:5, al.; before ὅτι, Mat.21:45, Jhn.4:1, al.; τί, Mat.6:3; ἀπό, Mrk.15:45; ὅ, Rom.7:15; τ. λεγόμενα, Luk.18:34; τ. θέλημα, Luk.12:47; τ. καρδίας, Luk.16:15; with accusative of person(s), of recognition by God, 1Co.8:3, Gal.4:9; by Christ, neg., Mat.7:23; frequently of the knowledge of divine things, of God and Christ;…
G1097.s: to "know" (absolutely) in a great variety of applications and with many implications (as follow, with others not thus clearly expressed)
G1097.o: a prolonged form of a primary verb;
G1097.k: allow, be aware (of), feel, (have) know(-ledge), perceived, be resolved, can speak, be sure, understand

G1098.d:
γλεῦκος (-εος), -ους, τό,
[in LXX for יַיִן, Job.32:19 * ;]
must, sweet new wine (Arist.): Act.2:13.†
(AS)
G1098.s: sweet wine, i.e. (properly) must (fresh juice), but used of the more saccharine (and therefore highly inebriating) fermented wine

G1099.d:
γλυκύς, -εῖα, -ύ,
[in LXX chiefly for מָתוֹק ;]
Jas.3:11, 12; opposite to πικρόν, ἁλυκόν, Rev.10:9, 10.†
(AS)

G1100.d:
γλῶσσα, -ης, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for לָשׁוֹן ;]
__1. the tongue, as the organ of speech: Mrk.7:33, 35 Luk.1:64 16:24, Act.2:26" (LXX), Rom.3:13 (LXX) 14:11 (LXX), 1Co.14:9, Php.2:11, Jas.1:26 3:5, 6 8, 1Pe.3:10" (LXX), 1Jo.3:18, Rev.16:10; of a tongue-like object, Act.2:3.
__2. a tongue, language: Act.2:11; joined with φυλή, λαός, ἔθνος, frequently in pl., Rev.5:9 7:9 10:11 11:9 13:7 14:6 17:15; λαλεῖν ἑτέραις γ., Act.2:4; γ. λαλεῖν καιναῖς, WH, txt. (RV, mg., omit καιναῖς), Mrk.16:17; λαλεῖν γλώσσαις, γλώσσῃ (see ICC, ll. with; DB, iv, 793ff.), Mrk.16:17, WH, txt., R, mg., Act.10:46 19:6, 1Co.12:30 13:1 14:2, 4-6, 13, 18, 23, 27, 39;…
G1100.s: the tongue; by implication, a language (specially, one naturally unacquired)

G1101.d:
γλωσσόκομον, -ου, τό, vernac. form of cl. γλωσσοκομεῖον
(γλῶσσα, κομέω), [in LXX for אָרוֹן, 2Ki.6:11, 2Ch.24:8, 10 11 * ;]
__1. = cl. -εῖον (see supr.), a case for holding the reeds or tongues of musical instruments.
__2. As in LXX, π. (MM, see word), a box, chest: Jhn.12:6 13:29.
† (AS)
G1101.s: properly, a case (to keep mouthpieces of wind-instruments in) i.e. (by extension) a casket or (specially) purse
G1101.o: from G1100 (γλῶσσα) and the base of G2889 (κόσμος);

G1102.d:
γναφεύς, -έως, ὁ, Ion. and κοινή form of Att. κναφεύς
(κνάπτω, to card wool), [in LXX for כָּבַס, 4Ki.18:17, Isa.7:3 36:2 * ;]
a fuller, cloth-dresser: Mrk.9:3.†
(AS)
G1102.o: by variation for a derivative from (to tease cloth);

G1103.d:
γνήσιος, -α, -ον
(γίγνομαι), [in LXX: Sir.7:18, 3Ma.3:19 * ;]
__1. prop., lawfully begotten, born in wedlock (in π., γυνὴ γ., a lawful wife; MM, see word).
__2. true, genuine, sincere: Php.4:3, 1Ti.1:2, Tit.1:4; as subst., τὸ γ. = ἡ γνησιότης, sincerity, 2Co.8:8.
† (AS)

G1104.d:
γνησίως, adv.,
[in LXX: 2Ma.14:8, 3Ma.3:23 * ;]
sincerely, honourably: Phi 2:20 (for a parallel in π., see MM, see word).†
(AS)

G1105.d:
γνόφος (later form of δν-),
[in LXX for אָפֵל, עֲרָפֶל, etc. ;]
darkness, gloom (including "an element of tempest," Tr., Syn., §with): Heb.12:18.†
SYN.: ἀχλύς, ζόφος, σκότος (Tr., l.with; DB, i, 457a). (AS)

G1106.d:
γνώμη, -ης, ἡ
(γιγνώσκω), [in LXX: Da TH 2:15 (דָּת), Ps 82(83):3 (סוֹד), elsewhere, chiefly II Es, for טְעֵם ;]
__1. a means of knowing, a token (Theogn.).
__2. In Attic writers, the mind, its operations and results (see Edwards, Lex., App., A);
__(a) mind, understanding;
__(b) purpose, intention: Act.20:3;
__(with) judgment, opinion: 1Co.1:10, Rev.17:13;
__(d) counsel, advice: 1Co.7:25, 40 2Co.8:10, Phm 14;
__(e) royal purpose, decree (as in Da, I and II Es): Rev.17:17 (Cremer, 671).
† (AS)
G1106.s: cognition, i.e. (subjectively) opinion, or (objectively) resolve (counsel, consent, etc.)
G1106.k: advice, + agree, judgment, mind, purpose, will

G1107.d:
γνωρίζω
(γιγνώσκω), [in LXX chiefly for ידע hi. ;]
__1. as most commonly in cl., to come to know, discover, know: Php.1:22 (but cf. R, mg.).
__2. to make known: with accusative, Rom.9:22, 23; with accusative of thing(s) da.t. of person(s), Luk.2:15, Jhn.15:15 17:26, Act.2:28" (LXX), 1Co.15:1, 2Co.8:1, Gal.1:11, Eph.1:9 6:19, 21 Col.4:7, 9 2Pe.1:16; with dative, before ὅτι, 1Co.12:3; before τί, Col.1:27; περί, Luk.2:17. Pass., Act.7:13, Rom.16:26, Eph.3:3, 6 10, Php.4:6 (Cremer, 677; cf. ἀνα-, δια-γνωρίζω).
† (AS)
