Moses: Mat.8:4 17:3-4, al.; νόμος Μωυσέως, Luk.2:22 24:44, Jhn.7:23, Act.13:39 15:5 28:23, 1Co.9:9, Heb.10:28; by meton., of the books of Moses, Luk.16:29 24:27, Act.15:21, 2Co.3:15
(AS)
G3475.s: Moseus, Moses, or Mouses (i.e. Mosheh), the Hebrew lawgiver

G3478.d:
Ναζαρά
(Mat.4:13­ L, -άθ­Luk.4:16)
Ναζαρέθ (Mat.21:11, Act.10:38),
Ναζαρέτ (so always Rec.; WH, in foll, instances, where -έθ, T), ἡ,
indecl. (Semitic form uncertain),
Nazareth: Mat.2:23, Mrk.1:9, Luk.1:26 2:4, 39 2:51, Jhn.1:45-46.†
(AS)
G3478.s: Nazareth or Nazaret, a place in Palestine

G3479.d:
Ναζαρηνός, -οῦ, ὁ
(on the Semitic form, see Dalman, Gr., 141 n.)
a Nazarene: Mrk.1:24 10:47 14:67 16:6, Luk.4:34 24:19.†
(AS)
G3479.s: a Nazarene, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth

G3480.d:
Ναζωραῖος, -ου, ὁ
(= -ρηνός, which see),
a Nazarene: Mat.2:23 (LXX) Mat.26:71, Luk.18:37, Jhn.18:5, 7 19:19, Act.2:22 3:6 4:10 6:14 22:8 24:5 26:9.†
(AS)
G3480.s: a Nazoræan, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth; by extension, a Christian

G3482.d:
Ναθαναήλ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. נְתַנְאֵל),
Nathaniel, prob. to be identified with Bartholomew (which see): Jhn.1:45-49 21:2.†
(AS)
G3482.s: Nathanaël (i.e. Nathanel), an Israelite and Christian

G3483.d:
ναί
particle of affirmation,
yea, verily, even so; in answer to a question: Mat.9:28 13:51 17:25 21:16, Jhn.11:27 21:15-16, Act.5:8 22:27, Rom.3:29; before λέγω ὑμῖν, Mat.11:9, Luk.7:26; repeated for emphasis, ναὶ ναί (opposite to oὒ oὔ): Mat.5:37; ἤτω ὑμῶν τὸ ναὶ ναί, Jas.5:12; ν. καὶ οὔ, 2Co.1:18-19; ἵνα ᾖ . . . τὸ ναὶ ναί, 2Co.1:17; τὸ ν., 2Co.1:20; in assent to an assertion: Mat.15:27, Mrk.7:28, Rev.14:13 16:7; in confirmation of a previous assertion: Mat.11:26, Luk.10:21 11:51 12:5, Php.4:3, Phm 20; in solemn asseveration Rev.1:7 22:20.†
(AS)
G3483.o: a primary particle of strong affirmation;
G3483.k: even so, surely, truth, verily, yea, yes

G3484.d:
Ναίν (Rec. Ναΐν), ἡ, indecl. (Heb. נָאָה),
Nain, a village of Galilee: Luk.7:11.†
(AS)

G3485.d:
ναός, -οῦ, ὁ
(Att.. νεώς; ναίω, to inhabit), [in LXX (νεώς, 2Ma.6:2, al.) chiefly for הֵיכָל ;]
__1. a temple (Hom., Find., al.).
__2. The inmost part of a temple, the shrine (Hat., Xen., al.); in NT,
__(a) generally: pl., Act.17:24; of silver models of a heathen shrine, Act.19:24;
__(b) of the temple building proper, or sanctuary, at Jerusalem, as distinct from τ. ἱερόν (which see), the whole temple enclosure: Mat.23:16-17, 35 27:5, 40, Mrk.14:58 15:29 Jhn.2:19-20, Rev.11:2; (τοῦ) θεοῦ, Mat.26:61 27:51, Mrk.15:38, Luk.1:9, 21-22 23:45, 1Co.3:17, 2Co.6:16, 2Th.2:4, Rev.11:1; of the temple in the Apocal. visions, Rev.3:12 7:15 11:19 14:15,…

G3487.d:
νάρδος, -ου, ἡ
(Heb. נֵרְדְּ, both from Sanscrit narda, see Boisacq, see word), [in LXX: Sng.1:12 4:13-14 (נֵרְדְּ)* ;]
nard;
__(a) an Indian plant, the Nardostachys nardus jatamansi, used for the preparation of a fragrant ointment;
__(b) ointment of nard: Mrk.14:3, Jhn.12:3.†
(AS)

G3488.d:
the narcissus , (Homeric Hymns), etc.
From ναρκάω, because of its narcotic properties. (ML)
G3488.o: a flower of the same name, from (stupefaction, as a "narcotic");

G3489.d:
ναυαγέω, -ῶ
(ναῦς, + ἄγνυμι, to break)
to suffer shipwreck: 2Co.11:25; metaphorically, before περὶ τ. πίστιν, 1Ti.1:19.†
(AS)
G3489.s: to be shipwrecked (stranded, "navigate"), literally or figuratively
G3489.o: from a compound of G3491 (ναῦς) and G71 (ἄγω);

G3491.d:
ναῦς, νεώς accusative ναῦν, ἡ,
[in LXX for עָנִי, אֲנִיָּה ;]
a ship: Act.27:41 (elsewhere in NT always τ. πλοῖον; see M, Pro.25:1-28 f.; Bl., Gosp., 186 f.).†
(AS)

G3492.d:
ναύτης, -ου, ὁ
(ναῦς), [in Aq.: Eze.27:9; Sm.: Eze.27:29 * ;]
a seaman, sailor: Act.27:27, 30, Rev.18:17.†
(AS)

G3494.d:
νεανίας, -ου, ὁ
(νεάν = νέος) [in LXX for נַעַר, בָּחוּר ;]
a young man: Act.7:58 20:9 23:17-18.†
(AS)
G3494.s: a youth (up to about forty years)

G3495.d:
νεανίσκος, -ου, ὁ
(dimin. of νεανίας) [in LXX chiefly for נַעַר, also for בָּחוּר, etc. ;]
a young man, youth: Mat.19:20, 22, Mrk.14:51 16:5, Luk.7:14, Act.2:17" (LXX) Act.23:18, 22, 1Jn.2:13-14; of an attendant (cf. Gen.14:24, al.) : Act.5:10.†
(AS)

G3496.d:
Νεάπολις, -εως, ἡ
Rec. for Νέα Πόλις (WH), the more frequently form (LS, see word),
Neapolis, a maritime city of Macedonia: Act.16:11.†
(AS)
G3496.s: new town; Neapolis, a place in Macedonia

G3498.d:
νεκρός, -α, -ον,
[in LXX chiefly for מֵת ;]
dead,
__I. as adj.,
__1. prop.: Act.5:10 20:9, Jas.2:26, Rev.1:18, al.; ὡσεὶ ν., Mat.28:4, Mrk.9:26, Rev.1:17; of that which is subject to death, Rom.8:10.
__2. Metaphorical,
__(a) of persons: Luk.15:24, 32; of those immersed in worldly cares, Mat.8:22, Luk.9:60; of spiritual death, Jhn.5:25, Rom.6:13, Eph.5:14, Rev.3:1; τ. παραπτώμασιν, Eph.2:1, 5 Col.2:13; of the opposite condition, ν. τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, Rom.6:11;
__(b) of things regarded as inoperative, devoid of power: ἁμαρτία, Rom.7:8; πίστις, Jas.2:17, 26; ἔργα, Heb.6:1 9:14.
__II. As subst., νεκρός, ὁ (Hom., al.),…
G3498.s: dead (literally or figuratively; also as noun)

G3499.d:
νεκρόω, ῶ
(νεκρός),
to make dead, put to death; pass., to be dead: hyperbolically, of impotent age, Heb.11:12; σῶμα, Rom.4:19. Trop., of carnal impulses, τὰ μέλη, Col.3:5.†
(AS)

G3500.d:
νέκρωσις, -εως, ἡ
(νεκρόω),
__1. a putting to death.
__2. a state of death, death: Rom.4:19, 2Co.4:10 (see Deiss., LAE, 94).†
(AS)

G3501.d:
νέος, -α, -ον
[in LXX for נַעַר (Gen.37:2, Exo_33:11, al.), חָדָשׁ (Lev.23:16, Num.28:26, al.), etc.; compar. -ώτερος for קָטָן, צָעִיר, etc. ;]
__1. young, youthful: Tit.2:4.
__2. new (prop., in respect of time; see: καινός): οἶνος (cf. οἶ. καινός, Mat.26:20), Mat.9:17, Mrk.2:22, Luk.5:37-39; φύραμα (figuratively), 1Co.5:7; διαθήκη (cf. καινὴ δ., Heb.9:15), Heb.12:24; metaphorically, ἄνθρωπος (cf. καινὸς ἀ, Eph.2:15), Col.3:10.
__3. Compar., -ώτερος, -α, -ον, younger: Luk.15:12-13 22:26, Jhn.21:18; pl., οἱ ν., Act.5:6 (Rackham, in l), 1Ti.5:11, Tit.2:6; opposite to πρεσβύτεροι, 1Ti.5:1, 1Pe.5:5; αἱ ν., 1Ti.5:2 5:14.
__4. Νέα Πόλις,…
G3501.s: "new", i.e. (of persons) youthful, or (of things) fresh; figuratively, regenerate
G3501.o: including the comparative ; a primary word;

G3502.d:
νοσσός (νεοσσός, Rec., as in cl. Att.. -ττός; Phryn. rejects the dissyl. form), -οῦ, ὁ
(νόος), [in LXX chiefly for בֵּן ;]
a young bird: Luk.2:24 (LXX).†
(AS)

G3503.d:
νεότης, -ητος, ἡ
(νέος), [in LXX chiefly for נָעוּר ;]
youth: Mrk.10:20, Luk.18:21, Act.26:4, 1Ti.4:12.†
(AS)

G3504.d:
νεό-φυτος, -ον
(νέος, φύω) [in LXX: Job.14:9, Psa.144:12, Isa.5:7 (נֶטַע), Psa.128:3 (שְׁתִל)* ;]
newly planted (LXX). Metaphorical, as subst., ὁ ν., a new convert, neophyte, novice: 1Ti.3:6†
(AS)
G3504.s: newly planted, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert ("neophyte")
G3504.o: from G3501 (νέος) and a derivative of G5453 (φύω);

G3506.d:
νεύω
[in LXX: Pro.4:5 21:1 * ;]
to nod or beckon, as a sign : with dative of person(s) and inf., Jhn.13:24, Act.24:10 (cf. δια-, ἐκ-, ἐν-, ἐπι-, κατα-νεύω).†
(AS)

G3507.d:
νεφέλη, -ης, ἡ
(νέφος), [in LXX chiefly for עָנָן, also for עָב, etc. ;]
a cloud (single and specific as opposite to νεφος, a great indefinite mass of vapour): Mat.17:5 24:30 26:64, Mrk.9:7 13:26 14:62, Luk.9:34-35 12:54 21:37, Act.1:9, 1Th.4:17, Ju 12, Rev.1:7 10:1 11:12 14:14-16; of the pillar of cloud in the wilderness (Exo.14:19-20, Psa.105:39, al.): 1Co.10:1-2.†
(AS)

G3508.d:
Νεφθαλείμ
(-λίμ, WH in Re, l.with), ὁ
indecl. (Heb. נַפְתָּלִי)
Naphtali: Mat.4:13, 15" (LXX) Rev.7:6.†
(AS)
G3508.s: Nephthaleim (i.e. Naphthali), a tribe in Palestine

G3509.d:
νέφος, -ους, τό
[in LXX for עָב, שַׁחַק, עָנַן ;]
a mass of clouds, a cloud (cf. νεφέλη); metaphorically as in Hom., Hdt., al.), of a dense throng: Heb.12:1.†
(AS)

G3510.d:
νεφρός, -οῦ, ὁ
[in LXX for כִּלְיָה, Exo.29:13, al.; metaphorically, Psa.7:9 16:7 26:2, Wis.1:6, al. ;]
a kidney; pl., the kidneys, reins; metaphorically, of the will and affections: ν. καί καρδίαι (thoughts), Rev.2:23.†
(AS)
G3510.s: a kidney (plural), i.e. (figuratively) the inmost mind

G3511.d:
νεω-κόρος, -ου
a temple-keeper; as honorary title given to a city (see DB, i, 722 b) : Act.19:35.†
(AS)
G3511.s: a temple-servant, i.e. (by implication) a votary
G3511.o: from a form of G3485 (ναός) and (to sweep);

G3512.d:
νεωτερικός, -ή, -όν
(νεώτερος), [in LXX: 3Ma.4:8 * ;]
= νεανικός,
youthful, esp. of qualities: ἐπιθυμίαι, 2Ti.2:22 (Polyb.).†
(AS)
G3512.s: appertaining to younger persons, i.e. juvenile

G3513.d:
νή
particle of affirmation employed in oaths, [in LXX: see τ. ὑγίειαν, Gen.42:15-16 (חַי) * ;]
by: with accusative, 1Co.15:31.†
(AS)
G3513.s: a particle of attestation (accompanied by the object invoked or appealed to in confirmation); as sure as
G3513.o: probably an intensive form of G3483 (ναί);

G3514.d:
νήθω
[in LXX for טָוָה, שָׁזַר hoph., Exo.26:31 35:25, al. ;]
to spin: Mat.6:28, Luk.12:27.†
(AS)

G3515.s: to act as a babe, i.e. (figuratively) innocently

G3516.d:
νήπιος, -α, -ον
[in LXX chiefly for עוֹלֵל, also for פְּתִי, etc. ;]
infant; of children and minors: Mat.21:16 (LXX), 1Co.13:11, Gal.4:1 (see Lft., in l). Metaphorical, childish, unskilled, simple (Psa.19:8, Pro.1:32 al.): Mat.11:25, Luk.10:21, Rom.2:20, Gal.4:3, Eph.4:14, 1Th.2:7 (WH, fox ἤπιοι); opposite to τέλειος, Heb.5:13; ν. ἐν Χριστῷ, 1Co.3:1.†
(AS)
G3516.s: not speaking, i.e. an infant (minor); figuratively, a simple-minded person, an immature Christian
G3516.o: from an obsolete particle (implying negation) and G2031 (ἔπος);

G3517.d: Nereus , a sea-god, son of Πόντος (the sea) , father of the Nereids, (Hesiod) (ML)
G3517.o: apparently from a derivative of the base of G3491 (ναῦς) (meaning wet);

G3519.d:
νησίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of νῆσος), = νησίς (Hdt., Thuc., al.)
a small island: Act.27:16.†
(AS)

G3520.d:
νῆσος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for אִי ;]
an island: Act.13:6 27:26 28:1, 7 28:9, 11 Rev.1:9 6:14 16:20.†
(AS)
G3520.o: probably from the base of G3491 (ναῦς);

G3521.d:
νηστεία, -ας, ἡ
(νηστεύω), [in LXX for צוֹם ;]
fasting, a fast;
__(a) of voluntary abstinence from food: Mat.17:21 (WH, R, txt., om.), Mrk.9:29 (WH, txt., R, txt., om.), Luk.2:37, Act.14:23; of the Day of Atonement, Act.27:9;
__(b) of involuntary abstinence: 2Co.6:5 11:27.†
SYN.: ἀσιτία, q.v (AS)
G3521.s: abstinence (from lack of food, or voluntary and religious); specially, the fast of the Day of Atonement

G3522.d:
νηστεύω
(νῆστις), [in LXX for צוּם ;]
to fast (Arist., Aristoph., al.): Mat.4:2 6:16-18 9:14-15 Mrk.2:18-20, Luk.5:33-35 18:12, Act.13:2-3.†
(AS)

G3523.d:
νῆστις, -ιος, ὁ, ἡ
(νη-, neg. prefix, + ἐσθίω),
in cl., chiefly poët.,
[in LXX: Dan LXX 6:18 (19) (טְוָת)* ;]
not eating, fasting: Mat.15:32, Mrk.8:3.†
(AS)
G3523.s: not eating, i.e. abstinent from food (religiously)
G3523.o: from the inseparable negative particle (not) and G2068 (ἐσθίω);

G3524.d:
νηφάλιος (-λεος, Rec., in 1Ti, ll. with), -ον (in cl., -α, -ον),
(νήφω),
__1. in cl., of drink, not mixed with wine.
__2. In later writers (Plut., al.), of persons, sober, temperate: 1Ti.3:2 3:11, Tit.2:2.†
(AS)

G3525.d:
νήφω
to be sober, abstain from wine; metaphorically, of moral alertness, to be sober, calm, circumspect: 1Th.5:6 5:8, 2Ti.4:5 (see Ellic., in l), 1Pe.1:13 4:7 5:8 (cf. ἐκ-, ἐκ-νήφω, and see MM, xvii).†
SYN.: ἀγρυπνέω, γρηγορέω (AS)
G3525.s: to abstain from wine (keep sober), i.e. (figuratively) be discreet

G3528.d:
νικἀω, -ῶ
(νίκη), [in LXX: Psa.51:4 (זָכָה), Pro.6:25 frequently (חָמַד); in 4Mac ;]
to conquer, prevail: absol., of Christ, Rev.3:21 6:2; C. inf., Rev.5:5; of Christians, Rev.2:7, 11 2:17, 26 3:5, 12 3:21 21:7; before ἐκ (RV, come victorious from), Rev.15:2; as law-term (cl.), Rom.3:4 (LXX); with accusative of person(s), Luk.11:22, Rev.11:7 13:7 ([WH], R, mg., om.); of Christ, Jhn.16:33 (τ. κόσμον), Rev.17:14; of Christians, 1Jn.4:4; τ. πονηρόν, 1Jn.2:13-14; αὐτόν (ref. to ὁ κατήγωρ, 1Jn.2:10), Rev.12:11; with accusative of thing(s), τὸν κόσμον, Jhn.16:33, 1Jn.5:4-5; τὸ κακόν, Rom.12:21; pass., μὴ νικῶ ὑπὸ τ. κακοῦ, ib. (cf. ὑπερ-νικάω).†
(AS)
G3528.k: conquer, overcome, prevail, get the victory

G3529.s: conquest (abstractly), i.e. (figuratively) the means of success

G3530.s: victorious among his people; Nicodemus, an Israelite

G3531.s: a Nicolaite, i.e. adherent of Nicolaus

G3532.s: victorious over the people; Nicolaus, a heretic

G3533.d:
Νικόπολις, -εως, ἡ
Nicopolis, prob. the city of that name in Epirus (CGT, in l): Tit.3:12†
(AS)
G3533.s: victorious city; Nicopolis, a place in Macedonia

G3534.d:
νῖκος, -ους, τό late form of νίκη,
[in LXX: La 3:18 (נֶצַח), I Est.3:9, 2Ma.10:38, 4Ma.17:12; εἰς ν. (instead of εἰς τέλος, Job.14:20), 2Ki.2:26, Job.36:7, Amo.1:11 8:7, Jer.3:5, La 5:20 (נֶצַח, as נ֝ in Syr., = victory)* ;]
victory: Mat.12:20 (Isa.42:3, LXX ἀλήθεια), 1Co.15:54 (Isa.25:8, Aq., Th.), 1Co.15:55 (Hos.13:14, LXX δίκη), 1Co.15:57.†
(AS)

G3535.s: Ninevi (i.e. Nineveh), the capital of Assyria

G3536.s: a Ninevite, i.e. inhabitant of Nineveh

G3538.d:
νίπτω late form of νίζω,
[in LXX chiefly for רָחַץ ;]
to wash, usually of a part of the body: with accusative of person(s), Jhn.13:8; τ. πόδας, Jhn.13:5-6, 8 13:12, 14, 1Ti.5:10; mid., reflexive,
to wash oneself: Jhn.9:7, 11 9:15; τ. χεῖρας, Mat.15:2, Mrk.7:3; τ. πόδας, Jhn.13:10; τ. πρόσωπον, Mat.6:17 (in cl. Att.. prose, used only in compounds; cf. ἀπο-νίπτω).†
νίζω, see: νίπτω
SYN.: λούω (which see), πλύνω (AS)
G3538.s: to cleanse (especially the hands or the feet or the face); ceremonially, to perform ablution

G3539.d:
νοιεω νοέω, -ῶ
(νοῦς), [in LXX chiefly for בִּין, also for שָׂכַל hi., etc ;]
__1. to perceive with the mind, understand (for the phrase νοῶν κ. φρονῶν, in wills, see MM, xvii): absol., Mat.16:9, Mrk.8:17; with accusative, Eph.3:4, 1Ti.1:7; with dative instr., τ. καρδίᾳ, Jhn.12:40; pass., Rom.1:20; before ὅτι, Mat.15:17 16:11, Mrk.7:18; with accusative and inf., Heb.11:8.
__2. to think, consider: absol., Mat.24:15, Mrk.13:14, Eph.3:20; with accusative of thing(s), 2Ti.2:7
(cf. -εὐ, κατα-, μετα-, προ-, ὑπο-νοέω).†
(AS)
G3539.s: to exercise the mind (observe), i.e. (figuratively) to comprehend, heed

G3540.d:
νόημα, -τος, τό
(νοέω) [in LXX: Sir.21:11, Bar.2:8, 3Ma.5:30 * ;]
a thought, purpose, design: 2Co.2:11 10:5 11:3, Php.4:7. Meton., of the mind, 2Co.3:14 4:4.†
(AS)
G3540.s: a perception, i.e. purpose, or (by implication) the intellect, disposition, itself

G3541.d:
νόθος, -η, -ον
[in LXX: Wis.4:3 * ;]
a bastard, base born, i.e. born of a slave or concubine: Heb.12:8.†
(AS)

G3542.d:
νομή, -ῆς, ἡ
(νέμω, to pasture), [in LXX chiefly for מִרְעֶה, also for נָוֶה, etc. ;]
__1. a pasture, pasturage: figuratively, Jhn.10:9
__2. a grazing, feeding; metaphorically, of a spreading sore, 2Ti.2:17 (Polyb.).†
(AS)
G3542.s: pasture, i.e. (the act) feeding (figuratively, spreading of a gangrene), or (the food) pasturage
G3542.o: feminine from the same as G3551 (νόμος);

G3543.d:
νομίζω
(νόμος), [in LXX: Wis.13:2 17:3, Sir.29:4, 1-28; 2Ma.4:1-50, 4Ma.8:1-29 * ;]
__1. to practise, hold by custom: Act.16:13 (Rec., but see infr.).
__2. to deem, consider, suppose: Mat.5:17 10:34 20:10, Luk.2:44 3:23, Act.7:25 8:20 14:19 16:13, 27 17:29 21:29, 1Co.7:26 7:36, 1Ti.6:5.†
SYN.: ἡγέομαι, q.v (AS)
G3543.s: properly, to do by law (usage), i.e. to accustom (passively, be usual); by extension, to deem or regard

G3544.d:
νομικός, -ή, -όν
(νόμος), [in LXX: 4Ma.5:4 * ;]
__1. relating to law: μάχαι, Tit.3:9.
__2. learned in the law; as subst., ὁ ν. (EV, lawyer): Mat.22:35, Luk.10:25, Tit.3:13; pl., Luk.7:30 11:45-46, 52 14:3 (cf. MM, xvii).†
SYN.: γραμματεύς, q.v (AS)
G3544.s: according (or pertaining) to law, i.e. legal (ceremonially); as noun, an expert in the (Mosaic) law

G3545.s: legitimately (specially, agreeably to the rules of the lists)
G3545.o: adverb from a derivative of G3551 (νόμος);

G3546.d:
νόμισμα, -τος, τό
(νομίζω), [in LXX: Est.8:36 (דָּת), Neh.7:71 R (דַּרְכְּמוֹן), 1Ma.15:6 * ;]
__1. that which is established by usage, a custom.
__2. The current coin of a state: Mat.22:19.†
(AS)
G3546.s: what is reckoned as of value (after the Latin numisma), i.e. current coin

G3547.d:
νομο-διδάσκαλος, -ου, ὁ
a teacher of the law: Luk.5:17, Act.5:34, 1Ti.1:7 (NT and eccl. only; cf. νομοδείκτης, -διδάκτης, Plut.).†
SYN.: γραμματεύς, q.v (AS)
G3547.s: an expounder of the (Jewish) law, i.e. a Rabbi

G3548.s: legislation (specially, the institution of the Mosaic code)

G3549.d:
νομοθετέω, -ῶ
[in LXX for יָרָה hi. ;]
__1. intrans., to make laws; pass., to be furnished with laws: Heb.7:11.
__2. Trans., to ordain by law, enact: pass., Heb.8:6.†
(AS)
G3549.s: to legislate, i.e. (passively) to have (the Mosaic) enactments injoined, be sanctioned (by them)

G3550.d:
νομο-θέτης, -ου, ὁ
(νόμος, τίθημι), [in LXX: Psa.9:20 * ;]
a law­giver: Jas.4:12.†
(AS)
G3550.o: from G3551 (νόμος) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι);

G3551.d:
νόμος, -ου, ὁ
(νέμω, to deal out, distribute), [in LXX chiefly for תּוֹרָה, also for חֻקָּה, etc. ;]
that which is assigned, hence, usage, custom, then law; in NT (only in Mt, Jo, Ja, and the Lucan and Pauline bks.);
__1. of law in general: Rom.3:27 5:13b; pl., of divine laws, Heb.8:10 10:16; ὁ ν. τ. Χριστοῦ, Gal.6:2; (τ.) ἐλευθερίας, Jas.1:25 2:12; βασιλικιός (Hort., in l.; Deiss., LAE, 267:3), Jas.2:8.
__2. Of a force or influence impelling to action: Rom.7:21, 23a, 25 8:2.
__3. Of the Mosaic law: Mat.5:18, Luk.2:27, Jhn.1:17, Act.6:13, Rom.2:15, 1Co.9:8, 1Ti.1:8, Heb.7:19; al.; Μωυσέως, Luk.2:22, Jhn.7:23,…
G3551.s: law (through the idea of prescriptive usage), genitive case (regulation), specially, (of Moses (including the volume); also of the Gospel), or figuratively (a principle)
G3551.o: from a primary (to parcel out, especially food or grazing to animals);

G3552.d:
νοσέω, -ῶ
(νόσος), [in LXX (metaphorically): Wis.17:8 * ;]
to be sick: metaphorically, of mental ailment, before περί, 1Ti.6:4 (cf. Plat., Mor., 546 d).†
(AS)
G3552.s: to be sick, i.e. (by implication, of a diseased appetite) to hanker after (figuratively, to harp upon)

G3554.d:
νόσος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for חֲלִי, etc. ;]
disease, sickness: Mat.4:23-24 8:17 (Aq.) Mat.9:35 10:1, Mrk.1:34, Luk.4:40 6:17 7:21 9:1, Act.19:12.†
SYN.: see: ἀσθένεια (AS)
G3554.s: a malady (rarely figuratively, of moral disability)

G3555.d:
νοσσιά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(νοσσός),
late form of cl., νεοσσιά,
[in LXX chiefly for קֵן ;]
__1. a nest of birds.
__2. a brood of young birds: Luk.13:34.†
(AS)

G3556.d:
νοσσίον, -ου, τό dimin. of νοσσός, which see,
[in LXX: Psa.84:3 (אֶפְרֹחַ) * ;]
a young bird: Mat.23:37.†
(AS)

G3557.d:
νοσφίζω
(νόσφι, apart, aside), [in LXX: Jos.7:1 (לָקַח), 2Ma.4:32 * ;]
__1. in Hom., as depon., to turn away (from), abandon.
__2. After Hom., in act., to set apart, remove. Mid., to set apart for oneself, peculate, purloin: absol., Tit.2:10 (for ex. in π., see MM, xvii); before ἀπό, Act.5:2-3.†
(AS)
G3557.s: to sequestrate for oneself, i.e. embezzle

G3558G.d:
νότος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶב, also for דָּרוֹם, תֵּימָן and קָדִים ;]
__1. prop., the south wind: Luk.12:55, Act.27:13 28:13
__2. South: Luk.13:29, Rev.21:13
__3. the South, as a region (cf. נֶגֶב): Mat.12:42, Luk.11:31.†
(AS)
G3558G.s: the south(-west) wind; by extension, the southern quarter itself

G3558H.d:
νότος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶב, also for דָּרוֹם, תֵּימָן and קָדִים ;]
__1. prop., the south wind: Luk.12:55, Act.27:13 28:13
__2. South: Luk.13:29, Rev.21:13
__3. the South, as a region (cf. נֶגֶב): Mat.12:42, Luk.11:31.†
(AS)
G3558H.s: the south(-west) wind; by extension, the southern quarter itself

G3559.d:
νουθεσία, -ας ἡ
(νουθετέω),
= cl. νουθέτησις
[in LXX: Wis.6:6 * ;]
admonition: 1Co.10:11, Eph.6:4, Tit.3:10 (Aristoph., Diod., al.).†
(AS)
G3559.s: calling attention to, i.e. (by implication) mild rebuke or warning
G3559.o: from G3563 (νοῦς) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι);

G3560.d:
νουθετέω, -ῶ
(νοῦς, τίθημι, hence, put in mind), [in LXX: 1Ki.3:13 (כָּהָה pi.), Job.8:1-22 (יָסַר pi., בִּין), Wis.11:10 12:2, 26 * ;]
to admonish, exhort: with accusative of person(s), Act.20:31, Rom.15:14, 1Co.4:14, Col.1:28 3:16, 1Th.5:12 5:14, 2Th.3:15.†
(AS)
G3560.s: to put in mind, i.e. (by implication) to caution or reprove gently

G3561.d:
νεομηνία (Att.. contr., νουμ-, Rec.), -ας, ἡ
(νέος, μήν), [in LXX chiefly for חֹדֶשׁ ;]
new moon: of the Jewish festival, Col.2:16.†
(AS)
G3561.o: feminine of a compound of G3501 (νέος) and G3376 (μήν) (as noun by implication, of G2250 (ἡμέρα));

G3562.s: in a mind-having way, i.e. prudently
G3562.o: adverb from a comparative of the accusative case of G3563 (νοῦς) and G2192 (ἔχω);

G3563.d:
νοῦς
(contr. from νόος), ὁ, genitive, dative, νοός, νοΐ (late forms, = cl., νοῦ, νῷ; Bl., § 9, 3), accusative, νοῦν, [in LXX chiefly for לֵב, לֵבָב ;]
__1. prop., of the ruling faculty, mind, understanding, reason (see Lft., Notes, 88 f.; Vaughan on Rom.7:23): Luk.24:45, Rom.1:28 7:23 12:2 14:5, Eph.4:17, 23 Php.4:7, 2Th.2:2, 1Ti.6:5, 2Ti.3:8, Tit.1:15, Rev.13:18 17:9; ν. τ. σαρκός (ICC, in l), Col.2:18; opposite to σάρξ, Rom.7:25; to πνεῦμα, 1Co.14:14-15; to γλῶσσα, 1Co.14:19
__2. By meton., of an act of mind, a mind, thought, purpose: Rom.11:34 = 1Co.2:16" (LXX), 1Co.1:10.†
νόος, see: νοῦς
SYN.: see: πνεῦμα (AS)
G3563.s: the intellect, i.e. mind (divine or human; in thought, feeling, or will); by implication, meaning
G3563.o: probably from the base of G1097 (γινώσκω);

G3564.d:
Νυμφᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ (WH, R, mg., Νύμφα, which see),
Nymphas: Col.4:15, R, txt. (cf. ICC, Lft., in l).†
Νύμφα (Rec., R, txt., Νυμφᾶς, which see), -ης, ἡ, Nympha (see M, Pr., 48): Col.4:15, WH, R, mg.†
(AS)
G3564.o: probably contracted for a compound of G3565 (νύμφη) and G1435 (δῶρον);

G3565.d:
νύμφη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for כַּלָּה ;]
__1. cl., a bride, young wife, young woman: Mat.25:1, WH, mg., Jhn.3:29, Rev.18:23 21:2, 9 22:17.
__2. As frequently in LXX (Gen.38:11, al., for כַּלָּה;
__(a) bride;
__(b) daughter-in-law) and in MGr. (νύφφη, νύφη), a daughter-in-law: Mat.10:35, Luk.12:53.†
(AS)
G3565.s: compare Latin "nupto," to marry); a young married woman (as veiled), including a betrothed girl; by implication, a son's wife
G3565.o: from a primary but obsolete verb (to veil as a bride;

G3566.d:
νυμφίος, -ου, ὁ
(νύμφη), [in LXX for חָתָן ;]
a bridegroom: Mat.9:15 25:1, 5-6 25:10, Mrk.2:19-20, Luk.5:34-35, Jhn.2:9 3:29, Rev.18:23.†
(AS)

G3567.d:
νυμφών, -ῶνος, ὁ
(νύμφη), [in LXX: Tob.6:13,16* ;]
the bride-chamber (Heb. חֻפָּה, LXX, παστός, Psa.19:5, Jol.2:16): Mat.22:10 (WE; γάμος, RV); οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ ν. (cf. cl. νυμφαγωγός, νυμφευτής), the bridegroom's friends who have charge of the nuptial arrangements: Mat.9:15, Mrk.2:19, Luk.5:34.†
(AS)

G3568.d:
νῦν, adv.,
[in LXX chiefly for עַתָּה ;]
__1. prop., of time, now, i.e. at the present time: as opposite to past, Jhn.4:18, Act.7:52, Rom.13:11, 2Co.7:9, Col.1:24, al.; opposite to fut., Jhn.12:27, Rom.11:31, al.; with art., ὁ (ἡ, τὸ) and subst., the present: Rom.3:26, Gal.4:25, 1Ti.6:17, Tit.2:12, al.; απὸ τοῦ ν. (LXX for מֵעַתָּה), Luk.1:48, Act.18:6, al.; ἄχρι τοῦ ν., Rom.8:22, Php.1:5; ἕως τοῦ ν. (LXX for עַד עַתָּה), Mat.24:21, Mrk.13:19; τὰ ν., as regards the present, Act.5:38; with pret., just now, but now, Mat.26:65, Jhn.11:8 21:10; with fut., now, presently, Jhn.12:31, Act.20:22; so with praes., presently,…
G3568.s: "now" (as adverb of date, a transition or emphasis); also as noun or adjective present or immediate
G3568.o: a primary particle of present time;
G3568.k: henceforth, + hereafter, of late, soon, present, this (time)

G3569.s: the things now, i.e. (adverbially) at present
G3569.o: from neuter plural of G3588 (ὁ) and G3568 (νῦν);

G3570.d:
νῦνί an Attic strengthened form of νῦν
(in cl. always of time, and most often strictly of the pres.), [in LXX : Job.5:1-27, Psa.2:1-12, 1-12, 4Ma.4:1-26, Ep. Je* ;]
now;
__1. of time: with praes., Act.24:13, Rom.15:23, 25, 1Co.13:13, 2Co.8:11 8:22, Phm 9 11; with pf., Rom.3:21; with pret., Rom.6:22 11:30 (WH, mg.) Rom.7:6, Eph.2:13, Col.1:21 3:8; ἡ ν. ἀπολογία, Act.22:1.
__2. Of logical sequence (not so in cl.): Rom.7:17, 1Co.5:11 (νῦν, WH) 1Co.12:18 (νῦν, WH, txt.) 1Co.15:20, Heb.8:6 (νῦν, WH, txt.), Heb.9:26 (cf. WM, 24, 579n).†
(AS)
G3570.o: a prolonged form of G3568 (νῦν) for emphasis;

G3571.d:
νύξ genitive νυκτός, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for לַיִל ;]
night: Mat.12:40, Mrk.6:48, Jhn.13:30, al.; genitive temp. (of the time within which something happens; M, Pr., 73; B1., § 36, 13), νυκτός, by night, Mat.2:14, Jhn.3:2, 1Th.5:7, al.; ν. κ. ἡμέρας, Mrk.5:5, 1Th.2:9, al.; ἡμέρας κ. ν., Luk.18:7, Rev.4:8, al.; μέσης ν., Mat.25:6; dative, νυκτί, in ans. to the question, "when?" (rare in cl.; Hdt., Soph.), ταύτῃ τ. ν., Luk.12:20, al.; ἐκείνῃ Act.12:6; ἐπιούσῃ, Act.23:11; accusative durat. (Bl., § 34, 8; Kühner3, III, 314b), ν. κ. ἠμέραν, Luk.2:37 Act.20:31; τ. νύκτας, Luk.21:37; διὰ νυκτός (= cl. νυκτός; Bl., § 42, 1; 46, 7), Act.5:19 16:9 17:10 23:31; δι᾽ ὅλης…

G3572.d:
νύσσω
(Att.. -ττω), [in LXX: Sir.22:19, 3Ma.5:14 * ;]
to pierce: τ. πλευρὰν λόγχῃ, Jhn.19:34, [Mat.27:49], WH.†
(AS)

G3573.d:
νυστάζω
(cf. νεύω), [in LXX for נוּם, etc ;]
to nod in sleep, fall asleep: Mat.25:5. Metaphorical, of negligence or delay, ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν οὐ νυστάζει (cf. Psa.121:4, Isa.5:27) : 2Pe.2:3.†
(AS)
G3573.s: to nod, i.e. (by implication) to fall asleep; figuratively, to delay
G3573.o: from a presumed derivative of G3506 (νεύω);

G3574.d:
νυχθήμερος, -α, -ον
(νύξ, ἡμέρα, see B1., § 28, 4),
lasting a night and a day; as subst., (τὸ) ν., a night and a day: 2Co.11:25 (pl., Or. Sib., 8, 203).†
(AS)
G3574.s: a day-and-night, i.e. full day of twenty-four hours

G3575.d:
Νῶε
(as LXX, FlJ, who also gives Νώεος, Νῶχος), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נֹחַ)
Noah: Mat.24:37-38, Luk.3:36 17:26-27 Heb.11:7, 1Pe.3:20, 2Pe.2:5.†
(AS)

G3576.d:
νωθρός, -ά, -όν
[in LXX: Pro.22:29 (חָשֹׁךְ), Sir.4:29 11:12 * ;]
sluggish, slothful: Heb.5:11 6:12 (for similar usage in π., see MM, xvii).
SYN.: ἀργός (which see), βραδύς (AS)

G3577.d:
νῶτος, -ου, ὁ
in Att.. most frequently τὸ νῶτον, and in pl. always τὰ νῶτα, [in LXX, ὁ ν., pl., οἱ νῶτοι and τὰ νῶτα, chiefly for כָּתֵף, also for עֹרֶף, מֹתֶן ;]
/the back: Rom.11:10 (LXX).†
(AS)

G3578.d:
ξενία, -ας, ἡ
(ξένος), [in LXX: Sir.29:27 Bl* ;]
hospitality, enter­tainment: Phm 22 (cf. ICC, in l, but see infr.). By meton., a place of entertainment, a lodging-place: Act.28:23, and so perh. Phm 22 (Lft., in l, Phi., p. 9; but see supr., and cf. MM, xvii).†
(AS)
G3578.s: hospitality, i.e. (by implication) a place of entertainment

G3579.d:
ξενίζω
(ξένος), [in LXX: Est.3:13, Sir.29:25, 2Ma.9:6, 3Ma.7:3 * ;]
__1. to receive as a guest, entertain: with accusative of person(s), Act.10:23 28:7, Heb.13:2; pass., Act.10:6, 18 10:32 21:16.
__2. In late writers (Polyb., al.; 2Mac, l.with), to surprise, astonish by strangeness: Act.17:20; pass., 1Pe.4:4 4:12.†
(AS)
G3579.s: to be a host (passively, a guest); by implication, be (make, appear) strange

G3580.d:
ξενοδοχέω late Gk. for -κέω
(ξένος, δέχομαι),
to entertain strangers: 1Ti.5:10.†
(AS)
G3580.o: from a compound of G3581 (ξένος) and G1209 (δέχομαι);

G3581.d:
ξένος, -η, -ον
[in LXX chiefly for נׇכְרִי ;]
__(a) foreign, alien: δαιμόνια, Act.17:18; διδαχαί Heb.13:9;
__(b) with genitive of thing(s), strange to, estranged from, ignorant of: Eph.2:12;
__(with) strange, unusual: 1Pe.4:12.
As subst., ὁ ξ.,
__(a) a foreigner, stranger: Mat.25:35, 38 25:43-44 27:7, Act.17:21, 3Jn.5; ξέίνοι κ. τάροικοι (opposite to συμπολῖται, οίκεῖοι), Eph.2:19; ξ. καὶ παρεπίδημοι, Heb.11:13;
__(b) one of the parties bound by ties of hospitality;
__α the guest;
__β the host (= ξενοδόκος, Hom., Ii, xv, 532) : Rom.16:23.†
(AS)
G3581.s: foreign (literally, alien, or figuratively, novel); by implication, a guest or (vice-versa) entertainer

G3582.d:
ξέστης, -ου, ὁ
(a Sicilian corruption of Lat. sextarius), [in Al. : Lev.14:10 (לֹג, LXX κοτύλη)* ;]
__1. a sextarius (about a pint).
__2. In NT, a pitcher of wood or stone : Mrk.7:4.†
(AS)
G3582.s: by implication, (of friction) to boil or heat); a vessel (as fashioned or for cooking) (or perhaps by corruption from the Latin sextarius, the sixth of a modius, i.e. about a pint), i.e. (specially), a measure for liquids or solids, (by analogy, a pitcher)

G3583.d:
ξηραίνω
(ξηρός), [in LXX chiefly for יָבֵשׁ ;]
to dry up, parch, wither. with accusative, τ. χόρτον, Jas.1:11; pass., to become or be dry or withered. of plants, Mat.13:6 21:19-20, Mrk.4:6 11:20-21, Luk.8:6, Jhn.15:6, 1Pe.1:24; of ripened crops, Rev.14:15; of liquids, Mrk.5:20, Rev.16:12; of members of the body, to waste away, Mrk.3:1 (cf. 3Ki.13:4) Mrk.9:18.†
(AS)
G3583.s: to desiccate; by implication, to shrivel, to mature
G3583.k: dry up, pine away, be ripe, wither (away)

G3584.d:
ξηρός, -ά, -όν
[in LXX chiefly for יָבֵשׁ, its parts and deriva­tives, also for חָרָבָה, etc. ;]
dry: metaphorically (of a sinner), ξύλον ξ., Luk.23:31; of members of the body shrunken by disease, withered: Jhn.5:3; of the hand, Mat.12:10 Mrk.3:3, Luk.6:6, 8; of the dry land, ἡ ξηρά (sc. γῆ, cf. Gen.1:9-10; Jon.1:19, al.): Mat.23:15; γῆ, Heb.11:29.†
(AS)
G3584.s: arid; by implication, shrunken, earth (as opposed to water)
G3584.o: from the base of G3582 (ξέστης) (through the idea of scorching);

G3585.d:
ξύλινος, -η, -ον
(ξύλον) [in LXX chiefly for עֵץ ;]
wooden: 2Ti.2:20, Heb.9:20 (cf. Ep. Jer.4:1-31 ff).†
(AS)

G3586.d:
ξύλον, -ου, τό
[in LXX chiefly for עֵץ ;]
__1. wood: 1Co.3:12, Rev.18:12.
__2. a piece of wood, hence, anything made of wood, as,
__(a) a cudgel, staff: pl., Mat.26:47, 55, Mrk.14:43, 48, Luk.22:52;
__(b) stocks, for confining the feet (Job.33:11, סַד) : Act.16:24;
__(with) a beam to which malefactors were bound (late Gk.), in LXX, of a gibbet (Deu.21:22-23), in NT, of the Cross: Act.5:30 10:39 13:29, Gal.3:13, 1Pe.2:24.
__3. In late writers (see MM, xvii), a tree (Gen.1:29, Isa.14:8, al.) : Luk.23:31; ξ. τῆς ζωῆς, Rev.2:7 22:2, 14 22:19.†
(AS)
G3586.s: timber (as fuel or material); by implication, a stick, club or tree or other wooden article or substance
G3586.o: from another form of the base of G3582 (ξέστης);

G3587.d:
ξυράω, -ῶ
late form of ξυρέω (which see) : 1Co.11:6 (ξυρᾶσθαι, Rec. and Edd., but see: ξύρω).†
ξύρω, rare form of ξυρέω (Veitch, see word), aor. mid., ξύρασθαιι (Bl., § 24, see word; Zorell, see word, etc.) for -ᾶσθαι (Rec., Edd.) : 1Co.11:6.†
(AS)
G3587.o: from a derivative of the same as G3586 (ξύλον) (meaning a razor);

G3588.d:
ὁ, ἡ, τό,
the prepositive article (ἄρθρον προτακτικόν), originally a demonstr. pron. (so usually in Hom.), in general corresponding to the Eng. definite article.
__I. As demonstr. pron.
__1. As frequently in Hom., absol., he (she, it), his (etc.): Act.17:28 (quoted from the poet Aratus).
__2. Distributive, ὁ μὲν . . . ὁ δέ, the one . . . the other: 1Co.7:7, Gal.4:22; pl., Act.14:4, 17:32, Php.1:16, al.; οἱ μὲν . . . ἄλλοι δέ, Mat.16:14, Jhn.7:12; οἱ μεν̀ . . . ὁδέ, Heb.7:21, 23.
__3. In narration (without ὁ μὲν preceding), ὁ δέ, but he: Mat.2:14, Mrk.1:45, Luk.8:21, Jhn.9:38, al. mult.
__II. As prepositive article, the,…
G3588.s: the (sometimes to be supplied, at others omitted, in English idiom)
G3588.k: the, this, that, one, he, she, it, etc

G3589.d: eighty , Lat. octoginta, (Thucydides), etc.:—;ionic and doric ὀγδώκοντα, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G3590.d:
ὄγδοος, -η, -ον
the eighth. Luk.1:59, Act.7:3" (LXX), Rev.17:11 21:20; one of eight, with seven others (usually, in this sense, with αὐτός added, but cf. Plat., Legg., iii, 695 with; Plut., Pelop., 13; 2Ma.5:27): 2Pe.2:5.†
(AS)

G3591.d:
ὄγκος, -ου, ὁ
bulk, mass; metaphorically, an encumbrance: Heb.12:1.†
SYN.: βάρος, a weight; φορτίον, a burden, that which is borne (AS)
G3591.s: a mass (as bending or bulging by its load), i.e. burden (hindrance)
G3591.o: probably from the same as G43 (ἀγκάλη);

G3592.d:
ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε
(the old demonstr. pron., ὁ + the enclitic δε), = Lat. hicce, this (here),
referring prop, to what is present, can be seen or pointed out: of a person just named, τῇδε (= ταύτῃ), Luk.10:39; neut. pl., τάδε (λέγει), referring to words which follow (so in Att.., and see MM, xvii) : Act.21:11, Rev.2:1, 8 2:12, 18 3:1, 7 3:14; εἰς τήνδε τ. πόλιν (= Att.. τῇ καὶ τῇ, Plat., Legg., iv, 721 B), such and such a city, Jas.4:13.†
(AS)
G3592.s: the same, i.e. this or that one (plural these or those); often used as a personal pronoun

G3593.d:
ὁδεύω
(ὁδός), [in LXX : 3Ki.6:12 A (metaphorically, הָלַךְ), Tob.6:5, Wis.5:7 (figuratively)* ;]
to travel, journey: Luk.10:33 (cf.δι-, συν-οδεύω).†
(AS)

G3594.d:
ὁδηγέω, -ῶ,
(ὁδηγός) [in LXX chiefly for נוּחַ, also for דֶּרֶךְ hi., הָלַךְ hi., etc. ;]
to lead on one's way, to guide: with accusative of person(s), Mat.15:14, Luk.6:39; id. before ἐπί, Rev.7:17. Metaphorical, to guide, instruct, teach: Act.8:31; before εἰς τ. ἀλήθειαν (ἐν τ. ἀ., WH, mg.), Jhn.16:13 (cf. Psa.25:5).†
(AS)
G3594.s: to show the way (literally or figuratively (teach))

G3595.d:
ὁδηγός, -οῦ, ὁ
(ὁδός, ἡγέομαι) [in LXX : Est.8:1, Wis.7:15 18:3, 1Ma.4:2, 2Ma.5:15 * ;]
a leader on the way, a guide: Act.1:16. Fig., ὁ. τυφλῶν, Rom.2:19; pl., Mat.15:14 23:16, 24.†
(AS)

G3596.d:
ὁδοιπορέω, -ῶ
(ὁδοιπόρος, a traveller, Gen.37:25, al.),
to travel, journey: Act.10:9.†
(AS)
G3596.s: to be a wayfarer, i.e. travel
G3596.o: from a compound of G3598 (ὁδός) and G4198 (πορεύομαι);

G3597.d:
ὁδοιπορία, -ας, ἡ
(see supr.), [in LXX : Wis.13:18 18:3 19:5, 1Ma.6:41 * ;]
a journey. Jhn.4:6, 2Co.11:26.†
(AS)

G3598.d:
ὁδός, -οῦ, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly (very freq.) for דֶּרֶךְ ;]
__1. a way, path, road: Mat.2:12, Mrk.10:46, Luk.3:5 al.; κατὰ τὴν ὁ., Luk.10:4, al.; παρὰ τὴν ὁ., Mat.13:4, al.; with genitive of person(s), (subj.), τὴν ὁ. ἑτοιμάζειν (fig.), Mat.3:3, Mrk.1:3, al.; with genitive term. (obj.), ἐθνῶν, Mat.10:5; τ. ἁγίων (figuratively), Heb.9:8; accusative, ὁδόν, with force of prep. (like Heb. דֶּרֶךְ; Bl., §34, 8; 35, 5), ὁ. θαλάσσης, Mat.4:15 (LXX).
__2. A traveller's way, journey: ἐν τ. ὁ., Mat.5:25, Mrk.8:27, al.; ἐξ ὁ., Luk.11:6; εἰς ὁ., Mat.10:10; τ. ὁδὸν πορεύεσθαι, Act.8:39; ὁ. ἡμέρας, Luk.2:44; ὁδὸν ποιεῖν (= cl., ὁ. ποιεῖσθαι; V. Field, Notes, 25),…
G3598.s: a road; by implication, a progress (the route, act or distance); figuratively, a mode or means

G3599.d:
ὀδούς, -όντος, ὁ
[in LXX for שֵׁן ;]
a tooth: Mat.5:38, Mrk.9:18, Act.7:54; pl., Rev.9:8, ὁ βρυγμὸς (which see) τ. ὀδόντων, Mat.8:12 13:42, 50 22:13 24:51 25:30, Luk.13:28.†
(AS)
G3599.o: perhaps from the base of G2068 (ἐσθίω);

G3600.d:
ὀδυνάω, -ῶ
(ὀδύνη), [in LXX: Zec.9:5 (חוּל), Zec.12:10 (מָרַר hi.), La 1:13 (דָּוֶה), Wis.14:24, al. ;]
to cause pain or suffering; pass. and mid., to suffer pain, be tormented or greatly distressed: Luk.2:48 16:24-25 (ὀδυνᾶσαι, see M, Pr., 53 f.); before ἐπί, Act.20:38.†
(AS)

G3601.d:
ὀδύνη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX for יָגוֹן, מַר, etc. (26 words in all) ;]
pain, distress, of body or mind : Rom.9:2, 1Ti.6:10.†
(AS)

G3602.d:
ὀδυρμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(ὀδύρομαι, to lament), [in LXX : Jer.31:15 (תַּמְרוּר), 2Ma.11:6 * ;]
lamentation, mourning: Mat.2:18 (LXX), 2Co.7:7.†
(AS)
G3602.o: from a derivative of the base of G1416 (δύνω);

G3603.d:
1. as Substantive Verb, to be, to exist , οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ οὗτος ἀνήρ, οὐδ᾽ ἔσσεται (Odyssey by Homer); τεθνηῶτος, μηδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἐόντος (Odyssey by Homer); οὐκέτ᾽ ἔστι he is no more , (Euripides); θεοὶ αἰὲν ἐόντες (Iliad by Homer); ἐσσόμενοι posterity, (Iliad by Homer); ζώντων καὶ ὄντων Ἀθηναίων (Demosthenes Orator):—;so of cities, etc., ὄλωλεν, οὐδ᾽ ἔτ᾽ ἔστι Τροία (compare Troja fuit) , (Euripides)
2. of things, to be, exist , εἰ ἔστιν ἀληθέως [ ἡ τράπεζα] (Herdotus Historicus); ἕως ἂν ὁ πόλεμος ἦι so long as it last , (Thucydides)
3. to be , opposite to appearing to be , as esse to videri , τὸν ἐόντα λόγον the true story,…
G3603.o: from the neuter of G3739 (ὅς) and the third person singular present indicative of G1510 (εἰμί);
G3603.k: called, which is (make), that is (to say)

G3605.d:
ὄζω
[in LXX: Exo.8:14 (בָּאַשׁ)* ;]
to smell (i.e. emit a smell): Jhn.11:39.†
(AS)
G3605.o: a primary verb (in a strengthened form);

G3606.d:
ὅθεν
adv.,
whence;
__(a) of direction or source: Mat.12:44, Luk.11:24, Act.14:26 28:13; = ἐκεῖθεν ὅπου, Mat.25:24, 26 (cf. Thuc., i, 89, 3); ὅ. γινώσκομεν, 1Jn.2:18;
__(b) of cause, whence, wherefore: Mat.14:7, Act.26:19, Heb.2:17 3:1 7:25 8:3 9:18 11:19.†
(AS)
G3606.s: from which place or source or cause (adverb or conjunction)
G3606.o: from G3739 (ὅς) with the directive enclitic of source;

G3607.d:
ὀθόνη, -ης, ἡ
(of Semitic origin, cf. Heb. אֵטוּן, yarn)
__1. fine linen (Hom., al.).
__2. Later, a sheet or sail: Act.10:11 11:5.†
(AS)
G3607.s: a linen cloth, i.e. (especially) a sail

G3608.d:
ὀθόνιον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of ὀθόνη, which see), [in LXX: Jdg.14:13 (סָדִין), Hos.2:5, 9 (פִּשְׁתֶּה)* ;]
a piece of fine linen, a linen cloth; Luk.24:12 (WH, R, mg., om.), Jhn.19:40 20:5-7.†
(AS)
G3608.o: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3607 (ὀθόνη);

G3609.d:
οἰκεῖος, -α, -ον
(οἶκος), [in LXX for דּוֹד, שְׁאֵר, etc.; in Isa.58:7, οἰ. τοῦ σπέρματος for בָּשָׂר ;]
in or of the house (opposite to ξένος, ἀλλότριος);
__(a) of things; τὰ οἰ., household affairs or goods;
__(b) of persons, of the same family or kin; as subst., οἱ οἰ., kinsmen: 1Ti.5:8; with genitive of person(s), of the family of: metaphorically, τ. θεον, Eph.2:19; τ. πίστεως (Lft., in l), Gal.6:10.†
SYN,: συγγενής, ἴδιος (see Cremer, 446; Deiss., BS, 123)
(AS)
G3609.s: domestic, i.e. (as noun), a relative, adherent

G3610.d:
οἰκέτης, -ου, ὁ
(οἰκέω), [in LXX for עֶבֶד ;]
a house-servant: Luk.16:13, Rom.14:4; pl., Act.10:7, 1Pe.2:18 (In Plat., Hdt., Sir.4:30 6:11, the pl. includes all the inmates of the house, the familia, οἰκετεία.)†
SYN.. see: διάκονος (AS)
G3610.s: a fellow resident, i.e. menial domestic

G3611.d:
οἰκέω, -ῶ
(οἶκος), [in LXX chiefly for יָשַׁב ;]
__(a) trans., to inhabit: with accusative, 1Ti.6:16;
__(b) intrans., to dwell: before μετά (of married life), 1Co.7:12-13; metaphorically, before ἐν: ἀγαθόν, Rom.7:18; ἁμαρτία, Rom.7:20; πνεῦμα θεοῦ, Rom.8:9, 11, 1Co.3:16 (cf. ἐν-, κατ-, ἐν-κατ-, παρ-, περι-, συν-οικέω).†
(AS)
G3611.s: to occupy a house, i.e. reside (figuratively, inhabit, remain, inhere); by implication, to cohabit

G3612.d:
οἴκημα, -τος, τό
(οἰκέω), [in LXX: Eze.16:24 (גַב), Tob.2:4, Wis.13:15 * ;]
a dwelling. As a euphemism for other definite terms (e.g. brothel. Hdt., ii, 121; cf. Ez, l.with), a prison (Thus., iv, 47 f.); Act.12:7.†
(AS)

G3613.d:
οἰκητήριον, -ου, τό
(οἰκητήρ = οἰκήτωρ, an inhabitant), [in LXX: 2Ma.11:2, 3Ma.2:15 * ;]
a habitation: Ju 6; trop., 2Co.5:2.†
(AS)
G3613.o: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3611 (οἰκέω) (equivalent to G3612 (οἴκημα));

G3614G.d:
οἰκία, -ας, ἡ
(οἶκος), [in LXX chiefly (very freq.) for בַּיִת ;]
a house, dwelling: Mat.2:11 7:24-27, Mrk.1:29, al.; ἐν οἰκίᾳ (= cl. κατ ̓ οἰκίαν), at home, Luk.8:27; εἰς οἰ., II Jn 10; οἰ, with genitive of person(s), usually has the art. (Mat.8:14, al., but cf. οἶκος and see Bl., § 46, 9); ἡ οἰ. τ. πατρός μου, Jhn.14:2.
Metaphorical,
__(a) of the body as the dwelling of the soul: 2Co.5:1;
__(b) of property (as בַּיִת, Gen.45:18, LXX, τ. υπάρχοντα; 3Ki.13:8, LXX, οἶκος) = οἶκος (which see): Mrk.12:40, Luk.20:47;
__(with) of the inmates of the dwelling, the household: Mat.12:25; with genitive of person(s), Jhn.4:53, 1Co.16:15
…
G3614G.s: properly, residence (abstractly), but usually (concretely) an abode (literally or figuratively); by implication, a family (especially domestics)

G3614H.d:
οἰκία, -ας, ἡ
(οἶκος), [in LXX chiefly (very freq.) for בַּיִת ;]
a house, dwelling: Mat.2:11 7:24-27, Mrk.1:29, al.; ἐν οἰκίᾳ (= cl. κατ ̓ οἰκίαν), at home, Luk.8:27; εἰς οἰ., II Jn 10; οἰ, with genitive of person(s), usually has the art. (Mat.8:14, al., but cf. οἶκος and see Bl., § 46, 9); ἡ οἰ. τ. πατρός μου, Jhn.14:2.
Metaphorical,
__(a) of the body as the dwelling of the soul: 2Co.5:1;
__(b) of property (as בַּיִת, Gen.45:18, LXX, τ. υπάρχοντα; 3Ki.13:8, LXX, οἶκος) = οἶκος (which see): Mrk.12:40, Luk.20:47;
__(with) of the inmates of the dwelling, the household: Mat.12:25; with genitive of person(s), Jhn.4:53, 1Co.16:15
…
G3614H.s: properly, residence (abstractly), but usually (concretely) an abode (literally or figuratively); by implication, a family (especially domestics)

G3615.d:
οἰκιακός (in Plut., al., -ειακός), ή, όν
(οἰκία), = οἰκεῖος
belonging to the household, one's own: Mat.10:36; opposite to οἰκοδεσπότης, Mat.10:25.†
(AS)

G3616.s: to be the head of (i.e. rule) a family

G3617.d:
οἰκο-δεσπότης, -ου, ὁ
(οἶκος, δεσπότης),
the master of a house, a householder: Mat.10:25 13:27 20:11 24:43, Mrk.14:14, Luk.12:39 13:25 14:21; ἄνθρωπος οἰ., Mat.13:52 20:1 21:33; pleonast., oἰ. τ. οἰκίας, Luk.22:11 (see Bl., § 81, 4).†
(AS)
G3617.k: goodman (of the house), householder, master of the house

G3618.d:
οἰκοδομέω, -ῶ
(οἰκοδόμος), [in LXX chiefly for בָּנָה ;]
to build a house, to build: absol., Luk.11:48 14:30 17:28; οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες, the builders (as Psa.118:22, בָּנָה), Mat.21:42, Mrk.12:10, Luk.20:17, 1Pe.2:7" (LXX) ; ἐ π ̓ ἀλλότριον θεμέλιον οἰ., proverb., Rom.15:20; with accusative of thing(s), Gal.2:18; πύργον), Mat.21:33, Mrk.12:1, Luk.14:28; ἀποθήκας, Luk.12:18; ναόν, Mrk.14:58; pass., Jhn.2:20; οἰκία, Luk.6:48; with accusative of thing(s) before dative of person(s) (cf. Gen.8:20, Eze.16:24), Luk.7:5, Act.7:47, 49; accusative before ἐπί, Mat.7:24, 26 Luk.6:49; πόλιν ἐπ ̓ ὄρους, Luk.4:29; of rebuilding, or restoring, Mat.23:29 26:61 27:40, Mrk.15:29,…
G3618.s: to be a house-builder, i.e. construct or (figuratively) confirm

G3619.d:
οἰκοδομή, -ῆς, ἡ
(οἶκος, + δέμω, to build), [in LXX: 1Ch.29:1 A (בִּירָה), Eze.17:17 40:2 (בָּנָה, מִבְנֶה), Sir.22:16 40:19, al. ;]
= cl. οἰκοδομία (which see), -δόμησις (Thuc., Plat.),
__1. the act of building; in NT always metaphorically, building up, edifying: Rom.14:19 15:2, 1Co.14:26, 2Co.10:8 13:10, Eph.4:29; with genitive obj., 1Co.14:12, 2Co.12:19, Eph.4:12, 16; λαλεῖν, λαβεῖν, οἰ., 1Co.14:3.
__2. = οἰκοδόμημα, a building: Mat.24:1, Mrk.13:1-2; metaphorically, 1Co.3:9, 2Co.5:1, Eph.2:21.†
(AS)
G3619.s: architecture, i.e. (concretely) a structure; figuratively, confirmation
G3619.o: feminine (abstract) of a compound of G3624 (οἶκος) and the base of G1430 (δῶμα);

G3620.d:
οἰκοδομία, -ας, ἡ
(οἰκοδομέω),
the act of building: metaphorically, 1Ti.1:4 (BE for οἰκοδομία, which see).†
(AS)

G3621.d:
οἰκονομέω, -ῶ
(οἰκονόμος), [in LXX: Psa.112:5 (כּוּל pilp.), 2Ma.3:14 * ;]
to manage as house-steward, be a steward: absol., Luk.16:2; hence, generally (see: οἰκονομία), to manage, regulate, arrange (cl., 2Mac, Lc., 3Ma.3:2 R).†
(AS)
G3621.s: to manage (a house, i.e. an estate)

G3622.d:
οἰκονομία, -ας, ἡ
(οἰκονομέω), [in LXX: Isa.22:19, 21 (מַצָּב, מֶמְשָׁלָה)* ;]
__1. prop. (Plat., Arist.), the office of οἰκονόμος, stewardship: Luk.16:2-4.
__2. In later writers (Plut., al.; see AR on Eph.1:10; MM, xviii), generally, administration, dispensation: 1Co.9:17, Eph.1:10 3:2, 9, Col.1:25, 1Ti.1:4.†
(AS)
G3622.s: administration (of a household or estate); specially, a (religious) "economy"

G3623.d:
οἰκονόμος, -ου, ὁ
(οἶκος + νέμω, to manage) [in LXX chiefly for עַל ;]
__1. prop., the manager of a household or estate, a house- or land-steward (usually a slave or freedman): Luk.12:42 16:1, 3 16:8, 1Co.4:2, Gal.4:2; ὀ οἰ. τ. πόλεως (RV, treasurer; cf. I Est.4:49), Rom.16:23.
__2. Metaphorical (in wider sense; cf. οἰκονομία), an administrator, a steward: of Christian ministers, 1Co.4:1, Tit.1:7; of Christians generally, 1Pe.4:10.†
(AS)
G3623.s: a house-distributor (i.e. manager), or overseer, i.e. an employee in that capacity; by extension, a fiscal agent (treasurer); figuratively, a preacher (of the Gospel)
G3623.o: from G3624 (οἶκος) and the base of G3551 (νόμος);

G3624G.d:
οἶκος, -οῦ, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for בַּיִת, also for אֹהֶל ,הֵכָל, etc. ;]
__1. prop., a house, dwelling: Act.2:2 19:16; with genitive poss., Mat.9:6, 7 Mrk.2:11, Luk.1:23, al.; with genitive attrib., ἐμπορίου, Jhn.2:16; προσευχῆς, Mat.21:13, al.; of a sanctuary (Hdt., Eur.): οἶ. τ. θεοῦ, of the tabernacle, Mat.12:4, al.; the temple, Mat.21:13, al.; metaphorically of a city: Mat.23:38, Luk.13:35; of the body, Mat.12:44, Luk.11:24; of Christians, 1Pe.2:5; ἐν οἴ (M, Pr., 81f.), at home, Mrk.2:1, 1Co.11:34 14:35; so κατ ̓ οἶκον, Act.2:46 5:42; οἱ εἰς (= οἱ ἐν; see: εἰς) τ. οἶ., Luk.7:10 15:6; κατ ̓οἴκους, from house to house, Act.8:3 20:20; εἰς (κατ…
G3624G.s: a dwelling (more or less extensive, literal or figurative); by implication, a family (more or less related, literally or figuratively)

G3624H.d:
οἶκος, -οῦ, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for בַּיִת, also for אֹהֶל ,הֵכָל, etc. ;]
__1. prop., a house, dwelling: Act.2:2 19:16; with genitive poss., Mat.9:6, 7 Mrk.2:11, Luk.1:23, al.; with genitive attrib., ἐμπορίου, Jhn.2:16; προσευχῆς, Mat.21:13, al.; of a sanctuary (Hdt., Eur.): οἶ. τ. θεοῦ, of the tabernacle, Mat.12:4, al.; the temple, Mat.21:13, al.; metaphorically of a city: Mat.23:38, Luk.13:35; of the body, Mat.12:44, Luk.11:24; of Christians, 1Pe.2:5; ἐν οἴ (M, Pr., 81f.), at home, Mrk.2:1, 1Co.11:34 14:35; so κατ ̓ οἶκον, Act.2:46 5:42; οἱ εἰς (= οἱ ἐν; see: εἰς) τ. οἶ., Luk.7:10 15:6; κατ ̓οἴκους, from house to house, Act.8:3 20:20; εἰς (κατ…
G3624H.s: a dwelling (more or less extensive, literal or figurative); by implication, a family (more or less related, literally or figuratively)

G3625.d:
οἰκουμένη, -ης, ἡ
(fern. Pres. pass. ptcp. of οἰκέω; sc. γῆ) [in LXX chiefly for תֵּבֵל, אֶרֶץ ;]
the inhabited earth;
__(a) in cl., the countries occupied by Greeks, as disting. from barbarian lands (Hdt., Dem., al.);
__(b) in later writers, the Roman world: Luk.2:1, Act.11:28 24:5; by meton., of its inhabitants : Act.17:6 19:27;
__(with) in LXX (Psa.23:1 71:8, al.) and NT, also of the whole inhabited world: Mat.24:14, Luk.4:5 21:26, Rom.10:18, Heb.1:6, Rev.3:10 16:14; by meton. (ut supr.), Act.17:31, Rev.12:9;
__(d) of the Messianic age, ἡ οἰ. ἡ μέλλουσα = ὁ αἰὼ ὁ μέλλων: Heb.2:5.†
(AS)
G3625.s: land, i.e. the (terrene part of the) globe; specially, the Roman empire
G3625.o: feminine participle present passive of G3611 (οἰκέω) (as noun, by implication, of G1093 (γῆ));

G3626.d:
οἰκ-ουρός, -ον
(οἶκος + οὖρος, a keeper)
__1. watching or keeping the house; as subst., ἡ οἰ., a housekeeper (Soph., Eur.; see LS, see word).
__2. keeping at home: Tit.2:5, Rec. (see Field, Notes, 220 ff.; CGT, in l, and cf. οίκουργός).†
(AS)
G3626.s: be "ware"); a stayer at home, i.e. domestically inclined (a "good housekeeper")

G3627.d:
οἰκτείρω
(οἶκτος, pity), [in LXX for רָחַם pi., חָנַן, etc. ;]
to pity, have compassion on. with accusative of person(s), Rom.9:15 (LXX).†
SYN.: ἐλεέω, q.v (AS)

G3628.d:
οἰκτιρμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(οἰκτείρω), [in LXX, usually in pl., chiefly for רַחַם ;]
compassion, pity. σπλάγχνα οἰκτιρμοῦ, a heart of compassion, Col.3:12; in pl. (as LXX for Heb. רַחַם), οἰ. τ. θεοῦ, Rom.12:1, Heb.10:28; ό πατὴρ τῶν οἰ, 2Co.1:3; σπλάγχνα κ. οἰ., Php.2:1.†
SYN.: ἔλεος, q.v (AS)

G3629.d:
οἰκτίρμων, -ον
(οἰκτείρω), in cl. poët, for ἐλεήμων (which see), [in LXX chiefly for רַחוּם ;]
merciful: Luk.6:36, Jas.5:1.†
(AS)

G3630.d:
οἰνο-πότης, -ου, ὁ
(οίνος + πότης, a drinker), poët. and late prose, [in LXX: Pro.23:20 (יַיִן סָבָא)* ;]
a wine-drinker, wine-bibber: Mat.11:19, Luk.7:34.†
(AS)
G3630.o: from G3631 (οἶνος) and a derivative of the alternate of G4095 (πίνω);

G3631.d:
οἶνος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for יַיִן also for תִּירוֹשׁ, etc. ;]
wine; Mat.9:17, Luk.1:15, Jhn.2:3, al.; οἴνῳ προσέχειν, 1Ti.3:8; δουλοῦσθαι, Tit.2:3. Metaphorical, Rev.14:8, 10 16:19 17:2 18:3 19:15. By meton. for ἄμπελος, Rev.6:6
(AS)
G3631.o: a primary word (or perhaps of Hebrew origin (H03196));

G3632.d:
οἰνοφλυγία, -ας, ἡ
(φλύω, to bubble up, overflow), cf. -γέω, Deu.21:20
drunkenness, debauchery: 1Pe.4:3.†
SYN.: see: κραιπάλη (AS)
G3632.s: an overflow (or surplus) of wine, i.e. vinolency (drunkenness)
G3632.o: from G3631 (οἶνος) and a form of the base of G5397 (φλύαρος);

G3633.d:
οἴομαι, οἶμαι
[in LXX for הִנֵּה, Gen.37:7, al. ;]
to suppose, expect, imagine; with accusative and inf., Jhn.21:25; with inf., Php.1:17; before ὅτι, Jas.1:7.†
οἶμαι, see: οἴομαι
SYN.. see: ἡγέομαι (AS)
G3633.s: to make like (oneself), i.e. imagine (be of the opinion)

G3634.d:
οἷος, -α, -ον
relat. pron., qualitative (related to ὅς as qualis to qui), what sort or manner of, such as, in NT usually without its correl. τοιοῦτος : Mat.24:21, Mrk.9:3, 2Co.12:20, 1Th.1:5, 2Ti.3:11, Rev.16:18; before τοιοῦτος, 1Co.15:48 15:2 2Co.10:11; id. redundant, Mrk.13:19; τ. αὑτὸν . . . σἷον, Php.1:30; οὐχ οἷον δὲ ὅτι, elliptically, but it is not as though (RV), Rom.9:6.†
(AS)
G3634.s: such or what sort of (as a correlation or exclamation); especially the neuter (adverbially) with negative, not so
G3634.o: probably akin to G3588 (ὁ), G3739 (ὅς), and G3745 (ὅσος);
G3634.k: so (as), such as, what (manner of), which

G3635.d:
ὀκνέω, -ῶ
(ὄκνος, shrinking, hesitation), [in LXX: Num.22:16 (מָנַע ni.), Jdg.18:9 (אָצַל ni.), Tob.12:6, 13, Jdth.12:13, Sir.7:35, 4Ma.14:4 * ;]
to shrink from doing, hesitate to do (Hom., Thuc., al.); hence, to delay with inf., Act.9:38 (cf. Nu, l.with, and see MM, xviii).†
(AS)

G3636.d:
ὀκνηρός, -ά, -όν
(ὀκνέω), [in LXX forPro.6:6, 9 al. ;]
shrinking, hesitating, timid: with dative (Bl., § 38, 2), Rom.12:11; hence, slothful: Mat.25:26. Of things, that which causes shrinking, irksome: Php.3:1.†
(AS)

G3637.d:
ὀκταήμερος, -ον
(ὀκτώ, ἡμέρα),
of the eighth day, eight days old: with dative ref., περιτομῇ., Php.3:5 (words of this class denote duration, cf. τεταρταῖος).†
(AS)
G3637.s: an eight-day old person or act

G3638.d:
ὀκτώ, οἱ, αἱ, τά
indecl.,
eight: Luk.2:21, Jhn.5:5, al
(AS)

G3639.d:
ὄλεθρος, -ον
(ὄλλυμι, to destroy), [in LXX for שֹׁד. שָׁדַד, etc. ;]
ruin, destruction, death: 1Th.5:3, 1Ti.6:9; αἰώνιος, 2Th.1:9 (L, txt., ὀλέθριος, which see); εἰς ὄ. τῆς σαρκός, for physical discipline, to destroy carnal lusts, 1Co.5:5.†
(AS)
G3639.s: a prolonged form); ruin, i.e. death, punishment

G3640.d:
ὀλιγό-πιστος, -ον
of little faith or trust: Mat.6:30 8:26 14:31 16:8, Luk.12:28.†
(AS)

G3641.d:
ὀλίγος, -η, -ον
(on οὐχ ὁλ., see infr.), [in LXX chiefly for מָעַט ;]
of number, quantity, size, few, little, small, slight: Mat.9:37 15:34, Mrk.6:5 8:7, Luk.10:2 12:48 (sc. πληγάς, opposite to πολλάς), 1Ti.5:23, Heb.12:10, Rev.3:4 12:12; οὐκ ὀ. (in the best uncials written οὐκ ὁ.; see WH, App., 143; M, Pr., 44; Thackeray, Gr., 126 f.), Act.12:18 14:28 15:2 (with genitive part.) Act.17:4, 12 19:23-24 27:20; pl., absol., Mat.7:14 20:16 (WH, txt., RV, om.) Mat.22:14, Luk.13:23, 1Pe.3:20. Neut. sing (τὸ) ὀ.: Luk.7:47, 2Co.8:15; πρὸς ὀλίγον, 1Ti.4:8, Jas.4:14; ἐν ὀ., Act.26:28-29 (with little effort; see Page, in l); id., in brief, Eph.3:3;…
G3641.s: puny (in extent, degree, number, duration or value); especially neuter (adverbially) somewhat
G3641.k: + almost, brief(-ly), few, (a) little, + long, a season, short, small, a while

G3643.d:
ὀλιγωρέω, -ῶ
(ὀλίγος + ὤρα, care), [in LXX: Pro.3:11 (מָאַס)* ;]
to esteem lightly, think little of: with genitive, Heb.12:5 (LXX),†
(AS)
G3643.s: to have little regard for, i.e. to disesteem
G3643.o: from a compound of G3641 (ὀλίγος) and ("care");

G3644.s: a ruiner, i.e. (specially), a venomous serpent

G3645.d:
ὀλοθρεύω
(ὄλεθρος), late (Alex.) form of ὄλεθρεύω ω (cf. MGr., ξολοθρεύω) [in LXX for כָּרַת, שָׁחַת hi., etc. ;]
to destroy: Heb.11:28 (cf. ἐξ-ολοθρεύω).†
ὀλεθρεύω, see: ὀλοθρεύω
ὀλοθρεύω
(ὄλεθρος), late (Alex.) form of ὄλεθρεύω ω (cf. MGr., ξολοθρεύω) [in LXX for כָּרַת, שָׁחַת hi., etc. ;]
to destroy: Heb.11:28 (cf. ἐξ-ολοθρεύω).†
ὀλεθρεύω, see: ὀλοθρεύω
(AS)

G3646.d:
ὁλοκαύτωμα, -τος, τό
(ὅλος, καίω), [in LXX chiefly for עֹלָה ;]
a whole burnt offering: Mrk.12:33, Heb.10:6, 8" (LXX) (of. Kennedy, Sources, 113 f.).†
SYN.: see: θυσία (AS)
G3646.o: from a derivative of a compound of G3650 (ὅλος) and a derivative of G2545 (καίω);

G3648.d:
ὁλό-κληρος, -ον
(ὅλος, κλῆρος, i.e. with all that has fallen by lot), [in LXX: Lev.23:15, Eze.15:5 (תָּמִים), Deu.27:6, Jos.8:31 (9:2) (שָׁלֵם), Zec.11:16 (נָצַב ni.), Wis.15:3, 1Ma.4:47, 4Ma.15:17 * ;]
complete, entire; in NT in ethical sense (as Wis, 4Mac, ll. with), 1Th.5:23; ὁ. καὶ τέλειοι, Jas.1:4.†
SYN.: ὁλοτελής (which see), τελειος (Tr., Syn., § xxii) (AS)
G3648.s: complete in every part, i.e. perfectly sound (in body)

G3649.d:
ὀλολύζω
(onomatop.), [in LXX chiefly for יָלַל hi. ;] (in Hom., of women crying to the gods in prayer or thanksgiving),
to cry aloud: Jas.5:1.†
(AS)

G3650.d:
ὅλος, -η, -ον,
[in LXX chiefly for כֹּל ;]
of persons and things, whole, entire, complete;
__1. of indefinite ideas, with subst. anarth.: Luk.5:5, Act.11:26 28:30, Tit.1:11; ὅλον ἄνθρωπον (an entire man; see Field, Notes, 93), Jhn.7:23; ὅλη Ἰερουσαλήμ (= πᾶσα Ἰ, Mat.2:3; see Bl., §47, 9), Act.21:31.
__2. Definite, with art.;
__(a) preceding subst.: Mat.4:23, 24 Luk.8:39, 1Co.12:17, al.;
__(b) following subst.: Mrk.1:33, Luk.9:25, Jhn.4:53, Act.21:30, al.;
__(with) between art. and subst., where subst. is an abstract noun (Plat., al.).
__3. Attached to adj. or verb: Mat.13:33, Luk.13:21, Jhn.9:34, al.; adverbially, δι ̓ ὅλου…
G3650.s: "whole" or "all", i.e. complete (in extent, amount, time or degree), especially (neuter) as noun or adverb
G3650.k: all, altogether, every whit, + throughout, whole

G3651.d:
ὁλοτελής, -ές
(ὅλος, τίλος),
complete, perfect.. 1Th.5:23.†
SYN.: ὁλόκληρος (which see), τέλειος. "As regards meaning, ὁλόκληρος can hardly be distinguished from ὁλοτελής though, in accordance with its derivation, it draws more special attention to the several parts to which the wholeness spoken of extends, no part being wanting or lacking in completeness" (M, Th., 78) (AS)
G3651.s: complete to the end, i.e. absolutely perfect

G3652.o: probably a contraction from (Olympian-bestowed, i.e. heaven-descended);

G3653.d:
ὄλυνθος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Sng.2:13 (פַּג)* ;]
an unripe fig, which grows in winter and usually falls off in the spring : Rev.6:13.†
(AS)
G3653.s: an unripe (because out of season) fig

G3654.d:
ὅλως
adv. (ὅλος),
altogether, assuredly, actually (with neg., at all) : Mat.5:34, 1Co.5:1 6:7 15:29.†
(AS)
G3654.s: completely, i.e. altogether; (by analogy), everywhere; (negatively) not by any means

G3655.d:
ὄμβρος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Deu.32:2 (שָׂעִיר), Wis.16:16, al. ;]
a storm of rain, a shower: Luk.12:54.†
(AS)

G3656.d:
ὁμιλέω, -ῶ
(ὅμιλος), [in LXX: Pro.5:19 (רָוָה pi.), al. ;]
to be in company with, consort with; hence, to converse with: Act.20:11; with dative, Act.24:26; before πρός, Luk.24:14-15.†
(AS)
G3656.s: to be in company with, i.e. (by implication) to converse

G3658.d:
ὅμιλος, -ου, ὁ
[in Aq. : 1Ki.19:20 * ;]
a crowd, throng: Rev.18:17, Rec.†
(AS)
G3658.o: from the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ) and a derivative of the alternate of G138 (αἱρέομαι) (meaning a crowd);

G3659.d:
ὄμμα, -τος, τό in cl. chiefly poët.;
[in LXX for עַיִן (עַיִן (Pro.5:1-23, Wis.2:1-24, 4Ma.3:1-21)* ;]
an eye: p1., Mat.20:34 Mrk.8:23.†
(AS)
G3659.s: a sight, i.e. (by implication) the eye

G3660.d:
ὀμνύω
(so Hdt. and some Att.. writers) and ὄμνυμι (so generally in Att.. prose and always in Trag.; Mrk.14:71, -ύναι), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁבַע ni. ;]
to swear, affirm by oath: Mat.26:74, Mrk.14:71, Heb.7:21; before εἰ (q.v), Heb.3:11 4:3; with dative of person(s), Mrk.6:23; id. with inf., Heb.3:18; before ὅρκῳ, Act.2:30; ὀ. ὅρκον, πρός, with accusative of person(s) (cl.), Luk.1:73; with accusative (of that by which one swears; cl., see MM, xviii), Jas.5:12; before κατά, with genitive (LXX; Bl., § 34, 1), Heb.6:13, 16; before ἐν (εἰς), as in Heb. (El., § 39, 4), Mat.5:34, 36 23:16, 18 23:20-22 Rev.10:6 (Bl., § 70, 3).†
(AS)
G3660.s: to swear, i.e. take (or declare on) oath
G3660.o: a prolonged form of a primary, but obsolete , for which another prolonged form is used in certain tenses;

G3661.d:
ὁμοθυμαδόν
(ὁμός, θυμός), [in LXX for יַחַד (frequently in Jb), Wis.10:20 18:5, 12, al. ;]
with one mind, with one accord: Act.1:14 2:46 4:24 5:12 7:57 8:6 12:20 15:25 18:12 19:29, Rom.15:6 (Hatch, Essays, 63 f., argues that the un-cl. sense together, which is found in Job.3:18 38:33, Num.24:24, Wis.18:5, 12 (but not Wis.10:20), al., should be attached to the NT instances, but see Abbott, Essays, 96; MM, xviii).†
(AS)
G3661.o: adverb from a compound of the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ) and G2372 (θυμός);

G3662.d:
ὁμοιάζω
(ὅμοιος),
to be like: Mat.23:27 (L, Tr., txt., WH, mg.) Mat.26:73 (WH, mg.) (not found elsewhere. cf. παρ-ομοιάζω.) †
(AS)

G3663.d:
ὁμοιοπαθής, -ές
(ὅμοιος, πάσχω), [in LXX: Wis.7:3, 4Ma.12:13 * ;]
of like feelings or affections: with dative, Act.14:15, Jas.5:17.†
(AS)
G3663.o: from G3664 (ὅμοιος) and the alternate of G3958 (πάσχω);

G3664.d:
ὅμοιος, -οία, -οιον
[in LXX for כְּמוֹ, etc. ;]
like, resembling, such as, the same as: with dative, of form or appearance, Jhn.9:9, Rev.1:13 (WH, mg., R, but see infr.) Rev.1:15 2:18 4:6-7 9:7, 10 (B1., § 37, 62) Rev_9:19; Rev_11:1; Rev_13:2; Rev_13:11; ὁράσει, Rev_4:3; of nature, condition, ability, etc., Mat_22:39, Act_17:29, Gal_5:21, 1Jn_3:2, Rev_13:4; Rev_18:18; Rev_21:11; Rev_21:18; of comparison in parables, Mat_13:31 ff. Mat_20:1, Luk_13:18-19; Luk_13:21; of thinking, acting, etc., Mat_11:16; Mat_13:52, Luk_6:47-49; Luk_7:31-32 (T, with genitive; 131., § 36, 11) Luk_12:36, Joh_8:55, Jud_1:7; with accusative, Rev_1:13 (WH, txt.; Swete, Hort, in l)…

G3665.d:
ὁμοιότης, -ητος, ἡ
(ὅμοιος), [in LXX: Gen.1:11-12 (מִין), Wis.14:19, 4Ma.15:4 * ;]
likeness: καθ᾽ ὁμοιότητα, in like manner, Heb.4:15; id. with genitive (MM, xviii), after the likeness (of), Heb.7:15.†
(AS)

G3666.d:
ὁμοιόω, -ῶ
(ὅμοιος), [in LXX chiefly for דָּמָה ;]
__1. to make like, with genitive and dative; pass., to be made or become like: Mat.6:8 13:24 18:23 22:2 25:1, Act.14:11, Heb.2:17; before ὡς (cf. Eze.32:2, Heb.), Rom.9:29.
__2. to liken, compare: with dative, accusative, Mat.11:16, Luk.7:31 13:18, 20; πῶς όμοιώσωμεν, Mrk.4:30; pass., Mat.7:24, 26 (cf. ἀφ-ομοιόω).†
(AS)
G3666.s: to assimilate, i.e. compare; passively, to become similar

G3667.d:
ὁμοίωμα, -τος, τό
(ὁμοιόω), [in LXX for דְּמוּת, תַּבְנִית, תְּמוּנָה, etc. ;]
that which is made like something;
__(a) concrete, an image, like­ness (Psa.106:20, Eze.1:5, 1Ma.3:48, al.) : Rev.9:7;
__(b) abstract, like­ness, resemblance: Rom.5:14 6:5 8:3, Php.2:7; ἐν ὁ. εἰκόνος, Rom.1:23.†
SYN.: εἰκών (which see), ὁμοίωσις (AS)
G3667.k: made like to, likeness, shape, similitude

G3668.d:
ὁμοίως
(ὅμοιος),
adv.,
likewise, in like manner, equally: Mat.22:26, Mrk.4:16, Luk.10:37, al.; with dative, Mat.22:39, Luk.6:31; ὁ. καί, Mat.22:26, Mrk.15:31, al.; ὁ. καθώς, Luk.17:28; καθὼς . . . ὁ., Luk.6:31; ὁ. μέντοι καί, Ju 8
(AS)

G3669.d:
ὁμοίωσις, -εως, ἡ
(ὁμοιόω) [in LXX chiefly for דְּמוּת, Psa.58:4, al. ;]
__1. a making like, becoming like (Plat.).
__2. likeness: Jas.3:9 (LXX).†
SYN.: see: ὁμοίωμα, and cf. Tr., Syn., § xv (AS)

G3670.d:
ὁμολογέω, -ῶ
(ὁμόλογος, of one mind: Dan LXX Su 1:60 *), [in LXX: Job.40:9 (14) (יָדָה hi.), Jer.44:25 (נָדַר), al. ;]
__1. to speak the same language (Hdt.).
__2. to agree with (Hdt., Plat., al.).
__3. to agree, confess, acknowledge (Plat., al.) : absol., Jhn.1:20 12:42; pass., Rom.10:10; before ὅτι, ib., Heb.11:13; with accusative of thing(s), Act.23:8, 1Jn.1:9, Rev.3:5; id. with dative of person(s), Act.24:14; with accusative cogn., 1Ti.6:12; with accusative of person(s), 1Jn.2:23 Jn 4:3; id. before pred. accusative (Bl., § 34, 5; 73, 5), Jhn.9:22, Rom.10:9, 1Jn.4:2 Jn 4:15, 2Jn.7; with inf. (M, Pr., 229), Tit.1:16; with dative of person(s) before ὅτι,…
G3670.o: from a compound of the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ) and G3056 (λόγος);
G3670.k: con- (pro-)fess, confession is made, give thanks, promise

G3671.d:
ὁμολογία, -ας, ἡ
(όμολογέω), [in LXX: Deu.12:6, 17. Amo.4:5, Eze.46:12 (נְדָבָה), Lev.22:18, Jer.44:25 (נֶדֶר), I Est.9:8 * ;]
__1. in cl., an agreement assent, compact (in π., of a contract; Deiss., BS, 249).
__2. confession (prob. always in an objective sense): 2Co.9:13, 1Ti.6:12-13 Heb.3:1 4:14 10:13.†
(AS)

G3672.d:
ὁμολογουμένως
adv. (ὁμ oλογέω), [in LXX: 4Ma.6:31 4Mac 7:16 4Mac 16:1 * ;]
__1. as agreed, conformably with.
__2. confessedly, by common consent: 1Ti.3:16.†
(AS)
G3672.o: adverb of present passive participle of G3670 (ὁμολογέω);

G3673.d:
ὁμότεχνος, -ον
(ὁμός, τέχνη),
practising the same craft, of the same trade: Act.18:3.†
(AS)
G3673.o: from the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ) and G5078 (τέχνη);

G3674.d:
ὁμοῦ
adv. (ὁμός),
together;
__(a) prop., of place: Jhn.21:2, Act.2:1;
__(b) without idea of place: Jhn.4:36 20:4.†
(AS)
G3674.s: akin to G260 (ἅμα)) as adverb; at the same place or time

G3675.o: from the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ) and G5424 (φρήν);

G3676.d:
ὅμως
adv. (ὁμίς),
yet: ὅ. μέντοι,
but yet, nevertheless, Jhn.12:42; by hyperbaton, out of its proper position, 1Co.14:7, Gal.3:15 (but see Bl., § 77, 14).†
(AS)
G3676.s: at the same time, i.e. (conjunctionally) notwithstanding, yet still
G3676.o: adverb from the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ);

G3677.d:
ὄναρ, τό
indecl., used only in nom, and accusative sing. (the other cases are supplied by ὄνειρος), a dream: κατ᾽ ὄ. (in later writers only), in a dream, Mat.1:20 2:12-13, 19 2:22 27:19.†
(AS)

G3678.d:
ὀνάριον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of ὄνος),
a young ass: Jhn.12:14.†
(AS)
G3678.o: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3688 (ὄνος);

G3679.d:
ὀνειδίζω
(ὄνειδος), [in LXX chiefly for חָרַף pi. ;]
to reproach, upbraid: absol., Jas.1:5; with accusative of person(s) (in cl. more frequently with dative of person(s); Bl., § 34, 2; WM, 278), Mat.5:11, Mrk.15:32, 34, WH, mg., Luk.6:22, Rom.15:3" (LXX) ; τ. πόλεις, Mat.11:20; pass., 1Ti.4:10, WH, mg., 1Pe.4:14; with accusative of thing(s), Mrk.16:14; with dupl. accusative, Mat.27:44.†
(AS)
G3679.s: to defame, i.e. rail at, chide, taunt
G3679.k: cast in teeth, (suffer) reproach, revile, upbraid

G3680.d:
ὀνειδισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(ὀνειδίζω) [in LXX chiefly for חֶרְפָּה ;]
a reproach: Rom.15:3, Heb.10:33; εἰς ὀ. ἐμπεαεῖν, 1Ti.3:7; ὁ ὀ. τοῦ Χριστοῦ Heb.11:26 13:13.†
(AS)

G3681.d:
ὄνειδος, -ους, τό
[in LXX chiefly for חֶרְפָּה, also for כְּלִמָּה, etc. ;]
__1. reproach, censure, blame.
__2. matter of reproach, disgrace: Luk.1:25.†
(AS)
G3681.o: probably akin to the base of G3686 (ὄνομα);

G3682.d:
Ὀνήσιμος, -ου, ὁ
(i.e. profitable, ὄνησις, profit),
Onesimus: Col.4:9, Phm 10 (a common name among slaves; see MM, iii, xviii).†
(AS)

G3683.o: from a derivative of G3685 (ὀνίνημι) and G5411 (φόρος);

G3684.d:
ὀνικός, -ή, -όν
(ὄνος),
of or for an ass. μύλος ὀ., Mat.18:6, Mrk.9:42 (elsewhere only in π.; see MM, xviii).†
(AS)
G3684.s: belonging to a ass, i.e. large (so as to be turned by a ass)

G3685.d:
ὀνίνημι
[in LXX: Tob.3:8, Sir.30:2 * ;]
to profit, benefit, help; mid., to have profit, derive benefit: optative (M, Pr., 195), with genitive, Phm 20.†
(AS)
G3685.s: for which another prolonged form () is used as an alternate in some tenses (unless indeed it be identical with the base of G3686 (ὄνομα) through the idea of notoriety); to gratify, i.e. (middle voice) to derive pleasure or advantage from
G3685.o: a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb (, to slur);

G3686.d:
ὄνομα, -τος, τό,
[in LXX chiefly for שֵׁם ;]
__1. in general, the name by which a person or thing is called: Mat.10:2, Mrk.3:16, Luk.1:63, Jhn.18:10, al.; ἄνθρωπος (etc.), ᾧ (οὗ) ὄ. (τ. ὄ), sc. ἦν or ἐστίν (BL, §30, 3), Mrk.14:32, Luk.1:26, 27; with same ellipsis, καὶ τ. ὄ. αὐτοῦ, Luk.1:5, Jhn.1:6, al.; ὀνόματι, before nom. prop., Mat.27:32, Mrk.5:22, Luk.1:5, Act.5:1, al.; accusative absol. (Bl., §34, 7), τοὔνομα (= τ. ὄνομα), Mat.27:57; ὄ. μοι (sc. ἐστίν; cf. Hom., Od., ix, 366), Mrk.5:9 (cf. Luk.8:30); ἔξειν ὄ., Rev.9:11; καλεῖν (ἐπιτιθέναι) ὄ. (Bl., §33, 1), Mat.1:21, Mrk.3:16; τ. ὄ. ἐν (τ.) βίβλῳ ζωῆς (cf. Deiss., LAE, 121), Php.4:3, Rev.13:8,…
G3686.o: from a presumed derivative of the base of G1097 (γινώσκω) (compare G3685 (ὀνίνημι));

G3687.d:
ὀνομάζω
(ὄνομα), [in LXX for זָכַר, נָקַב, קָרָא ;]
__1. to name, mention, or address by name: Act.19:13; pass., Rom.15:20, Eph.1:21 5:3; of the use of the Divine name in praise and worship, 2Ti.2:19 (LXX, Num.16:26; cf. Isa.52:11, Amo.6:10).
__2. to name, call, give a name to: Mrk.3:14 (T, R, txt. om.), Luk.6:13-14; pass., 1Co.5:11; before ἐξ (cl.), Eph.3:15 (cf. ἐπ-ονομάζω).†
(AS)
G3687.s: to name, i.e. assign an appellation; by extension, to utter, mention, profess

G3688.d:
ὄνος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for חֲמוֹר, also for אָתוֹן, etc. ;]
an ass: Mat.21:2, 5" (LXX), Luk.14:5, Jhn.12:15" (LXX) ; ὁ, Luk.13:15; ἡ, Mat.21:7 .†
(AS)

G3689.d:
ὄντως
adv. (ὤν, ptcp. of εἰμί, sum) [in LXX: Num.22:37 (אׇמְנָם), Jer.3:23 (אָכֵן), Jer.10:19 (אַךְ), 3Ki.12:24, Wis.17:14 * ;]
really, actually, truly: Mrk.11:32, Luk.23:47 24:34, Jhn.8:36, 1Co.14:25, Gal.3:21 4:1-31 ἡ ὄ. ζωή, 1Ti.6:19; ἡ ὄ. χήρα, 1Ti.5:3 5:5 5:16 †
(AS)
G3689.o: adverb of the oblique cases of G5607 (ὤν);
G3689.k: certainly, clean, indeed, of a truth, verily

G3690.d:
ὄξος, -εος (-ους), τό
(ὄξύς), [in LXX: Num.6:3, Rut.2:14, Psa.69:21, Pro.25:20 (חֹמֶץ)* ;]
sour wine (posca, vin-Deu pays), the ordinary drink of labourers and common soldiers: Mat.27:48, Mrk.15:36, Luk.23:36, Jhn.19:29-30.†
(AS)

G3691.d:
ὄξύς, -εῖα, -ύ
[in LXX: Psa.57:4, al. (חַד), Amo.2:15 (קַל), Isa.5:28 (שָׁנַן), etc. ;]
__1. sharp: Rev.1:16 2:12 14:14, 17-18 19:15.
__2. Of motion, swift: Rom.3:15 (LXX ταχινός).†
(AS)
G3691.o: probably akin to the base of G188 (ἀκμήν) ("acid");

G3692.d:
ὀπή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX for חוֹר, חֲגָו, etc. ;]
an opening, a hole: Jas.3:11 (cf. Exo.33:22), Heb.11:33 (cf. Ob 3).†
(AS)
G3692.s: a hole (as if for light), i.e. cavern; by analogy, a spring (of water)

G3693.d:
ὄπισθεν
adv. of place, [in LXX chiefly for אָחוֹר, אַחַר ;]
behind, after: Mat.9:20, Mrk.5:27, Luk.8:44, Rev.4:6 5:1. As prep. with genitive: Mat.15:23, Luk.23:26, Rev.1:10 (WH, mg.).†
(AS)
G3693.s: from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι)) with enclitic of source; from the rear (as a secure aspect), i.e. at the back (adverb and preposition of place or time)

G3694.d:
ὀπίσω
adv.
of place and time,
[in LXX chiefly for אַחַר and cogn. forms ;]
__1. prop., as in cl., adv.,
__(a) of time (not in NT);
__(b) of place, back, behind, after: Mat.24:18, Luk.7:38; τὰ ὀ., Php.3:13; εἰς τὰ ὀ., Mrk.13:16, Luk.9:62 17:31, Jhn.6:66 18:6 20:14.
__2. By a usage not found in cl., and in LXX representing the Heb. prep. אַחַר (Bl., § 40, 8; Thackeray, Gr., 46 f.), but also prob. general in vernacular (M, Pr., 99), as prep. with genitive;
__(a) of time, after: Mat.3:11, Mrk.1:7 Jhn.1:15, 27 1:30;
__(b) of place, behind, after: Mat.4:19 10:38 16:23-24, Mrk.1:17, 20…
G3694.s: to the back, i.e. aback (as adverb or preposition of time or place; or as noun)
G3694.o: from the same as G3693 (ὄπισθεν) with enclitic of direction;

G3695.d:
ὁπλίζω
(ὅπλον), [in Sm.: Jer.52:25 * ;]
to make ready, equip; of soldiers, to arm. Mid., to arm oneself; figuratively, ἔννοιαν: 1Pe.4:1 (cf. θράσος ὁ., Soph., Elec., 995), (cf. καθ-ὁπλίζω).†
(AS)
G3695.s: to equip (with weapons (middle voice and figuratively))

G3696.d:
ὅπλον, -ου, τό
[in LXX for מָגֵן, צִנָּה, etc. ;]
__1. a tool, implement, instrument: ὅπλα ἀδικίας (Opp. to ὅ. δικαιοσύνης), Rom.6:13.
__2. Freq., in pl., arms, weapons: Jhn.18:3, 2Co.10:4; metaphorically, τ. φωτός, Rom.13:12; τ. δικαιοσύνης, 2Co.6:7.†
(AS)
G3696.s: an implement or utensil or tool (literally or figuratively, especially, offensive for war)
G3696.o: probably from a primary (to be busy about);

G3697.d:
ὁποῖος, -οία, -οῖον
[in LXX: Sng.5:10, 2Ma.11:37 * ;]
of what sort: 1Co.3:13, Gal.2:6, 1Th.1:9, Jas.1:24; τοιοῦτος ὁ., such as, Act.26:29.†
(AS)
G3697.s: of what kind that, i.e. how (as) great (excellent) (specially, as an indefinite correlative to the definite antecedent G5108 (τοιοῦτος) of quality)
G3697.k: what manner (sort) of, such as whatsoever

G3698.d:
1. of Time, correlated to πότε, much like ὅτε:
2. with the indicative, when , Lat. quando, (Homer): —; εἰς ὁπότε, with future, when, by what time , λέγειν εἰς ὁπότ᾽ ἔσται (Aeschines Orator)
3. with the optative in reference to the past, whenever , to express an event that has often occurred, ὁπότε Κρήτηθεν ἵκοιτο (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;also in oratio obliqua, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.
4. in indirect phrases, ἴδμεν, ὁππότε Τηλέμαχος νεῖται when he is to return , (Odyssey by Homer); with optative, δέγμενος ὁππότε ναυσὶν ἐφορμηθεῖεν (Iliad by Homer)
5. in causal sense, for that, because, since , like Lat.…
G3698.s: what(-ever) then, i.e. (of time) as soon as

G3699.d:
ὅπου
adv.
of place, correlat. of ποῦ (which see), where.
__I. Prop., of place,
__1. where;
__(a) in relative sentences, with indic: Mat.25:24, 26, Mrk.2:4 4:5, 15 5:40 13:14, Jhn.3:8 6:62 7:34, 36 11:32 14:3 17:24 20:19, Rom.15:20, Rev.2:13; after nouns of place, for relat. prepositional phrase (ἐν ᾧ., etc.), Mat.6:19-20 13:5 26:57 28:6, Mrk.6:55 9:48 Luk.12:33, Jhn.1:28 4:20, 46 6:23 7:42 10:40 11:30 12:1 18:1, 20 19:18, 20 19:41 20:12, Act.17:1, Rev.2:13 11:8 20:10; before ἐκεῖ., Mat.6:21, Luk.12:34 17:37 Jhn.12:26; id. pleonast. (= Heb. שָׁם . . . אֲשֶׁר; Aram. תַּמָּן . . דּ; of. Gen.13:3), ὅ. . . . ἐκεῖ, Rev.12:6, 14; ὅ. . . . ἐπ᾽…
G3699.s: what(-ever) where, i.e. at whichever spot
G3699.k: in what place, where(-as, -soever), whither (+ soever)

G3700.d:
ὀπτάνω
[in LXX: 3Ki.8:8 (רָאָה ni.), Tob.12:19 * ;]
late present as from ὤφθην (= ὁράω); mid., ὀπτάνομαι, to allow oneself to be seen, to appear. with dative, Act.1:3. (For exx. from π., see Deiss., LAE, 79, 2526; MM, ii, xviii.) †
(AS)
G3700.s: to gaze (i.e. with wide-open eyes, as at something remarkable; and thus differing from G991 (βλέπω), which denotes simply voluntary observation; and from G1492 (εἴδω), which expresses merely mechanical, passive or casual vision; while G2300 (θεάομαι), and still more emphatically its intensive G2334 (θεωρέω), signifies an earnest but more continued inspection; and G4648 (σκοπέω) a watching from a distance)
G3700.o: a (middle voice) prolonged form of the primary (middle voice) ; which is used for it in certain tenses; and both as alternate of G3708 (ὁράω);

G3701.d:
ὀπτασία, -ας, ἡ
(ὀπτάζομαι, Num.14:14* = ὀπτάνομαι), later form of ὄψις, [in LXX: Mal.3:2 (רָאָה ni.), Da TH Dan.9:23 10:1, 7-8 10:16 (מַרְאֶה, מַרְאָה LXX, ὅραμα, -σις), Est.4:7, Sir.43:2, 16 * ;]
__1. an appearing, coming into view (Ma, Es, Sir, ll. with).
__2. a vision: Luk.1:22 24:23, Act.26:19, 2Co.12:1 (Da, ll. with, also in MGr.).†
(AS)
G3701.o: from a presumed derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι);

G3702.o: from an obsolete verb akin to (to "steep");

G3703.d:
ὀπώρα, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX: Jer.48:32 40:10, 12 (קַיִץ) * ;]
__1. late summer, early autumn (the time between the risings of Sirius and Arcturus, i.e. late July, all August and early September).
__2. By meton. (as being fruit-time), ripe fruits Rev.18:14 (cf. φθινοπωρινά, Ju 12).†
(AS)
G3703.s: properly, even-tide of the (summer) season (dog-days), i.e. (by implication) ripe fruit
G3703.o: apparently from the base of G3796 (ὀψέ) and G5610 (ὥρα);

G3704.d:
ὅπως
__I. Relat. adv. of manner, as, how: with indic., Luk.24:20.
__II. Conj., with subjc. (in cl. also with opt., indic.: so in Mat.26:59, LT, Tr.), in order that, to the end that, that;
__1. final, denoting purpose or design (in which the original idea of modality has been merged): after pres., Mat.6:2, al.; pf., Act.9:17, al.; impf., Act.9:24; aor., Act.9:2, al.; plpf., Jhn.11:57; fut., Mat.23:35; imperat., Mat.2:8, al.; ὅ. μή (M, Pr., 185), Mat.6:18, Luk.16:26, Act.20:16, 1Co.1:29; ὅ. πληρωθῇ, Mat.2:23 8:17 13:35; ὅ. ἄν (B1., § 65, 2; WM, § 42, 5), Luk.2:35, Act.3:19 15:17, Rom.3:4 (cf. Gen.12:13, Psa.59:7. 1Mac 1032, al.).
__2. After…
G3704.s: what(-ever) how, i.e. in the manner that (as adverb or conjunction of coincidence, intentional or actual)

G3705.d:
ὅραμα, -τος, τό
(ὁράω), [in LXX for חָזוֹן, מַרְאֶה, etc. ;]
that which is seen;
__(a) a sight, spectacle: Mat.17:9, Act.7:31;
__(b) an appearance, vision: Act.9:10, 12 (Rec.) Act.10:3, 17 10:19 11:5 12:9 16:9-10 18:9 (cf. ὀπτασία).†
(AS)
G3705.s: something gazed at, i.e. a spectacle (especially supernatural)

G3706.d:
ὅρασις, -εως, ἡ
(ὁράω) [in LXX chiefly for מַרְאֶה, חָזוֹן and cognate forms ;]
__1. in Arist. and later writers, the act of seeing, the sense of sight, and by meton., pl., the eyes.
__2. appearance (Num.24:4, Eze.1:5, Sir.41:20, al.): Rev.4:3.
__3. = ὅραμα, a vision: Act.2:17 (LXX), Rev.9:17.†
(AS)
G3706.s: the act of gazing, i.e. (externally) an aspect or (internally) an inspired appearance

G3707.s: gazed at, i.e. (by implication) capable of being seen

G3709.d:
ὀργή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for אַף, also for חָרוֹן, חֵמָה, קָצַף, etc. ;]
__1 1, impulse, propensity, disposition.
__2. anger, wrath;
__(a) of men: Mrk.3:5, Eph.4:31, Col.3:8, 1Ti.2:8, Jas.1:19-20;
__(b) of God;
__α that reaction of the divine nature against sin which in anthropomorphic language is called anger: Rom.1:18 9:22 12:19, (ICC, in l), 1Th.1:10 2:16, Heb.3:11 4:3" (LXX) Rev.14:10 16:19 19:15;
__β of the effect of God's anger: Mat.3:7, Luk.3:7 21:23, Jhn.3:36, Rom.2:5, 8 3:5 4:15 5:9 13:4-5 Eph.5:6, Col.3:6, 1Th.5:9, Jas.1:20, Rev.6:16-17 11:18; σκεύη ὀργῆς, Rom.9:22; τέκνα ὀργῆς, Eph.2:3.†
…
G3709.s: properly, desire (as a reaching forth or excitement of the mind), i.e. (by analogy), violent passion (ire, or (justifiable) abhorrence); by implication punishment

G3710.d:
ὀργίζω
(ὀργή), [in LXX chiefly for חָרָה, also for קָצַף, etc. ;]
to make angry, provoke to anger; in cl. most frequently in pass., and so always in NT, to be provoked to anger, be angry: absol., Mat.18:34 22:7, Luk.14:21 15:28, Eph.4:26" (LXX), Rev.11:18; with dative, Mat.5:22; before ἐπί, with dative (3Ki.11:9, al.), Rev.12:17 (cf. παρ-ὀργίζω).†
(AS)
G3710.s: to provoke or enrage, i.e. (passively) become exasperated

G3711.d:
ὀργίλος, -η, -ον
(ὀργή), [in LXX: Pro.22:24 29:22 (חֵמָה), etc. ;]
inclined to anger, passionate: Tit.1:7.†
(AS)

G3712.d:
ὀργυιά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(ὀρέγω),
the length of the outstretched arms, a fathom: Act.27:28.†
(AS)
G3712.s: a stretch of the arms, i.e. a fathom

G3713.d:
ὀρέγω
[in Sm.: Job.8:20, Eze.16:49 * ;]
to reach, stretch out; pass. and mid., to stretch oneself out, reach forth; metaphorically, to reach after, grasp at, aspire to: with genitive of thing(s), 1Ti.3:1, Heb.11:16; φιλαργυρίας (see Ellic. and CGT, in l), 1Ti.6:10.†
SYN.: ἐπιθυμέω, to desire (which see) (AS)
G3713.s: to stretch oneself, i.e. reach out after (long for)
G3713.o: middle voice of apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary (compare G3735 (ὄρος));

G3714.d:
ὀρεινός (WH, ὀριν-; see MM, xviii,) -ή, -όν
(ὄρος),
mountainous, hilly; ἡ ὀ. (sc. χώρα), the hill-country (LXX for הַר): Luk.1:39, 65 †
(AS)
G3714.s: mountainous, i.e. (feminine by implication, of G5561 (χώρα)) the Highlands (of Judæa)

G3715.d:
ὄρεξις, -εως, ἡ
(ὀρέγομαι), [in LXX Wis.14:2 15:5 16:2-3, Sir.18:30 23:6, 4Ma.1:33 4Mac 1:35 * ;]
the most general ward for all kinds of desire, longing, appetite: of lust, Rom.1:27
SYN.: see: πάθος (AS)
G3715.s: excitement of the mind, i.e. longing after

G3716.d:
ὀρθοποδέω, -ῶ
(ὀρθό-πους, going straight),
= cl. εὐθυπορέω, to walk straight: metaphorically, Gal.2:14 (not elsewhere).†
(AS)
G3716.s: to be straight-footed, i.e. (figuratively) to go directly forward
G3716.o: from a compound of G3717 (ὀρθός) and G4228 (πούς);

G3717.d:
ὀρθός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX chiefly for יָשָׁר ;]
straight;
__(a) in height, straight, upright: Act.14:10;
__(b) in line, straight, direct: figuratively, Heb.12:13 (LXX).†
(AS)
G3717.s: right (as rising), i.e. (perpendicularly) erect (figuratively, honest), or (horizontally) level or direct
G3717.o: probably from the base of G3735 (ὄρος);

G3718.d:
ὀρθοτομέω, -ῶ
(- ὀρθός, τέμνω), [in LXX: Pro.3:6 11:6 (יָשַׁר pi.)* ;]
to cut straight, as a road (τ. ὁδούς, figuratively, Pr, ll with). Metaphorical, τ. λόγον τ. ἀληθείας, 2Ti.2:15 (V. Ellic. and CGT, in l; not found elsewhere).†
(AS)
G3718.o: from a compound of G3717 (ὀρθός) and the base of G5114 (τομώτερος), to make a straight cut, i.e. (figuratively) to dissect (expound) correctly (the divine message)

G3719.d:
ὀρθρίζω
(ὄρθρος), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁכַם hi., Gen.19:2, al.; also for שָׁחַר pi., Psa.63:1, al., etc. ;]
= cl. poët., ὀρθρεύω, to rise early: before πρός, with accusative of person(s) (as Ps, l.with, al.), Luk.21:38 (see Thumb, Hellen., 123).†
(AS)
G3719.s: to use the dawn, i.e. (by implication) to repair betimes

G3720.d:
ὀρθρινός, -ή, -όν
(ὄρθρος), [in LXX: Hos.6:4 13:3 (שָׁכַם hi.), Hag.2:14, Wis.11:22 * ;]
late form of ὄρθριος (which see), early: Luk.24:22.†
(AS)
G3720.s: relating to the dawn, i.e. matutinal (as an epithet of Venus, especially brilliant in the early day)

G3721.d:
ὄρθριος, -α, -ον
(ὄρθρος), [in LXX: 1Ki.28:14, Job.29:7, 1-25; 3Ma.5:10 3Mac 5:23 * ;]
early, in the early morning: Luk.24:22, Rec. (see: ὀρθρινός).†
(AS)
G3721.s: in the dawn, i.e. up at day-break

G3722.d:
ὄρθρος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for שַׁחַר, בֹּקֶר, etc. ;]
daybreak, dawn: ὄρθρου βαθέως (M, Pr., 73), at early dawn, Luk.24:1; ὄρθρου, Jhn.8:2; ὑπὸ τὸν ὄ., Act.5:21 (cf. MM, xviii).†
(AS)
G3722.s: dawn (as sun-rise, rising of light); by extension, morn

G3723.s: in a straight manner, i.e. (figuratively) correctly (also morally)

G3724.d:
ὁρίζω
(ὅρος, a boundary), [in LXX for אָסַר, גְּבוּל, etc. ;]
__1. to separate, mark off by boundaries (so Num.34:6, Jhn.13:27).
__2. to determine, appoint, designate: of time, with accusative, Act.17:26, Heb.4:7; with accusative of person(s), Act.17:31; with inf., Act.11:29; pass., Luk.22:22, Act.2:23 10:42, Rom.1:4 (cf. ὀφ-, ἀπο- δι-, τρο-ορίζω),†
(AS)
G3724.s: to mark out or bound ("horizon"), i.e. (figuratively) to appoint, decree, specify

G3725.d:
ὅριον, -ου, τό
(ὅρος, a boundary), [in LXX chiefly for גְּבוּל ;]
a boundary, bound; chiefly in pl., and so always in NT: Mat.2:16 4:13 8:34 15:22, 39 19:1, Mrk.5:17 7:24, 31 10:1, Act.13:50.†
(AS)
G3725.s: a boundary-line, i.e. (by implication) a frontier (region)
G3725.o: neuter of a derivative of an apparently primary (a bound or limit);

G3726.d:
ὁρκίζω
(ὅρκος), [in LXX: Gen.24:37, al. (שָׁבַע hi.) ;]
__1. to make one swear (Xen., Polyb., a1.).
__2. to adjure: with dupl. accusative, Mrk.5:7, Act.19:13 (cf. ἐν-, ἐξ-ορκίζω).†
(AS)
G3726.s: to put on oath, i.e. make swear; by analogy, to solemnly enjoin

G3727.d:
ὅρκος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for שֶׁוַע, שִׁבְעָה and cogn. forms ;]
an oath: Mat.14:7 26:72, Luk.1:73, Act.2:30, Heb.6:16-17, Jas.5:12; p1., Mat.5:33 (LXX) Mat.14:9, Mrk.6:26.†
(AS)
G3727.s: perhaps akin to G3725 (ὅριον)); a limit, i.e. (sacred) restraint (specially, an oath)

G3728.d:
ὁρκωμοσία, -ας, ἡ
(ὅρκος, ὄμνυμι; by metapl. for τὰ ὁρκωμόσια, asseverations on oath; see MM, xviii), [in LXX: Eze.17:18-19 (עָלָה) 1Es 9:93* ;]
affirmation on oath, an oath: Heb.7:20-21, 28.†
(AS)
G3728.o: from a compound of G3727 (ὅρκος) and a derivative of G3660 (ὀμνύω);

G3729.d:
ὁρμάω, -ῶ
(ὁρμή), [in LXX for שׁוּב, etc. ;]
__1. causal, to set in motion, urge on.
__2. Intrans., to hasten on, rush: before εἰς, Mat.8:32, Mrk.5:13, Luk.8:33, Act.19:29; ἐπί, with accusative, Act.7:57.†
(AS)
G3729.s: to start, spur or urge on, i.e. (reflexively) to dash or plunge

G3730.d:
ὁρμή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX: Pro.3:25 (שׁוֹא), etc. ;]
__1. a violent movement, impulse: Jas.3:4;
__2. a hostile movement, onset, assault. Act.14:5.†
(AS)

G3731.d:
ὅρμημα, -τος, τό
(ὁρμάω) [in LXX: Hos.5:10, Amo.1:11 (עֶבְרָה), etc. ;]
a rush: Rev.18:21.†
(AS)

G3732.d:
ὄρνεον, -ου, τό = ὄρνις,
[in LXX chiefly for צִפּוֹר ;]
a bird: Rev.18:2 19:17, 21 (Hom., al.).†
(AS)
G3732.o: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3733 (ὄρνις);

G3733.d:
ὄρνις, -ιθος, ὁ, ἡ
[in LXX: ὄ. ἐκλεκταί, I2Ki.3:1 4:23 (3Ki.5:3) (בַּרְבֻּר)* ;]
a bird; specif., a cock, a hen: Mat.23:3, Luk.13:34 (WH).†
(AS)
G3733.s: a bird (as rising in the air), i.e. (specially), a hen (or female domestic fowl)
G3733.o: probably from a prolonged form of the base of G3735 (ὄρος);

G3734.d:
ὁροθεσία, -ας, ἡ
(ὅρος, a boundary, + τίθημι)
a setting of boundaries; in pl., bounds; Act.17:26.†
(AS)
G3734.o: from a compound of the base of G3725 (ὅριον) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι);

G3735.d:
ὄρος, -ους, τό
[in LXX chiefly, and very freq., for הַר ;]
