[in LXX for דָּרַשׁ ;]
__1. to inquire: with accusative of thing(s), Jhn.4:42, Act.23:20; before quæst. indir., Mat.2:4, Luk.15:25 18:36, Act.10:18 21:33; quæst. dir., Act.4:7 10:20 23:10; before παρά, with genitive of person(s), Mat.2:4, Jhn.4:52.
__2. to learn by inquiry: before ὅτι, Act.23:34.†
(AS)
G4441.s: to question, i.e. ascertain by inquiry (as a matter of information merely; and thus differing from G2065 (ἐρωτάω), which properly means a request as a favor; and from G154 (αἰτέω), which is strictly a demand for something due; as well as from G2212 (ζητέω), which implies a search for something hidden; and from G1189 (δέομαι), which involves the idea of urgent need); by implication, to learn (by casual intelligence)
G4441.o: middle voice prolonged from a primary (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses);

G4442.d:
πῦρ genitive, πυρός, τό,
[in LXX chiefly and very frequently for אֵשׁ ;]
fire: Mrk.9:22, Luk.3:9, Jhn.15:6, Act.2:10, 1Co.3:13, Jas.3:5, Rev.8:5, al; π. καὶ θεῖον, Luk.17:29; κατακαίειν (ἐν) π., Mat.13:40, Rev.17:16 18:8; καίεσθαι πυρί, Heb.12:18, Rev.8:8 21:8; φλὸξ πυρός, Act.7:30, 2Th.1:8, Heb.1:7, Rev.1:14 2:18 19:12; λαμπάδες πυρός, Rev.4:5; στῦλοι πυρός, Rev.10:1; ἄνθρακες πυρός, Rom.12:20 (LXX); γλῶσσαι ὡσεὶ πυρός, Act.2:3; δοκιμάζειν (πυροῦσθαι) διὰ πυρός, 1Pe.1:7, Rev.3:18; ὡς διὰ. π. (Lft., Notes, 193), 1Co.3:15. Of the fire of hell (cf. Dalman, Words,161): Mrk.9:48 (LXX); τὸ π. τὸ αἰώνιον, Mat.18:8 25:41 (cf. 4Ma.12:12); ἄσβεστον, Mrk.9:43;…

G4443.d:
πυρά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(πῦρ) [in LXX: Jdth.7:5, Wis.17:6, al. ;]
a fire: Act.28:2-3.†
(AS)

G4444.d:
πύργος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for מִגְדָּל ;]
a tower: Luk.13:4; of a watch-tower in a vineyard (Isa.5:2): Mat.21:33, Mrk.12:1, and prob., Luk.14:28.†
(AS)

G4445.d:
πυρέσσω
(πῦρ)
to be ill of a fever: Mat.8:14, Mrk.1:3.†
(AS)
G4445.s: to be on fire, i.e. (specially), to have a fever

G4446.d:
πυρετός, -οῦ, ὁ
(πῦρ) [in LXX: Deu.28:22 (קַדַּחַת) * ;]
a fever: Mat.8:15, Mrk.1:31, Luk.4:39, Jhn.4:52, Act.28:8; π. μέγας, a high fever: Luk.4:38 (on the technical phrase here, see MM, xxii).†
(AS)
G4446.s: inflamed, i.e. (by implication) feverish (as noun, fever)

G4448.d:
πυρόω, -ῶ
(πῦρ) [in LXX chiefly for צָרַף ;]
to set on fire, burn up. In NT always pass.,
__1. to be set on fire, to burn: Eph.6:16, 2Pe.3:12; ptcp., glowing, Rev.1:15. Metaphorical, of grief or indignation, 2Co.11:29; of lust, 1Co.7:9.
__2. Of metals (cf. Job.22:25, Psa.12:7, Zec.13:9), to be refined or purified by fire: Rev.3:18 (and so in RV, Rev.1:15, but see supr.).†
(AS)
G4448.s: to kindle, i.e. (passively) to be ignited, glow (literally), be refined (by implication), or (figuratively) to be inflamed (with anger, grief, lust)
G4448.k: burn, fiery, be on fire, try

G4449.d:
πυρράζω
(πυρρός), [in LXX, πυρρίζω: Lev.13:19, 42 ff. Lev.14:37 (אֲדַמְדָּם) * ;]
to be fiery red: Mat.16:2-3.†
(AS)

G4450.d:
πυρρός -ά, -όν
(πῦρ) [in LXX for אֱדֹם ;]
fiery red: Rev.6:4 12:3.†
Πύρρος, -ου, ὁ,
Pyrrhus: Act.20:4.†
(AS)

G4451.d:
πύρωσις, -εως, ἡ
(πυρόω), [in LXX: Pro.27:21 (כּוּר), Amo.4:9 (שְׁדֵפָה) * ;]
__1. a burning: Rev.18:9, 18.
__2. a refining or trial by fire: metaphorically, 1Pe.4:12.†
(AS)
G4451.s: ignition, i.e. (specially), smelting (figuratively, conflagration, calamity as a test)

G4452.d:
πω
enclit. part.,
yet, see: μή-πω, μηδέ-πω, οὔ-πω, οὐδέ-πω, πώ-ποτε
πώ-ποτε
adv.,
ever yet: Luk.19:30, Jhn.1:18 5:37 6:35 8:33, 1Jn.4:12.†
(AS)
G4452.s: an enclitic particle of indefiniteness; yet, even; used only in the comparative. See G3369 (μηδέπω), G3380 (μήπω), G3764 (οὐδέπω), G3768 (οὔπω), G4455 (πώποτε).
G4452.o: another form of the base of G4458 (-πώς);

G4453.d:
πωλέω, -ῶ
[in LXX chiefly for מָכַר ;]
__1. to exchange or barter.
__2. to sell: Luk.17:28, Rev.13:17; οἱ πωλοῦντες, Mat.21:12 25:9, Mrk.11:15, Luk.19:45; with accusative of thing(s), Mat.13:44 19:21 21:12, Mrk.10:21 11:15, Luk.12:33 18:22 22:36, Jhn.2:14, 16 Act.5:1 (sc. αὐτά, αὐτόν), Act.4:34, 37. Pass., 1Co.10:25; with genitive pretii, Mat.10:29, Luk.12:6.†
(AS)
G4453.s: to barter (as a pedlar), i.e. to sell
G4453.o: probably ultimately from (to be busy, to trade);

G4454.d:
πῶλος, -ου, ὁ
(in cl. also ) [in LXX chiefly for עַיִר ;]
a foal, colt, prop., of a horse, then the young of other animals; in NT of the colt of an ass: Mat.21:2, 5" (LXX), Mat.21:7, Mrk.11:2, 4-5 11:7, Luk.19:30, 33 19:35, Jhn.12:15" (LXX) .†
(AS)
G4454.s: a "foal" or "filly", i.e. (specially), a young ass

G4455.s: at any time, i.e. (with negative particle) at no time
G4455.k: at any time, + never (…to any man), + yet, never man

G4456.d:
πωρόω, -ῶ
(πῶρος, 1. a stone. 2. a callus) [in LXX: Job.17:7 B(כָּהָה), Pro.10:20 A * ;]
to petrify, harden, form a callus. Metaphorical, π. τ. καρδίαν, Jhn.12:40. Pass., Rom.11:7; τ. νοήματα, 2Co.3:14; ἡ καρδία, Mrk.6:52 8:17 †
(AS)
G4456.s: to petrify, i.e. (figuratively) to indurate (render stupid or callous)

G4457.d:
πώρωσις, -εως, ἡ
(πωρόω),
a covering with a callus, a hardening: metaphorically, Mrk.3:6, Rom.11:2, Eph.4:18.†
(AS)

G4458.d:
πως,
enclit. part.,
at all; see: εἴπως, μήπως.
μήπως
or μή πως (so WH),
negative particle,
__1. as conjc., lest haply: in final sentences, 1Co.9:27, 2Co.2:7 9:4; after verbs of fearing or taking heed, 1Co.8:9, 2Co.11:3 12:20, Gal.4:11; with an ellipse of ptcp. (sc. φοβούμενος; cf. B1., § 65, 3; Burton, § 225), 1Th.3:5 (but see infr.).
__2. As interrogative, whether haply: Gal.2:2, 1Th.3:5 (cf. M, Th., in l, but see supr.).†
μήπου
(WH, μή που),
lest anywhere, lest haply: Act.27:29.†
(AS)
G4458.s: an enclitic particle of indefiniteness of manner; somehow or anyhow; used only in composition
G4458.o: adverb from the base of G4225 (πού);

G4459.d:
πῶς, interrog. adv., correl. of ὅπως,
__1. prop., in direct questions, how?: with indic., Mat.12:29, Mrk.3:23, Luk.11:18, Jhn.3:4, al.; καὶ π., Mrk.4:13, Luk.20:44; π. οὖν, Mat.12:26; π. οὐ, Mat.16:11, Luk.12:56; in deliberative questions (cf. Bl., §64, 6), with subjc., Mat.23:33 26:54; π. οὖν, Rom.10:14; π. δέ, Rom.10:14, 15; before ἄν, with optative, Act.8:31.
__2. As sometimes in cl. but more frequently and increasingly so in late writers (see WM, §57, 2; Bl., §70, 2; Thumb, MGr., 192; Jannaris, Gr., App., vi, 13f.), = ὅπως, ὥς;
__(a) in indirect discourse: with indic., Mat.6:28, Mrk.12:41, Luk.8:36, Jhn.9:15, Act.9:27, al.;…
G4459.s: an interrogative particle of manner; in what way? (sometimes the question is indirect, how?); also as exclamation, how much!
G4459.o: adverb from the base of G4226 (ποῦ);

G4460.d:
Ῥαάβ
(and Ραχάβ, Mat.1:5; Ραχάβη, -ης, in FlJ), ἡ, indecl. (Heb. רָחָב)
Rahab (LXX, Jos.2:1, al.): Heb.11:31, Jas.2:25.†
(AS)

G4461.d:
ῥαββεί (Rec. -βί, see WH, App., 155) (Heb. and Aram. רַב, my master; see Dalman, Words, 327, 331 ff.),
a title of respectful address to Jewish teachers, Rabbi: Mat.23:7-8; of John, Jhn.3:26; of Christ, Mat.26:25, 49, Mrk.9:5 11:21 14:45, Jhn.1:30, 50 3:2 4:31 6:25 9:2 11:8; κύριε ῥ Mrk.10:51 (WH, mg., see: ῥαββουνεί).†
ῥαββουνεί (Rec. -βονί, see: ῥαββεί) (Aram. רַבּוֺנִי, later, רִבּוֺנִי my master; on the Greek vocalization and the relation of the word to ῥαββεί, see Dalman, Words, 324, 340; Gr., 140; DB, iv, 190)
Rabboni: Mrk.10:51 (WH, mg., κύριε ῥαββεί), Jhn.20:16.†
(AS)
G4461.s: my master, i.e Rabbi, as an official title of honor
G4461.o: of Hebrew origin (H07227 with pronominal suffix);

G4462.d:
ῥαββουνεί (Rec. -βονί, see: ῥαββεί) (Aram. רַבּוֺנִי, later, רִבּוֺנִי my master; on the Greek vocalization and the relation of the word to ῥαββεί, see Dalman, Words, 324, 340; Gr., 140; DB, iv, 190)
Rabboni: Mrk.10:51 (WH, mg., κύριε ῥαββεί), Jhn.20:16.†
(AS)

G4463.d:
ῥαβδίζω
(ῥάβδος), [in LXX: Jdg.6:11 Rut.2:17 (חָבַט) * ;]
to beat with a rod: Act.16:22, 2Co.11:25.†
(AS)
G4463.s: to strike with a stick, i.e. bastinado

G4464.d:
ῥάβδος, -ου, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for מַטֶּה (e.g. Gen.47:31, MT, מַטֶּה, bed), also for מַקֵּל, שֵׁבֶט, etc. ;]
a staff, rod: Heb.9:4, Rev.11:1; in particular,
__(a) a staff, such as is used on a journey: Mat.10:10, Mrk.6:8, Luk.9:3, Heb.11:21" (LXX) ;
__(b) a ruler's staff, a sceptre: Heb.1:8 (LXX) Rev.2:27 12:5 19:15;
__(with) a rod for chastisement (cf. ῥαβδίζω): ἐν ῥ. (see: ἐν): 1Co.4:21.†
(AS)
G4464.s: a stick or wand (as a cudgel, a cane or a baton of royalty)

G4465.d:
ῥαβδοῦχος, -ου, ό
(ῥαβδος, ἔχω),
one who carries a rod or staff of office;
__(a) an umpire or judge (Plat.);
__(b) in late writers, a Roman lictor: Act.16:38.†
(AS)
G4465.s: a rod- (the Latin fasces) holder, i.e. a Roman lictor (constable or executioner)

G4466.d:
Ῥαγαύ (Rec. -αῦ), ὁ, indecl. (LXX for Heb. רְעוּ, Gen.11:18, al.),
Reu: Luk.3:35.†
(AS)

G4467.d:
ῥᾳδιούργημα, -τος, τό
(ῥᾳδιουργέω, to act recklessly or wrongly)
__1. a reckless act.
__2. crime, villany: Act.18:14.†
(AS)
G4467.s: easy-going behavior, i.e. (by extension) a crime
G4467.o: from a comparative of (easy, i.e. reckless) and G2041 (ἔργον);

G4468.d:
ῥᾳδιουργία, -ας, ἡ
(see: ῥᾳδιούργημα),
__1. ease in doing, facility (Xen.).
__2. easiness, laziness (Xen.).
__3. recklessness, wickedness (of lewdness, Xen.; fraud, Plut.; in π., of theft, MM, xxii): Act.13:10.†
(AS)

G4469.d:
ῥακά (T, ῥαχά),
usually taken to represent the Aram. רֵיקָא, a shortened form of H7386, " empty," as vocalized in the Galilæan dialect; an expression of contempt, raca: Mat.5:22 (cf. DB, iv, 191 f.; and for other explanations, see Zorell, see word).†
(AS)
G4469.s: O empty one, i.e. thou worthless (as a term of utter vilification)

G4470.d:
ῥάκος, -ους, τό
[in LXX: Isa.64:6 (5) (בֶּגֶד), Jer.38:11 (סְחָבָה), Est.4:17 * ;]
__1. a ragged garment (Hom.).
__2. a rag, remnant, piece of cloth: Mat.9:16, Mrk.2:21.†
(AS)

G4471.s: Rama (i.e. Ramah), a place in Palestine

G4472.d:
ῥαντίζω
[in LXX: Lev.6:27 (20), 4Ki.9:33 (נָזָה), Psa.51:7 (חָטָא pi.) * ;]
= cl., ῥαίνω,
to sprinkle, besprinkle: with accusative, Heb.9:13, 19; id. and dative, Heb.9:21; pass., Rev.19:13, WH; of cleansing by sprinkling, Heb.10:22 (see M, Gr., ii, 100); mid., Mrk.7:4 (WH, txt., R, mg.).†
περι-ραίνω
(-ρραίνω, Rec., see WH, App., 139 f.), [in LXX for נָזָה hi. ;]
to sprinkle around: Rev.19:13 T (ῤεραντισμένον, WH; ῤε-, R, txt.; βεβαμμένον, Rec., R, mg.).†
(AS)
G4472.s: to render besprinkled, i.e. asperse (ceremonially or figuratively)

G4473.d:
ῥαντισμός, -ῦo, ὁ
(ῥαντίζω), [in LXX for נִדָּה ;]
sprinkling: of the ceremonial sprinkling of blood for purification, Heb.12:24, 1Pe.1:2 (see Hort, Pe., 23 ff.).†
(AS)

G4474.d:
ῥαπίζω
(ῥαπίς, a rod), [in LXX: Jdg.16:25, Heb.11:4, I Est.4:11 * ;]
__1. prop., to strike with a rod.
__2. In late writers, to strike (the face) with the palm of the hand: Mat.26:67; with accusative of person(s), before εἰς τ. σιαγόνα, Mat.5:39 (cf. Field, Notes, 40, 105).†
(AS)
G4474.o: from a derivative of a primary (to let fall, "rap");
G4474.k: smite (with the palm of the hand)

G4475.d: a stroke, a slap on the face , (Lucian) (ML)
G4475.k: (+ strike with the) palm of the hand, smite with the hand

G4476.d:
ῥαφίς, -ίδος, ἡ
(ῥάπτω, to sew),
a needle: Mat.19:24, Mrk.10:25 (cf. βελόνη).†
(AS)
G4476.s: perhaps rather akin to the base of G4474 (ῥαπίζω) through the idea of puncturing); a needle

G4477.d:
A woman living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Jos.2.1;
mother of: Boaz (H1162)(?)
§ Rahab, "spacious, broad"
Rachab, (Proper name), indeclinable, Mt. 1:5*

G4479.s: Rebecca (i.e. Ribkah), the wife of Isaac

G4480.d:
ῥέδη (see WH, App., 151), -ης, ἡ
(a Gallic word),
a chariot: Rev.18:13.†
(AS)
G4480.s: a rheda, i.e. four-wheeled carriage (wagon for riding)

G4481.d:
Ῥεμφάν, Ῥεφάς, see: Ῥομφά.
Ῥομφά (-άν, T; Ῥεφάν, LTr.; Ῥεμφάν, Rec.; see WH, App., 92),
[in LXX: Amo.5:26 (Ῥαιμφάν or Ῥεφάν, Heb. כִּיּוּן)* ;]
Rompha, Rephan (RV), one of the names of Seb, the Egyptian Saturn: Act.7:43 (LXX).†
(AS)
G4481.o: by incorrect transliteration for a word of Hebrew origin (H03594);

G4482.d:
ῥέω
[in LXX chiefly for זוּב ;]
to flow: Jhn.7:38 (cf. παραρρέω).†
(AS)
G4482.s: for some tenses of which a prolonged form is used to flow ("run"; as water)

G4483.d:
λέγω,
[in LXX very freq., chiefly for אמר; λέγει for נְאֻם, Gen.22:16, al. ;]
__1. in Hom., to pick out, gather, reckon, recount.
__2. In Hdt. and Att., to say, speak, affirm, declare: absol., Act.13:15, 24:10; before orat. dir., Mat.9:34, Mrk.3:11, Jhn.1:29, al.; before ὅτι recit., Mrk.3:21, Luk.1:24, Jhn.6:14, al.; accusative and inf., Luk.11:18, Jhn.12:29, al.; after another verb of speaking, προσφωνεῖν κ. λέγειν, Mat.11:17, al.; ἀπεκρίθη (ἐλάλησεν) λέγων (καὶ λέγει; Dalman, Words, 24 ff.), Mat.25:9, Mrk.3:33, 7:28, Luk.24:6, 7, al.; of unspoken thought, λ. ἐν ἑαυτῷ, Mat.3:9, Luk.3:8, al.; of writing, 2Co.8:8, Php.4:11, al.; λέγει ἡ γραφή,…
G4483.s: to utter, i.e. speak or say
G4483.o: perhaps akin (or identical) with G4482 (ῥέω) (through the idea of pouring forth);

G4484.d:
Ῥήγιον, -ου, τό
Rhegium, a town in Sicily: Act.28:13.†
(AS)

G4485.d:
ῥῆγμα, -τος, τό
(ῥήγνυμι), [in LXX: 3Ki.11:30-31 12:24, 4Ki.2:12 (קֶרַע), Amo.6:12 (11) A (בְּקִיעַ) * ;]
__1. cl. (and so in LXX), a fracture; then by meton., that which is torn.
__2. In NT, ruin: Luk.6:49.†
(AS)
G4485.s: something torn, i.e. a fragment (by implication and abstractly, a fall)

G4486.d:
ῥήγνυμι and (Mrk.9:18) ῥήσσω,
[in LXX chiefly for בָּקַע, also for קָרַע, etc. ;]
__1. to rend, break asunder: Mat.7:6, Mrk.2:22, Luk.5:37; pass., Mat.9:17.
__2. Of the voice, with accusative, φωνήν, etc. (Hdt., al.), to break forth into speech: absol., Gal.4:27 (LXX).
__3. = ῥήσσω (Dem., al.), to throw or dash down: Mrk.9:18, Luk.9:42
(cf. δια-, περι-, προσ-ρήγνυμι).†
SYN.: θραύω, κατάγνυμι (AS)
G4486.s: G2608 (κατάγνυμι) being its intensive (with the preposition in composition), and G2352 (θραύω) a shattering to minute fragments; but not a reduction to the constituent particles, like G3089 (λύω)) or disrupt, lacerate; by implication, to convulse (with spasms); figuratively, to give vent to joyful emotions
G4486.o: both prolonged forms of (which appears only in certain forms, and is itself probably a strengthened form of (see in G2608 (κατάγνυμι))) to "break," "wreck" or "crack", i.e. (especially) to sunder (by separation of the parts;

G4487.d:
ῥῆμα, -τος, τό
[in LXX chiefly for דָּבָר, also for פֶּה, and Aram. פִּתְגָּם, etc. ;]
__1. prop., of that which is said or spoken,
__(a) a word: Mat.27:14, 2Co.12:4; pl., τὰ ῥ., of speech, discourse, Luk.7:1, Jhn.8:20, Act.2:14, Rom.10:18, 2Pe.3:2, al.;
__(b) opposite to ὄνομα (a single word), a saying, statement, word of prophecy, instruction or command (in cl., phrase): Mat.26:75, Mrk.9:32, Luk.1:38 2:50, Act.11:16, Rom.10:8, Heb.11:3; ῥ. θεοῦ (κυρίου), Luk.3:2, Act.11:16, Eph.6:17, Heb.6:5 11:3, 1Pe.1:25" (LXX) ; τὰ ῥ. τ. θεοῦ, Jhn.3:34 8:47; ῥ. ἀργόν, Mat.12:36;ῥ. ἄρρητα, 2Co.12:4.
__2. Like Heb. דָּבָר (but perh. also a Gk.…
G4487.s: an utterance (individually, collectively or specially),; by implication, a matter or topic (especially of narration, command or dispute); with a negative naught whatever

G4488.o: probably of Hebrew origin (apparently for H07509);

G4489.d:
ῥήτωρ, -ορος, ὁ
a public speaker, an orator: Act.24:1.†
(AS)
G4489.s: a speaker, i.e. (by implication) a forensic advocate

G4490.o: adverb from a derivative of G4483 (ῥέω);

G4491.d:
ῥίζα, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁרַשׁ ;]
a root: Mat.3:10, Luk.3:9; ἐκ ῥιζῶν, Mrk.11:20; ῥ. ἔχειν, Mat.13:6, Mrk.4:6; id. before ἐν ἑαυτῷ, figuratively, Mat.13:21, Mrk.4:17, Luk.8:13. Metaphorical (as in various senses in cl.), of cause, origin, source, etc.;
__(a) of things, ῥ. πάντων τ. κακῶν (Eur.), 1Ti.6:10;
__(b) of persons: of ancestors, Rom.11:16-18; ῥ. πικρίας, Heb.12:15. Of that which springs from a root, a shoot; metaphorically, of offspring, Rom.15:12 (LXX) Rev.5:5 22:16.†
(AS)

G4492.d:
ῥιζόω, -ῶ
(ῥίζα), [in LXX: Isa.40:24, Jer.12:2 (שָׁרַשׁ), Sir.3:28 24:12 * ;]
to cause to take root. Metaphorical, to plant, fix firmly, establish: pass. (EV, rooted), ἐν ἀγάπῃ, Eph.3:18(17); ἐν Χριστῷ, Col.2:7 (cf. ἐκ ριζόω).†
(AS)

G4493.d:
ῥιπή, ῆς, ἡ
(ῥίπτω),
poët. in cl., any rapid movement such as the throw or flight of a javelin, the rush of wind or flame, the flapping of wings, the twinkling of lights; ῥ. ὀφθαλμοῦ, the twinkling of an eye: 1Co.15:52 (L, mg., ῥοπή, which see).†
(AS)
G4493.s: a jerk (of the eye, i.e. (by analogy) an instant)

G4494.d:
ῥιπίζω
(ῥιπίς, a fan) [in LXX: Dan LXX 2:35 (נְשָׂא) * ;]
primarily, to fan a fire, hence generally, to make a breeze (Plut., al.). In pass. (cf. Philo, de inter. round., 24), to be tossed or blown by the wind: of waves, ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ, blown and raised with the wind (Hort, in l), Jas.1:6.†
(AS)
G4494.s: to breeze up, i.e. (by analogy) to agitate (into waves)
G4494.o: from a derivative of G4496 (ῥίπτω) (meaning a fan or bellows);

G4495.d:
ῥιπτέω, see: ῥίπτω.
ῥίπτω and (Act.22:23) ῥιπτέω (strengthened form; see Veitch, see word ῥίπτω, fin.),
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁלַךְ hi. ;]
__1. to throw, cast, hurl: with accusative of thing(s), Mat.27:5, Act.27:19, 29; with accusative of person(s), Mat.15:30, Luk.4:35; pass., Luk.17:2; ptcp., ἐριμμένοι, cast down, prostrate (Polyb., al.): Mat.9:36; of garments, to throw off (for flight, Eur., Xen., al.; ὅπλα, 1Ma.5:43; so EV in Act.22:23, but see infr.).
__2. = ῥιπτάζω, to shake, toss, throw about: τ. ἱμάτια, Act.22:23 (EGT, Page, Rackham, in l; Field, Notes, 136; but see supr.).†
(AS)

G4496.d:
ῥίπτω and (Act.22:23) ῥιπτέω (strengthened form; see Veitch, see word ῥίπτω, fin.),
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁלַךְ hi. ;]
__1. to throw, cast, hurl: with accusative of thing(s), Mat.27:5, Act.27:19, 29; with accusative of person(s), Mat.15:30, Luk.4:35; pass., Luk.17:2; ptcp., ἐριμμένοι, cast down, prostrate (Polyb., al.): Mat.9:36; of garments, to throw off (for flight, Eur., Xen., al.; ὅπλα, 1Ma.5:43; so EV in Act.22:23, but see infr.).
__2. = ῥιπτάζω, to shake, toss, throw about: τ. ἱμάτια, Act.22:23 (EGT, Page, Rackham, in l; Field, Notes, 136; but see supr.).†
(AS)
G4496.s: to fling (properly, with a quick toss, thus differing from G906 (βάλλω), which denotes a deliberate hurl; and from (see in G1614 (ἐκτείνω)), which indicates an extended projection); by qualification, to deposit (as if a load); by extension, to disperse
G4496.o: a primary verb (perhaps rather akin to the base of G4474 (ῥαπίζω), through the idea of sudden motion);

G4499.d: the isle of Rhodes , (Iliad by Homer), etc. (ML)
G4499.s: Rhodus, an island of the Mediterranean

G4500.d:
ῥοιζηδόν
adv. (ῥοῖζος, the whistling of an arrow),
with rushing sound (as of roaring flames): 2Pe.3:10.†
(AS)
G4500.o: adverb from a derivative of (a whir);

G4501.d:
ῥομφαία, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for חֶרֶב ;]
a large broad sword, used by the Thracians (see DB, iv, 634); then generally (in LXX used interchangeably with μάχαιρα, which see), a sword: Rev.1:16 2:12, 16 6:8 19:15, 21; metaphorically, Luk.2:35.†
(AS)
G4501.s: a sabre, i.e. a long and broad cutlass (any weapon of the kind, literally or figuratively)

G4505.d:
ῥύμη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX: Isa.15:3 (רְחֹב), Pro.31:23 א, Tob.13:18, Sir.9:7 א1* ;]
__1. in cl., the force, rush, swing, of a moving body; esp. of a charge of soldiers.
__2. In late Greek (as in Macedonian, see Kennedy, Sources, 15), a narrow road, lane, street: in Polyb., of a road in camp; in LXX and NT (π. also) of streets in a town, Mat.6:2, Luk.14:21 Act.9:11 12:10 (cf. Rutherford, NPhr., 488).†
(AS)
G4505.o: prolongation from G4506 (ῥύομαι) in its original sense;

G4506.d:
ῥύομαι
[in LXX chiefly for נָצַל hi., also for גָּאַל, פָּלַט pi., etc. ;]
to draw to oneself, hence, to rescue, deliver: with accusative of person(s), Mat.27:43, 2Pe.2:7; id. before ἀπό, Mat.6:13, Luk.11:4 (Rec., R, mg.), 2Ti.4:18; before ἐκ, Rom.7:24, 2Co.1:10, Col.1:13, 1Th.1:10, 2Ti.3:11, 2Pe.2:9; absol., ὁ ῥυύμενος, the deliverer, Rom.11:26. Passive: before ἀπό, Rom.15:31, 2Th.3:2; before ἐκ, Luk.1:74, 2Ti.4:17.†
(AS)
G4506.s: compare G4511 (ῥύσις)); to rush or draw (for oneself), i.e. rescue
G4506.o: middle voice of an obsolete verb, akin to G4482 (ῥέω) (through the idea of a current;

G4507.d:
ῥυπαρία, -ας, ἡ
(ῥυπαρός)
filthiness: metaphorically, of moral defile­ment, Jas.1:21.†
(AS)

G4508.d:
ῥυπαρός, -ά, -όν
(ῥύπος), [in LXX: Zec.3:4-5, (3-4) (צוֹא)* ;]
filthy, dirty: of old, shabby clothing (Za, l.with), Jas.2:2; metaphorically, of moral defilement, Rev.22:11.†
(AS)
G4508.s: dirty, i.e. (relatively) cheap or shabby; morally, wicked

G4509.d:
ῥύπος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Isa.4:4 (צוֹאָה), Job.14:4 (טָמֵא), etc. ;]
dirt, filth: 1Pe.3:21.†
(AS)

G4510.d:
ῥυπόω, -ῶ
(ῥύπος),
to make filthy: Rev.22:11 Rec. (AV, tr. as = ῥυπάω, to be filthy).†
(AS)
G4510.s: to soil, i.e. (intransitively) to become dirty (morally)

G4511.d:
ῥύσις, -εως, ἡ
(ῥέω), [in LXX chiefly for זוֹב ;]
a flowing, issue: τ. αἵματος, Mrk.5:25, Luk.8:43-44.†
(AS)
G4511.o: from G4506 (ῥύομαι) in the sense of its congener G4482 (ῥέω);

G4512.d: a fold or pucker in the face, a wrinkle , Lat. ruga, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)
G4512.s: a fold (as drawing together), i.e. a wrinkle (especially on the face)

G4513.d:
Roman, a Roman , (Polybius Historicus), etc.; adverb -κῶς, in Latin , [variant datesAnthology Palantina
(ML)

G4515.s: Romaistically, i.e. in the Latin language
G4515.o: adverb from a presumed derivative of G4516 (Ῥώμη);

G4516.s: strength; Roma, the capital of Italy

G4517.d:
ῥώννυμι
[in LXX: 2Ma.9:20 2Mac 11:21 2Mac 11:28 2Mac 11:33 2Mac 11:1-38; 3Ma.6:1-41 * ;]
to strengthen; most frequently in pf., ἔρρωμαι, to put forth strength, be strong, hence, often in imperat., ἔρρωσο, ἔρρωσθε, farewell (Lat. vale): Act.15:29 23:30 Rec., R, mg.†
(AS)
G4517.s: probably akin to G4506 (ῥύομαι)); to strengthen, i.e. (impersonal passive) have health (as a parting exclamation, good-bye)

G4518.d:
σαβαχθανεί (Rec. -νί; ζαφθανεί, Mt, l.with, WH, mg.) (Aram. שְׁבַקְתַּנִי),
sabachthani, i.e. thou host forsaken me: Mat.27:46, Mrk.15:34 (Psa.22:2, Heb. עָזַב).†
ζαφθανεί (cf. Heb. עָזַב),
zaphthanei: Mat.27:46 (WH, mg., for Rec. σεβαχθανεί, which see; "probably an attempt to reproduce the Heb. as disting from Aram. forms," WE, Notes, 21; cf. also Dalman, Words, 53 f.).†
(AS)
G4518.s: thou hast left me; sabachthani (i.e. shebakthani), a cry of distress
G4518.o: of Chaldee or (H07662 with pronominal suffix);

G4519.d:
σαβαώθ indecl.,
[in LXX for צָבָא, chiefly in Isaiah (in other places, the phrase is also rendered by κύριος παντοκράτωρ, κ. τῶν δυνάμεων; see DB, iii, 137 f.) ;]
Sabaoth, i.e. hosts or armies (see DB, l.with): Rom.9:29 (LXX), Ja 54.†
(AS)
G4519.s: armies; sabaoth (i.e. tsebaoth), a military epithet of God
G4519.o: of Hebrew origin (H06635 in feminine plural);

G4520.d:
σαββατισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(σαββατίζω, to keep the sabbath, Exo.16:30, al.),
a keeping sabbath, a sabbath rest: metaphorically, as in Mishna (Zorell, see word), Heb.4:9.†
(AS)
G4520.s: a "sabbatism", i.e. (figuratively) the repose of Christianity (as a type of heaven)

G4521.d:
σάββατον, -ου, τό (Aram. שַׁבָּתָא, transliterated σάββατα, and this being mistaken for a pl., the sing. σάββατον was formed from it), and σάββατα, -ων, τά
[in LXX for שַׁבָּת, שַׁבָּתוֹן ;]
__1. the seventh day of the week, the sabbath
__(a) the sing. form -ον, τὸ σ.: Mat.12:8, Mrk.2:27, Luk.6:5, al.; ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ σ. (in LXX, Exo.20:8, al., usually τῶν σ., see infr.), Luk.13:16 14:5; ὁδὸς σαββάτου, Act.1:12 (cf. Mat.24:29); dative, of time (τῷ) σ., Luk.6:9 14:1; ἐν (τῷ) σ., Mat.12:2, Luk.6:7, Jhn.5:16, al.; accusative, of duration, τὸ σ., Luk.23:56; κατὰ πᾶν σ., Act.13:27 15:21 18:4; pl., σ. τρία, Act.17:2 R, txt. (but see infr.);
__(b) as most frequently in LXX…
G4521.s: the Sabbath (i.e. Shabbath), or day of weekly repose from secular avocations (also the observance or institution itself); by extension, a se'nnight, i.e. the interval between two Sabbaths; likewise the plural in all the above applications

G4522.d:
σαγήνη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for חֵרֶם ;]
a drag-net, seine: Mat.13:47.†
SYN.: ἀμφίβληστρον (which see), δίκτυον (AS)
G4522.o: from a derivative of (to equip) meaning furniture, especially a pack-saddle (which in the East is merely a bag of netted rope);

G4523.s: a Sadducæan (i.e. Tsadokian), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite

G4524.d:
Σαδώκ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. צָדוֹק, see supr., see word Σαδδουκαῖος)
Sadoc, Zadok: Mat.1:14.†
(AS)

G4525.d:
σαίνω
__1. prop. (Hom., al.), of dogs, to wag the tail, fawn.
__2. Metaphorical, of persons, with accusative, to fawn upon, flatter, beguile: pass., 1Th.3:3 (for conjectural emendations of the text, see ICC, and M, Th., in l).†
(AS)
G4525.s: to wag (as a dog its tail fawningly), i.e. (generally) to shake (figuratively, disturb)

G4526.d:
σάκκος also written σάκος, -ου, ὁ
(cf. Heb. שַׂק, which it renders in LXX),
__1. a coarse cloth, sackcloth, usually made of hair: Rev.6:12.
__2. Anything made of sackcloth;
__(a) a sack (Gen.42:25, al.);
__(b) a garment of sackcloth, expressive of mourning or penitence: Mat.11:21, Luk.10:13, Rev.11:3.†
(AS)
G4526.s: "sack"-cloth, i.e. mohair (the material or garments made of it, worn as a sign of grief)

G4527G.d:
Σαλά, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שֶׁלַח),
Sala, Shalah: Luk.3:32 (R, txt., Σαλμών, which see), Luk.3:35.†
(AS)

G4527H.d:
Σαλά, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שֶׁלַח),
Sala, Shalah: Luk.3:32 (R, txt., Σαλμών, which see), Luk.3:35.†
(AS)

G4529.d:
Σαλαμίς, -ῖνσς, ἡ
Salamis, the chief city of Cyprus: Act.13:5.†
(AS)
G4529.o: probably from G4535 (σάλος) (from the surge on the shore);

G4530.d:
Σαλείμ, τό indecl.,
Salim: Jhn.3:23 (see Westc., in l; DB, iii, 354).†
(AS)
G4530.o: probably from the same as G4531 (σαλεύω);

G4531.d:
σαλεύω
(σάλος), [in LXX for מוֹט, זוּעַ, etc. ;]
prop., of the action of wind, storm, etc., to agitate, shake: of a reed, Mat.11:7, Luk.7:24; a house, Luk.6:48, Act.4:31 16:26; the earth, Heb.12:26; the heavenly bodies, Mat.24:29, Mrk.13:25, Luk.21:26; of a vessel shaken in filling, Luk.6:38. Metaphorical,
__(a) to shake, i.e. to render insecure: τὰ σαλευόμενα, τὰ μὴ., Heb.12:27;
__(b) with accusative of person(s), to cast down from a sense of security and happiness: Act.2:25 (LXX);
__(with) to unsettle or drive away: pass., before ἀπὸ τ. νοός, 2Th.2:2;
__(d) to stir up: τ. ὄχλους, Act.17:13.†
(AS)
G4531.s: to waver, i.e. agitate, rock, topple or (by implication) destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite
G4531.k: move, shake (together), which can(-not) be shaken, stir up

G4532.s: Salem (i.e. Shalem), a place in Palestine

G4533.d:
Σαλμών, ὁ indecl. (Heb. שַׂלְמוֹן),
Salmon: Mat.1:4-5, Luk.3:32 (Σαλά, WH, R, mg.).†
(AS)

G4534.d:
Σαλμώνη, -ης, ἡ
Salmone, a promontory of Crete: Act.27:7.†
(AS)
G4534.o: perhaps of similar origin to G4529 (Σαλαμίς);

G4535.d:
σάλος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for מוֹט, etc. ;]
in poets and late prose, a tossing, as of an earthquake; esp. the tossing, the rolling swell of the sea: Luk.21:25.†
(AS)
G4535.o: probably from the base of G4525 (σαίνω);

G4536.d:
σάλπιγξ, -ιγγος, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for שׁוֹפָר, חֲצֹצְרָה ;]
a trumpet, used in war and in religious ceremonies: 1Co.14:8, Heb.12:19, Rev.1:10 4:1 8:2, 6 8:11 9:14 By meton., a trumpet blast: μετὰ σ. μεγάλης, Mat.24:31; ἐν σ. θεοῦ, 1Th.4:16; ἐν τ. ἐσχάτῃ σ., 1Co.15:52.†
(AS)
G4536.o: perhaps from G4535 (σάλος) (through the idea of quavering or reverberation);

G4537.d:
σαλπίζω
[in LXX chiefly for תָּקַע ;]
to sound a trumpet: Rev.8:6 ff. Rev.9:1, 13 10:7 11:15; metaphorically, Mat.6:2. Impers., the trumpet sounds: 1Co.15:52.†
(AS)
G4537.s: to trumpet, i.e. sound a blast (literally or figuratively)

G4538.d:
σαλπιστής
(so Inscr. and late writers for Mt. σαλπιγκτής), οῦ, ὁ,
a trumpeter: Rev.18:22.†
(AS)

G4539.o: probably of Hebrew origin (feminine from H07965);

G4540.d:
Σαμαρία (Rec. -άρεια), -ας, ἡ (Heb. שֹׁמְרוֹן; Aram. שָׁמְרַיִן),
Samaria;
__(a) the city: Act.8:5 (and perhaps also Act.8:9, 14);
__(b) the region: Luk.17:11, Jhn.4:4-5, 7, Act.1:8 8:1 (and perhaps also Act.8:9, 14) Act.9:31 15:3.†
(AS)
G4540.s: Samaria (i.e. Shomeron), a city and region of Palestine

G4541.d:
Σαμαρείτης
(-ίτης, Τ; see WH, App., 154; BI., § 3, 4), -ον, ό,
a Samaritan, i.e. an inhabitant of the city or the region of Samaria, in NT always the latter (see: Σαμαρία): Mat.10:5, Luk.9:52 10:33 17:16, Jhn.4:9, 39-40, Act.8:25; as an opprobrious epithet, Jhn.8:48.†
(AS)
G4541.s: a Samarite, i.e. inhabitant of Samaria

G4561.d:
σάρξ, σαρκός, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for בָּשָׂר ;]

__(a) prop., of the soft substance of the animal body: 1Co.15:39, 2Co.12:7, Gal.6:13, al.; σ. καὶ αἷμα, 1Co.5:50; σ. καὶ ὀστέα, Luk.24:39; pl., of the flesh of many or parts of the flesh of one (cl.), Rev.17:16 19:18; φαγεῖν, Re, ll. with (cf. κατεσθίειν, 4Ki.9:36, al., and βιβρώσκειν, frequently in l.); metaphorically, Jas.5:3; mystically, φ. (τρώγειν) τὴν σ. τοῦ υἱοῦ τ. ἀνθρώπου, Jhn.6:52-56;
__(b) Of the whole substance of the body, = σῶμα: Act.2:26 (LXX), 31, 2Co.12:7, Gal.4:14, Eph.5:29; μία σ., Mrk.10:8; εἰς σ. μίαν (Gen.2:24), Mat.19:5, Mrk.10:8, 1Co.6:16,…

G4561.o: probably from the base of G4563 (σαρόω);

of Sidon, Sidonian;
__(a) the region: sc. χώρα, Luk.4:26;
__(b) the people: Act.12:20.†
(AS)
G4606.s: a Sidonian, i.e. inhabitant of Sidon

G4607.d:
σικάριος, -ου, ὁ
(Lat.; sica, a dagger carried under their clothing by the Sicarii),
a bandit, assassin, one of the Sicarii (FlJ, B.J., ii, 17, 6, al.): Act.21:38.†
(AS)
G4607.s: a dagger-man or assassin; a freebooter (Jewish fanatic outlawed by the Romans)

G4608.d:
σίκερα, τό indecl.
(Aram. שִׁכְרָא), [in LXX for שֵׁכָר (also rendered μέθυσμα, Jdg.13:4, Mic.2:11), Lev.10:9, al. ;]
fermented liquor, strong drink: Luk.1:15.†
(AS)
G4608.s: an intoxicant, i.e. intensely fermented liquor

G4609.d:
Σίλας, -α (accusative to BL, § 29, W-Schm., 74, -ᾶς, -ᾶ), ὁ (Aram. שׁאִילָא; see Dalman, Gr., 157.5),
Silas (called also Σιλουανός, which see): Act.15:22, 27 15:32, 34 15:40 16:19, 25 16:29 17:4, 10 17:14-15 18:5 †
(AS)

G4610.d:
Σιλουανός
(in MSS also Σιλβανός, a form frequently in π.), -οῦ, ὁ,
Silvanus, latinized name of Silas: 2Co.1:19, 1Th.1:1, 2Th.1:1, 1Pe.5:12.†
(AS)

G4611.d:
Σιλωάμ (indecl., but in FlJ, genitive, ᾶ, B.J., ii, 16, 2), ὁ (Heb. שִׁלֹחַ),
Siloam (see DB, iii, 515 f.): Luk.13:4, Jhn.9:7, 11.†
(AS)
G4611.s: Siloam (i.e. Shiloach), a pool of Jerusalem

G4612.d:
σιμικίνθιον (also written σημι-), -ου, τό (Lat. semicinctium),
a work­man's apron: Act.19:12.†
(AS)
G4612.s: a semicinctium or half-girding, i.e. narrow covering (apron)

G4613G.d:
Σίμων, -ωνος, ὁ
a Greek name (transliterated סִימוֺן in Heb.) used as a substitute for Συμεών (which see), Simon
__1. Simon Peter: Mat.17:25, Mrk.1:29, al.
__2. Simon the Zealot (see: ζηλωτής, Καναναῖος): Mat.10:4, Mrk.3:18, Luk.6:15, Act.1:13.
__3. One of the Brethren of our Lord (see: ἀδελψός): Mat.13:55, Mrk.6:3.
__4. The father of Judas Iscariot, himself surnamed Ἰσκαριώτης (which see): Jhn.6:71 12:4 (Rec.) 13:2,26
__5. Simon the Cyrenian: Mat.27:32, Mrk.15:21, Luk.23:26.
__6. Simon the Pharisee: Luk.7:40, 43-44.
__7. Simon of Bethany, surnamed ὁ λεπρός: Mat.26:6, Mrk.14:3.
__8.…
G4613G.s: Simon (i.e. Shimon), the name of nine Israelites

G4614.d:
Σινά
(-ᾶ, Rec.),
indecl. (but τὸ Σιναῖον, FlJ, Ant., iii, 5, 1; τὸ Σιναῖον ὄρος, ib. ii, 12, 1), τό
(Heb. סִינַי),
Sinai (Exo.19:11, al.): Act.7:30, 38, Gal.4:24-25†
(AS)
G4614.s: Sina (i.e. Sinai), a mountain in Arabia

G4615.d:
σίναπι, -εως, τό
(prob. Egyptian), = Attic τὸ νᾶπυ
mustard: Mat.13:31 17:20, Mrk.4:31, Luk.13:19 17:6.†
(AS)

G4616.d:
σινδών, -όνος, ἡ
[in LXX: Jdg.14:12-13 A, Pro.31:24 (סָדִין), 1Ma.10:64 A * ;]
fine linen cloth;
__(a) as used for swathing dead bodies (cf. Hdt., ii, 86): Mat.27:59, Mrk.15:46, Luk.23:53;
__(b) a garment or wrap of this material (cf. ICC, Jg, l.with): Mrk.14:51-52.†
(AS)
G4616.s: byssos, i.e. bleached linen (the cloth or a garment of it)

G4617.d:
σινιάω
(σίνιον, a sieve), = σήθω,
to sift, winnow: figuratively, Luk.22:31.†
(AS)

G4618.d:
σιτευτός, -ή, -όν
(σιτεύω, to feed, fatten), [in LXX: 3Ki.4:23 (אָבַס), etc. ;]
fattened: Luk.15:23, 27 15:30.†
(AS)

G4619.d:
σιτιστός, -ή, -όν
(σιτίζω, to fatten) [in Sm.: Psa.22:13, Jer.46:21 * ;]
= σιτευτός, fattened; as subst., pl., τὰ σ., fatlings: Mat.22:4.†
(AS)

G4620.d:
σιτομέτριον, -ου, τό
(σιτομετρέω, Gen.47:12, 14 *, = Attic τὸν σῖτον μετρέω),
a measured portion of food: Luk.12:42 (for exx. in π., see Deiss., BS, 158; LAE, 103.1).†
(AS)
G4620.s: a grain-measure, i.e. (by implication) ration (allowance of food)

G4621.d:
σῖτος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for דָּגָן ;]
wheat, corn: Mat.3:12 13:25, 29-30 Mrk.4:28, Luk.3:17 12:18 16:7 22:32, Jhn.12:24, Act.27:38, 1Co.15:37, Rev.6:6 18:13.†
σιτίοι, -ου, τό
(dimin. of σῖτος), [in LXX: Pro.30:22 (לֶחֶם)* ;]
__1. corn, grain: Act.7:12 (but see 131., § 9, 1).
__2. Mostly in pl., σιτία, bread, food, provisions (LXX, l.with, Hdt., al.).†
(AS)

G4622.d:
Σιών
indecl.,
in NT anarth., but in LXX when used of the city of Jerusalem, ἡ Σ.
(Heb. צִיּוֹן),
Zion;
__1. the mountain: in typical sense, of the Church, Heb.12:22; of heaven, Rev.14:1.
__2. The city, i.e. Jerusalem; in poetical sense;
__(a) of the inhabitants: θυγάτηρ Σ, Mat.21:5, Jhn.12:15" (LXX) ;
__(b) in wider sense, of Israel: Rom.11:26;
__(with) figuratively: τίθήμι ἐν Σ λίθον, Rom.9:33, 1Pe.2:6" (LXX) .†
(AS)
G4622.s: Sion (i.e. Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively, the Church (militant or triumphant)

G4623.d:
σιωπάω, -ῶ
(σιωπή, silence) [in LXX for חָשָׁה, חָרַשׁ hi., etc. ;]
to be silent or still, keep silence: Mat.20:31 26:63, Mrk.3:4 9:34 10:48 14:61, Luk.19:4, Act.18:9; of one dumb, Luk.1:20 (cf. 4Ma.10:18); addressed rhetorically to the sea, σιώπα, Mrk.4:39.†
SYN.: ἡσυχάζω, σιγάω (which see) (AS)
G4623.s: properly, muteness, i.e. involuntary stillness, or inability to speak; and thus differing from G4602 (σιγή), which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to be dumb (but not deaf also, like 2974 properly); figuratively, to be calm (as quiet water)

G4624.d:
σκανδαλίζω
(σκάνδαλον), [in LXX: Dan LXX 11:41 (כָּשַׁל ni.), Sir.9:5 (Sir.35:15 32:15) (יָקֹשׁ ho.) Sir.23:8 (also in Aq., Sm., Th., and in Psa Sol Psa.16:7; not elsewhere, except NT and eccl.)* ;]
prop., to put a snare or stumbling-block in the way; in NT always metaphorically of that which hinders right conduct or thought, to cause to stumble: with accusative of person(s), Mat.5:29-30 17:27 18:6, 8-9 Mrk.9:42-43, 45 9:47 Luk.17:2, Jhn.6:61, 1Co.8:13. Pass., to be made to stumble, to stumble: Mat.11:6 13:21, 57 15:12 24:10 26:31, 33, Mrk.4:17 6:3 14:27, 29, Luk.7:23, Jhn.16:1, Rom.14:21 (WH, R, txt., om.), 2Co.11:29,†
(AS)
G4624.s: to entrap, i.e. trip up (figuratively, stumble (transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure)

G4625.d:
σκάνδαλον, -ου, τό
(late form of the rare word σκανδάληθρον, see LS, see word) [in LXX chiefly for מוֹקֵשׁ, מִכְשׁוֹל ;]
prop., the bait-stick of a trap, a snare, stumbling-block (Lev.19:14, Jdth.5:1): figuratively, Rom.9:33, 1Pe.2:8 (Isa.8:14; aliter in LXX; στερεὸν σκανδάλου in Aq.). Metaphorical, of that which causes error or sin;
__(a) of persons: Mat.13:41 16:23; Χριστὸς ἐσταυρωμένος, 1Co.1:23;
__(b) of things: Mat.18:7, Rom.11:9" (LXX) Rom.14:13, 1Jn.2:10 Rev.2:14; τὸ σ. τοῦ σταυροῦ, Gal.5:11; pl., Mat.18:7, Luk.17:1, Rom.16:17.†
SYN.: πρόσκομμα (AS)
G4625.s: a trap-stick (bent sapling), i.e. snare (figuratively, cause of displeasure or sin)
G4625.o: ("scandal"); probably from a derivative of G2578 (κάμπτω);
G4625.k: occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends, stumblingblock

G4627.d:
σκάφη, -ης, ἡ
(σκάπτω), [in LXX: Dan LXX Bel 1:32, TH Bel 1:33 * ;]
anything scooped out, esp. a light boat, skiff: Act.27:16, 30 27:32.†
(AS)
G4627.s: a "skiff" (as if dug out), or yawl (carried aboard a large vessel for landing)

G4628.d:
σκέλος, -ους, τό
[in LXX for רֶגֶל, etc. ;]
the leg from the hip downwards: ?Jhn.19:3-33 †
(AS)
G4628.s: through the idea of leanness); the leg (as lank)

G4629.d:
σκέπασμα, -τος, τό
(σκεπάζω, to cover),
a covering, esp. clothing: 1Ti.6:8.†
(AS)
G4629.s: perhaps akin to the base of G4649 (σκοπός) through the idea of noticeableness); clothing

G4632.d:
σκεῦος, -ους, τό
[in LXX chiefly for כְּלִי ;]
a vessel, implement (for exx. in various senses, see MM, xxii): Mrk.11:16, Luk.8:16, Jhn.19:29, Act.10:11, 16 11:5, Rom.9:21, Rev.18:12; pl., 2Ti.2:20, Rev.2:27; τὰ σ. τῆς λειτουργίας, Heb.9:21; pl., τὰ σ., utensils, goods, Mat.12:29, Mrk.3:27, Luk.17:31; id. of the tackle or gear of a ship (Xen., Polyb., al.); so in sing., τὸ σ., Act.27:17. Metaphorical, of persons: σ. ἐκλογῆς, Act.9:15; ὀργῆς, Rom.9:22; ἐλέους, Rom.9:23; σ. εἰς τιμήν (cf. Rom.9:21), 2Ti.2:21; of woman, ἀσθενέστερον σ., 1Pe.3:7; so perh. τ. ἑαυτοῦ σ., 1Th.4:4 (but see infr.); of the body, 2Co.4:7; so perh. 1Th.4:4 (but see supr., and see: κτάομαι).†
…
G4632.s: a vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus (literally or figuratively [specially, a wife as contributing to the usefulness of the husband])

G4633.d:
σκηνή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for אֹהֶל, also for מִשְׁכָּן, סֻכָּה, etc. ;]
a tent, booth, tabernacle: Mat.17:4, Mrk.9:5, Luk.9:33, Heb.11:9; αἱ αἰώνιοι σ., Luk.16:9; of the Mosaic tabernacle, Heb.8:5 9:2-3, 6 9:8, 21; σ. τ. μαρτυρίου, Act.7:44; of its heavenly prototype, Heb.8:2 9:11, Rev.13:6 15:5 21:3; of the temple, Heb.13:10; ἡ σ. τοῦ Μολόχ, Act.7:43 (LXX); metaphorically, ἡ σ. Δαυείδ Act.15:16 (LXX).†
(AS)
G4633.s: a tent or cloth hut (literally or figuratively)
G4633.o: apparently akin to G4632 (σκεῦος) and G4639 (σκιά);

G4634.d:
σκηνοπηγία, -ας, ἡ
(σκηνή, πήγνυηι), [in LXX for סֻכָּה, Deu.16:16 31:10, Zec.14:16, 18-19; I Est.5:51, 1Ma.10:21, 2Ma.1:9 2Mac 1:18 * ;]
prop., the setting up of tents or dwellings (Arist.); in LXX and NT, ἡ σ., ἡ ἑορτή τῆς σ. (called also ἑορτὴ σκηνῶν, Lev.23:34, al.; see Deiss., LAE, 116 f.), the feast of Tabernacles: Jhn.7:2.†
(AS)
G4634.s: the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from the custom of erecting booths for temporary homes)

G4635.d:
σκηνοποιός, -όν
(σκηνή, ποιέω),
making tents; as subst., ὁ σ., a tent-maker: Act.18:3.†
(AS)

G4636.d:
σκῆνος, -ους, τό
[in LXX: Wis.9:15 * ;]
= σκηνή,
a tent, tabernacle (C.1., 3071). Metaphorical, of the body as the tabernacle of the soul: 2Co.5:1 5:4.†
(AS)
G4636.s: a hut or temporary residence, i.e. (figuratively) the human body (as the abode of the spirit)

G4637.d:
σκηνόω, -ῶ
(σκηνή), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁכַן ;]
to have one's tabernacle, to dwell (in π. of temporary dwelling, see MM, Exp., xxii): before ἐπί, with accusative of person(s), Rev.7:15; before ἐν, with dative of person(s), Jhn.1:14; id. with dative loc., Rev.12:12 13:6; before μετά, with genitive of person(s), Rev.21:3 (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκηνόω).†
(AS)
G4637.s: to tent or encamp, i.e. (figuratively) to occupy (as a mansion) or (specially), to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle of old, a symbol of protection and communion)

G4638.d:
σκήνωμα, -τος, τό
(σκηνόω), [in LXX chiefly for אֹהֶל ;]
a tent, tabernacle (cf. σκηνή, σκῆνος): of the temple as God's dwelling (Psa.132:5, al.), Act.7:46. Metaphorical, of the body: 2Pe.1:13-14.†
(AS)
G4638.s: an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God's residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul)

G4639.d:
σκιά, -ᾶς, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for צֵל, 4Ki.20:9 ff., Psa.57:1, al.; but σ. and σ. θανάτου are also used for צַלְמָוֶת, Job.3:5, Psa.3:4, Isa.9:2 (1) (see ICC, in l), al. ;]
__1. shadow, shade, caused by interception of light: Mrk.4:32, Act.5:15; metaphorically, σ. θανάτου, of ignorance and error, Mat.4:16, Luk.1:79" (LXX) .
__2. a shadow, the image or outline cast by an object: figuratively, ὑπόδειγμα καὶ σ., Heb.8:5; opposite to σῶμα, Col.2:17; opposite to εἰκών, Heb.10:1.†
(AS)
G4639.s: "shade" or a shadow (literally or figuratively (darkness of error or an adumbration))

G4640.d:
σκιρτάω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Gen.25:22 (רָצַץ hithpo.), Psa.114:4, 6 (רָקַד), etc. ;]
to leap: Luk.1:41, 44 6:23.†
(AS)
G4640.s: to jump, i.e. sympathetically move (as the quickening of a fetus)

G4641.d:
σκληρο-καρδία, -ας, ἡ
(σκληρός, καρδία), [in LXX: Deu.10:16, Jer.4:4 (לֵבָב עׇרְלָה), Sir.16:10 (cf. καρδία σκληρά, Sir.3:26-27) * ;]
hardness of heart: Mat.19:8, Mrk.10:5 16:14.†
(AS)
G4641.o: feminine of a compound of G4642 (σκληρός) and G2588 (καρδία);

G4642.d:
σκληρός, -ά, -όν
(σκέλλω, to dry), [in LXX chiefly for קָשָׁה ;]
hard to the touch, rough, harsh, (opposite to μαλακός); metaphorically, in various uses;
__(a) of men, hard, stern, severe: Mat.25:24;
__(b) of things, hard, rough, violent: σκληρόν σοι (ἐστι), Act.26:14; λόγος, Jhn.6:60; ἄνεμος, Jas.3:4; σκληρὰ λαλεῖν, Ju 15.†
SYN.: αὐστηρός, q.v (AS)
G4642.s: dry, i.e. hard or tough (figuratively, harsh, severe)

G4643.d:
σκληρότης, -ητος, ἡ
(σκληρός), [in LXX: Deu.9:27 (קְשִׁי), etc. ;]
hardness; metaphorically, of stubbornness: Rom.2:5.†
(AS)

G4644.d:
σκληρο-τράχηλος, -ον
(σκληρός, τράχηλος), [in LXX: Exo.33:3, 5 (עֹרֶף ־קָשֶׁה), etc. ;]
stiff-necked: metaphorically, Act.7:51.†
(AS)

G4645.d:
σκληρύνω
(σκληρός), [in LXX chiefly for קָשָׁה hi., also for חָזַק ;]
to harden. Metaphorical, to harden, make stubborn: with accusative of person(s), Rom.9:18; T. καρδίας (Psa.95:8), Heb.3:8, 15 4:7. Pass., to become hardened: Act.19:9, Heb.3:13.†
(AS)

G4646.d:
σκολιός, -ά, -όν
[in LXX: Deu.32:5 (עִקֵּשׁ), Pro.28:18 (σ. ὁδοῖς πορεύεσθαι, for: דֶּרֶךְ עָקַשׁ), Isa.40:4 (עָקֹב), etc. ;]
curved, bent, winding (opposite to ὀρθός, εὐθύς): Luk.3:5 (LXX). Metaphorical, crooked, perverse, unjust: Act.2:40, Php.2:15, 1Pe.2:18.†
(AS)

G4647.d:
σκόλοψ, -οπος, ὁ
[in LXX: Num.33:55 (שֵׂךְ), Hos.2:6 (8) (סִיר), Eze.28:24 (סִלּוֹן), Sir.43:19 * ;]
anything pointed, esp.
__1. in cl., a stake
__2. In Hellenistic vernacular, a thorn (cf. LXX, ll. with): σ. τῇ σαρκί, 2Co.12:7 (cf. MM, i., xxiii; DB, iii, 700 f.; Deiss., St. Paul, 62 f.; Field, Notes, 187).†
(AS)
G4647.s: withered at the front, i.e. a point or prickle (figuratively, a bodily annoyance or disability)
G4647.o: perhaps from the base of G4628 (σκέλος) and G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι);

G4648.d:
ακοπέω, -ῶ
(σκοπός), [in LXX: Est.8:13, 2Ma.4:5 * ;]
to look at, behold, watch, contemplate. Metaphorical, to look to, consider: with accusative of thing(s), 2Co.4:13, Php.2:4; with accusative of person(s), Rom.16:17, Php.3:17; before μή, Luk.11:35; σεαυτόν, before μή (see M, Pr., 192), Gal.6:1 (cf. ἐπι-, κατα-σκοπέω).†
SYN.: βλέπω, θεωρέω, ὁράω (AS)
G4648.s: to take aim at (spy), i.e. (figuratively) regard
G4648.k: consider, take heed, look at (on), mark

G4649.d:
σκοπός, -οῦ, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for צָפָה ;]
__1. a watcher, watchman (Eze.3:17, al.).
__2. a mark on which to fix the eye (Wis.5:12, 21, al.). Metaphorical, of an aim or object: Php.3:14.†
(AS)
G4649.s: perhaps akin to G4626 (σκάπτω) through the idea of concealment; compare G4629 (σκέπασμα)); a watch (sentry or scout), i.e. (by implication) a goal

G4650.d:
σκορπίζω
[in LXX for פּוּץ hi., etc. ;]
in vernac. and in Ion, and late writers for σκεδάννυμι (see MM, xxiii; Rutherford, NPhr., 295), to scatter: ὁ λύκος, Jhn.10:12; ὁ μὴ συνάγων μετ᾽ ἐμοῦ σκορπίζει, Mat.12:30, Luk.11:23; pass., before εἰς, with accusative loc., Jhn.16:32; of one who dispenses blessings, 2Co.9:9 (LXX) (of. δια-σκορπίζομαι).†
(AS)
G4650.s: to dissipate, i.e. (figuratively) put to flight, waste, be liberal
G4650.o: apparently from the same as G4651 (σκορπίος) (through the idea of penetrating);

G4651.d:
σκορπίος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for עַקְרָב ;]
a scorpion: Luk.10:19 11:12, Rev.9:3, 5 9:10 †
(AS)
G4651.o: probably from an obsolete (perhaps strengthened from the base of G4649 (σκοπός) and meaning to pierce);

G4652.d:
σκοτεινός (WH. -τινός), -ή, -όν
(σκότος), [in LXX chiefly for חֹשֶׁךְ and cogn. forms ;]
dark: opposite to φωτεινός, Mat.6:23, Luk.11:34, 36.†
(AS)

G4653.d:
σκοτία, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX: Job.28:3 (אֹפֶל), Mic.3:6 (חָשַׁךְ), Isa.16:3 * ;]
in late writers = σκότος,
darkness: Jhn.6:17 20:1. Metaphorical,
__(a) of secrecy (opposite to ἐν τ. φωτί): Mat.10:27, Luk.12:3;
__(b) of spiritual darkness: Mat.4:16, Jhn.1:5 8:12 12:35, 40, 1Jn.1:5 Jn 2:8-9 Jn 2:11.†
(AS)

G4654.d:
σκοτίζω
(σκότος), [in LXX for חָשַׁךְ ;]
to darken; in NT always pass., -ομαι, to be darkened: of the heavenly bodies, Mat.24:29, Mrk.13:24, Luk.23:45 (Rec., WH, mg.), Rev.8:12. Metaphorical, of the mind, Rom.1:21 11:10" (LXX) (cf. σκοτόω).†
(AS)

G4655.d:
σκότος, -ου, ὁ the more usual cl. form (cf.σ., τό),
darkness: Heb.12:18, Rec.†
(AS)

G4656.d:
σκοτόω, -ῶ
(σκότος), [in LXX for חָשַׁךְ, קָדַר, שָׁחַר ;]
to darken: Rev.9:2 16:10. Metaphorical, of the mind! pass., Eph.4:18 (cf. σκοτίζω).†
(AS)
G4656.s: to obscure or blind (literally or figuratively)

G4657.d:
σκύβαλον, -ου, τό
[in LXX: Sir.27:4 * ;]
refuse, esp. dung (see MM, ii, iii, xxiii): Php.3:8.†
(AS)
G4657.s: what is thrown to the dogs, i.e. refuse (ordure)
G4657.o: neuter of a presumed derivative of G1519 (εἰς) and G2965 (κύων) and G906 (βάλλω);

G4658.d:
Σκύθης, -ου, ὁ
Scythian, an inhabitant of Scythia, i.e. Russia and Siberia, a synonym with the Greeks for the wildest of barbarians: Col.3:11.†
(AS)
G4658.s: a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. (by implication) a savage

G4659.d:
σκυθρωπός, -όν (also -ή, -όν)
(σκυθρός, sullen, + ὤψ), [in LXX: Gen.40:7 (רַע), etc. ;]
of a gloomy countenance: Mat.6:16, Luk.24:17.†
(AS)
G4659.s: angry-visaged, i.e. gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance
G4659.o: from (sullen) and a derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι);

G4660.d:
σκύλλω
__1. in cl., to skin, flay, rend (Æsch., Anthol.).
__2. In Hellenistic writers, to vex, trouble, annoy: with accusative of person(s), Mrk.5:35, Luk.8:49; pass., ἐσκυλμένοι, distressed, Mat.9:36; mid., to trouble oneself, μὴ σκύλλου, Luk.7:6 (frequently in π.; see MM, i, ii, and cf. M, Pr., 89; Abbott, Essays, 87; Kennedy, Sources, 82).†
(AS)

G4661.d:
σκῦλον
(Rec. σκύλον), -ου, τό [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלָל ;]
mostly in pl., σκίλα, arms stripped from a foe, spoils: Luk.11:22.†
(AS)
G4661.s: something stripped (as a hide), i.e. booty

G4662.d:
σκωληκό-βρωτος, -ον
(σκώληξ, βιβρώσκω),
eaten of worms: Act.12:23 (cf. 2Ma.9:9, and see MM, xxiii) †
(AS)
G4662.o: from G4663 (σκώληξ) and a derivative of G977 (βιβρώσκω);

G4663.d:
σκώληξ, -ηκος, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for תּוֹלָע and cogn. forms ;]
a worm: of the kind which preys upon dead bodies, metaphorically, of fut. punishment, Mrk.9:48 (LXX, Isa.66:24; cf. Sir.7:17, Jdth.16:17).†
(AS)

G4664.d:
σμαράγδινος
(σμάραγδος, which see),
__1. of emerald (Luc., V.H., ii, 11).
__2. As in π. (Deiss., BS, 267), emerald-green: Rev.4:3 (for the construction, see Swete, in l; Zorell, see word).†
(AS)

G4665.d:
σμάραγδος, -ου, ἡ
(and in late writers also ὁ), [in LXX: Exo.28:9 (שֹׁהַם) Exo.36:17 (Exo.39:10) (בָּרֶקֶת), Eze.28:13 (יַהֲלֹם), etc. ;]
emerald or other trans parent green stone (LS, see word; DB, iv, 620; Swete, Ap., 67, 288): Rev.21:19.†
(AS)
G4665.s: the emerald or green gem so called

G4666.d:
σμύρνα
(in some MSS, ζμ-; see Bl., § 3, 9), -ης, ἡ, [in LXX for מֹר ;]
myrrh, a resinous gum used as an unguent and for em­balming: Mat.2:11, Jhn.19:39.†
(AS)

G4667.d:
Σμύρνα (T, Ζμ-; B1., § 3, 9), -ας, ἡ
Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean: Rev.1:11 2:8.†
Ζμύρνα, -ης, ἡ,
Rev.1:11 2:8 T, for Σμ-, which see (cf. B1., § 3, 9; Mayser, 204).†
(AS)
G4667.s: Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor

G4668.d:
Σμύρνα (T, Ζμ-; B1., § 3, 9), -ας, ἡ
Smyrna, an Ionian city on the Ægean: Rev.1:11 2:8.†
Ζμύρνα, -ης, ἡ,
Rev.1:11 2:8 T, for Σμ-, which see (cf. B1., § 3, 9; Mayser, 204).†
(AS)

G4669.d:
σμυρνίζω
(σιύρνα),
__1. intrans., to be like myrrh (Diosc., i, 79).
__2. Trans., to mingle or drug with myrrh: pass., Mrk.15:23.†
(AS)
G4669.s: to tincture with myrrh, i.e. embitter (as a narcotic)

G4670.s: Sodoma (i.e. Sedom), a place in Palestine

G4671.d:
αὐτός, -ή, -ό,
determinative pron., in late Gk. much more frequently than in cl. (WM, 178f.; Jannaris, HGG, §1399).
__1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., see infr., iii);
__(1) self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, Luk.5:37; αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, Jhn.2:25; αὐ.ὑμεῖς, Jhn.3:28; καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, Rom.15:14; αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, Jhn.2:24; αὐ. καὶ οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ, Mrk.2:25; ὑμεῖς αὐ., Mrk.6:31; esp. (as freq in cl.) αὐ. ὁ, Mat.3:4, Mrk.6:17, Jhn.16:27, 1Th.3:11, al.; in late Gk., sometimes weakened, ἐν αὐτῇ τ. ὥρᾳ, in that hour, Luk.10:21 (M, Pr., 91; MM, see word);
__(2) emphatic,…

G4672G.d:
Σολομών, -ῶνος (so prop., but Rec. has frequently -ῶν, -ῶντος, as also WH in Act.3:11 5:12; in Act.7:47 T has Σαλωμών, as LXX freq., indecl.; see B1., § 10, 1; Tdf., Prol., 104, 119; WH, App., 158), ὁ (Heb. שְׁלֹמֹה),
Solomon: Mat.1:6-7 6:29 12:42, Luk.11:31 12:27, Jhn.10:23, Act.3:11 5:12 7:47.†
(AS)
G4672G.s: Solomon (i.e. Shelomoh), the son of David

G4672H.d:
Σολομών, -ῶνος (so prop., but Rec. has frequently -ῶν, -ῶντος, as also WH in Act.3:11 5:12; in Act.7:47 T has Σαλωμών, as LXX freq., indecl.; see B1., § 10, 1; Tdf., Prol., 104, 119; WH, App., 158), ὁ (Heb. שְׁלֹמֹה),
Solomon: Mat.1:6-7 6:29 12:42, Luk.11:31 12:27, Jhn.10:23, Act.3:11 5:12 7:47.†
(AS)
G4672H.s: Solomon (i.e. Shelomoh), the son of David

G4673.d:
σορός, -οῦ, ἡ
[in LXX: Gen.50:26 (אָרוֹן), Job.21:32 A * ;]
__(a) a cinerary urn (Hom.);
__(b) a coffin (Hdt., i, 68, 3, a1.): Luk.7:14.†
(AS)
G4673.s: a funereal receptacle (urn, coffin), i.e. (by analogy) a bier
G4673.o: probably akin to the base of G4987 (σωρεύω);

G4674.d:
σός, -ή, -όν
possess. prop. of second of person(s),
thy, thine: Mat.7:3, al.; as subst., οἱ σοί, thy kinsfolk, friends, Mrk.5:19; τὸ σόν, what is thine, Mat.20:14 25:25; τὰ σά, thy goods, Luk.6:30
(AS)

G4675.d:
αὐτός, -ή, -ό,
determinative pron., in late Gk. much more frequently than in cl. (WM, 178f.; Jannaris, HGG, §1399).
__1. Emphatic (so always in nom. exc. when preceded by the art., see infr., iii);
__(1) self (ipse), expressing opposition, distinction, exclusion, etc., αὐ. ἐκχυθήσεται, Luk.5:37; αὐ. ἐγινώσκεν, Jhn.2:25; αὐ.ὑμεῖς, Jhn.3:28; καὶ αὐ. ἐγώ, Rom.15:14; αὐ. Ἰησοῦς, Jhn.2:24; αὐ. καὶ οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτοῦ, Mrk.2:25; ὑμεῖς αὐ., Mrk.6:31; esp. (as freq in cl.) αὐ. ὁ, Mat.3:4, Mrk.6:17, Jhn.16:27, 1Th.3:11, al.; in late Gk., sometimes weakened, ἐν αὐτῇ τ. ὥρᾳ, in that hour, Luk.10:21 (M, Pr., 91; MM, see word);
__(2) emphatic,…
G4675.k: X home, thee, thine (own), thou, thy

G4676.d:
σουδάριον, -ου, τό(Lat.),
handkerchief, kerchief: Luk.19:20, Act.19:12; used as a head covering for the dead, Jhn.11:44 20:7 (cf. Deiss., BS, 223).†
(AS)
G4676.s: a sudarium (sweat-cloth), i.e. towel (for wiping the perspiration from the face, or binding the face of a corpse)

G4677.d:
Σουσάννα, -ης
(cf. Dan LXX TH Su, inscr., 2, 7, al.)
Susanna: Luk.8:3.†
(AS)

G4678.d:
σοφία, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for חׇכְמָה ;]
skill, intelligence, wisdom, ranging from knowledge of the arts and matters of daily life to mental excellence in its highest and fullest sense;
__(a) of human wisdom: 1Co.2:1 2:4-5, Jas.3:15, Rev.13:18 17:9; σ. Σολομῶνος, Mat.12:42, Luk.11:31; Αἰγυπτίων, Act.7:22; Ἕλληνες σ. ζητοῦσιν, 1Co.1:22; σ. λόγου, 1Co.1:17; τ. σοφῶν, 1Co.1:19 (LXX); τ. κόσμου, 1Co.1:20-21 3:19; ἀνθρωπίνη, 1Co.2:13; σαρκική, 2Co.1:12;
of wisdom in spiritual things: Luk.21:15, Act.6:3, 10 7:10, 1Co.2:6, Col.1:28 2:23 3:16 4:5, Jas.1:5 3:13, 17, 2Pe.3:15; λόγος σοφίας, 1Co.12:8; πνεῦμα σοφίας, Eph.1:17; σ. καὶ φρόνησις,…
G4678.s: wisdom (higher or lower, worldly or spiritual)

G4679.d:
σοφίζω
(σοφός), [in LXX chiefly for חָכָם ;]
to make wise, instruct: with accusative of person(s), 2Ti.3:15 (cf. Psa.19:8 (Psa.119:98). As depon., -ομαι;
__(a) intrans., to become wise (I2Ki.4:27 (3Ki.5:11), Ecc.2:15, and frequently in Sir.7:5, al.);
__(b) trans., to invent, devise cleverly: pass., 2Pe.1:16
(cf. κατα-σοφίζομαι).†
(AS)
G4679.s: to render wise; in a sinister acceptation, to form "sophisms", i.e. continue plausible error

G4680.d:
σοφός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX chiefly for חָכָם ;]
skilled, clever, wise, whether in handicraft, the affairs of life, the sciences or learning: Rom.16:19, 1Co.3:10; of the learned, Rom.1:14, 22, 1Co.1:19-20 1:26-27 3:18-20; of Jewish teachers, Mat.11:25, Luk.10:21; Christian, Mat.23:34; of those en­dowed with practical wisdom, 1Co.6:5, Eph.5:15, Jas.3:13; of God, Rom.16:27; compar., τ. μωρὸν τ. θεοῦ σοφώτερον, 1Co.1:25.†
SYN.: συνετός, φρόνιμος (see: σοφία, SYN.) (AS)

G4681.d:
Σπανία, -ας, ἡ
(= cl. Ἑσπερία or Ἰβηρία; late writers adopted the Roman name, Ἱσπανία (1Ma.8:3) or Σ. as here),
Spain: Rom.15:24, 28.†
(AS)

G4682.d:
σπαράσσω
[in LXX: 2Ki.22:8 B (גָּעַשׁ hith.), Jhn.4:19 (הָמָה) Dan LXX 8:7 (שָׁלַךְ hi.), 3Ma.4:6 * ;]
__1. to tear, rend, mangle.
__2. to convulse: Mrk.1:26 (see Swete, in l) Mrk.9:26, Luk.9:39
(cf. συν-σπαράσσω).†
(AS)
G4682.s: apparently strengthened from G4685 (σπάω) through the idea of spasmodic contraction); to mangle, i.e. convluse with epilepsy

G4683.d:
σπαργανόω, -ῶ
(σπάργανον, a swathing-band) [in LXX: Job.38:9, Eze.16:4 (חָתַל pu.)* ;]
to swathe, wrap in swaddling-clothes: Luk.2:7, 12 (Hipp., Arist., Plut.).†
(AS)
G4683.s: from a derivative of the base of G4682 (σπαράσσω) meaning to strap or wrap with strips); to swathe (an infant after the Oriental custom)

G4684.d:
σπαταλάω, -ῶ
(σπατάλη, wantonness, luxury, Sir.27:13 *), [in LXX: Eze.16:49 (שָׁקַט hi.), Sir.21:15 * ;]
to live riotously: 1Ti.5:6, Jas.5:5 (Polyb.).†
SYN.: στρηνιάω, τρυφάω (see Tr., Syn., § liv) (AS)

G4685.d:
σπάω
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁלַף, ;]
in cl. poët. for ἕλκω; mostly used in mid. (cf. M, Pr., 157),
to draw: μάχαιραν, Mrk.14:47, Act.16:27,†
(AS)

G4686.d:
σπείρα, -ης
(on this form of genitive, see M, Pr., 38, 48; Bl., § 7, 1; Mayser, 12; Deiss., BS, 186), [in LXX: Jdth.14:11, 2Ma.8:23 2Mac 12:20 2Mac 12:22 * ;]
__1. (= Lat. spira) anything wound or rolled up, a coil.
__2. As a military term used (by Polyb. and later writers) of a body of soldiers, a maniple (third part of a cohort) or cohort (see Swete, Mk., 375; Westc., Jo., 251 f.): Mat.27:27, Mrk.15:16, Jhn.18:3, 12, Act.10:1 21:31 27:1.†
(AS)
G4686.s: a coil (spira, "spire"), i.e. (figuratively) a mass of men (a Roman military cohort; also (by analogy) a squad of Levitical janitors)
G4686.o: of immediate Latin origin, but ultimately a derivative of G138 (αἱρέομαι) in the sense of its cognate G1507 (εἱλίσσω);

G4687.d:
σπείρω
[in LXX chiefly for זָרַע ;]
to sow (seed): absol., Mat.6:26 13:3-4, 18 25:24, 26, Mrk.4:3-4, Luk.8:5 12:24, Jhn.4:36, 2Co.9:10; with accusative of thing(s), Mat.13:24, 27 13:37, 39, Mrk.4:32, Luk.8:5, 1Co.15:36-37; before εἰς, Mat.13:22, Mrk.4:18; ἐν, Mat.13:24, 31; ἐπί, with genitive, Mrk.4:31; ἐπί, with accusative, Mat.13:20, 23, Mrk.4:16, 20; παρά, with accusative, Mat.13:19. Metaphorical: 1Co.9:11 15:42-44, Gal.6:7-8, Jas.3:18; in proverbial sayings, Mat.25:24, 26, Luk.19:21-22, Jhn.4:37, 2Co.9:6, Gal.6:7; in interpretation of parables, Mat.13:19-23 Mrk.4:14-20 †
(AS)
G4687.s: to scatter, i.e. sow (literally or figuratively)
G4687.o: probably strengthened from G4685 (σπάω) (through the idea of extending);

G4688.d:
σπεκουλάτωρ, -ορος (Rec. -ωρος), ὁ (Lat. speculator),
__1. prop., a spy or scout.
__2. An executioner: Mrk.6:27 (see Swete, in l).†
(AS)
G4688.s: a speculator, i.e. military scout (spy or (by extension) life-guardsman)

G4689.d:
σπένδω
[in LXX chiefly for נָסַךְ hi. ;]
to pour out as a drink-offering, make a libation; pass., figuratively, σπένδομαι, I am poured out or offered as a libation (in the shedding of my life-blood): Php.2:17 (see Lft., in l), 2Ti.4:6 (for exx. from π., see Milligan, Selections, 114 f.; MM, xxiii).†
(AS)
G4689.s: to pour out as a libation, i.e. (figuratively) to devote (one's life or blood, as a sacrifice) ("spend")

G4690G.d:
σπέρμα, -τος, τό
(σπείρω) [in LXX chiefly for זֶרַע ;]
seed;
__(a) of plants: Mat.13:24, 27 13:37-38, 2Co.9:10; pl., Mat.13:32, Mrk.4:31, 1Co.15:33; metaphorically, of an escaping remnant (שָׂרִיד, Isa.1:9; cf. Wis.14:6; Plat., Tim., 23c; FlJ, Ant., xi, 5, 3), Rom.9:29;
__(b) of men (as γονή; Lat. semen genitale; so in cl.; cf. in LXX, Lev.15:16, al.): Heb.11:11; metaphorically, of the divine influence, 1Jn.3:9; by meton. (as frequently in poets), seed, offspring, posterity: Mat.22:24-25, Mrk.12:19-22, Luk.1:55 20:28" (LXX) Jhn.7:42 8:33, 37 Act.3:25 7:5-6 13:23, Rom.1:3 4:13, 18 9:7-8 11:1, 2Co.11:22, Gal.3:16, 19, 2Ti.2:8, Heb.2:16…
G4690G.s: something sown, i.e. seed (including the male "sperm"); by implication, offspring; specially, a remnant (figuratively, as if kept over for planting)

G4690H.d:
σπέρμα, -τος, τό
(σπείρω) [in LXX chiefly for זֶרַע ;]
seed;
__(a) of plants: Mat.13:24, 27 13:37-38, 2Co.9:10; pl., Mat.13:32, Mrk.4:31, 1Co.15:33; metaphorically, of an escaping remnant (שָׂרִיד, Isa.1:9; cf. Wis.14:6; Plat., Tim., 23c; FlJ, Ant., xi, 5, 3), Rom.9:29;
__(b) of men (as γονή; Lat. semen genitale; so in cl.; cf. in LXX, Lev.15:16, al.): Heb.11:11; metaphorically, of the divine influence, 1Jn.3:9; by meton. (as frequently in poets), seed, offspring, posterity: Mat.22:24-25, Mrk.12:19-22, Luk.1:55 20:28" (LXX) Jhn.7:42 8:33, 37 Act.3:25 7:5-6 13:23, Rom.1:3 4:13, 18 9:7-8 11:1, 2Co.11:22, Gal.3:16, 19, 2Ti.2:8, Heb.2:16…
G4690H.s: something sown, i.e. seed (including the male "sperm"); by implication, offspring; specially, a remnant (figuratively, as if kept over for planting)

G4691.d:
σπερμολόγος, -ον
(σπέρμα, λέγω)
a seed picker;
__(a) prop., of birds (Arist., Aristoph, al.);
__(b) in Attic slang, of an idler who lives on scraps picked up in the agora; hence, as subst., ὁ σ., an idle babbler: Act.17:18.†
(AS)
G4691.s: a seed-picker (as the crow), i.e. (figuratively) a sponger, loafer (specially, a gossip or trifler in talk)

G4692.d:
σπεύδω
[in LXX chiefly for מָהַר pi., also for בָּהַל pi., hi., etc. ;]
__1. most frequently intrans., to hasten: with inf. (as frequently in cl.), Act.20:16; ptcp. with indic., Luk.2:16; with imperat., Luk.19:5-6; σπεῦσον κ. ἔξελθε, Act.22:18
__2. Trans., with accusative;
__(a) to hasten, urge on, accelerate (as Hom., Od., xix, 137; Eur., Med., 152; Sir.33:8 (Sir.36:8): 2Pe.3:12, R, mg. (cf. Mayor and ICC, in l, but see infr.);
__(b) to desire eagerly (find., Pyth., iii, 110; Eur., Suppl., 161; Isa 165): 2Pe, l.with, R, txt. (but see supr.).†
(AS)
G4692.s: to "speed" ("study"), i.e. urge on (diligently or earnestly); by implication, to await eagerly

G4693.d:
σπήλαιον, -ου, τό
[in LXX chiefly for מְעָרָה ;]
a cave, cavern: Jhn.11:38, Heb.11:38, Heb.6:15; σ. (EV, den) λῃστῶν (Jhn.7:11), Mat.21:13, Mrk.11:17, Luk.19:46.†
(AS)
G4693.s: a cavern; by implication, a hiding-place or resort
G4693.o: neuter of a presumed derivative of (a grotto);

G4694.d:
σπιλάς, -άδος, ἡ
(on the gender in Ju, l.with, see Mayor, Ju., 41),
__1. poët. in cl., a rock or reef over which the sea dashes (Polyb., FlJ, al.). Metaphorical, of men whose conduct causes danger to others, Ju 12, R, txt. (but see infr.).
__2. In late writers = σπίλος (which see), a spot, stain; metaphorically, Ju, l.with, R, mg. (cf. Mayor, 41, but see supr.).†
(AS)
G4694.s: a ledge or reef of rock in the sea

G4695.d:
σπιλόω
[in LXX: Wis.15:4 * ;]
to stain, spot, defile: with accusative, Jas.3:6, Ju 23.†
(AS)
G4695.s: to stain or soil (literally or figuratively)

G4696.d:
σπίλος (Rec. σπῖλος), -ου, ὁ
__1. a rock, cliff (Arist., al.).
__2. In late writers = Att.. κηλίς (see Rutherford, NPhr., 87 f.), a spot, stain; metaphorically,
__(a) of moral blemish: Eph.5:27
__(b) of riotous and lascivious persons (cf. Dion. Hal., quoted by Mayor, in l): 2Pe.2:13.†
(AS)
G4696.s: a stain or blemish, i.e. (figuratively) defect, disgrace

G4697.d:
σπλαγχνίζομαι
(σπλάγχνον), [in LXX (act., -ίζω): Pro.17:5 A, 2Ma.6:8 (= -εύω) * ;]
to be moved as to the σπλάγχνα (which see), hence, to feel pity or compassion: absol., Luk.10:33 15:20; ptcp., σπλαγχνισθείς, with indic., Mat.18:27 20:34, Mrk.1:41; before ἐπί, with dative of person(s), Mat.14:14, Luk.7:13; ἐπί, with accusative, Mat.15:32, Mrk.6:34 8:2 9:22; ωερί, Mat.9:36. (The word is elsewhere found only in Sm: 1Ki.23:21, Eze.24:21, Test. Zeb., 4:6-7; see Thayer, see word; MM, xxiii quote Thumb, Hellen., 123 as practically confirming Lft. on Php.1:8, in the suggestion that the verb was a coinage of the Jewish dispersion.) †
(AS)
G4697.s: to have the bowels yearn, i.e. (figuratively) feel sympathy, to pity

G4698.d:
σπλάγχνον, -ου, τό mostly (in NT always) in pl., σπλάγχνα, -ων, τά,
[in LXX: Pro.12:10 (רַחַם, elsewhere rendered by οἰκτιρμοί, Psa.25:6 40:12 and by ἔλεος, Isa.47:6), Pro.26:22 (בֶּטֶן), Wis.10:5, Sir.30:7, 2Ma.9:5 (6), al. ;]
the inward parts (heart, liver, lungs, etc.; Lat. viscera): Act.1:18. Metaphorical, of the seat of the feelings and of the feelings themselves (in Gk. poets, of anger, anxiety, etc.), the heart, affections (the characteristic LXX and NT reference of the word to feelings of kindness, benevolence and pity, is found in π.; see MM, xxiii; cf. Lft. on Php.1:8): 2Co.6:12 7:15, Phm 7 12 20, 1Jn.3:17; σ. οἰκτιρμοῦ, Col.3:12; σ. καὶ οἰκτιρμοὶ, Php.2:1;…
G4698.s: an intestine (plural); figuratively, pity or sympathy

G4700.d:
σποδός, -oῦ, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for אֵפֶר ;]
ashes: Heb.9:13; ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σ. (Isa.58:5, Jhn.3:6, Dan LXX 9:3, al.), Mat.11:21, Luk.10:13.†
(AS)

G4701.d:
σπορά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(σπείρω), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:29 (זָרַע), 1Ma.10:30 * ;]
__1. a sowing.
__2. seedtime.
__3. seed sown (of human offspring, Soph., Tr., 316, 420): 1Pe.1:23
(cf. σπέρμα, and see Milligan, NTD, 105 f.).†
(AS)

G4702.d:
σπόριμος, -ον
(σπείρω) [in LXX: Gen.1:29, Lev.11:37 (זָרַע), Sir 40:22 א1 * ;]
fit for sowing, sown; as subst., τὰ σ., corn-fields: Mat.12:1, Mrk.2:23, Luk.6:1.†
(AS)
G4702.s: sown, i.e. (neuter plural) a planted field

G4703.d:
σπόρος, -ου, ὁ
(σπείρω), [in LXX chiefly for זֶרַע ;]
= σπορά,
__1. sowing or seedtime.
__2. seed sown (so usually in late Gk.): Mrk.4:26-27, Luk.8:5, 11, 2Co.9:10 a (LTr.); metaphorically, of almsgiving, 2Co.9:10 b.†
(AS)
G4703.s: a scattering (of seed), i.e. (concretely) seed (as sown)

G4704.d:
σπουδάζω
(σπουδή), [in LXX chiefly for בָּהַל ;]
to make haste; hence, to be zealous or eager, to give diligence: with inf. (see M, Pr., 205 f.), Gal.2:10, Eph.4:3, 1Th.2:17, 2Ti.2:15 4:9 4:21, Tit.3:12, Heb.4:11, 2Pe.1:10 3:14; with accusative and inf. (on this construction see Mayor in l; MM, xxiii), 2Pe.1:15 (for other constructions see LS, see word).†
(AS)
G4704.s: to use speed, i.e. to make effort, be prompt or earnest
G4704.k: do (give) diligence, be diligent (forward), endeavour, labour, study

G4705.d:
σπουδαῖος, -α, -ον
(σπουδή), [in LXX: Eze.41:25 * ;]
in haste; hence, zealous, eager, diligent, earnest: before ἐν, 2Co.8:22; compar., -οτεροσς 2Co.8:17 (here in superl. sense, see Bl., § 44, 3) 2Co.8:22.†
(AS)

G4706.d: - more earnestly diligently, seriously, earnestly  than others), i.e. very promptly
G4706.s: more earnestly than others), i.e. very promptly

G4708.d:
earnestly, zealously, with vigor; (compar.) all the more eager, with special urgency eagerly
earnestly, eagerly, diligently, Lk. 7:4; 2Tim. 1:17; Tit. 3:13; comparative σπουδαιοτέρως, more earnestly, with special urgency, Phil. 2:28
G4708.s: more speedily, i.e. sooner than otherwise

G4709.d:
σπουδαίως
adv. (σπουδαῖος), [in LXX: Wis.2:6 * ;]
__1. with haste or zeal, i.e. earnestly, zealously, diligently: Luk.7:4, 2Ti.1:17, Tit.3:13; compar., -οτέρως, Php.2:28 (RV, Lft., Weymouth, al., but see infr.)
__2. hastily, speedily: compar., -οτέρως, Php.2:28 (Thayer, Zorell, see word; ICC, in l, al., but see supr.).†
(AS)

G4710.d:
σπουδή, -ῆς, ἡ
(σπεύδω), [in LXX chiefly for בָּהַל, its parts and derivatives ;]
__1. haste, speed: μετὰ σ. (Wis.19:2), Mrk.6:25, Luk.1:39.
__2. zeal, diligence, earnestness: Rom.12:11, 2Co.7:11-12 8:7-8; ἐν σ., Rom.12:8 (see M, Pr, 104); before ὑπέρ, 2Co.8:16; σπουδὴν ἐνδείκνυσθαι, Heb.6:11; σ. παρεισφέρειν, 2Pe.1:5; πᾶσαν σ. ποιεῖσθαι, Ju 3 (see MM, xxiii; M, Pr., 214; Deiss., BS, 361, 364).†
(AS)

G4711.d:
σφυρίς (T, Rec. σπυρίς, see WH, App., 148; 131., § 6, 7), -ίδος, ἡ,
a flexible mat-basket for carrying provisions: Mat.15:37 16:10, Mrk.8:8, 20 Act.9:25 (see: κόφινος).†
(AS)

G4712.d:
στάδιον, -ου, τό pl., στάδια (Jhn.6:19, T), and metapl., στάδιοι (see B1., 9, 1),
[in LXX: Dan LXX 4:9, Sus 1:37, 2Ma.11:5 2Mac 12:9 ff. * ;]
a stadium, i.e.
__1. a measure of length = 600 Greek feet or 1⁄8 of a Roman mile Mat.14:24 (Rec., WH, txt., R, mg.), Luk.24:13, Jhn.6:19 11:18, Rev.14:20 21:16, and, this being the length of the Olympic course,
__2. a race-course: 1Co.9:24.†
(AS)
G4712.s: a stade or certain measure of distance; by implication, a stadium or race-course
G4712.o: from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι) (as fixed);

G4713.d:
στάρνος, -ου (ὁ and), ἡ
[in LXX: Exo.16:33 (צִנְצֶנֶת), 3Ki.12:24 14:3 (בַּקְבֻּק), Dan LXX Bel, 1:32 * ;]
prop., an earthen jar for racking off wine, hence, generally, a jar: Heb.9:4.†
(AS)
G4713.o: from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι) (as stationary);

G4714.d:
στάσις, -εως, ἡ
(ἵστημι), [in LXX chiefly for עָמַד, its parts and derivatives, also for רִיב (Pr 1714), etc. (see Deiss., BS, 158 f.) ;]
__1. a standing, place, status: σ. ἔχειν (Polyb., v, 5, 3; and cf. Lat. locum habere), Heb.9:8.
__2. insurrection, sedition: Mrk.15:7, Luk.23:19, 25, Act.19:40 24:5.
__3. In poets and late prose, strife, dissension (cf. MM, xxiii) Act.15:2 23:7, 10.†
(AS)
G4714.s: a standing (properly, the act), i.e. (by analogy) position (existence); by implication, a popular uprising; figuratively, controversy

G4715.d:
στατήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ
[in Aq., Sm., for מִשְׁקָל ;]
a stater;
__(a) a weight;
__(b) a coin (used by late writers of the Greek τετράδραχμον): Mat.17:27 26:16, WH, mg.†
(AS)
G4715.s: a stander (standard of value), i.e. (specially), a stater or certain coin

G4716.d:
σταυρός, -oῦ, ὁ
__1. an upright pale or stake (Hom., Hdt., Thuc., al.)
__2. In late writers (Diod., Plut., al.) of the Roman instrument of crucifixion, the Cross: of the Cross on which Christ suffered, Mat.27:32, 40 27:42, Mrk.15:21, 30 15:32, Luk.23:26, Jhn.19:17, 19 19:25, 31, Col.2:14, Heb.12:2; θάνατος σταυροῦ, Php.2:8; τ. αἷμα τοῦ σ., Col.1:20. Metaphorical, in proverbial sayings: αἴρειν (λαμβάνειν, βαστάζειν) τὸν σ., Mat.10:38 16:24, Mrk.8:34 10:21, 15:21, Luk.9:23 14:27 (for an interesting ex. of metaphorically use in π., see MM, xxiii) By meton., for Christ's death on the Cross: 1Co.1:17, Gal.5:11 6:12, 14, Eph.2:16, Php.3:18; ὁ λόγος ὁ τοῦ…
G4716.s: a stake or post (as set upright), i.e. (specially), a pole or cross (as an instrument of capital punishment); figuratively, exposure to death, i.e. self-denial; by implication, the atonement of Christ

G4717.d:
σταυρόω, -ῶ
(σταυρός), [in LXX: Est.7:9 (תָּלָה), Est.8:13 * ;]
__1. to fence with pales, impalisade (Thuc.).
__2. In late writers (Polyb., FlJ; but ἀνασταυρόω is more common) to crucify: with accusative of person(s), Mat.20:19 23:34 26:2 27:22 ff. Mat.28:5, Mrk.15:16 ff. Mrk.16:6, Luk.23:21, 23 23:33 24:7, 20, Jhn.19:6 ff., Act.2:36 4:10, 1Co.1:13 1:23 2:2 2:8, 2Co.13:4, Gal.3:1, Rev.11:8; metaphorically, Gal.5:24 6:14.†
(AS)
G4717.s: to impale on the cross; figuratively, to extinguish (subdue) passion or selfishness

G4718.d:
σταφυλή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX for עֵנָב ;]
a bunch of grapes: Mat.7:16, Luk.6:44, Rev.14:18. "σ. is properly the ripe grape-cluster as opposite to ὄμφαξ, cf. Gen.40:10, Job.15:33; as contrasted with βότρυς, it describes the grapes rather than the cluster on which they grow" (Swete, Apoc., 187 f.).†
(AS)
G4718.s: a cluster of grapes (as if intertwined)
G4718.o: probably from the base of G4735 (στέφανος);

G4719.d:
στάχυς, -υος, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for שִׁבֹּל ;]
an ear of corn: Mat.12:1, Mrk.2:23 4:28, Luk.6:1.†
(AS)
G4719.s: a head of grain (as standing out from the stalk)

G4720.d:
Στάχυς, -υος, ὁ
Stachys: Rom.16:9 (see Lft., Phi., 174; MM, xxiii).†
(AS)

G4721.d:
στέγη, -ης, ἡ
(στέγω) [in LXX: Gen.8:13 (מְכַסֶּה), etc. ;]
a roof: Mrk.2:4; of entering a house, εἰσέρχεσθαι ὑπὸ τὴν σ., Mat.8:8, Luk.7:6 (cf. MM, xxiii).†
(AS)
G4721.o: strengthened from a primary (a "thatch" or "deck" of a building);

G4722.d:
στέγω
(cf. Lat. tego), [in LXX: Sir.8:17 * ;]
__1. prop., to cover closely, to protect by covering, esp. to keep water in or out (Soph., Plat., al.).
__2. to cover, keep secret, conceal (Sir, l.with, Polyb., al.): 1Co.13:7, R, mg.
__3. By covering to ward of, bear up under, endure (for exx., see, Lft., Notes, 40; M, Th., 36): 1Co.9:12 13:7, 1Th.3:1 3:5.†
(AS)
G4722.s: to roof over, i.e. (figuratively) to cover with silence (endure patiently)

G4723.d:
στεῖρος, -ον also -α, -ον,
[in LXX for עָקָר ;]
barren: of a woman, Luk.1:7, 36 23:29, Gal.4:27" (LXX) .†
(AS)
G4723.o: a contraction from G4731 (στερεός) (as stiff and unnatural);

G4724.d:
στέλλω
[in LXX (mid.): Mal.2:5 (חָתַת ni.), Pro.31:24 (26), Wis.7:14 14:1, 2Ma.5:1, 3Ma.1:19 3Mac 4:11 * ;]
__1. prop., to set, place, arrange, fit out; hence, mid., to set oneself for, prepare (Wis, xi Mac, ll. with).
__2. to bring together, gather up (in Hom. of furling sails), hence to restrain, check; mid., to restrain or withdraw oneself, hold aloof, avoid: 2Co.8:20; before ἀπό, 2Th.3:6
(cf. ἀπο-, ἐξ-απο-, συν-απο-, δια-, ἐπι-, κατα-, συ(ν)-, ὑπο-στέλλω).†
(AS)
G4724.s: properly, to set fast ("stall"), i.e. (figuratively) to repress (reflexively, abstain from associating with)
G4724.o: probably strengthened from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι);

G4725.d:
στέμμα, -τος, τό
(στέφω, to put around, enwreath)
a wreath, garland: as used in sacrifices, Act.14:13.†
(AS)

G4726.d:
στεναγμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(στενάζω), [in LXX for אֲנָחָה, אֲנָקָה, נְאָקָה, etc. ;]
a groaning: Act.7:34 (LXX κραυγή), Rom.8:26.†
(AS)

G4727.d:
στενάζω
[in LXX for אָנַח ni., אָנַק, etc. ;]
to groan ("the word denotes feeling which is internal and unexpressed," Mayor, Ja., 162): Mrk.7:34, 2Co.5:2 5:4, Heb.13:17, Jas.5:9 (EV, murmur); ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, Rom.8:23 (cf. ἀνα-, συ(ν)-στενάζω).†
SYN.: see: κλαίω (AS)
G4727.s: to make (intransitively, be) in straits, i.e. (by implication) to sigh, murmur, pray inaudibly

G4728.d:
στενός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX for צַר, etc. ;]
narrow: fig (v MM, xxiii), Mat.7:13-14, Luk.13:24.†
(AS)
G4728.o: probably from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι);

G4729.d:
στενο-χωρέω, -ῶ
(στενός + χῶρος, space) [in LXX: Jos.17:15 (אוּץ), Jdg.16:16 (אָלַץ pi.), Isa.28:19 (20) (קָצַר) Isa.49:19 (צָרַר), 4Ma.11:11 * ;]
__1. to be straitened (cf. Isa.49:19); metaphorically, to be anxious (Hipp., al.).
__2. In late writers, trans., to straiten, compress (LXX, Diod., al.; π. ap. MM, xxiii): pass., trop., 2Co.4:8 6:12.†
(AS)
G4729.s: to hem in closely, i.e. (figuratively) cramp

G4730.d:
στενοχωρία, -ας, ἡ (see supr.)
[in LXX for צוֹק, etc. ;]
narrowness of space, want of room (Thuc., al.). Metaphorical (Ken., Polyb., Deu.28:53, Wis.5:3, al.), difficulty, distress: θλίψις καὶ (ἢ) σ., Rom.2:9 8:35 (EV, anguish); pl. (cf. Bl., § 32, 6; WM, 220), 2Co.6:4 12:10.†
SYN.: θλίψις, q.v (AS)
G4730.o: from a compound of G4728 (στενός) and G5561 (χώρα);

G4731.d:
στερεός, -ά, -όν
[in LXX: Num.8:4 (מִקְשָׁה); σ. πέτρα, Isa.5:28 (צַר), etc. ;]
hard, firm, solid: τροψή, Heb.5:12, 14; θεμέλιος, figuratively, 2Ti.2:19. Metaphorical,
__(a) in bad sense, hard, cruel (Hom., al.);
__(b) in good sense, steadfast, firm: τ. πίστει, 1Pe.5:9.†
(AS)
G4731.s: stiff, i.e. solid, stable (literally or figuratively)

G4732.d:
στερεόω, -ῶ
(στερεός), [in LXX: Isa.42:5 (רָקַע), Jer.5:3 (חָזַק pi.), etc. ;]
__(a) to make firm or solid;
__(b) to strengthen, make strong; with accusative of person(s), Act.3:16; τ. βάσεις, pass., Act.3:7. Metaphorical (cf. Je, l.with): τ. πίστει, pass., Act.16:5.†
(AS)
G4732.s: to solidify, i.e. confirm (literally or figuratively)

G4733.d:
στερέωμα, -τος, τό
(στερεόω), [in LXX: Gen.1:6 ff., Psa.19:1 150:1, Eze.1:22-26 10:1 13:5, Dan LXX, TH Dan.3:56, Dan.12:3 (רָקִיעַ), Deu.33:26 (שַׁחַק), Psa.18:2 71:3 (סֶלַע), Est.9:29, I Est.8:78 (82), Sir.43:1, 8, 1Ma.9:14 * ;]
a solid body;
__(a) a support, foundation (Arist., al.); metaphorically, strength (Psa.17:1-15 70:1-5, 1Mac, ll. with); steadfastness, firmness: τ. πίστεως, Col.2:5;
__(b) the dome of heaven (believed to be a solid canopy), the firmament (LXX).†
(AS)

G4735.d:
στέφανος, -ου, ὁ
(στέφω, to encircle), [in LXX chiefly for עֲטָרָה ;]
__1. that which surrounds or encompasses (as a wall, a crowd: Hom., al.).
__2. a crown, i.e. the wreath, garland or chaplet given as a prize for victory, as a festal ornament, or as a public honour for disting­uished service or personal worth (so to sovereigns, especially on the occasion of a παρουσία, which see; cf. Deiss., LAE, 372 ff.; on its use in LXX for the golden crown of royalty (prop., διάδημα, which see, cf. Hort and Mayor on Jas.1:12): Mat.27:29, Mrk.15:17, Jhn.19:2, 5, 1Co.9:25, Rev.4:4, 10 6:2 9:7 12:1 14:14. Metaphorical: Php.4:1, Rev.3:11; τ. δικαιοσύνης (cf. Deiss.,…
G4735.s: a chaplet (as a badge of royalty, a prize in the public games or a symbol of honor generally; but more conspicuous and elaborate than the simple fillet, G1238 (διάδημα)), literally or figuratively
G4735.o: from an apparently primary (to twine or wreathe);

G4737.d:
στεφανόω, -ῶ
(στέφανος), [in LXX for עָטַר ;]
with accusative of person(s),
to crown: of a victor, 2Ti.2:5. Metaphorical, δόξῃ κ. τιμῇ, Heb.2:7, 9" (LXX) .†
(AS)
G4737.s: to adorn with an honorary wreath (literally or figuratively)

G4738.d:
στῆθος, -ους, τό
[in LXX: Exo.28:23, 26 (29-30) (לֵב), etc. ;]
the breast: Jhn.13:25 21:10, Rev.15:6; as a sign of penitence, τύπτειν (εἰς) τὸ σ., Luk.18:13 23:48,†
(AS)

G4739.d:
στήκω late Pres., formed from perf., ἕστηκα (see B1., § 17; WH, App., 169; Kennedy, Sources, 158; M, Pr., 238; MM, xxiii),
[in LXX: Exo.14:13 A, Jdg.16:26 B, 3Ki.8:11 B * ;]
= ἵστημι, to stand: Mrk.3:31 11:25, Jhn.1:26, Rev.12:4 (ἕστηκεν T). Metaphorical, to stand firm, stand fast: absol., Gal.5:1 (but see Field, Notes, 189 f.), 2Th.2:15; before ἐν, Jhn.8:44 (ἕστηκεν, T, R, mg.), 1Co.16:13, Php.1:27 4:1; with dative, Rom.14:4.†
(AS)
G4739.s: to be stationary, i.e. (figuratively) to persevere
G4739.o: from the perfect tense of G2476 (ἵστημι);

G4740.d:
στηριγμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(στηρίζω), [in Sm.: Isa.3:1 * ;]
__1. a setting firmly, supporting.
__2. fixedness, firmness, steadfastness: 2Pe.3:17.†
(AS)

G4741.d:
στηρίζω
[in LXX for סָמַךְ, שׂוּם, etc. ;]
to fix, set fast, make fast: Luk.16:26; τ. πρόσωτον (Eze.6:2 13:17, al.; see Dalman, Words, 30 f.), Luk.9:51. Metaphorical, to confirm, establish: with, accusative, Luk.22:32, Act.18:23, Rom.1:11 16:25, 1Th.3:2 3:13, 2Th.3:3, Jas.5:8, 1Pe.5:10, Rev.3:2; id. before ἐν, 2Th.2:17, 2Pe.1:12.†
(AS)
G4741.s: to set fast, i.e. (literally) to turn resolutely in a certain direction, or (figuratively) to confirm
G4741.o: from a presumed derivative of G2476 (ἵστημι) (like G4731 (στερεός));

G4742.d:
στίγμα -τος, τό
(στίζω, to prick), [in LXX: Sng.1:11 (נְקֻדָּה) * ;]
a tattoed mark or brand: τὰ σ. τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, Gal.6:17 (see Lft., in l; Deiss., BS, 349; LAE, 303; MM, xxiii).†
(AS)
G4742.s: a mark incised or punched (for recognition of ownership), i.e. (figuratively) scar of service

G4743.d:
στιγμή, -ῆς, ἡ
(στίζω, to prick), [in LXX: Isa.29:5 (פֶּתַע), 2Ma.9:11 * ;]
a prick, a point; metaphorically, σ. χρόνου, a moment: Luk.4:5.†
(AS)
G4743.s: a point of time, i.e. an instant

G4744.d:
στίλβω
[in LXX: Nam.3:3 (לַהַב), etc. ;]
to shine, glisten: Mrk.9:3.†
(AS)

G4745.d:
στοά, -ᾶς, ἡ
[in LXX: Eze.40:18 (רִצְפָּה), etc. ;]
a portico: Jhn.5:2; used of the covered colonnade in the Temple (EV, porch), Jhn.10:23 Act.3:11 5:12 †
(AS)

G4746.d:
στοιβάς, see: στιβάς.
στιβάς, -άδος, ἡ,
[in Aq.: Eze.46:23 (טִירוֺת) * ;]
a litter of leaves or rushes: pl., Mrk.11:8 (Rec. στοιβ-).†
(AS)
G4746.s: a spread (as if tramped flat) of loose materials for a couch, i.e. (by implication) a bough of a tree so employed

G4747.d:
στοιχεῖον, -ου, τό
[in LXX: Wis.7:17 19:18, 4Ma.12:13 * ;]
prop., one of a row (στοῖχος) or series, hence,
__1. the shadow-line of a dial (Aristoph.).
__2. an elementary sound or letter of the alphabet (Anth., Plut., π.).
__3. the elements or rudiments of knowledge (Arist., al.) Heb.5:12; πτωχὰ σ., Gal.4:9; σ. τοῦ κόσμου, Gal.4:3, Col.2:8, 20 (but see infr.).
__4. The material elements of the universe (Plat.; LXX, ll. with): 2Pe.3:10 3:12.
__5. The heavenly bodies (Ding. Laert.).
__6. The demons or tutelary spirits of nature (Enoch., Test., Sol., al.; for this sense in Ga, Col, ll. with, see ICC on Col.2:8; Enc. Bibl., see word "…
G4747.s: something orderly in arrangement, i.e. (by implication) a serial (basal, fundamental, initial) constituent (literally), proposition (figuratively)
G4747.o: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of G4748 (στοιχέω);

G4748.d:
στοιχέω, -ῶ
(στοῖχος, a row), [in LXX: Ecc.11:6 (כָּשֵׁר) * ;]
to be in rows (of waves, plants, etc., as well as of men), to walk in line (esp. of marching in file to battle; Xen., Cyr., vi, 3, 34, al.). Metaphorical, in late writers, to walk by rule: Act.21:24; with dative, to walk by or in (as a rule of life), Rom.4:12 (cf. MM, xxiii), Gal.5:25 6:16, Php.3:16 (cf. συν-στοιχέω).†
(AS)
G4748.s: to march in (military) rank (keep step), i.e. (figuratively) to conform to virtue and piety
G4748.o: from a derivative of (to range in regular line);

G4749.d:
στολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(στέλλω), [in LXX chiefly for בֶּגֶד, also for לְבוּשׁ, etc. ;]
__1 1, an equipment, an armament (Æsch.).
__2. Equipment in clothes, apparel, esp. flowing raiment, a festal robe: (cf. Jon.3:6, Est.8:15, 1Ma.6:15): Mrk.12:38 16:5, Luk.15:22 20:46, Rev.6:11 7:9, 13-14 22:14.†
(AS)
G4749.s: equipment, i.e. (specially), a "stole" or long-fitting gown (as a mark of dignity)

G4750.d:
στόμα, -τος, τό
[in LXX chiefly for פֻּם ;]
the mouth: of man, Mat.15:11, Jhn.19:29, Act.11:8, al.; of animals, Mat.17:27, 2Ti.4:17 (fig.), Heb.11:33, Jas.3:3, al.; figuratively, of inanimate things (ποταμοῦ, Hom.), ἤνοιξεν ἡ γῆ τὸ σ., Rev.12:16; σ. μαχαίρας (Heb. חֶרֶב ־פֶּה, Gen.34:26 al.), the edge of the sword, Luk.21:24, Heb.11:34; esp. of the mouth as the organ of speech: opposite to καρδία, Mat.12:34, Rom.10:8, 10; in various phrases (some cl., some resembling Hebrew; cf. Bl., § 40, 9): ἀνοίγειν τ. σ. (see: ἀνοίγω); σ. πρὸς σ. (פֶּה ־אֵל פֶּה Num.12:8; = cl., κατὰ σ., Hdt., al.), face to face, II Jn 12, 3Jn.14; διὰ τοῦ σ. (of the Holy Spirit), Luk.1:70,…
G4750.s: the mouth (as if a gash in the face); by implication, language (and its relations); figuratively, an opening (in the earth); specially, the front or edge (of a weapon)
G4750.o: probably strengthened from a presumed derivative of the base of G5114 (τομώτερος);

G4751.d:
στόμαχος, -ου, ὁ
(στόμα),
prop., a mouth, an opening;
__(a) in early Gk. writers, the throat;
__(b) of the opening of the stomach (Arist.);
__(with) in later writers (Plut., al.), the stomach: 1Ti.5:23.†
(AS)

G4752.d:
στρατεία (on the orthogr., see Deiss., BS, 181 f.), -ας, ἡ
(οτρατεύω), [in LXX chiefly for צָבָא ;]
an expedition, a campaign, warfare: metaphorically, 2Co.10:4 (-τιά, T), 1Ti.1:18.†
(AS)
G4752.s: military service, i.e. (figuratively) the apostolic career (as one of hardship and danger)

G4753.d:
στράτευμα, -τος, τό
(στρατεύω), [in LXX: 1Ma.9:34, 2Ma.5:24 2Mac 8:21 2Mac 12:38 2Mac 13:13; pl., Jdth.11:8, 4Ma.5:1 * ;]
__1. = στρατεία (Hdt., al.).
__2. an army, a host: pl., Mat.22:7, Rev.9:16 19:14, 19; = soldiers, company of soldiers, Act.23:10, 27; pl., Luk.23:11.†
(AS)
G4753.s: an armament, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops (more or less extensive or systematic)

G4754.d:
στρατεύω and depon., -ομαι, so always in NT
(στρατός, an encamped army), [in LXX for מההּ hith., יָצָא, צָבָא; metaphorically, 4Ma.9:23 ;]
used of the general, to make war, do battle, and (chiefly) of the soldiers serving under him, to serve as a soldier: Luk.3:14, 1Co.9:7, 2Ti.2:4. Metaphorical (cf. MM, ii, xxiii), of spiritual conflict, to war, make war: 2Co.10:3, 1Ti.1:18, Jas.4:1, 1Pe.2:11.†
(AS)
G4754.s: to serve in a military campaign; figuratively, to execute the apostolate (with its arduous duties and functions), to contend with carnal inclinations
G4754.o: middle voice from the base of G4756 (στρατιά);

G4755.d:
στρατηγός, -οῦ, ὁ
(στραός, ἄγω), [in LXX chiefly for סָגָן (always in pl.), שַׂר ;]
__1. a military commander, a general (Hdt., al.).
