__2. A civic commander, a governor, magistrate (Hdt., Xen., al.): Act.16:20, 22 16:35-36, 38.
__3. The commander of the Levitical guard of the Temple, ὁ σ. τ. ἱεροῦ (EV, captain of the Temple): Act.4:1 5:24, 26; pl., Luk.22:4, 52.†
SYN.: ἄρχων (cf. EGT on Act.16:20; Ramsay, St. Paul, 217). (AS)
G4755.s: a general, i.e. (by implication or analogy) a (military) governor (prætor), the chief (præfect) of the (Levitical) temple-wardens
G4755.o: from the base of G4756 (στρατιά) and G71 (ἄγω) or G2233 (ἡγέομαι);

G4756.d:
στρατιά, -ᾶς, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for צָבָא ;]
__1. = στρατός, an army, a host: of angels (3Ki.22:19, al.), Luk.2:13; of the stars of heaven (Jer.8:2, 2Ch.33:3), Act.7:42.
__2. As sometimes in cl. (poët.), = στρατεία: 2Co.10:4, T (WH, RV, στρατεία).†
(AS)
G4756.s: from the base of G4766 (στρώννυμι), as encamped); camp-likeness, i.e. an army, i.e. (figuratively) the angels, the celestial luminaries
G4756.o: feminine of a derivative of (an army;

G4757.d:
στρατιώτης, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX; 2Ki.23:8 B1, 2Ma.5:12 2Mac 14:39, III Mac 3:12; 3Ma.3:4 Mac3 * ;]
a soldier: Mat.8:9, Mrk.15:16, Jhn.19:2, Act.10:7, al.; metaphorically, σ. Χριστοῦ Ἰησ., 2Ti.2:3.†
(AS)
G4757.s: a camper-out, i.e. a (common) warrior (literally or figuratively)
G4757.o: from a presumed derivative of the same as G4756 (στρατιά);

G4758.d:
στρατολογέω, -ῶ
(στρατός, λέγω),
to levy a troop, enlist soldiers: 2Ti.2:4 (Diod., Plut., al.).†
(AS)
G4758.s: to gather (or select) as a warrior, i.e. enlist in the army
G4758.o: from a compound of the base of G4756 (στρατιά) and G3004 (λέγω) (in its original sense);

G4759.d:
στρατοπέδ-αρχος (Rec. -ης), -ου, ὁ
(στρατόπεδον, ἄρχω), a military commander, esp. the Pretorian prefect: Act.28:16 (WH, om.).†
στρατοπεδάρχης, see: στρατοπέδαρχος
(AS)
G4759.s: a ruler of an army, i.e. (specially), a Prætorian præfect

G4760.d:
στρατό-πεδον, -ου, τό
(στρατός + πέδον, a plain), [in LXX: Jer.34:1 (חַיִל), 2Ma.8:12, al. ;]
__(a) a military camp;
__(b) an army: Luk.21:20.†
(AS)
G4760.s: a camping-ground, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops
G4760.o: from the base of G4756 (στρατιά) and the same as G3977 (πεδινός);

G4761.d:
στρεβλόω, -ῶ
(στρέφω), [in LXX: 2Ki.22:27 (פָּתַל hithp.), 3Ma.4:14, 4Ma.9:17 4Mac 12:4 4Mac 12:11 4Mac 15:14 * ;]
to twist, torture. Metaphorical (cf. 2Ki, l.with), to twist or pervert language: 2Pe.3:16.†
(AS)
G4761.s: to wrench, i.e. (specially), to torture (by the rack), but only figuratively, to pervert

G4762.d:
στρέφω
[in LXX chiefly for הָפַךְ, also for סָבַב, etc. ;]
to turn: with accusative of thing(s) dative of person(s), Mat.5:39; = ἀποσ-, to bring back, Mat.27:3 (cf. Isa.38:8); reflexively (WM, § 38, 1), to turn oneself, Act.7:42; with accusative before εἰς, = μετασ-, to change, Rev.11:6. Pass., reflexive, to turn oneself: before εἰς, Jhn.20:14, Act.7:39 13:46; ptcp., στραφείς, with indic., Mat.7:6 9:22 16:23, Luk.7:9 9:55 14:25 22:61, Jhn.1:38 20:16; id. before πρός, Luk.7:44 10:22 (WH, R, om.), Luk.7:23 23:28; metaphorically, to change: absol., Mat.18:3, Jhn.12:40 (cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ, ἐπι-, κατα-, μετα-, συ(ν)-, ὑπο-στρέφω).†
(AS)
G4762.s: to twist, i.e. turn quite around or reverse (literally or figuratively)
G4762.o: strengthened from the base of G5157 (τροπή);
G4762.k: convert, turn (again, back again, self, self about)

G4763.d:
στρηνιάω, ῶ
(στρῆνος, which see), [in Sm.: Isa.61:6 (אָכַל) * ;]
a word which first appears in the middle comedy (Rutherford, NPhr., 475 f.), to run riot, wax wanton: Rev.18:7-9 (cf. κατα-στρηνιάω).†
SYN.: σπαταλάω (which see), τρυφάω (AS)
G4763.o: from a presumed derivative of G4764 (στρῆνος);

G4764.d:
στρῆνος, -ους, τό
(cf. Lat. strenuus), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:28 (שַׁאֲנָן)* ;]
insolent luxury, wantonness: Rev.18:3 (a late word, first found in a Comic poet, B.C. 300, see Kennedy, Sources, 41, cf. στρηνιάω).†
(AS)

G4765.d:
στρουθίον, -ου, τό
[in LXX chiefly for צִפּוֹר ;]
dimin. of στρουθός
a sparrow: Mat.10:29, 31, Luk.12:6-7.†
(AS)

G4766.d:
στρωννύω or στρώννυμι
(seeBl., § 23, 1; Veitch, see word), [in LXX for יַצַע hoph., etc. ;]
to spread: ἱμάτια ἐν τ. ὁδῷ (εἰς τ. ὁδόν), Mat.21:8, Mrk.11:8; of making a bed, στρῶσον (sc. τ. κλίνην) σεαυτῷ, Act.9:34; of furnishing a room, ἐστρωμένον, spread with carpets or carpeted couches (cf. Eze.23:41), Mrk.14:15, Luk.22:12.†
(AS)
G4766.s: to "strew," i.e. spread (as a carpet or couch)
G4766.o: prolongation from a still simpler , (used only as an alternate in certain tenses) (probably akin to G4731 (στερεός) through the idea of positing);

G4767.o: from a derivative of an obsolete apparently primary (to hate);

G4768.d:
στυγνάζω
(στυγνός, sombre, gloomy, sullen, Isa.5:17, Wis.17:5, Dan LXX 2:12*), [in LXX: Eze.27:35 28:19 32:10 (שָׁמֵם)* ;]
to have a sombre, gloomy appearance: of the human countenance (RV, his countenance fell), Mrk.10:22; of the sky (so στυγνότης, Polyb., iv, 21, 1), Mat.16:3 ([WH], R, mg., om.).†
(AS)
G4768.s: to render gloomy, i.e. (by implication) glower (be overcast with clouds, or sombreness of speech)

G4769.d:
στύλος (T, στῦλος, as in cl.), -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for עַמּוּד, also for קֶרֶשׁ, etc. ;]
a pillar, regarded especially as a support: σ. πυρός, Rev.10:1; σ. ἐν τ. ναῷ, figuratively, Rev.3:12, Metaphorical, Gal.2:9; τ. ἀληθείας, 1Ti.3:15.†
(AS)
G4769.s: properly akin to the base of G2476 (ἵστημι)); a post ("style"), i.e. (figuratively) support

G4770.s: a "Stoic" (as occupying a particular porch in Athens), i.e. adherent of a certin philosophy

G4771.d:
σύ,
pron. of 2nd of person(s),
thou, you, genitive, σοῦ, dative, σοί, accusative, σέ, pl., ὑμεῖς, -ῶν, -ῖν, -ᾶς (enclitic in oblique cases sing., except after prep. (BL, §48, 3), though πρὸς σέ occurs in Mat.25:39). Nom. for emphasis or contrast: Jhn.1:30, 4:10, 5:33, 39, 44, Act.4:7, Eph.5:32; so also perhaps σὺ εἶπας, Mat.26:64, al. (M, Pr., 86); before voc., Mat.2:6, Luk.1:76, Jhn.17:5, al.; sometimes without emphasis (M, Pr., 85f.), as also in cl., but esp. as rendering of Heb. phrase, e.g. υἱός μου εἶ σύ (בְּנִי־אַתָּה, Psa.2:7), Act.13:33. The genitive (σοῦ, ὑμῶν) is sometimes placed bef. the noun: Luk.7:48, 12:30, al.; so also the enclitic…
G4771.o: the personal pronoun of the second person singular;

G4772.d:
συγγένεια, -ας, ἡ
(συγγενής), [in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁפָּחָה ;]
__1. kinship.
__2. By meton., kinsfolk, kindred: Luk.1:61, Act.7:3, 14 †
(AS)

G4773.d:
σνγγενής, -ές (dative pl., -εῦσιν, Mrk.6:4, Luk.2:44, as though from -εύς, see Swete, Mk., l.with; Bl., § 8, 6; cf. 1Ma.10:89 A א2 *;)
(σύν, γένος), [in LXX for דּוֹד, דּוֹדָה, מִשְׁפָּחָה ;]
__1. congenital, natural, innate.
__2. akin to; as subst., a kinsman: Mrk.6:4, Luk.1:58 2:44 14:12 21:16, Jhn.18:26, Act.10:24; of tribal kinship, Rom.9:3 16:7, 11 16:21.†
SYN.: ἴδιος, οἰκεῖος (which see) (AS)
G4773.s: a relative (by blood); by extension, a fellow countryman

G4774.d:
συν-γνώμη (Rec. συγγ-), -ης, ἡ
(συγγιγνώσκω, (a) to agree with; (b) to pardon), [in LXX: Sir prol.14 (B1N1 cm.) 313, 2Mac 14:20* ;]
__1. confession.
__2. fellow feeling; hence, concession, allowance: 1Co.7:6 (see ICC, in l).
__3. pardon.†
(AS)
G4774.o: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and G1097 (γινώσκω);

G4775.d:
συν-κάθημαι
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Psa.101:6 (יָשַׁב) * ;]
to sit together or with: with dative, Act.26:30; before μετά, with genitive, Mrk.14:54.†
(AS)
G4775.s: to seat oneself in company with

G4776.d:
περι-καθ-ίζω
[in LXX for חָנָה, לָחַם ni., etc. ;]
__1. to invest, besiege (Diod., 4Ki.6:24, 1Ma.11:61, al.).
__2. to sit around: Luk.22:55, L, txt.
† (AS)
G4776.s: to give (or take) a seat in company with

G4777.d:
συν-κακοπαθέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ,
to bear evil treatment along with, take one's share of ill-treatment: 2Ti.2:3; with dative commod., τ. εὐαγγελίῳ, 2Ti.2:18.†
(AS)
G4777.s: to suffer hardship in company with

G4778.d:
συν-κακουχέομαι (Rec. συγκ-), -οῦμαι, pass.
to endure adversity with: with dative of person(s), Heb.11:25. Not elsewhere.†
(AS)
G4778.s: to maltreat in company with, i.e. (passively) endure persecution together

G4779.d:
συν-καλέω
(Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ, [in LXX for קָרָא ;]
to call together: with accusative, Mrk.15:16, Luk.15:6, 9 (seel. -εῖται, see B1., § 55, 1), Act.5:21. Mid., to call together to oneself: Luk.9:1 (and seel. in Luk.15:6, 9 see supr.) Luk.23:13, Act.10:24 28:17.†
(AS)

G4780.d:
συν-καλύπτω
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX chiefly for כָּסָה pi. ;]
to veil or cover completely: with accusative, pass., Luk.12:2.†
(AS)

G4781.d:
συν-κάμπτω
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Psa.68:10, 23 (מעד hi.), etc. ;]
to bend completely, bend together: τ. νῶτον, figuratively, Rom.11:10 (LXX).†
(AS)
G4781.s: to bend together, i.e. (figuratively) to afflict

G4782.d:
συν-κατα-βαίνω
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Psa.49:17 (יָרַד), Wis.10:13, Dan LXX TH 3:49 * ;]
to go down with: Act.25:5. In late writers also metaphorically (Wis, l.with), to condescend, on WH. see Rutherford, NPhr., 485 f.†
(AS)

G4783.s: a deposition (of sentiment) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) accord with

G4784.d:
συν-κατα-τίθημι
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Exo.23:1 (שִׁית יָד), Exo.23:32 (בְּרִית), Da TH Su 1:20 * ;]
to deposit together. Mid., to deposit one's vote with, hence, to agree with, assent to: with dative, Luk.23:51.†
(AS)
G4784.s: to deposit (one's vote or opinion) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to accord with

G4785.d:
συν-κατα-ψηφίζω (Rec. συγκ-),
__1. to condemn with or together (Plut., Themist., 21).
__2. to vote one a place among: pass., Act.1:26. Not elsewhere .†
(AS)
G4785.s: to count down in company with, i.e. enroll among
G4785.o: from G4862 (σύν) and a compound of G2596 (κατά) and G5585 (ψηφίζω);

G4786.d:
συν-κεράννυμι
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Dan LXX 2:43 (עֲרַב ithpa.), 2Ma.15:39 * ;]
to mix or blend together, compound: with accusative, 1Co.12:24; ptcp. pf. pass., Heb.4:2, T, WH, mg., R, mg.; id., of persons, with dative instr., to be united with, agree with, ib., WH, txt., R, txt. (see Westc., in l).†
(AS)
G4786.s: to commingle, i.e. (figuratively) to combine or assimilate

G4787.d:
συν-κινέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ,
to move together. Metaphorical, to excite, stir up: τ. λαόν, Act.6:12 (Arist., Polyb., al.).†
(AS)
G4787.s: to move together, i.e. (specially), to excite as a mass (to sedition)

G4788.d:
συν-κλείω
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX chiefly for סגר ;]
to shut together, enclose, shut in on all sides: of a catch of fish, Luk.5:6; metaphorically (Psa.31:9, al.), Rom.11:32, Gal.3:22-23.†
(AS)
G4788.s: to shut together, i.e. include or (figuratively) embrace in a common subjection to

G4789.d:
συν-κληρο-νόμος (Rec. συγκ-), -ου, ὁ
a co-inheritor, fellow-heir: Rom.8:17, Eph.3:6; with genitive of thing(s), Heb.11:9, 1Pe.3:7 (for exx., see Deiss., LAE, 88 f.).†
(AS)
G4789.s: a co-heir, i.e. (by analogy) participant in common

G4790.d:
συν-κοινωνέω (Rec. συγκ-), -ῶ,
to have fellowship with or in (in cl., with genitive of thing(s), dative of person(s)): with dative of thing(s), Eph.5:11, Rev.18:4; id. with genitive of person(s), Php.4:14.†
(AS)
G4790.s: to share in company with, i.e. co-participate in
G4790.k: communicate (have fellowship) with, be partaker of

G4791.d:
συν-κοινωνός (Rec. συγκ-), όν,
partaking jointly of: with genitive of thing(s), Rom.11:17, 1Co.9:23; id. with genitive of person(s), Php.1:7; before ἐν, Rev.1:9.†
(AS)

G4792.d:
συν-κομίζω
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Job.5:26 (עָלָה) * ;]
__1. to bring together, collect (Hdt., Xen., al.).
__2. to take up a body for burial (Soph., Aj., 1048): Act.8:2 (see Field, Notes, 116).†
(AS)
G4792.s: to convey together, i.e. collect or bear away in company with others

G4793.d:
συν-κρίνω (Rec. συγκ-)
[in LXX chiefly for פָּתַר ;]
__1. to compound, combine: 1Co.2:13, R, mg.1 (Lft., Notes, 180 f.).
__2. In Arist. and later writers (Wis.7:29, a1.) = παραβάλλω, to compare: 1Co, l.with, R, txt. (Field, Notes, 168), 2Co.10:12
__3. In LXX, of dreams, to interpret (Gen.40:8, 1Co, l.with, R, mg. 2 (but see reff. supr.).†
(AS)
G4793.s: to judge of one thing in connection with another, i.e. combine (spiritual ideas with appropriate expressions) or collate (one person with another by way of contrast or resemblance)

G4794.d:
συν-κύπτω
(Rec. συγκ-), [in LXX: Job.9:27 (עָזַב), Sir.12:11 19:26 * ;]
__1. to bend forwards (Arist., al.).
__2. to be bowed down: Luk.13:11.†
(AS)
G4794.s: to stoop altogether, i.e. be completely overcome by

G4795.d:
συγκυρία, -ας, ἡ
(συγκυρέω, to happen), [in Sm.: 1Ki.6:9 (מִקְרֶה) * ;] (more frequently in late writers, συγκύρησις, -ημα),
chance, coincidence: κατὰ σ. (see MM, xxiii), Luk.10:31 (Hippocr., Eccl.).†
(AS)
G4795.s: from the base of G2962 (κύριος)); concurrence, i.e. accident
G4795.o: from a comparative of G4862 (σύν) and (to light or happen;

G4796.d:
συν-χαίρω
(Rec. συγ-), [in LXX: Gen.21:6 (צָחַק), 3Ma.1:8 R * ;]
__1. to rejoice with: with dative of person(s), Luk.1:58 15:6, 9, Php.2:17-18, EV; with dative of thing(s), 1Co.12:26 13:6.
__2. to congratulate (Æschin., Polyb., al.): Phi, l.with (Lft., in I.; cf. MM, xxiv).†
(AS)

G4797.d:
συν-χέω
(Rec. συγ-), [in LXX for בָּלַל, רָגַז, etc. ;]
to pour together, commingle, confuse; metaphorically, confound, throw into confusion, stir up trouble: Act.21:27 (cf. συν-χύννω).†
(AS)
G4797.s: to commingle promiscuously, i.e. (figuratively) to throw (an assembly) into disorder, to perplex (the mind)
G4797.o: from G4862 (σύν) and (to pour) or its alternate;
G4797.k: confound, confuse, stir up, be in an uproar

G4798.d:
συν-χράομαι
(Rec. συγ-), -ῶμαι, [in Al.: 1Ki.30:19 * ;]
to use together with. Metaphorical, with dative of person(s), to associate with: Jhn.4:9 (Polyb., a1.).†
(AS)
G4798.s: to use jointly, i.e. (by implication) to hold intercourse in common

G4799.d:
σύγχυσις, -εως, ἡ
(συγχέω), [in LXX: Gen.11:9 (בָּבֶל), 1Ki.5:6 5:12(11) 1Ki.14:20 (מְהוּמָה) * ;]
confusion: of a popular uproar, Act.19:29.†
(AS)

G4800.d:
συν-ζάω (Rec. συζ-),
to live with: opposite to συναποθανεῖν, 2Co.7:3; of life in union with Christ, here and hereafter, Rom.6:8, 2Ti.2:11.†
(AS)
G4800.s: to continue to live in common with, i.e. co-survive (literally or figuratively)

G4801.d:
συν-ζεύγνυμι
(Rec. συζ-), [in LXX: Eze.1:11, 23 (חָבַר) * ;]
to yoke to­gether: metaphorically, of union in wedlock, Mat.19:6, Mrk.10:9.†
(AS)
G4801.s: to yoke together, i.e. (figuratively) conjoin (in marriage)
G4801.o: from G4862 (σύν) and the base of G2201 (ζεῦγος);

G4802.d:
συν-ζητέω
(Rec. συζ-), -ῶ, [in LXX: Neh.2:4 AB1 (בָּקַשׁ pi.) * ;]
__1. to search or examine together (Plat.).
__2. In NT (and π., see MM, xxiii; also in MGr., see Kennedy, Sources, 155), to discuss, dispute: Mrk.1:27 12:28, Luk.24:15; before quæst. indir., Mrk.9:10; with dative of person(s), Mrk.8:11 Act.6:9; before πρός, with accusative of person(s), Mrk.9:14, 16, Act.9:29; id. before quæst. indir., Luk.22:23.†
(AS)
G4802.s: to investigate jointly, i.e. discuss, controvert, cavil

G4803.d:
συν-ζήτηαις (Rec. συζ-), -εως, ἡ
disputation: Act.28:29 (WH, R, txt., om.).†
(AS)

G4805.d:
σύν-ζυγος (Rec. ουζ-), or as WH, mg., Σύνζυγος, -ον
(συνζεύγνυμι), [in Aq., Eze.23:21 * ;]
a yoke fellow. Prob., as proper name, Σ. γνήσιε, genuinely Synzygus, S. properly so-called, Php.4:3 (see ICC, Lft., in l; MM, xxiii).†
(AS)
G4805.s: co-yoked, i.e. (figuratively) as noun, a colleague; probably rather as a proper name; Syzygus, a Christian

G4806.d:
συν-ζωο-ποιέω (Rec. συζ-), ῶ-,
to make alive or quicken together with; metaphorically, of the spiritual life: τ. Χριστῷ, Eph.2:5; σὺν τ. Χ., Col.2:13.†
(AS)

G4807.d:
συκάμινος, -ου, ἡ
[in LXX for שִׁקְמָה (pl.) ;]
the mulberry tree
(Lat. morus; cf. μόρον, 1Ma.6:34 *),
the sycamine: Luk.17:6. (In LXX, σ. appears to represent the συκόμορος (see: συκομορέα), but St. Luke distinguishes between the two; see ICC, in l; DB, iv, 634.) †
(AS)
G4807.o: of Hebrew origin (H08256) in imitation of G4809 (συκομωραία);

G4808.d:
συκῆ (contr. fr. συκέα), -ῆς, ἡ
(σῦκον), [in LXX for תְּאֵן ;]
a fig-tree: Mat.21:19-21 24:32, Mrk.11:13, 20-21 13:28, Luk.13:6-7 21:29, Jhn.1:49, 51, Jas.3:12, Rev.6:13.†
(AS)

G4809.d:
συκο-μορέα (Rec. -μωραία, L, -μωρέα), -ας, ἡ, more commonly (so Aq., Sm., Psa.78:47, Isa.9:10) συκόμορος
(σῦκον + μόρον, the black mulberry),
a fig-mulberry, a sycamore: Luk.19:4 (cf. συκάμινος).†
(AS)

G4810.d:
σῦκον, -ου, τό
[in LXX for תְּאֵן ]
a fig: Mat.7:16, Mrk.11:13, Luk.6:44 Jas.3:12.†
(AS)

G4811.d:
συκοφαντέω, -ῶ
(σῦκον, φαίνω), [in LXX: Gen.43:18 (גָּלַל hithpo.), Lev.19:11 (שָׁקַר pi.), Job.35:9, Psa.119:122, Pro.14:31 2:16 28:3, Ecc.4:1 (עָשַׁק) ;]
to act the συκοφάντης (on conjectures as to the origin of the term, see LS, see word), to accuse falsely (Aristoph., Xen., al.): Luk.3:14 (R, mg.) Luk.19:8 (RV, exact wrongfully; but cf. Hatch, Essays, 89 ff., see also Field, Notes, 56 f.; MM, xxiv).†
(AS)
G4811.s: to be a fig-informer (reporter of the law forbidding the exportation of figs from Greece), "sycophant", i.e. (genitive and by extension) to defraud (exact unlawfully, extort)
G4811.o: from a compound of G4810 (σῦκον) and a derivative of G5316 (φαίνω);
G4811.k: accuse falsely, take by false accusation

G4812.d:
συλαγωγέω, -ῶ
(σύλη, booty + ἄγω),
to carry off as spoil, lead captive (θυγατέρα, Heliod., Aeth., 10, 35): metaphorically, Col.2:8.†
(AS)
G4812.s: to lead away as booty, i.e. (figuratively) seduce
G4812.o: from the base of G4813 (συλάω) and (the reduplicated form of) G71 (ἄγω);

G4813.d:
συλάω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Ep. Jer.1:18 * ;]
with accusative of person(s), to strip, plunder, spoil: 2Co.11:8.†
(AS)
G4813.s: probably akin to G138 (αἱρέομαι); compare G4661 (σκῦλον)); to despoil

G4815.d:
συλ-λαμβάνω
[in LXX for תָּפַשׂ, הָרָה, etc. ;]
__1. with accusative, to bring together, collect.
__2. to seize, take: with accusative of person(s), as a prisoner, Mat.26:55, Mrk.14:48, Luk.22:54, Jhn.18:12, Act.1:16 12:3; pass., Act.23:27; mid., in sense of act., Act.26:21; σ. ἄγραν ἰχθύων, Luk.5:9.
__3. C. dative of person(s), to take part with, assist, succour; mid., in same sense: Luk.5:7, Php.4:3.
__4. Of a woman, to conceive: absol., Luk.1:24; before ἐν γαστρί, Luk.1:31; with accusative, Luk.1:36; ib. before ἐν τ. κοιλίᾳ, Luk.2:21; metaphorically, of lust producing sin, Jas.1:15.†
(AS)
G4815.s: to clasp, i.e. seize (arrest, capture); specially, to conceive (literally or figuratively); by implication, to aid

G4816.d:
συλ-λέγω
[in LXX chiefly for לָקַט ;]
to bring together, collect, gather up: with accusative of thing(s), Mat.13:28-30; pass., Mat.13:40; with accusative, before ἀπό, Mat.7:16; id. before ἐκ, Mat.13:41, Luk.6:44; before εἰς, Mat.13:48.†
(AS)
G4816.o: from G4862 (σύν) and G3004 (λέγω) in its original sense;

G4817.d:
συλ-λογίζομαι
[in LXX chiefly for חָשַׁב pi. ;]
__1. to compute.
__2. to reason: Luk.20:5.†
(AS)
G4817.s: to reckon together (with oneself), i.e. deliberate

G4818.d:
συν-λυπέω
(Rec. συλλ-), -ῶ, [in LXX: Psa.69:20, Isa.51:19 (נוּד) * ;]
to make to grieve with (Arist.). Pass., to be moved to grief by sympathy: before ἐπί, with dative, Mrk.3:5.†
(AS)
G4818.s: to afflict jointly, i.e. (passive) sorrow at (on account of) someone

G4819.d:
συμ-βαίνω
[in LXX for עָשָׂה, קָרָא, קָרָה, etc. ;]
__1. to stand with the feet together.
__2. to come together, come to terms.
__3. Of events, to come to pass, happen: with dative of person(s), Mrk.10:32, Act.3:10 20:19, 1Co.10:11, 1Pe.4:12, 2Pe.2:22; absol., τὰ σνμβεβηκότα, Luk.24:14 (cf. 1Ma.4:26); with accusative and nf., Act.21:35.†
(AS)
G4819.s: to walk (figuratively, transpire) together, i.e. concur (take place)
G4819.o: from G4862 (σύν) and the base of G939 (βάσις);

G4820.d:
συν-βάλλω
(Rec. συμ-), [in LXX: 2Ch.25:19 (גָּרָה hith.), Isa.46:6 (זוּל), Jer.43:3 (סוּת hi.), Wis.5:8, al. ;]
to throw together, hence,
__(a) of speech (before λόγους, Eur., al.), to discuss, confer (sc. λόγους): with dative of person(s), Luk.11:53, WH, mg., Act.17:18; before πρὸς ἀλλήλους, Act.4:15;
__(b) to reflect, consider, ponder: ἐν τ. καρδίᾳ, Luk.2:19;
__(with) to meet with, fall in with: Act.20:14; in hostile sense, εἰς πόλεμον, with dative (εἰς μάχην, Polyb.), Luk.14:31;
__(d) mid., to contribute (Polyb., al.; cf. MM, xxiv): Act.18:27.†
(AS)
G4820.s: to combine, i.e. (in speaking) to converse, consult, dispute, (mentally) to consider, (by implication) to aid, (personally) to join, attack
G4820.k: confer, encounter, help, make, meet with, ponder

G4821.d:
συμ-βουλεύω
[in LXX chiefly for יָעַץ ;]
__1. to advise, counsel: with dative of person(s), Jhn.18:14; id. before inf., Rev.3:18.
__2. Mid., to take counsel, consult: before ἵνα, Mat.26:4 ("reciprocal middle," see M, Pr., 157); with inf., Act.9:23.†
(AS)

G4822.d:
συν-βιβάζω
(Rec. συμ-), [in LXX: Exo.4:12, 15, Lev.10:11, Jdg.13:8, Psa.32:8 (יָרָה hi.); Exo.18:16, Deu.4:9, Isa.40:13 (יָדַע hi.), Isa.40:14 (בִּין hi.), Da TH Dan.9:22 (שָׂכַל hi.) * ;]
__1. to join or knit together, unite: Eph.4:16, Col.2:2 (but see infr.), Col.2:19.
__2. to compare, consider, conclude (Plat.): Act.16:10.
__3. to deduce, prove, demonstrate (Arist.): Act.9:22.
__4. As in LXX ("translation Greek," = ἐμβιβάζω, metaphorically), to teach, instruct: 1Co.2:16 Act.19:33, R, mg. (also in Vg., Col.2:2, instructi, but see supr.).†
(AS)
G4822.s: causative (by reduplication) of the base of G939 (βάσις)); to drive together, i.e. unite (in association or affection), (mentally) to infer, show, teach
G4822.k: compact, assuredly gather, intrust, knit together, prove

G4823.d:
1. to advise, counsel , Lat. consulere alicui, with dative pers. et infinitive, to advise one to do a thing, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.
2. without the infinitive, ς. τινί τι (Herdotus Historicus); ς. τι to recommend a measure, (Herdotus Historicus), attic:—;Pass., τὰ συμβουλευόμενα the advice given , (Xenophon Historicus)
3. absolute to advise, give advice , (Sophocles Tragicus); ὁ συμβουλεύων or -εύσας, an adviser , Lat. auctor sententiae, (Aristotle Philosopher)
4. Mid. to consult with a person, i. e. ask his advice , Lat. consulere aliquem, with dative,…
G4823.s: to give (or take) advice jointly, i.e. recommend, deliberate or determine

G4824.d:
συμβούλιον, -ου, τό
(σύμβουλος), [in LXX: 4Ma.17:17 א * ;]
a word of the Græco-Roman period (of. Lat. consilium, and see Deiss., BS, 238) = cl. συμβουλία (Arist., Xen.),
__1. counsel: σ. λαμβάνειν, Mat.12:14 22:15 27:7 28:12; διδόναι, Mrk.3:6 (ποιεῖν, Rec.); ποιεῖν, Mrk.15:1 (ἑτοιμάζειν, WH, mg.).
__2. By meton., a council (4Mac, l.with א; συνέδριον, AR): Act.25:12 (see MM, xxiv).†
(AS)
G4824.s: advisement; specially, a deliberative body, i.e. the provincial assessors or lay-court
G4824.o: neuter of a presumed derivative of G4825 (σύμβουλος);

G4825.d:
σύμβουλος, -ου, ὁ
(σύν, βουλή), [in LXX for יָעַץ and cogn. forms ;]
a counsellor, adviser: Rom.11:34 (LXX).†
(AS)

G4826G.d:
Συμεών, ὁ indecl., (Heb. שִׁמְעוֹן),
Simeon (so always AV; RV in Luk.2:25, 34 only), Symeon, a Heb. name for which the Gk. Σίμων, which see, was also used;
__1. the son of Jacob (Gen.29:33): Rev.7:7.
__2. An ancestor of our Lord: Luk.3:30
__3. An aged worshipper in the Temple: Luk.2:25, 34.
__4. One surnamed Niger: Act.13:1.
__5. The apostle Peter: Act.15:14, 2Pe.1:1 (R, txt., WH, txt., Σίμων).†
(AS)
G4826G.s: Symeon (i.e. Shimon), the name of five Israelites

G4826H.d:
Συμεών, ὁ indecl., (Heb. שִׁמְעוֹן),
Simeon (so always AV; RV in Luk.2:25, 34 only), Symeon, a Heb. name for which the Gk. Σίμων, which see, was also used;
__1. the son of Jacob (Gen.29:33): Rev.7:7.
__2. An ancestor of our Lord: Luk.3:30
__3. An aged worshipper in the Temple: Luk.2:25, 34.
__4. One surnamed Niger: Act.13:1.
__5. The apostle Peter: Act.15:14, 2Pe.1:1 (R, txt., WH, txt., Σίμων).†
(AS)
G4826H.s: Symeon (i.e. Shimon), the name of five Israelites

G4826I.d:
Συμεών, ὁ indecl., (Heb. שִׁמְעוֹן),
Simeon (so always AV; RV in Luk.2:25, 34 only), Symeon, a Heb. name for which the Gk. Σίμων, which see, was also used;
__1. the son of Jacob (Gen.29:33): Rev.7:7.
__2. An ancestor of our Lord: Luk.3:30
__3. An aged worshipper in the Temple: Luk.2:25, 34.
__4. One surnamed Niger: Act.13:1.
__5. The apostle Peter: Act.15:14, 2Pe.1:1 (R, txt., WH, txt., Σίμων).†
(AS)
G4826I.s: Symeon (i.e. Shimon), the name of five Israelites

G4826J.d:
Συμεών, ὁ indecl., (Heb. שִׁמְעוֹן),
Simeon (so always AV; RV in Luk.2:25, 34 only), Symeon, a Heb. name for which the Gk. Σίμων, which see, was also used;
__1. the son of Jacob (Gen.29:33): Rev.7:7.
__2. An ancestor of our Lord: Luk.3:30
__3. An aged worshipper in the Temple: Luk.2:25, 34.
__4. One surnamed Niger: Act.13:1.
__5. The apostle Peter: Act.15:14, 2Pe.1:1 (R, txt., WH, txt., Σίμων).†
(AS)
G4826J.s: Symeon (i.e. Shimon), the name of five Israelites

G4826K.d:
Συμεών, ὁ indecl., (Heb. שִׁמְעוֹן),
Simeon (so always AV; RV in Luk.2:25, 34 only), Symeon, a Heb. name for which the Gk. Σίμων, which see, was also used;
__1. the son of Jacob (Gen.29:33): Rev.7:7.
__2. An ancestor of our Lord: Luk.3:30
__3. An aged worshipper in the Temple: Luk.2:25, 34.
__4. One surnamed Niger: Act.13:1.
__5. The apostle Peter: Act.15:14, 2Pe.1:1 (R, txt., WH, txt., Σίμων).†
(AS)
G4826K.s: Symeon (i.e. Shimon), the name of five Israelites

G4827.d:
συν-μαθητής (Rec. συμμ-), -οῦ, ὁ
a fellow-disciple: Jhn.11:16 (on the use of συν- in such compounds as this, see Rutherford, NPhr., 255 f.).†
(AS)
G4827.o: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and G3129 (μανθάνω);

G4828.d:
συν-μαρτυρέω (Rec. συμμ-), -ῶ,
to bear witness with: Rom.2:15; with dative, Rom.8:16; before ὅτι, Rom.9:1.†
(AS)
G4828.s: to testify jointly, i.e. corroborate by (concurrent) evidence

G4829.d:
συν-μερίζω
(Rec. συμμ-), [in LXX: Pro.29:24 א2 (חָלַק) * ;]
to distri­bute in shares. Mid., to have a share in: 1Co.9:13 (Diod., al.).†
(AS)
G4829.s: to share jointly, i.e. participate in
G4829.o: middle voice from G4862 (σύν) and G3307 (μερίζω);

G4830.d:
συν-μέτοχος (Rec. συμμ-), -ον,
partaking together with; as subst., ὁ σ., a joint partaker (with dative of person(s) and genitive of thing(s), FlJ, BJ, i, 24, 6): with genitive of thing(s), Eph.3:6; with genitive of person(s), Eph.5:7 (Arist.).†
(AS)

G4831.d:
συν-μιμητής (Rec. συμμ-), -οῦ, ὁ
a fellow-imitator: with genitive obj., Php.3:17 (see ICC, in l). Not elsewhere.†
(AS)
G4831.o: from a presumed compound of G4862 (σύν) and G3401 (μιμέομαι);

G4832.d:
σύμ-μορφος, -ον
(σύν, μορφή),
__1. absol., similar (Luc.).
__2. con­formed to: with dative, Php.3:21; with genitive, Rom.8:29 (see B1., § 36, 11; 37, 6).†
(AS)

G4833.d: Pass. to be conformed to , τινι (New Testament) (ML)
G4833.s: to render like, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate

G4834.d:
συν-παθέω
(Rec. συμπ-), -ῶ, [in LXX: 4Ma.5:25 AR 4Ma.13:23 * ;]
to have a fellow feeling for or with, sympathize with or in: with dative of thing(s), Heb.4:15; dative of person(s), Heb.10:34 (Arist., Plut., al.).†
(AS)
G4834.s: to feel "sympathy" with, i.e. (by implication) to commiserate
G4834.k: have compassion, be touched with a feeling of

G4835.d:
συμπαθής, -ές
(σύν, πάσχω) [in LXX: Job.29:25 A (אָבֵל), 4Ma.5:25 א, 4Ma.13:23 4Mac 15:4 * ;]
__1. affected by like feelings, sympathetic: 1Pe.3:8.
__2. exciting sympathy (Jb, l.with; Dion. H.).†
(AS)
G4835.s: having a fellow-feeling ("sympathetic"), i.e. (by implication) mutually commiserative

G4836.d:
συν-παρα-γίνομαι
(Rec. συμπ-), [in LXX: Psa.83:8 (לָוָה ni.) * ;]
__1. to come up or be present together: before ἐπί, Luk.23:48.
__2. to come up to assist (Thuc., al.; 2Ti.4:16, Rec.).†
(AS)
G4836.s: to be present together, i.e. to convene; by implication, to appear in aid

G4837.d:
συν-παρα-καλέω (Rec. συμπ-), -ῶ,
to call upon or exhort together (Plat.). Pass., to be strengthened or comforted with and among: Rom.1:12.†
(AS)

G4838.d:
συν-παρα-λαμβάνω
(Rec. συμπ-), [in LXX: Gen.19:17 (סָפָה ni.), Job.1:4 (שָׁלַח ni), 3Ma.1:1 * ;]
to take along with: as a companion, with accusative, Act.12:25 15:37-38 (on the tenses, see M, Pr., 130), Gal.2:1.†
(AS)

G4839.s: to remain in company, i.e. still live

G4840.d:
συν-πάρειμι
(Rec. σνμπ-), [in LXX: Tob.12:12 ΑΒ, Pro.8:27 (?), Wis.9:10 * ;]
to be present together or with: with dative of person(s), Act.25:24.†
(AS)
G4840.s: to be at hand together, i.e. now present

G4841.d:
συν-πάσχω
(Rec. συμπ-), [in Al.: 1Ki.22:8 * ;]
__1. to suffer together or with: Rom.8:17, 1Co.12:28.
__2. to sympathize with (Plat., Arist.).†
(AS)
G4841.s: to experience pain jointly or of the same kind (specially, persecution; to "sympathize")
G4841.o: from G4862 (σύν) and G3958 (πάσχω) (including its alternate);

G4842.d:
συν-πέμπω (Rec. συμπ-)
to send together with: with accusative and dative, 2Co.8:22; id. before μετά, with genitive, 2Co.8:18.†
(AS)

G4843.d:
συν-περι-λαμβάνω (Rec. συμπ-),
__1. to enclose (Eze.5:3 (צוּר) *).
__2. to embrace: with accusative of person(s), Act.20:10.†
(AS)
G4843.s: to take by enclosing altogether, i.e. earnestly throw the arms about one
G4843.o: from G4862 (σύν) and a compound of G4012 (περί) and G2983 (λαμβάνω);

G4844.d:
συμπόσιον, -ου, τό
(συμπίνω), [in LXX: Est.7:7 (מִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן) Est.4:17, 1Ma.16:16, 2Ma.2:27, 3Ma.4:16 3Mac 5:36 3Mac 6:33; σ. οἴνου, Sir 34:31 (31:31) Sir.35:5 (32:5), Sir.49:1 * ;]
__1. a drinking party
__2. By meton., of the party itself, the guests (Plut); pl., σ. σ. (colloq.; see M, Pr., 97), in parties or companies: Mrk.6:39.†
(AS)
G4844.s: to partake a beverage in company

G4845.d:
συν-πληρόω
(Rec. συμπ-), -ῶ, [in LXX: Jer.25:12 (נָפַל) * ;]
__1. to fill up completely (Thuc., of manning ships): of a ship filling with water, and by meton., of those on board, Luk.8:23.
__2. to complete, fulfil: of time (Je, l.with, and see MM, xxiv), Luk.9:51, Act.2:1 (on the "durative inf.," see M, Pr., 233).†
(AS)
G4845.s: to implenish completely, i.e. (of space) to swamp (a boat), or (of time) to accomplish (passive, be complete)

G4846.d:
συν-πνίγω (Rec. συμπ-),
to choke: of thronging by a crowd, Luk.8:42. Fig., of seed, τ. λόγον, Mat.13:22, Mrk.4:7, 19, Luk.8:14.†
(AS)
G4846.s: to strangle completely, i.e. (literally) to drown, or (figuratively) to crowd

G4847.d:
συν-πολίτης (Rec. σνμπ-), -ου, ὁ
a fellow-citizen: pl., σ. τ. ἁγίων, opposite to ξένοι κ. πάροικοι, Eph.2:19 (Eur.; C.I., 6446; condemned by Atticists; see Rutherford, NPhr., 255 f.).†
(AS)
G4847.s: a native of the same town, i.e. (figuratively) co-religionist (fellow-Christian)

G4848.d:
συν-πορεύομαι
(Rec. σνμπ-), [in LXX chiefly for הָלַךְ ;]
__1. to journey together (Plat., al.): with dative of person(s), Luk.7:11 14:25 24:15.
__2. to come together: Mrk.10:1 (Plut., al.).†
(AS)
G4848.s: to journey together; by implication, to assemble

G4849.d:
1. a drinking-party, symposium , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.
2. the room in which such parties were given, drinking-room , (Lucian) (ML)
G4849.s: a drinking-party ("symposium"), i.e. (by extension) a room of guests
G4849.o: neuter of a derivative of the alternate of G4844 (συμπίνω);

G4851.d:
συμ-φέρω
[in LXX: Jer.33:14 (טוֹב), Pro.19:10 (נָאוֶה), Sir.30:19, al. ;]
__1. trans. to bring together: with accusative of thing(s), Act.19:19.
__2. Intrans., and mostly impers., συμφέρει, it is expedient, profitable or an advantage: 1Co.6:12 10:23, 2Co.8:10; with inf. (M, Pr., 210), Mat.19:10, Jhn.18:14; with dative, before ἵνα (Bl., § 69, 5), Mat.5:29-30 18:6, Jhn.11:50 16:7. Ptcp., ςυμφέρων, profitable: 1Co.12:7; pl., Act.20:20; (οὐ σ. sc. ἐστιν; = οὐ συμφέρει; cf. Thuc., iii, 44, 2), 2Co.12:1; as subst., τὸ σ., profit, Heb.12:10.†
(AS)
G4851.s: to bear together (contribute), i.e. (literally) to collect, or (figuratively) to conduce; especially (neuter participle as a noun) advantage
G4851.o: from G4862 (σύν) and G5342 (φέρω) (including its alternate);
G4851.k: be better for, bring together, be expedient (for), be good, (be) profit(-able for)

G4852.d:
σύν φημι (Rec. συμ-),
to consent, confess: with dative, before ὅτι, Rom.7:16.†
(AS)
G4852.s: to say jointly, i.e. assent to

G4853.d:
συμ-φυλέτης, -ου, ὁ
(σύν, φυλή; cf. σύμφυλος, Aq.: Zec.13:7; and see Rutherford, NPhr., 255 f.)
a fellow-tribesman, fellow-countryman: 1Th.2:14 (see M, Th., in l, and Intr. liii). Not found elsewhere.†
(AS)
G4853.s: a co-tribesman, i.e. native of the same country
G4853.o: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G5443 (φυλή);

G4854.d:
σύμ-φυτος, -ον
(συμφύω, to make to grow together) [in LXX: Zec.11:2 (בָּצַר), Est.7:7 Est.7:8 א2, Amo.9:13, 3Ma.3:22 * ;]
__1. congenital, innate (Plat., al.; 3Mac, l.with).
__2. grown along with, united with: τ. ὁμοιώματι τ. θανάτου αὐτσῦ (see Field, Notes, 155 f.), Rom.6:5.†
(AS)
G4854.s: grown along with (connate), i.e. (figuratively) closely united to
G4854.o: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G5453 (φύω);

G4855.d:
συν-φύω
(Rec. συμ-), [in LXX: Wis.13:13 * ;]
to cause to grow together. Pass., to grow together or with (Plat. al.): Luk.8:7.†
(AS)

G4856.d:
συμ-φωνέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX: Gen.14:3 (H2266) 2Ki.12:8 (9) (H225 ni.), Isa.7:2 (H5117), 4Ma.14:6 * ;]
prop., to agree in sound, be in harmony (Plat., Arist.). Metaphorical,
__(a) to agree with, agree together: Luk.5:36; with dative of thing(s), Act.15:15; before περί, Mat.18:19; pass., with dative of person(s), συνεφωνήθη ὑμῖν, Act.5:9;
__(b) to agree as to a price (Polyb., Diod.): with dative of person(s), genitive pret., Mat.20:13; before μετά . . . ἐκ, Mat.20:2.†
(AS)
G4856.s: to be harmonious, i.e. (figuratively) to accord (be suitable, concur) or stipulate (by compact)

G4857.d:
συμ-φώνησις, -εως, ἡ
(συμφωνέω),
concord, agreement: before πρός, with accusative of person(s), 2Co.6:15.†
(AS)

G4858.d:
συμφωνία, -ας, ἡ
(σύμφωνος), [in LXX: Dan LXX TH Dan.3:5, 15, TH Dan.3:7, 10 (סוּמְפּוֹנְיָה) 4Ma.14:3 A * ;]
__1. symphony, music: Luk.15:25
__2. a musical instrument (Polyb., al.; Da, ll. with; v MM, xxiv).†
(AS)
G4858.s: unison of sound ("symphony"), i.e. a concert of instruments (harmonious note)

G4859.d:
σύμφωνος, -ον
(ούν, φωνή), [in LXX: Ecc.7:14 (עֻמָּה), 4Ma.7:7 4Mac 14:7 * ;]
agreeing in sound. Metaphorical, harmonious, agreeing: ἐκ συμφώνου (for exx. from π., see Deiss., BS, 255), by agreement, 1Co.7:5.†
(AS)
G4859.s: sounding together (alike), i.e. (figuratively) accordant (neuter as noun, agreement)

G4860.d:
συμ-ψηφίζω
[in LXX: Jer.29:20 (Jer.49:20) A * ;]
to reckon together, count up: Act.19:19.†
(AS)

G4862.d:
σύν (old Att. ξύν),
prep. with dative,
expressing association, fellowship and inclusion. It gradually gave way to μετά, with genitive (cf. LS, see word; Bl., §41, 3), and is therefore comparatively infrequent in NT, being rare in Mat.4, Mrk.6, Jhn.3, and elsewhere (exx. Jas.1:11, 2Pe.1:18) only in Lk (Gosp. and Ac) and Paul. With, together with: of companionship and association, Luk.2:13, Jhn.21:3, Act.10:23, al.; εἶναι σύν τινι, Luk.7:12, Act.4:13, Php.1:23, al.; of partisanship, Act.4:13; οἱ σύν τινι, of attendants, companions or colleagues, Mrk.2:26, Luk.5:9, Act.5:17, al.; of assistance, ἡ χάρις τ. θεοῦ σὺν ἐμοί, 1Co.15:10; of two or more things together,…
G4862.s: with or together (but much closer than G3326 (μετά) or G3844 (παρά)), i.e. by association, companionship, process, resemblance, possession, instrumentality, addition, etc.

G4863.d:
συν-άγω
[in LXX chiefly for אָסַף, also for קָבַץ, etc. (cf. Kennedy, Sources, 128) ;]
to gather or bring together: of things, Jhn.6:12-13; before εἰς, Mat.3:12, al.; ἐκεῖ, Luk.12:18; ποῦ, Luk.12:17; συναγαγὼν πάντα (sc. εἰς ἀργύριον; see Field, Notes, 68, MM, xxiv), having sold off all: Luk.15:13; of persons, Jhn.11:52; esp. of assemblies, Mat.2:4, Jhn.11:47, Act.14:27, al. Pass., to be gathered or come together: Mat.22:41, Mrk.2:2, Luk.22:66, al.; before ἐπί Mrk.5:21, Act.4:27; πρός, Mat.13:2, Mrk.4:1, al.; εἰς, Rev.19:17; ἐν, Act.11:26; μετά, Mat.28:12; οὗ, Mat.18:20; ὅπου, Mat.26:57; ἐκεῖ, Jhn.18:2, al.
In late writers (see…
G4863.s: to lead together, i.e. collect or convene; specially, to entertain (hospitably)
G4863.k: + accompany, assemble (selves, together), bestow, come together, gather (selves together, up, together), lead into, resort, take in

G4864.d:
συν-αγωγή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for עֵדָה, also for קָהָל, etc. ;]
prop., a bringing together;
__1. of things,
__(a) a gathering in of harvest;
__(b) a collection of money.
__2. Of persons,
__(a) a collecting, assembling (Polyb.);
__(b) an assembly (MM, xxiv; Deiss., LAE, 101 ff.): Rev.2:9 3:9; esp. of a Jewish religious assembly, a synagogue: Luk.12:11, Act.9:2, al.; of a Christian assembly, Jas.2:2. By meton., of the building in which the assembly is held, a synagogue: Mat.10:17, Mrk.1:21, al. (cf. Cremer, see word ἐκκλησία)
SYN.: ἐκκλησία (which see) (AS)
G4864.s: an assemblage of persons; specially, a Jewish "synagogue" (the meeting or the place); by analogy, a Christian church

G4865.d:
συν-αγωνίζομαι
to strive together with, to help (prop., of sharing in a contest): with dative of person(s) and of thing(s), Rom.15:30.†
(AS)
G4865.s: to struggle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to be a partner (assistant)

G4866.d:
συν-αθλέω, -ῶ
= συναγωνίζομαι: with dative commod., Php.1:27; with dative of person(s), before ἐν, Php.4:3.†
(AS)
G4866.s: to wrestle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to seek jointly

G4867.d:
συν-αθροίζω
[in LXX chiefly for קָבַץ ;]
to gather together, assemble: with accusative of person(s), Act.19:25; pass., Act.12:12.†
ἀθροίζω
(ἀθρόος, assembled in crowds, MM, VGT, see word; θρόος, a noise, tumult), [in LXX chiefly for קָבַץ ;]
to Gather, assemble: Luk.24:33.†
(AS)

G4868.d:
συν-αίρω
[in LXX: Exo.23:5 (עָזַב) * ;]
to take up together: σ. λόγον (of which there are several exx. in π.; see Deiss., LAE, 118 f.; MM, i, xxiv; M, Pr., 160), to settle accounts, Mat.18:23-24; before μετά, C. genitive of person(s), Mat.25:19.†
(AS)
G4868.s: to make up together, i.e. (figuratively) to compute (an account)

G4869.d:
συν-αιχμάλωτος, -ου, ὁ
a fellow prisoner (prop., of a captive in war, see Lft., Col., 234): Rom.16:7, Col.4:10, Phm 23.†
(AS)

G4870.d:
συν-ακολουθέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: 2Ma.2:4 2Mac 2:6 * ;]
to follow along with, accompany: with dative of person(s), Mrk.14:51, Luk.23:49; before μετά, with genitive of person(s), Mrk.5:37.†
(AS)

G4871.d:
συν-αλίζω
[in Al.: Psa.141:4 * ;]
to assemble with: Act.1:4 (EV, mg., eating with, but on this rendering and on the force of the Pres. ptcp. here, see Field, Notes, 110).†
(AS)

G4872.d:
συν-ανα-βαίνω
[in LXX for עָלָה ;]
to go up with: with dative of person(s), before εἰς, with accusative loc., Mrk.15:41, Act.13:31.†
(AS)

G4873.d:
συν-ανά-κειμαι
[in LXX: 3Ma.5:39 * ;]
to recline with or together at table: Mat.14:9, Mrk.6:22, Luk.7:49 14:15; with dative of person(s), Mat.9:10, Mrk.2:15, Luk.14:10.†
(AS)
G4873.s: to recline in company with (at a meal)
G4873.k: sit (down, at the table, together) with (at meat)

G4874.d:
συν-ανα-μίγνυμι
(accusative to Bl., 8, -μείγνυμι), [in LXX: Hos.7:8 A ( hithpo.), Eze.20:18 A * ;]
to mix up together; pass., reflex, and metaphorically, to associate with (Plut., Ath., al.): 1Co.5:9 5:11, 2Th.3:14 (see M, Th., 117).†
(AS)
G4874.s: to mix up together, i.e. (figurative) associate with
G4874.o: from G4862 (σύν) and a compound of G303 (ἀνά) and G3396 (μίγνυμι);

G4875.d:
συν-ανα-παύομαι
[in LXX: Isa.11:6 (רָבַץ) * ;]
with dative of person(s), to lie down to rest with, sleep with. Metaphorical, to be refreshed in spirit with: Rom.15:32 (L, om.).†
(AS)
G4875.s: to recruit oneself in company with

G4876.d:
συν-αντάω, -ῶ
[in LXX for פָּגַע, פָּגַשׁ, קָרָא, קָרָה, etc. ;]
to meet with: with dative of person(s), Luk.9:18, 37 22:10, Act.10:25, Heb.7:1, 10. Metaphorical, of events, to happen, befall (Ding. L., Plut., al.): Act.20:22.†
(AS)
G4876.s: to meet with; figuratively, to occur
G4876.o: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G473 (ἀντί);

G4877.d:
συν-άντησις, -εως, ἡ
Rec. for ὑπάντησις (which see), Mat.8:34.†
(AS)

G4878.d:
συν-αντι-λαμβάνομαι
[in LXX: Gen.30:8 R (†), Exo.18:22, Num.11:17 (נָשָׂא), Psa.89:21 (כּוּן ni.) * ;]
to take hold with at the side for assistance; hence, to take a share in, help in bearing, and generally, help (with various constructions, see LXX, ll. with, Deiss., LAE, 83 f.): with dative, Luk.10:40, Rom.8:26.†
(AS)
G4878.s: to take hold of opposite together, i.e. co-operate (assist)

G4879.d:
συν-απ-άγω
[in LXX: Exo.14:6 (לָקַח) * ;]
to lead away with or together (Ex, l.with). Pass., metaphorically (as συμπεριφέρομαι, see LS, see word), to be carried away with: with dative, Gal.2:13, 2Pe.3:17; of accommodating one­self to (EV, condescend to) things or persons (on the meaning, see ICC, in I.; Field, Notes, 163), Rom.12:16.†
(AS)
G4879.s: to take off together, i.e. transport with (seduce, passively, yield)

G4880.d:
συν-απο-θνήσκω
[in LXX: Sir.19:10 * ;]
to die with or together: Mrk.14:31, 2Co.7:3 (see Meyer, in l), 2Ti.2:11.†
(AS)
G4880.s: to decease (literally) in company with, or (figuratively), similarly to

G4881.d:
συν-απ-όλλυμι
[in LXX chiefly for סָפָה ;]
to destroy with or together. Pass., to perish together (with): with dative of person(s), Heb.11:31.†
(AS)
G4881.s: to destroy (middle voice or passively, be slain) in company with

G4882.d:
συν-απο-στέλλω
[in LXX: Exo.33:2, 12 (שָׁלַח), I Est.5:2 * ;]
to send along with: with accusative, 2Co.12:18 (cf. MM, xxiv).†
(AS)
G4882.s: to despatch (on an errand) in company with

G4883.d:
συν-αρμολογέω, -ῶ
(ἁρμός, λέγω), = cl. συναρμόζω,
to fit or frame together: of the parts of a building, Eph.2:21; of the members of the body, Eph.4:16 (Eccl.).†
(AS)
G4883.s: to render close-jointed together, i.e. organize compactly
G4883.o: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of a compound of G719 (ἁρμός) and G3004 (λέγω) (in its original sense of laying);

G4884.d:
συν-αρπάζω
[in LXX: Pro.6:25 (לָקַח), 2Ma.3:27 2Mac 4:41, 4Ma.5:4 * ;]
"perfective " of ἁοπάζω (see M, Pr., 113),
__(a) to seize and carry away (so most commonly) : Act.27:15;
__(b) to seize and hold: Luk.8:29, Act.6:12 19:29.†
(AS)

G4885.d:
συν-αυξάνω
[in LXX: 2Ma.4:4, 4Ma.13:27 * ;]
to cause to increase or grow together. Pass., to grow together: Mat.13:30 (Xen., al.).†
(AS)

G4886.d:
σύν-δεσμος, -ου, ὁ
(συνδέω), [in LXX for קֶשֶׁר, קְטַר, etc. ;]
that which binds together, a bond: of the ligaments of the body, Col.2:19. Metaphorical, σ. ἀδικίας, Act.8:23; τ. τελειότητος, Col.3:14; τ. εἰρήνης, Eph.4:3 (see Lft., Col., ll. with).†
(AS)
G4886.s: a joint tie, i.e. ligament, (figuratively) uniting principle, control

G4887.d:
συν-δέω
[in LXX for שָׁבַץ, etc. ;]
__(a) to bind together;
__(b) to bind together with: pass., Heb.13:3.†
(AS)
G4887.s: to bind with, i.e. (passively) be a fellow-prisoner (figuratively)

G4888.d:
συν-δοξάζω
__1. to join in approving (Arist.).
__2. In NT only, to glorify together: pass., Rom.8:17.†
(AS)
G4888.s: to exalt to dignity in company (i.e. similarly) with

G4889.d:
σύν-δουλος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Est.4:7, 9 4:17, 23 5:3, 6 6:6, 13 (כְּנָת) * ;]
a fellow-servant: Mat.18:28-33 24:49; of servants of the same divine Lord, Col.1:7 4:7, Rev.6:11; so of angels, Rev.19:10 22:9.†
(AS)
G4889.s: a co-slave, i.e. servitor or ministrant of the same master (human or divine)

G4890.d:
συνδρομή, -ῆς, ἡ
(συντρέχω), [in LXX: Jdth.10:18, 3Ma.3:8 * ;]
concourse, esp. of a riotous gathering: Act.21:30 (Arist., Polyb., al.).†
(AS)

G4891.d:
συν-εγείρω
[in LXX: Exo.23:5 B2 (עָזַב), Isa.14:9 (עוּר pil.), 4Ma.2:14 * ;]
to raise together: metaphorically, of the Christian's mystical resur­rection with Christ, Eph.2:6; pass., Col.2:12 3:1.†
(AS)
G4891.s: to rouse (from death) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to revivify (spirtually) in resemblance to

G4892.d:
συνέδριον, -ου, τό
(σύν + ἕδρα, a seat) [in LXX: Pro.11:13 15:22, Jer.15:17 (סוֹד), Psa.26:4 (מַת), Pro.22:10 (דִּין) Pro.26:26 (קָהָל); Pro.24:7 27:22 31:23, 2Ma.14:5, 4Ma.17:17 * ;]
__1. a council (Plat., Xen., al.; LXX; in π., σ. τ. πρεσβυτέρων, Deiss., BS, 156): of a local Jewish tribunal, Mat.10:17, Mrk.13:9.
__2. The supreme ecclesiastical court of the Jews, the Sanhedrin (i.e. Talmudic סַנְהֵדְרִין = συνέδριον): Mat.5:22 26:59, Mrk.14:55 15:1, Luk.22:66, Act.5:21, 27 5:34, 41 6:12, 15 22:30 23:1, 6 23:15, 20 23:28 (WH, R, mg., om.) Act.24:20 of a meeting of the Sanhedrin, Jhn.11:47; of the place of meeting, Act.4:15.†
(AS)
G4892.s: a joint session, i.e. (specially), the Jewish Sanhedrin; by analogy, a subordinate tribunal
G4892.o: neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of G4862 (σύν) and the base of G1476 (ἑδραῖος);

G4893.d:
συν-είδησις, -εως, ἡ
(συνεῖδον), [in LXX: Ecc.10:20 (מַדָּע), Wis.17:11, Sir.42:18 א * ;]
__1. consciousness: with genitive obj., Heb.10:2, 1Pe.2:19.
__2. In ethical sense, innate discernment, self-judging consciousness, conscience (Stoics and late writers): Rom.2:15 9:1, 1Co.10:29, 2Co.1:12 4:2 5:11, 1Ti.4:2, Heb.9:14; σ. ἀγαθή, Act.23:1, 1Ti.1:5 1:19, 1Pe.3:16 3:21; ἀσθενής, 1Co.8:7 8:10; ἀσθενοῦσα, 1Co.8:12; ἀπρόσκοπος, Act.24:16; καθαρά, 1Ti.3:9, 2Ti.1:3; καλή, Heb.13:18; πονηρά, Heb.10:22; ὁ νοῦς καὶ ἡ σ., Tit.1:15; διὰ τὴν σ., Rom.13:5, 1Co.10:25 10:27-28; κατὰ σ., Heb.9:9; ὑπὸ (τῆς) σ., Jhn.8:1-59 [9] (Rec.), 1Co.10:29 (cf. Cremer, 233 ff.;…
G4893.o: from a prolonged form of G4894 (συνείδω);

G4894.d:
συν-εῖδον irreg. aorist of συνοράω (see: εἶδον),
[in LXX: 1Ma.4:21 א, 2Ma.2:24 2Mac 4:4 2Mac 4:41 R 2Ma.5:17 2Mac 7:4 2Mac 7:20 2Mac 8:8, 3Ma.2:8 A * ;]
__1. to see together or at the same time (Arist., Xen.).
__2. to see in one view, hence, of mental vision, to comprehend, understand (LXX, Polyb., Plut., al.) : Act.12:12 14:6 (on the related σύνοιδα, see see word).†
(AS)
G4894.s: to see completely; used (like its primary) only in two past tenses, respectively meaning to understand or become aware, and to be conscious or (clandestinely) informed of
G4894.k: consider, know, be privy, be ware of

G4895.d:
σύν-ειμι
(εἰμί to be), [in LXX: Jer.3:20 (רֵעַ), al. ;]
to be with: Luk.9:18 (WH, mg., συνήντησαν), Act.22:11.†
(AS)
G4895.s: to be in company with, i.e. present at the time
G4895.o: from G4862 (σύν) and G1510 (εἰμί) (including its various inflections);

G4897.d:
συν-εισ-έρχομαι
[in LXX: Job.22:4 (עִם בּוֹא), etc. ;]
to enter together: with dative of person(s), before εἰς, with accusative loc., Jhn.6:22 18:15.†
(AS)
G4897.k: go in with, go with into

G4898.s: a co-absentee from home, i.e. fellow-traveller
G4898.o: from G4862 (σύν) and the base of G1553 (ἐκδημέω);

G4899.d:
συν-εκ-λεκτός, -ή, -όν
chosen together with, co-elect: ἡ ἐν Βαβυλῶνι συνεκλεκτή (on the meaning, see ICC, in l), 1Pe.5:13.†
(AS)
G4899.s: chosen in company with, i.e. co-elect (fellow Christian)
G4899.o: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and G1586 (ἐκλέγομαι);

G4900.d:
συν-ελαύνω
[in LXX: 2Ma.4:26 2Mac 4:42 2Mac 5:5 * ;]
to drive together, force together: εἰς εἰρήνην, Act.7:26, Rec. (WH, RV, συνήλλασσεν).†
(AS)
G4900.s: to drive together, i.e. (figuratively) exhort (to reconciliation)

G4901.d:
συν-επι-μαρτυρέω, -ῶ
to join in attesting, bear witness together with: Heb.2:4 (Arist., Polyb., a1.).†
(AS)
G4901.s: to testify further jointly, i.e. unite in adding evidence

G4902.d:
συν-έπομαι
[in LXX: 2Ma.15:2, 3Ma.5:48 R 3Ma.6:21 * ;]
to follow with, accompany: with dative of person(s), Act.20:4.†
(AS)
G4902.o: middle voice from G4862 (σύν) and a primary (to follow);

G4903.d:
συνεργέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: I Est.7:2, 1Ma.12:1 * ;]
__1. prop., to work together (with): absol., Mrk.16:20, 1Co.16:16, 2Co.6:1; with dative, Jas.2:22; dative commod., Rom.8:28, T, R, txt. (but see infr.).
__2. In Hellenistic writers (M, Pr., 65), trans., to cause to work together (cf. ICC, in l): with accusative of thing(s), Rom.8:28 [WH] R, mg. (but see supr.).†
(AS)
G4903.s: to be a fellow-worker, i.e. co-operate

G4904.d:
συνεργός, -όν
[in LXX: 2Ma.8:7 Mac 14:5 * ;]
a fellow-worker: with genitive of person(s), Rom.16:3, 9 16:21, Php.2:25 4:3, 1Th.3:2, Rec., Phm 1 24; θεοῦ (cf. Lft., Notes, 41, 188), 1Co.3:9 (pl.), 1Th.3:2 [WH] R, mg. (R, txt., διάκονον τοῦ θ.; on the original reading, see ICC, in l); τ. χαρᾶς ὑηῶν, 2Co.1:24; τ. ἀληθείᾳ, III Jn 8; before εἰς, 2Co.8:23, Col.4:11.†
(AS)
G4904.o: from a presumed compound of G4862 (σύν) and the base of G2041 (ἔργον);
G4904.k: companion in labour, (fellow-)helper(-labourer, -worker), labourer together with, workfellow

G4905.d:
συν-έρχομαι
[in LXX for הָלַךְ, בּוֹא, אָסַף ni., etc. ;]
__1. (cl.) to come together, assemble: Mrk.3:20 14:53, T, WH, txt., Act.1:6 2:6 10:27 16:13 19:32 21:22 22:30 28:17, 1Co.14:26; before εἰς, with accusative loc., Act.5:16; ἐπὶ τ. αὐτό, 1Co.11:20 14:23; with dative of person(s), Mrk.14:53, WH, mg., R (πρὸς αὐτόν, see Field, Notes, 40), Jhn.11:33; ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ, 1Co.11:18; ἐνθάδε, Act.25:17; Mrk.6:33, WH, mg. (cf. WH, Intr., 95 ff.); ὅπου, Jhn.18:20; with inf., Luk.5:15; εἰς τ. φαγεῖν, 1Co.11:33; εἰς τ. ἧσσον, 1Co.11:17 11:34; of sexual intercourse (Xen., al.; γυναικί or absol.), Mat.1:18.
__2. In later sense (see exx. in Milligan, Selections,…
G4905.s: to convene, depart in company with, associate with, or (specially), cohabit (conjugally)
G4905.k: accompany, assemble (with), come (together), come (company, go) with, resort

G4906.d:
συν-εσθίω
[in LXX: Gen.43:32, Exo.18:12 (אָכַל), 4Ki.12:17 (בָּרָה), Psa.101:5 * ;]
to eat with one: with dative of person(s), Luk.15:2, Act.10:41 11:3, 1Co.5:11; before μετά, with genitive of person(s), Gal.2:12.†
(AS)
G4906.s: to take food in company with
G4906.o: from G4862 (σύν) and G2068 (ἐσθίω) (including its alternate);

G4907.d:
σύνεσις, -εως, ἡ
(συνίημι), [in LXX for בִּינָה and cogn. forms, מַשְׂכִּית, דַּעַת, חׇכְמָה, etc. ;]
__1. a running or flowing together (Hom.).
__2. (a) understanding: Luk.2:47, 1Co.1:19" (LXX), Eph.3:4, Col.1:9 2:2, 2Ti.2:7
__(b) the understanding, the mind or intelligence: Mrk.12:33.†
SYN.: see: σοφία (AS)
G4907.s: a mental putting together, i.e. intelligence or (concretely) the intellect

G4908.d:
συνετός, ή, -όν
(συνίημι), [in LXX for בִּין, חָכָם, etc. ;]
intelligent, sagacious, understanding: Mat.11:25, Luk.10:21, Act.13:7, 1Co.1:19" (LXX) .†
(AS)
G4908.s: mentally put (or putting) together, i.e. sagacious

G4909.d:
συν-ευ-δοκέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: 1Ma.1:57, 1Ma.4:28 א1, 2Ma.11:24 2Mac 11:35 * ;]
to join in approving, consent, agree to or with: absol., Act.22:20; with dative of person(s), Rom.1:32; with dative of thing(s), Luk.11:48, Act.8:1; with inf., 1Co.7:12-13 (chiefly in late writers).†
(AS)
G4909.s: to think well of in common, i.e. assent to, feel gratified with
G4909.k: allow, assent, be pleased, have pleasure

G4910.d:
συν-ευωχέω, -ῶ
to entertain together. Pass., to fare sumptuously or feast together or with: Ju 12; with dative of person(s), 2Pe.2:13 (Arist., Luc., al.).†
(AS)
G4910.s: to entertain sumptuously in company with, i.e. (middle voice or passive) to revel together
G4910.o: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of a presumed compound of G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of G2192 (ἔχω) (meaning to be in good condition, i.e. (by implication) to fare well, or feast);

G4911.d:
συν-εφ-ίστημι
to place over. Pass.,
__1. to stand over (Thuc.).
__2. to rise together: before κατά, with genitive of person(s) (against), Act.16:22.†
(AS)
G4911.s: to stand up together, i.e. to resist (or assault) jointly

G4912.d:
συν-έχω
[in LXX for עָצָר, חָבַר, etc. ;]
__1. to hold together (τ. συνέχον τ. πάντα, Wis.1:7): of closing the ears, Act.7:57 (τ. στόμα, Isa.52:15); to hem in, press on every side: Luk.8:45 19:43.
__2. to hold fast;
__(a) of a prisoner, to hold in charge (Luc.; cf. exx. in Deiss., BS, 160; MM, xxiv): Luk.22:63;
__(b) to constrain: 2Co.5:14; pass., Luk.12:50, Act.18:5 (τ. λόγῳ; cf. Field, Notes, 128), Php.1:23; in pass., of ills, to be seized or afflicted by, suffering from: Mat.4:24, Luk.4:38 8:37, Act.28:8.†
(AS)
G4912.s: to hold together, i.e. to compress (the ears, with a crowd or siege) or arrest (a prisoner); figuratively, to compel, perplex, afflict, preoccupy
G4912.k: constrain, hold, keep in, press, lie sick of, stop, be in a strait, straiten, be taken with, throng

G4913.d:
συν-ήδομαι
to rejoice together; with dative, to rejoice with or in: τ. νόμῳ τ. θεοῦ, Rom.7:22 (see Lft., Notes, 304).†
(AS)
G4913.s: to rejoice in with oneself, i.e. feel satisfaction concerning
G4913.o: middle voice from G4862 (σύν) and the base of G2237 (ἡδονή);

G4914.d:
συνήθεια, -ας, ἡ
(ἦθος), [in LXX: 4Ma.2:12 4Mac 6:13 4Mac 13:22 4Mac 13:27 * ;]
__1 1 intimacy.
__2. habit, custom: Jhn.18:39, 1Co.11:16; with genitive obj. (cf. Æschin., 23, 37, and see MM, xxiv), habitual use, force of habit with respect to, 1Co.8:7.†
(AS)
G4914.o: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and G2239 (ἦθος);

G4915.d:
συν-ηλικιώτης
(ἡλικία), = συνῆλιζ (Æsch.),
one of the same age, an equal in age: Gal.1:14.†
(AS)
G4915.s: a co-aged person, i.e. alike in years
G4915.o: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G2244 (ἡλικία);

G4916.d:
συν-θάπτω
to bury together with: in symbolical sense, of baptism, σὐτῷ (with Christ), Rom.6:4, Col.2:12.†
(AS)
G4916.s: to inter in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate spiritually (to Christ by a sepulture as to sin)

G4917.d:
συν-θλάω, -ῶ
[in LXX for מָחַץ etc. ;]
to crush together, crush: Mat.21:44 ([WH], R, mg., om.), Luk.20:18.†
(AS)

G4918.d:
συν-θλίβω
[in LXX: Ecc.12:6 א A (רָצַץ), Sir.34:14 (31:14), 1Ma.15:14 A * ;]
to press together, press on all sides: Mrk.5:24, 31.†
(AS)
G4918.s: to compress, i.e. crowd on all sides

G4919.d:
συν-θρύπτω
to break in pieces, crush: metaphorically, τ. καρδίαν, Act.21:13.†
(AS)
G4919.s: to crush together, i.e. (figuratively) to dispirit

G4920.d:
συν-ίημι and συνίω (see Bl., § 23, 7),
[in LXX chiefly for בִּין hi., שָׂכַל hi. ;]
__1. to bring or set together.
__2. Metaphorical, to perceive, understand: Mat.13:13-15 (LXX), Mat.13:19 15:10, Mrk.4:9 (WH, mg.), Mrk.4:12 7:14 8:17, 21 Luk.8:10, Act.7:25 28:26-27, Rom.15:21" (LXX), 2Co.10:12; with accusative of thing(s), Mat.13:23, 51, Luk.2:50 18:34 24:45; before ὅτι, Mat.16:12 17:13; before quæst. indir., Eph.5:17; ἐπὶ τ. ἄρτοις, Mrk.6:52; as subst., συνίων (ὁ σ., WH, mg.), a man of understanding, i.e. in moral and religious sense, Rom.3:11 (LXX).†
(AS)
G4920.s: to put together, i.e. (mentally) to comprehend; by implication, to act piously

G4921.d:
συν-ίστημι
[in LXX for צָוָה pi., קָהַל ni., etc.; 1Ma.12:43, 2Ma.4:24, 3Ma.1:19 (and frequently in these books) ;]
__1. trans.,
__(a) to commend, recommend: with accusative of person(s), 2Co.3:1 6:4 10:12 10:18; id. with dative, Rom.16:1 (as frequently at the beginning of a letter; Deiss., LAE, 226), 2Co.5:12; before πρός, 2Co.4:2; pass., before ὑπό, 2Co.12:11;
__(b) to show, prove, establish: with accusative, Rom.3:5 5:8, 2Co.6:4; dupl. accusative, Gal.2:13; accusative and inf., 2Co.7:11
__2. Intrans., pf., συνέστηκα (as also 2 aor. and plpf.);
__(a) to stand with or near: Luk.9:32;
__(b) to be composed of, consist,…
G4921.s: to set together, i.e. (by implication) to introduce (favorably), or (figuratively) to exhibit; intransitively, to stand near, or (figuratively) to constitute
G4921.o: from G4862 (σύν) and G2476 (ἵστημι) (including its collateral forms);

G4922.d:
συν-οδεύω
[in LXX: Zec.8:21 א1 (הָלַךְ), Tob.5:16 א, Wis.6:23 * ;]
to journey with: with dative of person(s), Act.9:7 (Plut., al.).†
(AS)

G4923.d:
συνοδία, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX: Neh.7:5, 64 (יָחַשׂ) * ;]
__1. a journey in company (Plut., al.).
__2. By meton., κ company of travellers, a caravan: Luk.2:44.†
(AS)
G4923.s: companionship on a journey, i.e. (by implication), a caravan
G4923.o: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and G3598 (ὁδός) ("synod");

G4924.d:
συν-οικέω, -ῶ
[in LXX for בַּעַל etc. ;]
to dwell together: of man and wife (Hdt., al.), with dative of person(s), 1Pe.3:7,†
(AS)

G4925.d:
συν-οίκοδομέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: I Est.5:68 * ;]
__1. to build together or with (with dative of person(s), 1Esdras, l.with).
__2. Of various materials, to build up together (Thuc., al.): metaphorically, of Christians, Eph.2:22.†
(AS)
G4925.s: to construct, i.e. (passively) to compose (in company with other Christians, figuratively)

G4926.d:
συν-ομιλέω, -ῶ
to converse with (absol., FlJ, Bl, v, 13, 1; before μετά, Cebes, 13): with dative of person(s), Act.10:27.†
(AS)

G4927.o: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of a compound of the base of 3674 and the base of G3725 (ὅριον);

G4928.d:
συν-οχή, -ῆς, ή
(συνέχω), [in LXX: Jdg.2:3 (?), Job.30:3 (שׁוֹא), Job.38:28 A; Mic.5:1 (4:14), Jer.52:5 (מָצוֹר) * ;]
__1. a holding or being held together.
__2. a narrow place (Hom., al.). Metaphorical, straits, distress: Luk.21:25; καρδίας, 2Co.2:4.†
(AS)

G4929.d:
συν-τάσσω
[in LXX chiefly for צָוָה pi. ;]
to prescribe, ordain, arrange: with dative of person(s), Mat.21:6 26:19 27:10" (LXX) .†
(AS)
G4929.s: to arrange jointly, i.e. (figuratively) to direct

G4930.d:
συντέλεια, -ας, ἡ
(συντελέω), [in LXX chiefly for כָּלָה and (in Da) for קוּם ;]
__1. in cl., a joint payment or contribution for public service; hence, generally, joint action (Plat.).
__2. In late writers (Polyb., al.), consummation, completion: σ. τ. αἰῶνος, -ων (cf. Dan LXX TH Dan.12:13, al.), Mat.13:39-40, 49 24:3 28:20, Heb.9:26.†
(AS)
G4930.s: entire completion, i.e. consummation (of a dispensation)

G4931.d:
συν-τελέω, -ῶ
[in LXX chiefly for כָּלָה pi., also for עָשָׂה, תָּמַם, etc. ;]
"perfective" of τελέω (cf. M, Pr., 118),
__1. to complete, finish, bring to an end: Luk.4:13; pass., Luk.4:2, Jhn.2:3, WH, mg., Act.21:27.
__2. to effect, accomplish, bring to fulfilment (cf. MM, xxiv): Mrk.13:4, Rom.9:28, Heb.8:8.†
(AS)
G4931.s: to complete entirely; generally, to execute (literally or figuratively)

G4932.d:
συν-τέμνω
[in LXX chiefly for חָרַץ ;]
__1. to cut in pieces.
__2. to cut down, cut short: metapb., λόγον, Rom.9:28 (LXX) (Hdt., Plat., Fur., al.).†
(AS)
G4932.s: to contract by cutting, i.e. (figuratively) do concisely (speedily)
G4932.o: from G4862 (σύν) and the base of G5114 (τομώτερος);

G4933.d:
συν-τηρέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Eze.18:19 (שָׁמַר), Da TH Dan.7:28 A (נְטַר), Sir.13:12 and freq., Tob.1:11, 2Ma.12:42, al. ;]
"perfective" of τηρέω (see M, Pr., 113, 116),
to preserve, keep safe, keep close: with accusative of person(s), Mrk.6:20; with accusative of thing(s), Mat.9:17; ἐν τ. καρδίᾳ, Luk.2:19 (Arist. and later writers; cf. MM, xxiv).†
(AS)
G4933.s: to keep closely together, i.e. (by implication) to conserve (from ruin); mentally, to remember (and obey)

G4934.d:
συν-τίθημι
[in LXX: 1Ki.22:13 (קָשַׁר), etc. ;]
to place or put together, in various senses. Mid.,
__(a) to observe, perceive;
__(b) to determine, agree, covenant: with inf., Luk.22:5; before τοῦ, with inf., Act.23:20; before ἵνα, Jhn.9:22.†
συν-επι-τίθημι,
[in LXX for שִׁית, etc. ;]
to help in putting on. Mid., to join in attacking (Thuc.): Act.24:9 (RV, joined in the charge).†
(AS)
G4934.s: to place jointly, i.e. (figuratively) to consent (bargain, stipulate), concur
G4934.o: middle voice from G4862 (σύν) and G5087 (τίθημι);

G4935.d:
συν-τόμως,
adv. (συντέμνω) [in LXX: Pro.13:23 23:28, 3Ma.5:25 * ;]
concisely, briefly: Act.24:4 (for a similar ex., see MM, xxiv).†
(AS)
G4935.o: adverb from a derivative of G4932 (συντέμνω);

G4936.d:
συν-τρέχω
[in LXX: Psa.50:18 (עִם רָצָה), עִם רָצָה), 2Ma.2:1-32, Jdt.4.1-15 * ;]
to run together or with: before ἐκεῖ, Mrk.6:33; πρόσ, with accusative, Act.3:11; metaphorically, 1Pe.4:4.†
(AS)
G4936.s: to rush together (hastily assemble) or headlong (figuratively)
G4936.o: from G4862 (σύν) and G5143 (τρέχω) (including its alternate);

G4937.d:
συν-τρίβω
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁבַר ;]
to shatter, break in pieces: Mat.12:20 (LXX), Mrk.5:4 14:3, Jhn.19:36" (LXX), Rev.2:27; of persons and parts of the body, to break, crush, bruise: Luk.9:39; figuratively, Rom.16:20.†
(AS)
G4937.s: to crush completely, i.e. to shatter (literally or figuratively)
G4937.o: from G4862 (σύν) and the base of G5147 (τρίβος);
G4937.k: break (in pieces), broken to shivers (+ -hearted), bruise

G4938.d:
σύν-τριμμα, -τος, τό
(συντρίβω), [in LXX (Lev.21:19, al.) chiefly for שֶׁבֶר; also for שֹׁד (Isa.59:7), etc. ;]
a fracture (Arist.; Le, l.with, al.). Metaphorical, calamity, destruction (Isa, l.with, Wis.3:3, al.): Rom.3:16" (LXX) .†
(AS)
G4938.s: concussion or utter fracture (properly, concretely), i.e. complete ruin

G4939.d:
σύν-τροφος, -ου, ὁ
(συντρέφομαι, to be brought up together) [in LXX: 3Ki.12:24, 1Ma.1:6 R, 2Ma.9:29 * ;]
__1. prop., one nourished or brought up with, a foster-brother: Act.13:1 EV.
__2. In Hellenistic usage, as a court term, an intimate friend of a king (see Deiss., BS, 305, 310 f.): Act.13:1 (cf. also MM, xxiv).†
(AS)
G4939.o: from G4862 (σύν) and G5162 (τροφός) (in a passive sense);

G4940.d:
συν-τυγχάνω
[in LXX: 2Ma.8:14 * ;]
to meet with, fall in with: with dative of person(s), Luk.8:19.†
(AS)
G4940.s: to chance together, i.e. meet with (reach)

G4941.s: an accident; Syntyche, a Christian female

G4942.d:
συν-υπο-κρίνομαι
to play a part with, dissemble with: with dative, Gal.2:13 (Polyb.).†
(AS)
G4942.s: to act hypocritically in concert with

G4943.d:
συν-υπουργέω, -ῶ
to help together, join in serving: with dative instr., 2Co.1:11.†
(AS)
G4943.s: to be a co-auxiliary, i.e. assist
G4943.o: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and the base of G2041 (ἔργον);

G4944.d:
συν-ωδίνω
to be in travail together (Arist.): metapb. (Eur.), Rom.8:22.†
(AS)
G4944.s: to have (parturition) pangs in company (concert, simultaneously) with, i.e. (figuratively) to sympathize (in expectation of relief from suffering)

G4945.d:
συνωμοσία, -ας, ή
(συνόμνυμι, to conspire), [in Sm.: Eze.22:25 * ;]
a conspiracy: Act.23:13.†
(AS)
G4945.s: a swearing together, i.e. (by implication) a plot
G4945.o: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and G3660 (ὀμνύω);

G4946.d: ionic Συρήκουσαι, doric Συράκοσαι, and Σῦράκοσσαι, Syracuse , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G4947.s: Syria (i.e. Tsyria or Tyre), a region of Asia

G4948.d:
Σύρος, -ου, ὁ, fem. Σύρα
a Syrian: Luk.4:27, Mrk.7:26, WH, mg.†
(AS)
G4948.s: a Syran (i.e. probably Tyrian), a native of Syria

G4949.d:
Συροφοινίκισσα (Rec. -φοίνισσα), -ης, ἡ
a Syropænician woman: Mrk.7:26, WH, txt., RV (cf. ἡ Φοινίκη Συρία, Diod., 19, 93).†
(AS)
G4949.s: a Syro-phœnician woman, i.e. a female native of Phœnicia in Syria
G4949.o: feminine of a compound of G4948 (Σύρος) and the same as G5403 (Φοινίκη);

G4950.d:
Σύρτις (L, σῦρτις), -εως, accusative -ιν, ἡ,
Syrtis, the name of two large sand-banks on the Libyan coast: Act.27:17.†
(AS)
G4950.s: a shoal (from the sand drawn thither by the waves), i.e. the Syrtis Major or great bay on the north coast of Africa

G4951.d:
σύρω
[in LXX: 4Ki.17:13 (סָחַב), 4Ma.6:1, al. ;]
to draw, drag: with accusative of thing(s), Jhn.21:8, Rev.12:4; with accusative of person(s), of taking to trial or punish­ment, Act.8:3; ἔξω τ. πόλεως, Act.14:19; ἐπὶ τ. πολιτάρχας (cf. 4Mac, l.with), Act.17:6 (cf. κατα-ούρω).†
(AS)

G4952.d:
συ-σπαράσσω
to convulse completely: with accusative of person(s), Mrk.9:20, Luk.9:42 (cf. σπαράσσω).†
(AS)
G4952.s: to rend completely, i.e. (by analogy) to convulse violently

G4953.d:
σύσ-σημον (T, συν-), -ου, τό
(σῆμα), [in LXX: Jdg.20:38, 40 (מַשְׂאֵת), Isa.5:26 49:22 62:10 (נֵס) * ;]
a fixed sign or signal: Mrk.14:44. (Strab., Plut., al.; condemned by Atticists, see Rutherford, NPhr., 492 f.) †
(AS)
G4953.s: a sign in common, i.e. preconcerted signal
G4953.o: neuter of a compound of G4862 (σύν) and the base of G4591 (σημαίνω);

G4954.s: of a joint body, i.e. (figuratively) a fellow-member of the Christian community

G4955.d:
στασιαστής
(στασιάζω, to stir up sedition, Jdth.7:15, 2Ma.4:30 2Mac 14:6 *)
= Att.. στασιώτης,
a rebel, revolutionist, one who stirs up sedition: Mrk.15:7 (FlJ, al.).†
συ-στασιαστής, -οῦ, ὁ,
a fellow-rioter: Mrk.15:7, Rec.†
(AS)
G4955.o: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G4714 (στάσις);

G4956.d:
συ-στατικός (Tr. συν-), -ή, -όν
(συνίστημι),
__1. for putting together, constructive.
__2. for bringing together, introductory, commendatory: ἐπιστολή (Arist., Diog. L., al.; and see MM, xxiv), 2Co.3:1.†
(AS)

G4957.d:
συν-σταυρόω (Rec. συσ-), -ῶ,
to crucify together with: pass., with dative, Jhn.19:32; id. before σύν, Mat.27:44, Mrk.15:32. Metaphorical, of the mystical death of the Christian with Christ: Rom.6:6, Gal.2:20 (Eccl.).†
(AS)
G4957.s: to impale in company with (literally or figuratively)

G4958.d:
συν-στέλλω
(Rec. συσ-), [in LXX: Jdg.8:28 11:33 (כָּנַע ni.), Sir.4:31, al. ;]
__1. to draw together, contract, shorten: of time, 1Co.7:29.
__2. to wrap up: of enshrouding a body for burial (Eur.), with accusative, Act.5:6.†
(AS)
G4958.s: to send (draw) together, i.e. enwrap (enshroud a corpse for burial), contract (an interval)

G4959.d:
συν-στενάζω (Rec. συσ-),
to groan together or with: Rom.8:22 (with dative of person(s), Eur., Ion., 935).†
(AS)
G4959.s: to moan jointly, i.e. (figuratively) experience a common calamity

G4960.d:
συν-στοιχέω (Rec. συσ-), -ῶ,
to stand in the same rank or line (Polyb). Metaphorical, to correspond to: Gal.4:25 (see Lft., in l).†
(AS)
G4960.s: to file together (as soldiers in ranks), i.e. (figuratively) to correspond to

G4961.d:
συν-στρατιώτης (Rec. συσ-), -ου, ὁ
a fellow-soldier (Plat., Xen., al.). Metaphorical, of fellowship in Christian service: Php.2:25, Phm 2 .†
(AS)
G4961.s: a co-campaigner, i.e. (figuratively) an associate in Christian toil

G4962.d:
συ-στέφω
[in LXX chiefly for קָשַׁר ;]
__1. to twist together: with accusative of thing(s), Act.28:3.
__2. Pass., of persons, to gather themselves together: Mat.17:22 (WH, R, mg.).†
(AS)
G4962.s: to twist together, i.e. collect (a bundle, a crowd)

G4963.d:
συ-στροφή, -ῆς, ἡ
(συστρέφω), [in LXX: Rom.4:19 13:12 (צָרַר); σ. ποιεῖσθαι, Amo.7:10 (קָשַׁר), etc. ;]
__1. a twisting together (Plat.).
__2. a concourse, a riotous gathering (Polyb.): Act.19:40; σ. ποιεῖσθαι (Am, l.with), to make a compact (RV, banded themselves together): Act.23:12.†
(AS)
G4963.s: a twisting together, i.e. (figuratively) a secret coalition, riotous crowd

G4964.d:
συν-σχηματιζω (Rec. συσ-),
(σχῆμα),
to conform to (Arist.). Pass., to be conformed to, conform oneself to: Rom.12:2, 1Pe.1:14.†
(AS)
G4964.s: to fashion alike, i.e. conform to the same pattern (figuratively)
G4964.o: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G4976 (σχῆμα);
G4964.k: conform to, fashion self according to

G4965.d:
Συχάρ
(Ε, Σιχάρ), indecl., ἡ
Sychar, a town of Samaria: Jhn.4:5.†
(AS)
G4965.s: Sychar (i.e. Shekar), a place in Palestine

G4966.d:
Συχέμ indecl. (Heb. שְׁכֶם),
Shechem;
__1. the son of Hamor (Gen.33:19): Act.7:16 b, Rec.
__2. A city of Samaria (AV, Sychem; in LXX also sometimes Σίκιμα, -ων, as in FlJ): Act.7:16 a,b.†
(AS)
G4966.s: Sychem (i.e. Shekem), the name of a Canaanite and of a place in Palestine

G4967.d:
σφαγή, -ῆς, ἡ
(σφάζω), [in LXX for טָבַח, הֲרֵגָה, etc. ;]
slaughter: Act.8:32 (LXX); πρόβατα σφαγῆς, Rom.8:36 (LXX); ἡμέρα σφαγῆς, Jas.5:5.†
(AS)
G4967.s: butchery (of animals for food or sacrifice, or (figuratively) of men (destruction))

G4968.d:
σφάγιον, -ου, τό
(σφαγή), [in LXX: Amo.5:25 (זֶבַח), Eze.21:10, 15 21:28 (טֶבַח), Lev.22:23 (נְדָבָה) * ;]
a victim for slaughter: Act.7:42 (LXX).†
(AS)
G4968.o: neuter of a derivative of G4967 (σφαγή);

G4969.d:
σφάζω
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁחַט ;]
to slay, slaughter (esp. of victims for sacrifice): ἀρνίον, Rev.5:6, 12 13:8; of persons, 1Jn.3:12, Rev.5:9 6:4, 9 18:24; ἐσφαγμένη εἰς θάνατον (RV, smitten unto death), Rev.13:3 (cf. κατα-σφάζω).†
(AS)
G4969.s: to butcher (especially an animal for food or in sacrifice) or (generally) to slaughter, or (specially), to maim (violently)

G4970.d:
σφόδρα adv. (prop. neut. of σφοδρός, excessive, violent)
[in LXX chiefly for מְאֹד ;]
very, very much, exceedingly: with verbs, Mat.17:6, 23 18:31 19:25 26:22 27:54, Act.6:7; with adjectives, Mat.2:10, Mrk.16:4, Luk.18:23, Rev.16:21.†
(AS)
G4970.s: of uncertain derivation) as adverb; vehemently, i.e. in a high degree, much

G4971.o: adverb from the same as G4970 (σφόδρα);

G4972.d:
σφραγίζω
[in LXX chiefly for חָתַם (Deu.32:34, al.), also for סָתַם (Da TH Dan.8:26) ;]
to seal,
__(a) for security: Mat.27:66, Rev.20:3; τ. καρπὸν τοῦτον, figuratively (cf. Deiss., BS, 238 f.; MM, xxiv; DB, iv, 427a), Rom.15:28;
__(b) for concealment, hence, metaphorically, to hide (Da TH Dan.9:24, Jhn.14:17): Rev.10:4 22:10;
__(with) for distinction, Rev.7:3-8; metaphorically, Eph.4:30; mid., 2Co.1:22;
__(d) for authentication (Est.8:8): Jhn.3:33 6:27 (cf. κατα-σφραγίζω).†
(AS)
G4972.s: to stamp (with a signet or private mark) for security or preservation (literally or figuratively); by implication, to keep secret, to attest
G4972.k: (set a, set to) seal up, stop

G4973.d:
σφραγίς, -ῖδος, ἡ
[in LXX: Exo.28:11, al. (חוֹתָם) Exo.35:22 (חָח), Sir.17:22, al. ;]
__1. a seal, signet: Rev.7:2.
__2. The impression of a seal or signet, a seal (on its various purposes, see: σφραγίζω): on a book or roll, Rev.5:1-2, 5 5:9 6:1, 3 6:5, 7 6:9, 12 8:1; metaphorically, Rom.4:11, 1Co.9:2, 2Ti.2:19, Rev.9:4.†
(AS)
G4973.s: a signet (as fencing in or protecting from misappropriation); by implication, the stamp impressed (as a mark of privacy, or genuineness), literally or figuratively

G4974.d:
σφυρόν, -οῦ, τό,
[in LXX: Job.41:21 (לָהַט) * ;]
the ankle: Act.3:7, Rec. (T, WH, σφυδρόν; see Bl., § 6, 8).†
(AS)
G4974.s: compare the feminine , a hammer); the ankle (as globular)
G4974.o: neuter of a presumed derivative probably of the same as (a ball, "sphere";

G4975.d:
σχέδον
adv. (ἔχω), [in LXX: 2Ma.5:2, 3Ma.5:14 3Mac 5:45 * ;]
__1. of place, near.
__2. Of degree, almost, nearly: Act.13:44 19:26, Heb.9:22.†
(AS)
G4975.o: neuter of a presumed derivative of the alternate of G2192 (ἔχω) as adverb;

G4976.d:
σχῆμα, -τος, τό
(ἔχω), [in LXX: Isa.3:17 (פֹּת) * ;]
figure, fashion: 1Co.7:31, Php.2:8.†
SYN.: see: μορφή (AS)
G4976.s: a figure (as a mode or circumstance), i.e. (by implication) external condition

G4977.d:
σχίζω
[in LXX chiefly for בָּקַע ;]
to cleave, rend: Mat.27:51, Mrk.1:10 15:38, Luk.5:36 23:45, Jhn.19:24 21:11; metaphorically, in pass., to be divided into factions, Act.14:4 23:7.†
(AS)
G4977.s: to split or sever (literally or figuratively)
G4977.k: break, divide, open, rend, make a rent

G4978.d:
σχίσμα, -τος, τό
(σχίζω),
a rent (Arist., al.): Mat.9:16, Mrk.2:21. Metaphorical, a dissension, division: Jhn.7:43 9:16 10:19, 1Co.1:10 11:18 12:25.†
SYN.: see: αἵρεσις (AS)
G4978.s: a split or gap ("schism"), literally or figuratively

G4979.d:
σχοινίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of σχοῖνος, a rush),
[in LXX chiefly for a rope (prop., one made of rushes): Jhn.2:15, Act.27:32.†
(AS)
G4979.s: of uncertain derivation); a rushlet, i.e. grass-withe or tie (generally)

G4980.d:
σχολάζω
(σχολή), [in LXX: Exo.5:8, 17, Psa.46:10 (רָפָה ni., hi.) * ;]
to be at leisure, hence, to have time or opportunity for, to devote oneself to, be occupied in: 1Co.7:5; of things, to be unoccupied, empty (Plut., Eur., al.): οἶκος, Mat.12:44, Luk.11:25 (T [WH], R, om.).†
(AS)
G4980.s: to take a holiday, i.e. be at leisure for (by implication, devote oneself wholly to); figuratively, to be vacant (of a house)

G4981.d:
σχολή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX: Gen.33:14 (κατὰ σ., אַט), Pro.28:19, Sir.38:24 * ;]
__1. leisure.
__2. Later (from Plato on),
__(a) that for which leisure is employed, a disputation, lecture;
__(b) the place where lectures are delivered, a school: Act.19:9 (for the later sense of employment, see MM, xxiv).†
(AS)
G4981.s: properly, loitering (as a withholding of oneself from work) or leisure, i.e. (by implication) a "school" (as vacation from physical employment)
G4981.o: probably feminine of a presumed derivative of the alternate of G2192 (ἔχω);

G4982.d:
σώζω (on the more accurate σῴζω, see WH, Intr., §410; Bl., §3, 1-3),
[in LXX chiefly for ישׁע hi., also for מלט ni., נצל ni., etc. ;]
to save from peril, injury or suffering: Mat.8:25, Mrk.13:20, Luk.23:35, al.; τ. ψυχήν, Mat.16:25, al.; before ἐκ, Jhn.12:27, Heb.5:7, Ju 5; of healing, restoring to health: Mat.9:22, Mrk.5:34, al. In NT, esp. of salvation from spiritual disease and death, in which sense it is "spoken of in Scripture as either (1) past, (2) present, or (3) future, according as redemption, grace, or glory is the point in view. Thus (1) Rom.8:24, Eph.2:5, 8 2Ti.1:9, Tit.3:5; (2) Act.2:47, 1Co.1:18, 15:2, 2Co.2:15; (3) Mat.10:22,…
G4982.s: to save, i.e. deliver or protect (literally or figuratively)
G4982.k: heal, preserve, save (self), do well, be (make) whole

G4983.d:
σῶμα, -τος, τό,
[in LXX for גְּוִיָּה ,בָּשָׂר, etc., and for Aram. נְבֵלָה ;]
a body.
__1. Prop., of the human body,
__(a) as always in Hom. (opposite to δέμας), of the dead body: Mat.27:58, 59 Mrk.15:43, al.;
__(b) of the living body: Luk.11:34, 1Co.6:13, al.; ἐν σ. εἶναι, Heb.13:3; as the instrument of the soul, τὰ διὰ τοῦ σ., 2Co.5:10; opposite to πνεῦμα, Rom.8:10, 1Co.5:3 7:4, Jas.2:26; to ψυχή, Mat.6:25 10:28, Luk.12:22 (cf. Wis.1:1, al.); to τὸ π. καὶ ἡ ψ., 1Th.5:23; σ. ψυχικόν, opposite to σ. πνευματικόν, 1Co.15:44; ὁ ναὸς τοῦ σ. αὐτοῦ (genitive epexeg.), Jhn.2:21; τὸ σ. τ. ταπεινώσεως (Hebraistic "genitive of definition"; M, Pr.,…
G4983.s: the body (as a sound whole), used in a very wide application, literally or figuratively

G4984.d:
σωματικός, -ή, -όν
(σῶμα), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:32 4Mac 3:1 * ;]
__(a) of or for the body, bodily: γυμνασία, 1Ti.4:8;
__(b) (opposite to ἀσώματος) bodily, corporeal: εἶδος, Luk.3:22.†
(AS)

G4986.s: of a safe father; Sopatrus, a Christian
G4986.o: from the base of G4982 (σώζω) and G3962 (πατήρ);

G4987.d:
σωρεύω
[in LXX: Pro.25:22 (חָתָה), Jdth.15:11 * ;]
__(a) to heap on: with accusative before ἐπί with accusative, Rom.12:20 (LXX) (Arist., al.);
__(b) to heap with: with accusative and dative, metaphorically, ἁμαρτίαις, 2Ti.3:6 (overwhelmed with, Field, Notes, 217) (Polyb.).†
(AS)

G4988.s: of safe strength; Sosthenes, a Christian
G4988.o: from the base of G4982 (σώζω) and that of G4599 (σθενόω);

G4990.d:
σωτήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ
(σώζω), [in LXX for יָשַׁע and cognate forms ;]
saviour, deliverer, preserver, a frequently epithet of kings in the Ptolemaic and Rom. periods (Deiss., BS, 83; LAE, 368 f.; MM, xxiv), in NT,
__(a) of God (as LXX: Psa.24:5, Isa.12:2, al.): Luk.1:47, 1Ti.1:1 2:3 4:10, Tit.1:3 2:10 3:4, Ju 25;
__(b) of Christ: Luk.2:11, Act.5:31 13:23, Php.3:20; τ. κόσμου, Jhn.4:42, 1Jn.4:14 (for the general use of the word, see Westc., in l); ἡμῶν, 2Ti.1:10, Tit.1:4 3:6; θεὸς (κύριος) καὶ σ. (see Deiss., LAE, 348.4; M, Pr., 84), Tit.2:13, 2Pe.1:1 1:11 2:20 3:2 3:18; σ. τοῦ σώματος (i.e. of the Church; see: σῶμα, 5), Eph.5:23.†
(AS)
G4990.s: a deliverer, i.e. God or Christ

G4991.d:
σωτηρία, -ας, ἡ
(σωτήρ), [in LXX for יֶשַׁע, יְשׁוּעָה, תְּשׁוּעָה, פְּלֵיטָה, etc. ;]
deliverance, preservation, salvation, safety (Lat. salus): Act.7:25 27:34, Heb.11:7; ἐξ ἐχθρῶν, Luk.1:71. In NT esp. of Messianic and spiritual salvation (see: σώζω): Luk.19:9, Jhn.4:22, Act.4:12 13:47, Rom.11:11, 2Th.2:13, 2Ti.3:15, Heb.2:3 6:9, 2Pe.3:15, Ju 3; opposite to ἀπηώλεια, Php.1:28; αἰώνιος-., Heb.5:9; ὁ λόγος (τὸ εὐαγγέλιον) τῆς σ., Act.13:26, Eph.1:13; ὁδὸς σωτηρίας, Act.16:17; κέρας σωτηρίας, Luk.1:69; ἡμέρα σωτηρίας, 2Co.6:2 (LXX); κατεργάζεσθαι τὴν ἑαυτοῦ σ., Php.2:12; κληρονομεῖν σ., Heb.1:14; ὁ ἀρχηγὸς τῆς σ., Heb.2:10; εἰς σ., Rom.1:16 10:1, 10, 1Pe.2:2; σ. as a…
G4991.o: feminine of a derivative of G4990 (σωτήρ) as (properly, abstract) noun;

G4992.d:
σωτήριος, -ον
(σωτήρ), [in LXX for יְשׁוּעָה, שֶׁלֶם, etc. ;]
saving, bringing salvation, in NT always in spiritual sense (see: σώζω, σωτηρία): ἡ χάρις ἡ σ., Tit.2:1. Neut., -τὸ σ., as subst. (cl.), salvation: Luk.2:30; τ. σ. τ. θεοῦ, Luk.3:6, Act.28:28; περικεφαλαίαν τοῦ σ., Eph.6:17.†
(AS)
G4992.o: neuter of the same as G4991 (σωτηρία) as (properly, concretely) noun;

G4993.d:
σωφρονέω, -ῶ
(σώφρων),
__(a) to be of sound mind or in one's right mind: Mrk.5:15, Luk.8:35; opposite to ἐκστῆναι, 2Co.5:13 (Hdt.);
__(b) to be temperate, discreet, self-controlled (opposite to μαίνεσθαι, ὑβρίζειν, etc.; sch., Thuc., al.): Tit.2:6; opposite to ὑπερφρονεῖν, Rom.12:3; σ. καὶ νήφειν, 1Pe.4:7.†
(AS)
G4993.s: to be of sound mind, i.e. sane, (figuratively) moderate
