a shallow bowl (= Lat. patera), used for pouring libations, etc.: Rev.5:8 15:7 16:1-17 17:1 21:9.†
(AS)

G5358.d:
φιλ-άγαθος, -ον
[in LXX: Wis.7:22 * ;]
loving that which is good, loving goodness: Tit.1:8 (Arist., Polyb., a l.).†
(AS)
G5358.s: fond to good, i.e. a promoter of virtue

G5359.d:
Φιλαδελφία (Rec. -έλφεια), -ας, ἡ
Philadelphia, a city of Lydia: Rev.1:11 3:7.†
(AS)
G5359.s: Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor
G5359.o: from (the same as G5361 (φιλάδελφος)), a king of Pergamos;

G5360.d:
φιλαδελφία, -ας, ἡ
(φιλάδελφος), [in LXX: 4Ma.13:23 4Mac 13:26 4Mac 14:1 * ;]
the love of brothers, brotherly love: of Christians' mutual love as brethren (see: ἀδελφός), Rom.12:10, 1Th.4:9, Heb.13:1, 1Pe.1:22, 2Pe.1:7.†
(AS)
G5360.k: brotherly love (kindness), love of the brethren

G5361.d:
φιλ-άδελφος, -ον
[in LXX: 2Ma.15:14, 4Ma.13:21 4Mac 15:10 * ;]
loving one's brother, loving like a brother (Soph., Xen., al.): of Christians' love for one another (EV, loving as brethren), 1Pe.3:8.†
(AS)

G5362.d:
φίλανδρος, -ον
__1. loving men (Æsch.).
__2. Of a wife, loving her husband (frequently in epitaphs, see LS, see word, Deiss., BS, 255): Tit.2:4.†
(AS)
G5362.s: fond of man, i.e. affectionate as a wife

G5363.d:
φιλανθρωπία, -ας, ἡ
(φιλάνθρωπος, humane), [in LXX: Est.8:13, 2Ma.6:22 2Mac 14:9, 3Ma.3:15 3Mac 3:18 * ;]
humanity, kindness (see Field, Notes, 147 f.): Act.28:2, Tit.3:4 (cf. also DCG, ii, 356 ff.).†
(AS)

G5364.o: adverb from a compound of G5384 (φίλος) and G444 (ἄνθρωπος);

G5365.d:
φιλαργυρία, -ας, ἡ
(φιλάργυρος), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:26 4Mac 2:15 א1 * ;]
love of money, avarice: 1Ti.6:1.†
SYN.: πλεονεξία, covetousness (see Tr., Syn., § xxiv) (AS)

G5367.d:
φίλ-αυτος, -ον
loving oneself (Arist.); in bad sense (ib.), selfish: 2Ti.3:2.†
SYN.: αὐθάδης (see Tr., Syn., § xciii) (AS)

G5368.d:
φιλέω, -ῶ
(φίλος), [in LXX: Gen.27:4, 9, al. (אָהַב), Gen.27:27, al. (נָשַׁק), La 1:2 (רֵעַ) Wis.8:2, al. ;]
__1. to love (with the love of emotion and friendship, Lat, amare; v, SYN.): with accusative of person(s), Mat.10:37, Jhn.5:20; Jhn.11:3, 36 15:19 16:27 20:2 21:15-17, 1Co.16:22, Rev.3:19; ἐν πίστει, Tit.3:15; with accusative of thing(s), Mat.23:6, Luk.20:46, Jhn.12:25, Rev.22:15; with inf. (Isa.56:10; cf. Bl., § 69, 4), Mat.6:5.
__2. to kiss: with accusative of person(s), Mat.26:48, Mrk.14:44, Luk.22:47 (cf. κατα-φιλέω).†
SYN.: ἀγαπάω ω (which see), the love of duty and respect (AS)
G5368.s: to be a friend to (fond of (an individual or an object)), i.e. have affection for (denoting personal attachment, as a matter of sentiment or feeling; while G25 (ἀγαπάω) is wider, embracing especially the judgment and the deliberate assent of the will as a matter of principle, duty and propriety: the two thus stand related very much as G2309 (θέλω) and G1014 (βούλομαι), or as G2372 (θυμός) and G3563 (νοῦς) respectively; the former being chiefly of the heart and the latter of the head); specially, to kiss (as a mark of tenderness)

G5370.d:
φίλημα, -τος, τό
(φιλέω), [in LXX: Pro.27:6, Sng.1:2 (נְשִׁיקָה) * ;]
a kiss: Luk.7:45 22:48; as a token of Christian brotherhood, φ. ἅγιον, Rom.16:16, 1Co.16:20, 2Co.13:12, 1Th.5:26; φ. ἀγάπης, 1Pe.5:14 (see Lft., Notes, 90; DB, DCA, see word "Kiss").†
(AS)

G5372.s: amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity

G5373.d:
φιλία, -ας, ἡ
(φίλος), [in LXX chiefly for אַהֲבָה ;]
friendship: with genitive obj., Jas.4:4.†
(AS)

G5374.d:
φιλιππήσιος, -ου, ὁ
(for other forms in use, see Lft., in l)
a Philippian: Php.4:15.†
(AS)
G5374.s: a Philippesian (Philippian), i.e. native of Philippi

G5375.d:
φίλιπποι, -ων, οἱ
(on the pl., see WM, § 27, 3)
Philippi: Act.16:12 20:6, Php.1:1, 1Th.2:2.†
(AS)

G5376G.d:
φίλιππος, -ου, ὁ
Philip;
__1. the husband of Herodias: Mat.14:3, Mrk.6:17.
__2. The tetrarch: Mat.16:13, Mrk.8:27, Luk.3:1.
__3. The apostle: Mat.10:3, Mrk.3:18, Luk.6:14, Jhn.1:44-49 6:5, 7 12:21-22 14:8-9, Act.1:13.
__4. The deacon and evangelist: Act.6:5 8:5-40 21:8.†
(AS)
G5376G.s: fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites

G5376H.d:
φίλιππος, -ου, ὁ
Philip;
__1. the husband of Herodias: Mat.14:3, Mrk.6:17.
__2. The tetrarch: Mat.16:13, Mrk.8:27, Luk.3:1.
__3. The apostle: Mat.10:3, Mrk.3:18, Luk.6:14, Jhn.1:44-49 6:5, 7 12:21-22 14:8-9, Act.1:13.
__4. The deacon and evangelist: Act.6:5 8:5-40 21:8.†
(AS)
G5376H.s: fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites

G5376I.d:
φίλιππος, -ου, ὁ
Philip;
__1. the husband of Herodias: Mat.14:3, Mrk.6:17.
__2. The tetrarch: Mat.16:13, Mrk.8:27, Luk.3:1.
__3. The apostle: Mat.10:3, Mrk.3:18, Luk.6:14, Jhn.1:44-49 6:5, 7 12:21-22 14:8-9, Act.1:13.
__4. The deacon and evangelist: Act.6:5 8:5-40 21:8.†
(AS)
G5376I.s: fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites

G5376J.d:
φίλιππος, -ου, ὁ
Philip;
__1. the husband of Herodias: Mat.14:3, Mrk.6:17.
__2. The tetrarch: Mat.16:13, Mrk.8:27, Luk.3:1.
__3. The apostle: Mat.10:3, Mrk.3:18, Luk.6:14, Jhn.1:44-49 6:5, 7 12:21-22 14:8-9, Act.1:13.
__4. The deacon and evangelist: Act.6:5 8:5-40 21:8.†
(AS)
G5376J.s: fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites

G5376K.d:
φίλιππος, -ου, ὁ
Philip;
__1. the husband of Herodias: Mat.14:3, Mrk.6:17.
__2. The tetrarch: Mat.16:13, Mrk.8:27, Luk.3:1.
__3. The apostle: Mat.10:3, Mrk.3:18, Luk.6:14, Jhn.1:44-49 6:5, 7 12:21-22 14:8-9, Act.1:13.
__4. The deacon and evangelist: Act.6:5 8:5-40 21:8.†
(AS)
G5376K.s: fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites

G5378.d:
1. fond of speaking , (Plato Philosophus)
2. fond of learning, literary , Lat. studiosus, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)
G5378.s: fond of words, i.e. talkative (argumentative, learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian

G5379.d:
φιλονεικία, -ας, ἡ
(φιλόνεικος), [in LXX: 2Ma.4:4, 4Ma.1:26 4Mac 8:26 * ;]
love of strife, rivalry, emulation (Plat., al.), but mostly in bad sense (Thuc., al.), contentiousness, contention: Luk.22:24 (but see Field, Notes, 75 f.).†
(AS)

G5380.d:
φιλό-νεικος, -ον
(νεῖκος, strife) [in LXX: Eze.3:7 (חָזָק ־מֵצַח)* ;]
fond of strife, contentious: 1Co.11:16.†
(AS)
G5380.s: probably akin to G3534 (νῖκος)); fond of strife, i.e. disputatious

G5381.d:
φιλο-ξενία, -ας, ἡ
(φιλόξενος),
love of strangers, hospitality: Rom.12:13, Heb.13:2.†
(AS)

G5383.d:
φιλο-πρωτιύω
(φιλόπρωτος, Plut., al.)
to strive to be first: III Jn 9 (eccl.).†
(AS)
G5383.s: to be fond of being first, i.e. ambitious of distinction
G5383.o: from a compound of G5384 (φίλος) and G4413 (πρῶτος);

G5384.d:
φίλος, -η, -ον
[in LXX chiefly for רֵעַ, אָהַב ;]
__1. pass., beloved, dear (Hom., Eur., al.).
__2. Act., loving, friendly (in cl. less frequently and only in poets): Act.19:31. As subst., a friend;
__(a) masc., ὁ φ.: Luk.7:6 11:5 14:10 15:6 16:9 21:16 23:12, Act.27:3, 3Jn.14; opposite to δοῦλος, Jhn.15:15; φ. ἀναγκαῖοι, Act.10:24; with genitive subj., Mat.11:19, Luk.7:34 11:6, 8 12:4 14:12 15:29, Jhn.11:11 15:13-14; ὁ φ. τοῦ νυμφίου, Jhn.3:29; τ. Καίσαρος (see Deiss., BS 167; LAE, 382 f.), Jhn.19:12; θεοῦ (see Hort, in l), Jas.2:23; with genitive of thing(s), τ, κόσμου, Jas.4:4;
__(b) fem., ἡ φ., Luk.15:9,†
(AS)
G5384.s: actively, fond, i.e. friendly (still as a noun, an associate, neighbor, etc.)

G5385.d:
Φιλο-σοφία, -ας, ἡ
(φιλόσοφος), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:1 4Mac 5:10 4Mac 5:22 4Mac 7:9 4Mac 7:21 * ;]
the love and pursuit of wisdom; hence, philosophy, investi­gation of truth and nature: of the so-called philosophy of false teachers, Col.2:8 (see Lft., ICC, in l).†
(AS)

G5386.d:
φιλό-σοφος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Dan LXX 1:20 (אַשָּׁף), 4Ma.1:1 4Mac 5:35 4Mac 7:7 * ;]
a philosopher: Act.17:18.†
(AS)
G5386.s: fond of wise things, i.e. a "philosopher"

G5387.d:
φιλόστοργος, -ον
(στοργή, family affection), [in LXX: 4Ma.15:13 * ;]
tenderly loving, affectionate (Xen., Plut., al.): of Christians, Rom.12:10.†
(AS)
G5387.s: fond of natural relatives, i.e. fraternal towards fellow Christian
G5387.o: from G5384 (φίλος) and (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children);

G5388.d:
φιλότεκνος, -ον
(φίλος, τέκνον), [in LXX: 4Ma.15:4-6 * ;]
loving one's children (Hdt., Arist., Plut., al.): of women, joined with φίλανδρος, which see, Tit.2:4.†
(AS)
G5388.s: fond of one's children, i.e. maternal

G5389.d:
φιλοτιμέομαι, -οῦμαι
(φίλος, τιμή), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:35 A ;]
to love or seek after honour, hence, to be ambitious, emulous (Plat., Plut., al.): with inf., Rom.15:20, 2Co.5:9, 1Th.4:11.†
(AS)
G5389.s: to be fond of honor, i.e. emulous (eager or earnest to do something)
G5389.o: middle voice from a compound of G5384 (φίλος) and G5092 (τιμή);

G5390.s: with friendliness of mind, i.e. kindly

G5392.d:
φιμόω, -ῶ
(φιμός, a muzzle), [in LXX: Deu.25:4 (חָסַם), Dan LXX Su 1:61, 4Ma.1:35 א R * ;]
to muzzle: 1Co.9:9, 1Ti.5:18" (LXX) ; metaphorically, to put to silence: with accusative of person(s), Mat.22:34, 1Pe.2:15; pass., to be silenced, silent: Mat.22:12, Mrk.1:25 4:39, Luk.4:35.†
(AS)

G5393.o: active participle of the base of G5395 (φλόξ);

G5394.d:
φλογίζω
(φλόξ), [in LXX: Exo.9:24 (לָקַח hith.), Num.21:14 (†), Psa.97:3 (לָהַט pi.), Da TH Dan.3:27(94) (חָרַךְ ithp.), Sir.3:30, 1Ma.3:5 * ;]
to set on fire, burn, burn up: figuratively, Jas.3:6 (on the meaning of the sentence, see Hort, in l).†
(AS)
G5394.s: to cause a blaze, i.e. ignite (figuratively, to inflame with passion)

G5395.d:
φλόξ genitive, φλογός,
[in LXX chiefly for לַהַב, לֶהָבָה ;]
a flame: Luk.16:24; φ, πυρός, Act.7:30, 2Th.1:8, Heb.1:7" (LXX), Rev.1:14 2:18 19:12.†
(AS)

G5396.d:
φλυαρέω, -ῶ
(φλύαρος),
to talk nonsense: with accusative of person(s), ἡμᾶς (EV, prating against us), III Jn 10.†
(AS)
G5396.s: to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously

G5397.d:
φλύαρος, -ον
(φλύω, to babble), [in LXX: 4Ma.5:10 * ;]
babbling, garrulous: 1Ti.5:13 (EV, tattlers; of things, φιλοσοφία, 4Mac, l.with).†
(AS)

G5398.d:
φοβερός, -ά, -όν
(φοβέω), [in LXX chiefly for יָרֵא, also for דְּחַל, אָיֹם ;]
fearful, whether act, or pass.;
__1. act., = δεινός, causing fear, terrible (LXX): Heb.10:27, 31 12:21
__2. Pass., = δειλός, feeling fear, timid (cl. in both senses).†
(AS)

G5399.d:
φοβέέω, ῶ
(φόβος) [in LXX chiefly for מִן יָרֵא ;]
__1. in Hem., to put to flight. Pass., to be put to flight, to flee affrighted
__2. to terrify, frighten (Wis 179; Hdt. and Att..). Pass. (so always in NT; cf. M, Pr., 162), to be seized with fear, be affrighted, fear: Mat.10:31 14:27, Mrk.5:33 6:50, Luk.1:13 8:50, Jhn.6:19 12:15, Act.16:38, al.; opposite to ὑψηλοφρονεῖν, Rom.11:20; σφόδρα, Mat.17:6 27:54; with cogn. accusative, φόβον μέγαν, Mrk.4:41, Luk.2:9 (1Ma.10:8); φόβον αὐτῶν (obj, genitive, but cf. ICC, in l), 1Pe.3:14; πτόησιν, 1Pe.3:6; with accusative of person(s), Mat.10:26, Mrk.11:18, Luk.19:21, Jhn.9:22, Act.9:26,
Rom.13:3, al.;…
G5399.s: to frighten, i.e. (passively) to be alarmed; by analogy, to be in awe of, i.e. revere

G5400.d:
φόβητρον (LTr., WH, -θρον), -ου, τό
(φοβέω), [in LXX: Isa.19:17 (חָגָא) * ;]
that which causes fright, a terror: pl. (as always, exc.Isa, l.with), Luk.21:11 (Hipp., Plat.).†
(AS)
G5400.s: a frightening thing, i.e. terrific portent
G5400.o: neuter of a derivative of G5399 (φοβέω);

G5401.d:
φόβος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for יִרְאָה, also for פַּחַד, אֵימָה, etc. ;]
__1. in Hom., flight.
__2. That which causes flight, fear, dread, terror: Luk.1:12, Act.5:5, 1Ti.5:20. 1Jn.4:18, al.; cogn. accusative, φοβεῖσθαι φ., Mrk.4:41, Luk.2:9; with genitive obj., Jhn.7:13 19:33 20:19, Heb.2:5, 1Pe.3:14 (but cf. ICC, in l);ἀπὸ (τοῦ) φ., Mat.14:26, Luk.21:26; εἰς φ., Rom.8:15; μετὰ φόβου, Mat.28:8; φ. καὶ τρόμος (Lft., Notes, 172), 1Co.2:3, 2Co.7:15, Eph.6:5, Php.2:12; by meton., of that which causes fear, Rom.13:3; of reverential fear, Rom.13:7, 1Pe.1:17 2:18 3:2 3:15; τ. κυρίου, Act.9:31, 2Co.5:11 (see Field, Notes, 183); Χριστοῦ, Eph.5:21;…
G5401.o: from a primary (to be put in fear);

G5402.d:
φοίβη, -ης, ἡ
Phæbe, a deaconess of Cenchræa: Rom.16:1.†
(AS)
G5402.s: probably akin to the base of G5457 (φῶς)); Phœbe, a Christian woman

G5403.s: palm-country; Phœnice (or Phœnicia), a region of Palestine

G5404.d:
Φοῖνιξ (on the accent, see Bl., § 4, 2; WM, § 6, lc), -ικος, ὁ,
[in LXX for תָּמָר תִּמֹּר ;]
the date palm, palm: τὰ βαΐα τῶν φ., Jhn.12:13; of palm branches, φοίνικες (as Arist., 2Ma.10:7, al.), Rev.7:9.†
(AS)

G5405.d:
φοῖνιξ, -ικος, ο, ἡ
Phænix, a city of Crete: Act.27:12.†
(AS)

G5406.d:
φονεύς, -έως, ὁ
(φόνος) [in LXX: Wis.12:5 * ;]
a murderer: Mat.22:7 Act.7:52 28:4, 1Pe.4:15, Rev.21:8 22:15; ἀνὴρ φ., Act.3:14.†
SYN.: ἀνθρωποκτόνος (AS)
G5406.s: a murderer (always of criminal (or at least intentional) homicide; which G443 (ἀνθρωποκτόνος) does not necessarily imply; while G4607 (σικάριος) is a special term for a public bandit)

G5407.d:
φονεύω
(φονεύς), [in LXX chiefly for רָצַח ;]
to kill, murder. absol., Mat.5:21, Jas.4:2; μὴ (οὐ) φονεύσῃς (-εις), Mat.5:21 19:18, Mrk.10:19, Luk.18:20, Rom.13:9, Jas.2:11 (all from Exo.20:13-14); with accusative, Mat.23:31, 35, Jas.5:6.†
(AS)

G5408.d:
φόνος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for דָּם, פֶּה, etc. ;]
murder, slaughter: Mrk.15:7, Luk.23:19, 25, Act.9:1, Rom.1:29; φ. μαχαίρης (cf. Exo.17:13, al.), Heb.11:37; pl., Mat.15:19, Mrk.7:21, Rev.9:21.†
(AS)

G5409.d:
φορέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Pro.16:23 (יָסַף hi.), Sir.11:5, al. ;]
frequent. of φέρω, denoting repeated or habitual action (cf. Tr., Syn., § lviii), most commonly used of clothing, weapons, etc., to bear constantly, wear: Mat.11:8, Jhn.19:5, Rom.13:4, 1Co.15:49, Jas.2:3.†
(AS)
G5409.s: to have a burden, i.e. (by analogy) to wear as clothing or a constant accompaniment

G5410.d:
φόρον, -ου, τό
(Lat. forum): Ἀππίου Φ., see: Ἄππιος
(AS)
G5410.s: a forum or market-place; only in comparative with G675 (Ἄππιος); a station on the Appian road

G5411.d:
φόρος, .-ου, ὁ
(φέρω), [in LXX chiefly for מַס, also for מִדָּה, etc. ;]
tribute paid by a subject nation (cf. 1Ma.10:33): φ. δοῦναι (1Ma.8:4 1Mac 8:7), Luk.20:22 23:2; ἀποδοῦναι, Rom.13:7; τελεῖν, Rom.13:6 (Hdt., al.).†
SYN.: κῆνσος, τέλος (which see) (AS)
G5411.s: a load (as borne), i.e. (figuratively) a tax (properly, an individual assessment on persons or property; whereas G5056 (τέλος) is usually a general toll on goods or travel)

G5412.d:
φορτίζω
(φόρτος), [in LXX: Eze.16:33 (שָׁחַד) * ;]
to load: with dupl. accusative, Luk.11:46; pass., to be laden: metaphorically (EV, heavy laden), Mat.11:28.†
(AS)
G5412.s: to load up (properly, as a vessel or animal), i.e. (figuratively) to overburden with ceremony (or spiritual anxiety)

G5413.d:
φορτίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of φόρτος), [in LXX chiefly for מַשָּׂא ;]
a burden, load: of the cargo of a ship (Hdt., al.), Act.27:10; metaphorically, Mat.11:30 23:4, Luk.11:46, Gal.6:5.†
SYN.: βάρος (which see), ὄγκος (AS)
G5413.s: an invoice (as part of freight), i.e. (figuratively) a task or service

G5414.d:
φόρτος, -ου, ὁ
(φέρω),
a load: esp. of a ship's cargo (Hom., Hdt., and late prose writers), Act.27:10, Rec.†
(AS)
G5414.s: something carried, i.e. the cargo of a ship

G5415.d:
φορτούνατος (Rec. Φουρ-, see Mayser, 116 f.), -ου, ὁ
(Lat.) Fortunatus: 1Co.16:17 (see Lft., Cl. Ro., 1Co., 59).†
(AS)

G5416.s: a whip, i.e. Roman lash as a public punishment
G5416.o: neuter of a derivative from the base of G5417 (φραγελλόω);

G5417.d:
φραγελλόω, -ῶ
(φραγέλλιον, which see),
to scourge: with accusative, Mat.27:26, Mrk.15:15 (eccl.).†
(AS)
G5417.s: to whip, i.e. lash as a public punishment
G5417.o: from a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum;

G5418.d:
φραγμός, -oῦ, ὁ
(φράσσω), [in LXX chiefly for גָּדֵר, גְּדֵרָה, also for גְּדֵרָה, etc. ;]
__1. prop., a fencing in (Soph., OT, 1387).
__2. = φράγμα, a fence: Mat.21:33, Mrk.12:1, Luk.14:23. Metaphorical, μεσότοιχον (which see) τοῦ φ., genitive epexeg., Eph.2:14 (see Ellic., in l).†
(AS)
G5418.s: a fence, or inclosing barrier (literally or figuratively)

G5419.d:
φράζω
[in LXX: Job.6:24 (בִּין hi.) Job.12:8 (יָרָה hi.), Dan LXX 2:4 (חָוָה pa.) * ;]
to show forth, tell, declare, explain: Mat.13:36 (WH, RV, διασάφησον) Mat.15:15.†
(AS)
G5419.s: to indicate (by word or act), i.e. (specially), to expound
G5419.o: probably akin to G5420 (φράσσω) through the idea of defining;

G5420.d:
φράσσω
[in LXX: Job.38:8 (סָכַךְ hi.), Hos.2:6(8) (שׂוּךְ), Pro.21:13 (אָטַם), etc. ;]
to fence in, stop, close: στόματα λεόντων, Heb.11:33; στόμα, metaphorically, Rom.3:19; pass., καύχησις, 2Co.11:10.†
(AS)
G5420.s: to fence or inclose, i.e. (specially), to block up (figuratively, to silence)
G5420.o: apparently a strengthening form of the base of G5424 (φρήν);

G5421.d:
φρέαρ, -ατος, τό
[in LXX chiefly for בְּאֵר ;]
a well: Luk.14:5, Sng.4:11-12; φ. τῆς ἀβύσσου, Rev.9:1-2.†
(AS)
G5421.s: a hole in the ground (dug for obtaining or holding water or other purposes), i.e. a cistern or well; figuratively, an abyss (as a prison)

G5422.d:
φρεν-απατάω, -ῶ
(φρεναπάτης),
to deceive one's mind (Lft., deceive by fancies, see Ga., l.with): with accusative of person(s), Gal.6:3.†
(AS)
G5422.s: to be a mind-misleader, i.e. delude

G5423.d:
φρεναπάτης, -ου, ὁ
(φρήν, ἀπάτη),
a deceiver (B1., deceiver of his own mind, § 28, 5.2, where see ref. to π.): Tit.1:10 (eccl.).†
(AS)

G5424.d:
φρήν genitive, φρενός, ἡ,
[in LXX most frequently in Pr (Pro.6:32, al.) and chiefly for לֵב; also 3Ma.4:16 3Mac 5:47 ;]
chiefly in Hom. and Trag., but also in Plat., al., both sing. and pl.;
__1. in physical sense, the parts about the heart, midriff.
__2. heart, mind, thought: pl., 1Co.14:20 (see Edwards, Eng.-Gr. Lex., App., 1).†
(AS)
G5424.s: the midrif (as a partition of the body), i.e. (figuratively and by implication, of sympathy) the feelings (or sensitive nature; by extension (also in the plural) the mind or cognitive faculties)
G5424.o: probably from an obsolete (to rein in or curb; compare G5420 (φράσσω));

G5425.d:
φρίσσω
(Att.. -ττω, and so 4Ma.14:9 4Mac 17:7) [in LXX: Job.4:15 ( pi.), etc. ;]
__1. to be rough, bristle.
__2. to shiver, shudder, tremble, from fear: Jas.2:19 (see Hort, in l).†
(AS)

G5426.d:
φρονέω, -ῶ
(φρήν), [in LXX: Deu.32:29, Zec.9:2 (חָכָם), Psa.94:8 (שָׂכַל hi.), Isa.44:18 (בִּין) Isa.44:28, Est.8:13, Wis.1:1 14:30, 1Ma.10:20, 2Ma.9:12; 2Ma.14:8 2Mac 14:26 * ;]
__1. to have understanding (Hon., al.).
__2. to think, to be minded in a certain way: ὡς νήπιος, 1Co.13:11; with accusative (usually neut., adj., or pron., as frequently in cl.), ὃ δεῖ, Rom.12:3; ἃ, Act.28:22; τοῦτο, Php.3:15; τι ἑτέρως, ib.; οὐδὲν ἄλλο, Gal.5:10; τ. αὐτὸ φ. (Deiss., BS, 256), to be of the same mind, 2Co.13:11, Php.2:2 4:2; id. before εἰς (ἐν) ἀλλήλους(οις), Rom.12:16 15:5; τ. ἓν φ., Php.2:2 (Lft., in l); before ὑπέρ, Php.1:7.
__3. to have in mind, be mindful…
G5426.s: to exercise the mind, i.e. entertain or have a sentiment or opinion; by implication, to be (mentally) disposed (more or less earnestly in a certain direction); intensively, to interest oneself in (with concern or obedience)
G5426.k: set the affection on, (be) care(-ful), (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let this) mind(-ed), regard, savour, think

G5427.d:
φρόνημα, -τος, τό
(φρονέω), [in LXX: 2Ma.7:21 2Mac 13:9 * ;]
that which is in the mind (the content of φρονεῖν, ICC, Ro., 88), the thought: Rom.8:6-7, 27.†
(AS)

G5428.d:
φρόνησις, -εως, ἡ
(φρονέω), [in LXX for בִּינָה, תָּבוּן, חׇכְמָה, etc. ;]
understanding, practical wisdom, prudence: Luk.1:17, Eph.1:8.†
SYN.: see: σοφία, and cf. Lft., Notes, 317 (AS)
G5428.s: mental action or activity, i.e. intellectual or moral insight

G5429.d:
φρόνιμος, -ον
(φρονέω), [in LXX for בִּין, חָכָם etc. ;]
practically wise, sensible, prudent: Mat.10:16 24:45, Luk.12:42, 1Co.10:15; opposite to μωρός, Mat.7:24 25:2, 4 25:8-9, 1Co.4:10; to ἄφρων, 2Co.11:19; φ. παρ᾽ ἑαυτῷ (EV, wise in one's own conceit), Rom.11:25 12:16 (cf. Pro.3:7); compar., -ώτερος, Luk.16:8.†
SYN.: see: σοψός (AS)
G5429.s: thoughtful, i.e. sagacious or discreet (implying a cautious character; while G4680 (σοφός) denotes practical skill or acumen; and G4908 (συνετός) indicates rather intelligence or mental acquirement); in a bad sense conceited (also in the comparative)

G5431.d:
φροντίζω
(φροντίς, thought), [in LXX: 1Ki.9:5 (דָּאַג), Psa.40:17 (חָשַׁב), al. ;]
to give heed, take thought (in cl. usually absol., with accusative, with genitive), with inf., Tit.3:8 (see Bl., § 69, 4; M, Pr., 206 f.).†
(AS)
G5431.s: to exercise thought, i.e. be anxious

G5432.d:
φρουρέω, -ῶ
(φρουρός, a guard), [in LXX: I Est.4:56, Jdth.3:6, Wis.17:16, 1Ma.11:3 * ;]
to guard, keep under guard, protect or keep by guarding: 2Co.11:32; metaphorically, Gal.3:23, Php.4:7, 1Pe.1:5.†
(AS)
G5432.s: to be a watcher in advance, i.e. to mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively, to hem in, protect
G5432.o: from a compound of G4253 (πρό) and G3708 (ὁράω);

G5433.d:
φρυάσσω
(so Ps, l.with, NT; elsewhere depon., φρυάσσομαι, Att.. -ττ-), [in LXX: Psa.2:1 (רָגַשׁ), 2Ma.7:34 R, 3Ma.2:2 * ;]
prop., of horses, to neigh, whinny and prance (Plut., al.). Metaphorical, to be wanton, insolent: Act.4:25 (LXX).†
(AS)
G5433.s: to snort (as a spirited horse), i.e. (figuratively) to make a tumult

G5434.d:
φρύγανον, -ου, τό
(φρύγω, to parch), [in LXX chiefly for קַשׁ, also for חָרוּל, etc. ;]
a dry stick: pl., brushwood: Act.28:3.†
(AS)
G5434.s: akin to the base of G5395 (φλόξ)); something desiccated, i.e. a dry twig

G5474.d:
χαλκο-λίβανον, -ου, τό
chalcolibanus, probably "a mixed metal of great brilliance" (Swete): Rev.1:15 2:18 (RV, burnished brass).†
(AS)
G5474.s: burnished copper, an alloy of copper (or gold) and silver having a brilliant lustre
G5474.o: neuter of a compound of G5475 (χαλκός) and G3030 (λίβανος) (in the implied mean of whiteness or brilliancy);

G5475.d:
χαλκός, -oῦ, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for נְחֹשֶׁת ;]
copper: 1Co.13:1, Rev.18:12; by meton., of copper coin, Mat.10:9, Mrk.6:8 12:41.†
(AS)
G5475.s: copper (the substance, or some implement or coin made of it)
G5475.o: perhaps from G5465 (χαλάω) through the idea of hollowing out as a vessel (this metal being chiefly used for that purpose);

G5476.o: adverb perhaps from the base of G5490 (χάσμα) through the idea of a fissure in the soil;

G5477.d:
Χαναάν, ἡ indecl. (Heb. כְּנַעַן),
Canaan: Act.7:11; γῆ Χ., Act.13:19.†
(AS)
G5477.s: Chanaan (i.e. Kenaan), the early name of Palestine

G5478.s: a Chanaanæan (i.e. Kenaanite), or native of gentile Palestine

G5479.d:
χαρά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(χαίρω), [in LXX for שִׂמְחָה, שָׂשׂוֹן, etc. ;]
joy, delight: Luk.1:14 15:7, 10, Jhn.15:11 16:22, 24 17:13, Act.8:8, 2Co.1:24 7:13 8:2, Gal.5:22, Col.1:11, Php.2:2, 1Jn.1:4, 2Jn.12; opposite to κατήφεια, Jas.4:9; to λύπη, Jhn.16:20; χ. τῆς πίστεως, Php.1:25; ἀγαλλιᾶσθαι (χαίρειν, which see), χαρᾷ, Jhn.3:29, 1Pe.1:8; χ. ἔχειν, Phm 7; πληροῦν (-οῦσθαι) χαρᾶς, Act.13:52, Rom.15:13, 2Ti.1:4; ποιεῖν χ. μεγάλην, Act.15:3; ἀπὸ τῆς χ., Mat.13:44, Luk.24:41, Act.12:14; ἐν χ., Rom.15:32; μετὰ χαρᾶς, Mat.13:20 28:8, Mrk.4:16, Luk.8:13 10:17 24:52, Php.1:4 2:29, Heb.10:34 13:17; id. beforeπνεύματος ἁγίου, 1Th.1:6; χ. ἐν π. ἁ, Rom.14:17; χ. ἐπί, 2Co.7:4; διά,…
G5479.k: gladness, X greatly, (X be exceeding) joy(-ful, -fully, -fulness, -ous)

G5480.d:
χάραγμα, -τος, τό
(χαράσσω, to engrave),
__(a) a stamp, impress, mark: Rev.13:16-17 14:9, 11 16:2 19:20 20:4 (see Deiss., BS, 240 ff.);
__(b) a thing graven: Act.17:29.†
(AS)
G5480.s: a scratch or etching, i.e. stamp (as a badge of servitude), or scupltured figure (statue)

G5481.d:
χαρακτήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ
(χαράσσω, to engrave), [in LXX: Lev.13:28 (צָרֶבֶת), 2Ma.4:10, 4Ma.15:4 א R * ;]
__1. a tool for graving.
__2. a stamp or impress: as on a coin or seal; metaphorically, χ. τ. ὑποστάσεως, Heb.1:3.†
(AS)
G5481.s: a graver (the tool or the person), i.e. (by implication) engraving (("character"), the figure stamped, i.e. an exact copy or (figuratively) representation)

G5482.d:
χάραξ, -ακος, ὁ
(χαράσσω), [in LXX for סֹלְלָה, מָצוֹר, etc. ;]
__1. a pointed stake
__2. a palisade or rampart: Luk.19:43.†
(AS)
G5482.s: akin to G1125 (γράφω) through the idea of scratching); a stake, i.e. (by implication) a palisade or rampart (military mound for circumvallation in a siege)

G5483.d:
χαρίζομαι
(χάρις), [in LXX: Est.8:7 (נָתַן), Sng.1:4 א, Sir.12:3, 2 -4Ma.9:1-32 * ;]
__1. to show favour or kindness: with dative of person(s), Gal.3:18.
__2. to give freely, bestow: with accusative and dative, Luk.7:21, Act.3:14 25:11, 16 27:24, Rom.8:32, 1Co.2:12, Php.1:29 2:9, Phm 22.
__3. In late Gk. (= Lat. condonare), to grant forgiveness, forgive freely: of debt, Luk.7:42-43 (EGT, in l); of sin, 2Co.2:7 2:10 12:13, Eph.4:32, Col.2:13 3:13 (cf. DB, ii, 57a).†
(AS)
G5483.s: to grant as a favor, i.e. gratuitously, in kindness, pardon or rescue

G5484.d:
therefore, because of this, for this reason
the acc. sg form of the noun χάριν which can be used as an improper preposition, on account of, because of, for this reason Lk. 7:47; Eph. 3:1, 14; 1Jn. 3:12; for the sake of, in order to, Gal. 3:19; Tit. 1:5, 11; Jude 16; on the score of, 1Tim. 5:14*
G5484.s: through favor of, i.e. on account of
G5484.o: accusative case of G5485 (χάρις) as preposition;
G5484.k: be-(for) cause of, for sake of, +…fore, X reproachfully

G5485.d:
χάρις, -ιτος, ἡ Abbott-Smith does not include the article here., accusative, χάριν (χάριτα in Act.24:27, Ju 4; see WH, App., 157),
[in LXX chiefly for חֵן ;]
__1. objectively, that which causes favourable regard, gracefulness, grace, loveliness of form, graciousness of speech (cl.; Ecc.10:12, Sir.21:16, al.): Col.4:6; λόγοι τ. χάριτος (genitive qual.), Luk.4:22.
__2. Subjectively,
__(a) on the part of the giver, grace, graciousness, kindness, goodwill, favour: Luk.2:52, Act.7:10, al.; esp. in NT of the divine favour, grace, with emphasis on its freeness and universality: Luk.1:30, Act.14:26, Rom.1:7, 1Co.1:3, al.; opposite to…
G5485.s: graciousness (as gratifying), of manner or act (abstract or concrete; literal, figurative or spiritual; especially the divine influence upon the heart, and its reflection in the life; including gratitude)
G5485.k: acceptable, benefit, favour, gift, grace(- ious), joy, liberality, pleasure, thank(-s, -worthy)

G5486.d:
χάρισμα, -τος, τό
(χαρίζομαι) [in LXX: Sir.7:33 א (AB, χάρις) Sir.38:30 Bl (א AB2R, χρῖσμα) * ;]
a gift of grace, a free gift, esp. of extra­ordinary operations of the Spirit in the Apostolic Church, but including all spiritual graces and endowments (Lft., Notes, 148 f.): Rom.1:11 5:15-16 6:23 11:29 12:6, 1Co.1:7 7:7 12:4 12:9 12:28 12:30-31, 2Co.1:11, 1Ti.4:14, 2Ti.1:6, 1Pe.4:10.†
(AS)
G5486.s: a (divine) gratuity, i.e. deliverance (from danger or passion); (specially), a (spiritual) endowment, i.e. (subjectively) religious qualification, or (objectively) miraculous faculty

G5487.d:
χαριτόω, -ῶ
(χάρις), [in LXX: Sir.18:17 (ἀνδρί κεχαριτωμένῳ; Vg., justificato; Syr., saintly) * ;]
to endow with χάρις (which see), i.e.
__1. (a) to make graceful;
__(b) to make gracious (Sir, l.with).
__2. In Hellenistic writings (for exx., see AR, Eph., 227; Lft., Notes, 315),
__(a) to cause to find favour;
__(b) to endue with grace (i.e. divine favour): Luk.1:28, Eph.1:6.†
(AS)
G5487.s: to grace, i.e. indue with special honor

G5488.d:
χαρράν
indecl. (in FlJ., Ant., i, 16, 1, Κάρρα, -ας, ib. 6, 5, Χαρρά, -ᾶς; so LXX: Gen.29:4 E, Eze.27:28 B, elsewhere -άν­Heb. חָרָן), Haran, a town in N.W. Mesopotamia: Act.7:2, 4.†
(AS)
G5488.s: Charrhan (i.e. Charan), a place in Mesopotamia

G5489.d:
χάρτης, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Isa.8:1 A, Jer.36:2, 6 36:23 (מְגִלָּה) * ;]
a sheet of paper, made of papyrus strips (see Kennedy, Sources, 42; Milligan, NTD, 10-12; DB, iv, 945 f.): II Jn 12 (Plat., Inscr.).†
(AS)
G5489.s: a sheet ("chart") of writing-material (as to be scribbled over)

G5490.d:
χάσμα, -τος, τό
(χάσκω, to yawn), [in LXX: 2Ki.18:17 (פַּחַת)* ;]
a chasm, wide space: Luk.16:26.†
(AS)
G5490.o: from a form of an obsolete primary (to "gape" or "yawn");

G5491.d:
χεῖλος, -ους, τό, genitive pl., -εων (see Bl., § 8, 4; Thackeray, Gr., I, 151),
[in LXX chiefly for שָׂפָה ;]
a lip (as in Heb., of the lip as the organ of speech): Mat.15:8, Mrk.7:6, Rom.3:13, 1Co.14:21, Heb.13:15, 1Pe.3:10" (LXX) . Metaphorical, of things, an edge, brink, etc. (Hom., Hdt., al.): of the sea­shore, Heb.11:12.†
(AS)
G5491.s: a lip (as a pouring place); figuratively, a margin (of water)
G5491.o: from a form of the same as G5490 (χάσμα);

G5492.d:
χειμάζω
(χεῖμα, winter cold) [in LXX: Pro.26:10 (†) * ;]
__1. to expose to winter cold, go into winter quarters.
__2. to drive with storm; pass., to be driven with storm, tempest-tossed: Act.27:18.†
(AS)
G5492.s: to storm, i.e. (passively) to labor under a gale

G5493.d:
χείμμαρος (shortened form of the more usual -οος, Attic contr., -ους), -ον
(χεῖμα, ῥέω) [in LXX chiefly for נַחַל ;]
winter-flowing; as subst., ὁ χ. (sc. ποταμός), a torrent: Jhn.18:1.†
(AS)
G5493.o: from the base of G5494 (χειμών) and G4482 (ῥέω);

G5494.d:
χειμών, -ῶνος, ὁ
[in LXX for גֶּשֶׁם, סְתָו ;]
__1. winter: Jhn.10:22, 2Ti.4:21; genitive, χειμῶνος, in winter, Mat.24:20, Mrk.13:18.
__2. Prop., a winter storm, hence, generally, a storm, tempest: Mat.16:3 (T, WH, R, mg., om.), Act.27:20.†
(AS)
G5494.s: akin to the base of 5490 through the idea of a channel), meaning a storm (as pouring rain); by implication, the rainy season, i.e. winter

G5495.d:
χείρ, genitive, χειρος (accusative, χεῖραν, 1Pe.5:6 T), ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for יָד ;]
the hand: Mat.3:12, Mrk.3:1, Luk.6:6, al. mult.; ἡ χ., acting subject, Luk.22:21; pl., Act.17:25 20:34, 1Jn.1:1; τ. ἔργα τῶν χ., Act.7:41, Rev.9:20; ὁ ἀσπασμὸς τ. ἐμῇ χ., 1Co.16:21, Col.4:18, 2Th.3:17; prepositional phrases, esp. those without art., similar to Heb. constructions (Bl., §32, 4; 40, 9; 46, 9), ἐν χ.; with genitive (Lft., in l.), Gal.3:19; σὺν χ. ἀγγέλου, Act.7:35; διὰ (τῶν) χειρῶν (διὰ χειρός), Mrk.6:2, Act.5:12 7:25, al.; ἐπὶ χειρῶν, Mat.4:6, Luk.4:11; ellipse of χ. (ἡ δεξία, ἀριστερα; Bl., §44, 1), Mat.6:3, al. By meton., for the power or activity of an individual,…
G5495.s: the hand (literally or figuratively (power); especially (by Hebraism) a means or instrument)
G5495.o: perhaps from the base of G5494 (χειμών) in the sense of its congener the base of G5490 (χάσμα) (through the idea of hollowness for grasping);

G5496.d:
χειραγωγέω, -ῶ
(χειραγωγός), [in LXX: Jdg.16:26 A (יָד חָזַק), Tob.11:16 א * ;]
to lead by the hand: Act.9:8 22:11.†
(AS)
G5496.s: to be a hand-leader, i.e. to guide (a blind person)

G5497.d:
χειρ-αγωγός, -όν
(χείρ, ἄγω)
leading by the hand. As subst., ὁ χ., one to lead by the head, a guide: Act.13:11.†
(AS)
G5497.s: a hand-leader, i.e. personal conductor (of a blind person)
G5497.o: from G5495 (χείρ) and a reduplicated form of G71 (ἄγω);
G5497.k: some to lead by the hand

G5498.d:
χειρόγραφος, -ον
(χείρ, γράφω), [in LXX: Tob.5:3 9:2, 5 * ;]
written with the hand. As subst., τὸ χ., a handwriting (Inscr., Polyb., al.): metaphorically, Col.2:14.†
(AS)
G5498.s: something hand-written ("chirograph"), i.e. a manuscript (specially, a legal document or bond (figuratively))
G5498.o: neuter of a compound of G5495 (χείρ) and G1125 (γράφω);

G5499.d:
χειρο-ποίητος, -ον
(χείρ, ποιέω), [in LXX (of idols) for אֱלִיל ;]
made by hand (i.e. of human handiwork): of temples, Mrk.14:58, Act.7:48 17:24, Heb.9:11, 24; of circumcision, Eph.2:11.†
(AS)
G5499.o: from G5495 (χείρ) and a derivative of G4160 (ποιέω);

G5500.d:
χειρο-τονέω, -ῶ
(χείρ, τείνω)
__1. to vote by stretching out the hand in the Athenian ἐκκλησία (Luc., Plut.).
__2. to appoint:
__(a) by vote, 2Co.8:19
__(b) without vote, Act.14:23 (see Rackham, in l) (cf. προχειροτονέω).†
(AS)
G5500.s: to be a hand-reacher or voter (by raising the hand), i.e. (generally) to select or appoint
G5500.o: from a comparative of G5495 (χείρ) and (to stretch);

G5501.d:
χείρων, -ον, compar. of κακός
[in LXX: 1Ki.17:43 B, Wis.15:18 17:6, 3Ma.5:20 * ;]
worse: Mat.9:16 12:45 27:64, Mrk.2:21, Luk.11:26, Jhn.5:14, 1Ti.5:8, Heb.10:29, 2Pe.2:20; εἰς (ἐπὶ) τὸ χεῖρον, Mrk.5:26, 2Ti.3:13.†
(AS)
G5501.s: from an obsolete equivalent (of uncertain derivation); more evil or aggravated (physically, mentally or morally)

G5502.d:
Χερουβείν (Rec. -βίμ), τά (Heb. כְּרוּב),
Cherubim: Heb.9:6 (cf. Exo.25:17 (18), al.; see DB, i, 377 ff.).†
(AS)

G5503.d:
χήρα, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for אַלְמָנָה ;]
a widow: Mat.23:13 (Rec., R, mg.), Mrk.12:40-43, Luk.2:37 4:25 7:12 18:3, 5 20:47 21:2-3, Act.6:1 9:39, 41, 1Co.7:8, 1Ti.5:3-5 5:11 5:16, Jas.1:27; γυνὴ χ., Luk.4:26; of one of an ordo viduarum (see CGT, in l), 1Ti.5:9; metaphorically, of a city forsaken, Rev.18:7.†
(AS)
G5503.s: a widow (as lacking a husband), literally or figuratively
G5503.o: feminine of a presumed derivative apparently from the base of G5490 (χάσμα) through the idea of deficiency;

G5504.d:
ἐχθές
(Rec. χθές), adv., [in LXX for תְּמוֹל, etc. ;]
yesterday: Jhn.4:52, Act.7:28, Heb.13:8 (on the form, see Rutherford, NPhr., 370 f.).†
ἐχθές,
adverb ={χθές}, yesterday, ( 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 175, “Th.” 616, etc.; ἀπ᾽ ἐ. “Anthologia Graeca” 11.35 (1st c.BC: Philodemus Gadarensis Epigrammaticus); μέσφα τό γ᾽ ἐ. 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 2.144 ); οὐ γάρ τι νῦν γε κἀ. today or yesterday, ( 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Antigone” 456; οὐκ ἐ. οὐδὲ πρῴην 5th c.BC: Antipho Orator “fragment” 58 ); ἐ. καὶ τρίτης [ἡμέρας] ( LXX.Ruth.2.11, compare 2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 10.7. (ἐχθές…
G5504.s: "yesterday"; by extension, in time past or hitherto

G5505.d:
χιλιάς, -άδος, ἡ
(χίλιοι), [in LXX for אֶלֶף ;]
the number one thousand, a thousand: Luk.14:31, Act.4:4, 1Co.10:8, Rev.5:11 7:4-8 11:13 14:1, 3 21:16.†
(AS)

G5506.d:
χιλίαρχος (in Hdt., al., -ης), -ου, ὁ
(χίλιοι, ἄρχω) [in LXX chiefly for אַלּוּף שַׂר ;]
a chiliarch, the commander of a thousand, esp. a Roman military tribune, the commander of a cohort: Jhn.18:12, Act.21:31-33, 37 22:24-29 23:10, 15 23:17-19, 22 24:7, 22 25:23; more generally, of officers of similar rank, Mrk.6:21, Rev.6:15 19:18 (see, DB, i, 352b; DCG, i, 271a, 307a).†
(AS)
G5506.s: the commander of a thousand soldiers ("chiliarch"; i.e. colonel

G5508.d:
χίος, -ου, ἡ
Chios, an island in Ægean Sea: Act.20:15.†
(AS)
G5508.s: Chios, an island in the Mediterranean

G5509.d:
χιτών, ῶνος, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for כְּתֹנֶת:]
the garment worn next the skin (though two tunics were sometimes worn, see Swete, Mk., 117), a tunic: Mat.10:10, Mrk.6:9 14:63, Luk.3:11 9:3, Ju 23; dieting. from ἱμάτιον (which see), Mat.5:40, Luk.6:29, Jhn.19:23, Act.9:39 (see DCG, i, 338, 340, 499)
(AS)

G5510.d:
χιών, -όνος, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for שֶׁלֶג also (in Da) for תְּלַג ;]
snow: Mat.28:3, Rev.1:14.†
(AS)
G5510.o: perhaps akin to the base of G5490 (χάσμα) (G5465 (χαλάω)) or G5494 (χειμών) (as descending or empty);

G5511.d:
χλαμύς, -ύδος, ἡ
[in LXX: 2Ma.12:35 * ;]
a chlamys, or short cloak worn over the χιτών (which see): Mat.27:28, 31 (see Tr., Syn., § 1).†
(AS)

G5512.d:
χλευάζω
(χλεύη, a jest), [in LXX: Wis.11:14, 2Ma.7:7, 4Ma.5:22 * ;]
to jest, mock, jeer: Act.17:32.†
(AS)
G5512.s: to throw out the lip, i.e. jeer at
G5512.o: from a derivative probably of G5491 (χεῖλος);

G5513.d:
χλιαρός, -ά, -όν
(χλίω, to become warm),
warm, tepid; metaphorically, of persons, luke-warm: Rev.3:16.†
(AS)

G5514.o: feminine of apparently a primary word;

G5514G.o: feminine of apparently a primary word;

G5515.d:
χλωρός, -ά, -όν
(χλόη), [in LXX for יֶרֶק, etc. ;]
__(a) pale green: χόρτος, Mrk.6:39, Rev.8:7; πᾶν χ., Rev.9:4;
__(b) pale: ἵππος, Rev.6:8.†
(AS)

G5516.d:
χξς ́
(on ς, see: Z), in T, Tr., Rec. for ἑξακόσιοι ἑξήκοντα ἕξ,
six hundred and sixty-six (L, mg., R, mg., six hundred and sixteen), the mystical number of the Beast: Rev.13:18 (on the interpretation, see Swete, Ap., 172 f.).†
(AS)
G5516.o: the 22nd, 14th and an obsolete letter (G4742 (στίγμα) as a cross) of the Greek alphabet (intermediate between the 5th and 6th), used as numbers; denoting respectively 600, 60 and 6;

G5517.s: dusty or dirty (soil-like), i.e. (by implication) terrene

G5518.d:
χοῖνιξ, -ικος, ἡ
[in LXX: Eze.45:10-11 (בַּת) * ;]
a chænix, a dry measure of rather less than a quart: Rev.6:6 (EV, measure).†
(AS)
G5518.s: a chœnix or certain dry measure

G5520.d:
χολάω, -ῶ
(χολή), [in LXX: 3Ma.3:1 R * ;]
__1. to be melancholy mad (Aristoph.).
__2. = χολοῦμαι, to be angry: with dative of person(s), Jhn.7:23.†
(AS)
G5520.s: to be bilious, i.e. (by implication) irritable (enraged, "choleric")

G5521.d:
χολή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX for רֹאשׁ, לַעֲנָה, מְרֵרָה ;]
gall: Mat.27:34 (here prob. = myrrh, cf. Mrk.15:23, see Swete, in l; DCG, i, 634); metaphorically, Act.8:23.†
(AS)
G5521.s: "gall" or bile, i.e. (by analogy) poison or an anodyne (wormwood, poppy, etc.)
G5521.o: feminine of an equivalent perhaps akin to the same as 5514 (from the greenish hue);

G5522.d:
χοῦς, -οός accusative, οῦν, ὁ, (contr. from χόος),
[in LXX chiefly for עָפָר ;]
__1. earth, soil.
__2. In later writers (Pint., LXX), = κονιορτός, dust: Mrk.6:11, Rev.18:19.†
(AS)
G5522.s: a heap (as poured out), i.e. rubbish; loose dirt

G5523.d:
Χοραζείν (Rec. -ζίν), ἡ,
Chorazin, a town of Galilee: Mat.11:21, Luk.10:13.†
(AS)

G5524.d:
χορηγέω, -ῶ
(χορός, ἡγέομαι) [in LXX for כּוּל pilp. ;]
__1. to lead a χορός (see LS, see word).
__2. to defray the cost of a χορός.
__3. In late writers, metaphorically, with accusative (see M, Pr., 65), to supply, furnish abundantly: 2Co.9:10, 1Pe.4:11 (Polyb., al.).†
(AS)
G5524.s: to be a dance-leader, i.e. (generally) to furnish
G5524.o: from a compound of G5525 (χορός) and G71 (ἄγω);

G5525.d:
χορός, -οῦ, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for מָחוֹל, מְחֹלָה ;]
a dance: pl., Luk.15:25.†
(AS)

G5526.d:
χορτάζω
(χόρτος), [in LXX for שָׂבַע, Psa.17:14 al. ;]
__(a) prop., of animals (see Lft. on Php.4:12), to feed, fatten: Rev.19:21;
__(b) in late Gk. (Kennedy, Sources, 82, 156), of persons, to fill or satisfy with food: with accusative of person(s), Mat.15:33; pass., Mat.14:20 15:37, Mrk.6:42 7:27 8:8, Luk.9:17, Jhn.6:26, Jas.2:16; opposite to πεινᾶν, Php.4:12; with genitive of thing(s), Mrk.8:4; ἀπό, Luk.16:21; ἐκ, Luk.15:16, WH, txt.; metaphorically, Mat.5:6, Luk.6:21.†
(AS)
G5526.s: to fodder, i.e. (generally) to gorge (supply food in abundance)

G5527.d:
χόρτασμα, -τος, τό
(χορτάζω), [in LXX: Gen.24:25, 32 42:27 43:24, Jdg.19:19 (מִסְפּוֹא), Deu.11:16 (עֶשֶׂב), (Sir.33:24) Sir.38:26 * ;]
fodder (Polyb., Plut., al.): pl., Act.7:11 (RV, sustenance).†
(AS)

G5528.d:
χόρτος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for עֶשֶׂב, also for חָצִיר, etc. ;]
__1. an enclosure, a feeding place (Hom.).
__2. food, esp. for cattle, grass: Mat.13:26 14:19, Mrk.4:28 6:39, Luk.12:28, Jhn.6:10, 1Co.3:12, Jas.1:10-11, 1Pe.1:24" (LXX), Rev.9:4; χ. χλωρός, Mrk.6:39, Rev.8:7.†
(AS)
G5528.s: a "court" or "garden", i.e. (by implication, of pasture) herbage or vegetation

G5530.d:
χράομαι, χρῶμαι
(χρή), [in LXX for עָשָׂה, etc. ;]
to use, make use of: with dative (cf. M, Pr., 64, 158), Act.27:17, 1Co.9:12 9:15, 1Ti.1:8 5:23; μᾶλλον χρῆσαι (i.e. the opportunity; see M, Pr., 247), 1Co.7:21; as some­times in late writers (cf. M, Pr., 64; Lft., Notes, 233), with accusative, 1Co.7:31; of feelings, etc., to exercise, shew: 2Co.1:17 3:12; with adv., ἀποτόμως, to deal sharply, 2Co.13:10; with dative of person(s) (cl.), to treat, deal with, Act.27:3.†
(AS)
G5530.s: to furnish what is needed; (give an oracle, "graze" (touch slightly), light upon, etc.), i.e. (by implication) to employ or (by extension) to act towards one in a given manner
G5530.o: middle voice of a primary verb (perhaps rather from G5495 (χείρ), to handle);

G5531.d:
χράω, κίχρημι
[in LXX for לָוָה, etc. ;]
to lend: Luk.11:5.†
(AS)
G5531.o: probably the same as the base of G5530 (χράομαι);

G5532.d:
χρεία, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX: 2Ch.2:16 (15) (צֹרֶךְ), Est.7:20 (חַשְׁחוּת) frequently in Sir.1:1-30 -2 Mac ;]
__1. need, necessity: Act.28:10, Tit.3:14; πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν τῆς χ. (RV, txt., for edifying as the need may be; but see Field, Notes, 192), Eph.4:29; ἕστι χ., Luk.10:42, Heb.7:11; χ. ἔχειν, with genitive, Mat.6:8 21:3, Mrk.11:3, Luk.9:11 15:7 19:31, 34 22:71, Jhn.13:29, 1Co.12:21 12:24, 1Th.4:12, Heb.10:36, Rev.21:23 22:5; before τοῦ, with inf. (Bl., § 71, 3), Heb.5:12; absol. (sc. genitive), Act.2:45 4:35; with genitive of person(s), Mat.9:12 26:65, Mrk.2:17 14:63, Luk.5:31; with inf. (Bl., § 69, 5), Mat.3:14 14:16, Jhn.13:10, 1Th.1:8 4:9; before ἵνα,…
G5532.s: employment, i.e. an affair; also (by implication) occasion, demand, requirement or destitution
G5532.o: from the base of G5530 (χράομαι) or G5534 (χρή);
G5532.k: business, lack, necessary(-ity), need(-ful), use, want

G5533.d:
χρεοφειλέτης (Rec. χρεω-, WH, χρεοφιλ-; see WH, App., 152, 154), -ου, ὁ,
(χρέος, a debt, + ὀφειλέτης) [in LXX: Job.31:37, Pro.29:13 * ;]
a debtor: Luk.7:41 16:5.†
(AS)
G5533.o: from a derivative of G5531 (χράω) and G3781 (ὀφειλέτης);

G5534.d:
χρή impers.
(χράω, see LS, see word),
it is necessary: Jas.3:10 (cf. δεῖ.).†
(AS)
G5534.o: third person singular of the same as G5530 (χράομαι) or G5531 (χράω) used impersonally;

G5535.d:
χρῄζω
(χρή) [in LXX Jdg.11:7, 1Ki.17:18 A * ;]
to need, have need of: with genitive of thing(s), Mat.6:32, Luk.11:8 12:30, 2Co.3:1; with genitive of person(s) before ἐν, Rom.16:2.†
(AS)
G5535.s: to make (i.e. have) necessity, i.e. be in want of

G5536.d:
χρῆμα, -τος, τό
(χράομαι) [in LXX: Jos.22:8, 2Ch.1:11-12 (נֶכֶס), Job.27:17 (כֶּסֶף), etc.; frequently in Sir (5:1, 8, al.), 2 and 4 Mac ;]
a thing that one uses or needs (and generally, a matter, event, business); hence in pl.,
__(a) wealth, riches: οἱ τά χ. ἔχοντες, Mrk.10:23-24, Luk.18:24;
__(b) money: Act.8:18, 20 24:26; sing. (rare in cl.) of a special sum of money, Act.4:37.†
(AS)
G5536.s: something useful or needed, i.e. wealth, price

G5537.d:
χρηματίζω
(χρῆμα), [in LXX: Jer.26:2 29:23 30:2 36:2, 4 A (דָבַר pi.), Jer.25:30) (שָׁאַג), 3Ki.18:27, Job.40:8 * ;]
__1. to transact business, hence, to consult, deliberate (Thuc., Dem., al.); hence in later writers,
__2. to make answer (esp. of offcial pronounce­ments by magistrates, etc.; in π. of the royal reply to an ἔντευξις, which see; cf. Deiss., BS, 122); of an answer by an oracle (Died., Plut., al.); in FlJ, LXX and NT, of divine communications, to instruct, admonish, warn: pass. (Bl., § 54, 3), Mat.2:22, Heb.8:5 11:7 12:25; with inf. (Bl., § 69,4; 70, 3; 72, 5), Mat.2:12, Luk.2:26, Act.10:22
__3. to assume a name (as in business), be…
G5537.s: to utter an oracle (compare the original sense of G5530 (χράομαι)), i.e. divinely intimate; by implication, (compare the secular sense of G5532 (χρεία)) to constitute a firm for business, i.e. (generally) bear as a title
G5537.k: be called, be admonished (warned) of God, reveal, speak

G5538.d:
χρηματισμός, -οῦ), ὁ
(χρηματίζω, which see), [in LXX: Pro.31:1 (מַשָּׂא), 2Ma.2:4 2Mac 11:17 * ;]
a divine response, an oracle: Rom.11:4 (Xen., Plat., al.).†
(AS)

G5540.d:
χρῆσις, -εως, ἡ
(χράομαι), [in LXX: 1Ki.1:28 (שָׁאַל), Sir.18:8, al. ;]
use: in a sexual sense, Rom.1:26; with genitive obj., θηλείας, Rom.1:27 (for exx., see Thayer, see word).†
(AS)
G5540.s: employment, i.e. (specially), sexual intercourse (as an occupation of the body)

G5541.s: to show oneself useful, i.e. act benevolently

G5542.d:
χρηστολογία, -ας, ἡ
(χρηστός, λέγω),
fair speaking: in bad sense, Rom.16:18 (in good sense also, eccl.).†
(AS)
G5542.o: from a compound of G5543 (χρηστός) and G3004 (λέγω);

G5543.d:
χρηστός, -ή, -όν
(χράομαι), [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב (frequently of God: Psa.25:8, al.), also for יָקָר (Eze.27:22 28:13), יָשָׁר (Pro.2:21 א A) ;]
serviceable, good;
__(a) of things, good, pleasant: of food (as often in cl.), οἶνος, Luk.5:39; ζυγός, Mat.11:30 (EV, easy); in ethical sense, ἤθη, 1Co.15:33;
__(b) of persons, good, kind, gracious: Eph.4:32; of God, Luk.6:35, 1Pe.2:3; τ. χρηστὸν (= ἡ χρηστότης) τοῦ θεοῦ, Rom.2:4.
† (AS)
G5543.s: employed, i.e. (by implication) useful (in manner or morals)

G5544.d:
χρηστότης, -ητος, ἡ
(χρηστός), [in LXX for טוּב and cogn. forms ;]
__1. goodness, excellence, uprightness: Rom.3:12 (LXX).
__2. goodness of heart, kindness: Rom.2:4, 2Co.6:6, Gal.5:22, Col.3:12, Tit.3:4; before ἐπί, with accusative of person(s), Eph.2:7; id., opposite to ἀποτομία, Rom.11:22.
SYN.: see: ἀγαθωσύνη. (AS)
G5544.s: usefulness, i.e. morally, excellence (in character or demeanor)

G5545.d:
χρίσμα (T, χρῖσμα, as in cl.; see Tdf., Pr., 102; Bl., § 4, 2), -τος, το
(χρίω),
later form of χρῖμα (Æsch., al.),
[in LXX for מִשְׁחָה and cogn. forms (Exo.29:7, al.) ;]
an anointing, unction (the result of the action χρίειν; ICC, in l; but cf. Westc., in l, for the view that the oil, not the act, is meant): 1Jn.2:20 Jn 2:27.†
(AS)
G5545.s: an unguent or smearing, i.e. (figuratively) the special endowment ("chrism") of the Holy Spirit

G5546.d:
Χριστιανός (D, Χρεισ-; on the form Χρησ-, see Bl., § 3, 6; 27, 4 on the ending, -ανος, see Bl., ll. with; Deiss., LAE, 382), -οῦ ὁ,
a Christian, the name first given to the disciples by pagan gentiles at Antioch: Act.11:26 26:28, 1Pe.4:16 (see reff. in Thayer, see word; also DB, i, 384).†
(AS)
G5546.s: a Christian, i.e. follower of Christ

G5547.d:
χριστός (Χρ-), -ή, -όν
(χρίω), [in LXX for מָשִׁיחַ and cogn. forms ;]
__1. 1. as adj.,
__(a) of things, anointing, to be used as ointment (Æsch., Eur., al.; τ. ἔλαιον τὸ χ., Lev.21:10);
__(b) of persons, anointed (ὁ ἰερεὺς ὁ χ., Lev.4:5; οἱ χ. ἰευρεῖς, 2Ma.1:10): ὁ χ. τοῦ κυρίου or Θεοῦ (1Ki.2:10, Psa.2:2, al.), of the Messiah (Aram., מְשִׁיחָא; cf. Dalman, Words, 289 ff.), Luk.2:11, 26 Jhn.1:41, Act.2:36 4:26, al.
__2. As subst., ὁ Χριστός, the Messiah, the Christ: Mat.2:4, Mrk.8:29, Luk.2:11, Jhn.1:20, Act.2:31, Rom.7:4, al.; Ἰησοῦς, Mrk.1:1, Jhn.1:17, Act.2:38, al.; Χ. Ἰησοῦς, Mat.1:18, WH, mg. Act.5:42, Rom.6:3, al.;…
G5547.s: anointed, i.e. the Messiah, an epithet of Jesus

G5548.d:
χρίω
to anoint (Hom., al.);
[in LXX chiefly for מָשַׁח of consecration to a sacred office: priest, Exo.28:41; prophet, 3Ki.19:16; king, 1Ki.10:1; of things, Exo.40:9, Lev.8:10, al.].
In NT, metaphorically, of God's anointing,
__(a) Christ: Act.4:27; with inf., Luk.4:18 (LXX); with dupl. accusative (see B1., § 34, 4), Heb.1:9 (LXX); πνεύματι ἁγίῳ, Act.10:38;
__(b) Christians: 2Co.1:21 (cf. Westc., Epp. Jo., 73) (cf. ἐν-, ἐπι-Χριω).†
SYN: see: ἀλείφω
(AS)
G5548.s: to smear or rub with oil, i.e. (by implication) to consecrate to an office or religious service
G5548.o: probably akin to G5530 (χράομαι) through the idea of contact;

G5549.d:
χρονίζω
(χρόνος), [in LXX chiefly for אָחַר pi. ;]
to spend or take time, to tarry, linger, delay: Mat.24:48 25:5, Heb.10:37; before ἐν, with dative loc., Luk.1:21; with inf., Luk.12:45.†
(AS)

G5550.d:
χρόνος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for יוֹם, also for עֵת, etc. ;]
time (a space of time, whether long or short; cf. Lft., Notes, 70): Mat.2:7, Mrk.9:21, Luk.1:57, Act.3:21 7:17, 23 13:18 17:30 27:9, Heb.11:32, 1Pe.1:17 4:3, Rev.10:6; στιγμὴ χρόνου, Luk.4:5; πλήρωμα τοῦ χ., Gal.4:4; ποιεῖν χ., Act.15:33 18:23; βιῶσαι, 1Pe.4:2; διδόναι, Rev.2:21; pl., χ. καὶ (ἢ) καιροί (Lft., l.with), Act.1:7, 1Th.5:1; ἐπ᾽ ἐσχάτου τῶν χ. (χρόνου), 1Pe.1:20, Ju 18; with prep., ἄχρι, Act.3:21; διὰ τὸν χ., Heb.5:12; ἐν χ., Act.1:6, 21; ἐπὶ (πλείονα) χ., Luk.18:4, Act.18:20; ἐφ᾽ ὅσον χ., Rom.7:1, 1Co.7:39, Gal.4:1; κατὰ τὸν χ., Mat.2:16; μετὰ τολὺν (τοσοῦτον) χ., Mat.25:19, Heb.4:7;…
G5550.s: a space of time (in general, and thus properly distinguished from G2540 (καιρός), which designates a fixed or special occasion; and from G165 (αἰών), which denotes a particular period) or interval; by extension, an individual opportunity; by implication, delay
G5550.k: + years old, season, space, (X often-)time(-s), (a) while

G5551.s: to be a time-wearer, i.e. to procrastinate (linger)
G5551.o: from a presumed compound of G5550 (χρόνος) and the base of G5147 (τρίβος);

G5552.d:
Χρύσεος, -εα, -εον (-οῦς, -ῆ, -οῦν; on accusative sing. fem., -ᾶν, Rev.1:13 and genitive pl. uncontr., -εων, Rev.2:1, LTr., see M, Pr., 48 and cf. Thackeray, Gr., x, 172 f.)
(χρυσός), [in LXX chiefly for זָהָב ;]
golden, i.e. made or overlaid with gold: 2Ti.2:20, Heb.9:4, Rev.1:12-13, 20 2:1 4:4 5:8 8:3 9:13, 20 14:14 15:6-7 17:4 21:15.†
(AS)

G5553.d:
χρυσίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of χρυσός, which see), [in LXX chiefly for זָהָב ;]
a piece of gold, gold: 1Co.3:12, Heb.9:4, 1Pe.1:7, Rev.3:18 21:18, 21; of golden ornaments, 1Ti.2:9 (WH, txt., RV), 1Pe.3:3, Rev.17:4 18:16 (WH, txt., R); of gold coin, money, Act.3:6 20:33, 1Pe.1:18.†
(AS)
G5553.s: a golden article, i.e. gold plating, ornament, or coin

G5554.s: gold-ringed, i.e. wearing a golden finger-ring or similar jewelry

G5555.d:
χρυσό-λιθος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Exo.28:20 36:20 (Exo.39:13), Eze.28:13 (תַּרְשִׁישׁ) * ;]
a chrysolite (on its identification, see Swete, Ap., 288 f.; DB, iv, 620): Rev.21:20.†
(AS)

G5557.d:
χρυσός, -οῦ, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for זָהָב ;]
gold: Mat.2:11, Rev.9:7; of golden ornaments, Mat.23:16-17, 1Ti.2:9 (Rec., WH, mg.), Jas.5:3, Rev.17:4 (Rec., WH, mg.) Rev.18:12, 16 (Rec., WH, mg.); of images, Act.17:29; of gold coin, Mat.10:9.†
(AS)
G5557.s: gold; by extension, a golden article, as an ornament or coin
G5557.o: perhaps from the base of G5530 (χράομαι) (through the idea of the utility of the metal);

G5558.d:
χρυσόω, -ῶ
(χρυσός) [in LXX chiefly for צָפָה pi. ;]
to gild, cover with gold: pass., with dative, χρυσίῳ (pleonast., cf. Exo.26:37), Rev.17:4 18:16.†
(AS)
G5558.s: to gild, i.e. bespangle with golden ornaments

G5559.d:
χρώς, genitive, χρωτός, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for בָּשָׂר ;]
in cl. rare in prose, the surface of the body, skin: Act.19:12.†
(AS)
G5559.s: the body (properly, its surface or skin)
G5559.o: probably akin to the base of G5530 (χράομαι) through the idea of handling;

G5561.d:
χώρα, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX for אֶרֶץ, מְדִינָה, etc. ;]
__1. most frequently in cl., a space, place.
__2. land, i.e.
__(a) a land, country, region: Mat.12:2, Mrk.5:10 6:55, Luk.2:8 15:13-15 19:12, Jhn.11:54, Act.13:49 27:27; χ. Γαλατική, Act.16:6 18:23; Τραχωνίτιδος, Luk.3:1; τ. Ἰουδαίας, Act.26:20; τ. Ἰουδαίων, Act.10:39; pl., τῆς Ἰουδαίας κ. Σαμαρείας, Act.8:1; Γεργεσηνῶν (Γερασηνῶν, Γαδαρηνῶν) Mat.8:28, Mrk.5:1, Luk.8:26; ἐν χ. καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου, Mat.4:16;
__(b) land, property: Luk.12:16;
__(with) the country, opposite to the town; so in pl., Luk.21:21, Jhn.4:35, Jas.5:4.†
SYN.: ἄγρος, τόπος (cf. DCG, i, 591a; LS, see word…
G5561.s: room, i.e. a space of territory (more or less extensive; often including its inhabitants)
G5561.o: feminine of a derivative of the base of G5490 (χάσμα) through the idea of empty expanse;
G5561.k: coast, county, fields, ground, land, region

G5562.d:
χωρέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Gen.13:6 (נָשָׂא), 3Ki.7:26 7:38 (כּוּל hi.), 2Ch.4:5 (חָזַק hi.), Wis.7:23-24, al. ;]
__I. Intrans.,
__1. to make room, give way, retire, pass: before εἰς, Mat.15:17; metaphorically (EV, come), εἰς μετάνοιαν, 2Pe.3:9.
__2. to go forward, advance, progress (Plat., Polyb., al.) ὁ λόγος ὁ ἐμὸς οὐ χωρεῖ. ἐν ὑμῖν, Jhn.8:37 (R, txt., hath not free course; R, mg., hath no place, for WH. cf. Field, Notes, 94 f.).
__II. Trans., to have space for holding, to hold: Mrk.2:2 (cf. Ge, l.with), Jhn.21:25; of measures (1Ki, 2Ch, ll. with), Jhn.2:6. Metaphorical, of having or making room in mind or heart: Mat.19:11-12 (EV, receive),…
G5562.s: to be in (give) space, i.e. (intransitively) to pass, enter, or (transitively) to hold, admit (literally or figuratively)
G5562.k: come, contain, go, have place, (can, be room to) receive

G5563.d:
χωρίζω
[in LXX: 2Ch.12:8, al. (בָּדַל ni., etc.), Wis.1:3, 2Ma.5:21, al. ;]
__1. to separate, divide, put asunder: with accusative of thing(s), opposite to συζεύγνυμι Mat.19:6, Mrk.10:9; with accusative of person(s), before ἀπό (Wis.1:3), Rom.8:35, 39; pf. pass ptcp., Heb.7:26.
__2. In late writers, mid. and 1 aor pass., to separate oneself, depart: Phm 15; before ἀπό Act.1:4, ἐκ, Act.18:1-2; of divorce (polyb., al.), 1Co.7:10-11 7:15 (cf. ἀπο-, δια-χωρίζω).†
(AS)
G5563.s: to place room between, i.e. part; reflexively, to go away

G5564.d:
χωρίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of χώρα, χῶρος), [in LXX: 1Ch.27:27 (כֶּרֶם), 2Ma.11:5 2Mac 12:7 2Mac 12:21, 4Ma.15:20 * ;]
__1. a place, region.
__2. an estate, property, piece of land: Mat.26:36, Mrk.14:32, Jhn.4:5, Act.1:18-19 4:34 5:3, 8 28:7.†
(AS)
G5564.s: a spot or plot of ground
G5564.k: field, land, parcel of ground, place, possession

G5564G.d:
χωρίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of χώρα, χῶρος), [in LXX: 1Ch.27:27 (כֶּרֶם), 2Ma.11:5 2Mac 12:7 2Mac 12:21, 4Ma.15:20 * ;]
__1. a place, region.
__2. an estate, property, piece of land: Mat.26:36, Mrk.14:32, Jhn.4:5, Act.1:18-19 4:34 5:3, 8 28:7.†
(AS)
G5564G.s: a spot or plot of ground
G5564G.k: field, land, parcel of ground, place, possession

G5564H.d:
χωρίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of χώρα, χῶρος), [in LXX: 1Ch.27:27 (כֶּרֶם), 2Ma.11:5 2Mac 12:7 2Mac 12:21, 4Ma.15:20 * ;]
__1. a place, region.
__2. an estate, property, piece of land: Mat.26:36, Mrk.14:32, Jhn.4:5, Act.1:18-19 4:34 5:3, 8 28:7.†
(AS)
G5564H.s: a spot or plot of ground
G5564H.k: field, land, parcel of ground, place, possession

G5565.d:
χωρίς
adv.,
__1. separately, apart: Jhn.20:7.
__2. As prep., with genitive,
__(a) separate from, apart from, without (practically equiv. to ἄνευ; see Field, Notes, 103): Mat.13:34, Mrk.4:34, Luk.6:49, Jhn.1:3 15:5, Rom.3:21, 28 4:6 7:8-9 10:14, 1Co.4:8 11:11, 2Co.12:3, Eph.2:12, Php.2:14, 1Ti.2:8 5:21, Phm 14, Heb.4:15 7:7, 20 9:7, 18 9:22, 28 10:25 11:6, 40 12:8, 14 (οὗ χωρίς; see Bl., § 82, 3), Jas.2:18, 20 2:26;
__(b) besides: Mat.14:21 15:38, 2Co.11:28.†
(AS)
G5565.s: at a space, i.e. separately or apart from (often as preposition)

G5567.d:
ψάλλω
[in LXX chiefly for זָמַר pi. (Jdg.5:3, Psa.7:17, al.), also for נָגַן pi. (1Ki.16:16 ff, al.) ;]
__1. to pull, twitch, twang (as a bowstring, etc.; Æsch., Eur., al.), hence,
__2. absol.,
__(a) to play a stringed instrument with the fingers (Hdt., Plat., al.);
__(b) later, to sing to a harp, sing psalms (LXX); in NT, to sing a hymn, sing praise: Jas.5:13; with dative of person(s), Rom.15:9 (LXX), Eph.5:19; dative instr., 1Co.14:15.†
(AS)
G5567.s: compare G5597 (ψώχω)); to twitch or twang, i.e. to play on a stringed instrument (celebrate the divine worship with music and accompanying odes)
G5567.o: probably strengthened from (to rub or touch the surface;

G5568.d:
ψαλμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(ψάλλω), [in LXX chiefly for מִזְמוֹר ;]
__1. a striking, twitching with the fingers (Eur., al.), hence, a striking of musical strings (Æsch., a1.), and hence in later writers,
__2. a sacred song sung to musical accompaniment, a psalm (LXX): 1Co.14:26, Eph.5:19, Col.3:16; of OT psalms, Luk.24:44, Act.13:33; βίβλος ψαλμῶν, Luk.20:42, Act.1:20.†
SYN.: see: ὕμνος (AS)
G5568.s: a set piece of music, i.e. a sacred ode (accompanied with the voice, harp or other instrument; a "psalm"); collectively, the book of the Psalms

G5569.d:
ψευδ-άδελφος, -ου, ὁ
a false brother: of professing Christians, 2Co.11:26, Gal.2:4.†
(AS)
G5569.s: a spurious brother, i.e. pretended associate

G5570.s: a spurious apostle, i.e. pretended pracher

G5571.d:
ψευδής, -ές
(ψεύδομαι), [in LXX for שֶׁקֶר, שָׁוְא, כָּזָב; etc. ;]
lying, false, untrue (of persons and things): Rev.2:2; μάρτυρες, Act.6:13; as subst., ὁ ψ., a liar: Rev.21:8.†
(AS)

G5572.s: a spurious teacher, i.e. propagator of erroneous Christian doctrine

G5573.s: mendacious, i.e. promulgating erroneous Christian doctrine

G5574.d:
ψεύδω to deceive by lies; more frequently in the depon. mid, form ψεύδομαι (so always in NT),
[in LXX chiefly for כָּחַשׁ pi. ;]
__1. absol., to lie: Heb.6:18, 1Jn.1:6, Rev.3:9; οὐ ψεύδομαι, Rom.9:1, 2Co.11:31, Gal.1:20, 1Ti.2:7 with dative of person(s) (Psa.18:45, Jhn.5:12, al.), Act.5:4; before εἰς, Col.3:9; κατά, Jas.3:14 (Hort, in l).
__2. Like act., with accusative, to deceive by lies (Æsch., al.): Act.5:3.†
(AS)
G5574.s: to utter an untruth or attempt to deceive by falsehood
G5574.o: middle voice of an apparently primary verb;

G5575.d:
ψευδο-μάρτυς, -υρος, ὁ
[in LXX: Dan LXX Su 1:60-61 Bl * ;]
a false witness: Mat.26:60; with genitive obj. (see WM, § 30, 1a), 1Co.15:15.†
(AS)
G5575.s: a spurious witness, i.e. bearer of untrue testimony
G5575.o: from G5571 (ψευδής) and a kindred form of G3144 (μάρτυς);

G5576.d:
ψευδο-μαρτυρέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Exo.20:16, Deu.5:20 (17) (עָנָה), Da TH Su 1:61 AB2R (see ψευδομάρτυς) * ;]
to bear false witness: Mat.19:18, Mrk.10:19, Luk.18:20" (LXX) ; before κατά, with genitive of person(s), Mrk.14:56-57 (Xen., Plat., al.).†
(AS)
G5576.s: to be an untrue testifier, i.e. offer falsehood in evidence

G5578.d:
ψευδο-προφήτης, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Zec.13:2, Jer.1:9 (Jer.6:13, al.) (נָבִיא)* ;]
a false prophet (= cl. ψευδόμαντις): Mat.7:15 24:11, 24, Mrk.13:22 (see Swete, in l), Luk.6:26, Act.13:6, 2Pe.2:1, 1Jn.4:1, Rev.16:13 19:20 20:10 †
(AS)
G5578.s: a spurious prophet, i.e. pretended foreteller or religious impostor

G5579.d:
ψεῦδος, -εος (-ους), τό
[in LXX chiefly for שֶׁקֶר, also for כַּחַשׁ, כָּזָב ;]
a falsehood, untruth, lie: Rev.14:15; opposite to ἡ ἀλήθεια, Jhn.8:44, Rom.1:25, Eph.4:25, 2Th.2:11, 1Jn.2:21; to τὸ ἀληθές, 1Jn.2:27; ποιεῖν ψ., Rev.21:27 22:15; ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει κ. σημείοις κ. τέρασιν ψεύδους (genitive qual., see M, Th., 104; and on the meaning and construction, see also ICC, in l), 2Th.2:9.†
(AS)

G5580.d:
ψευδό-χριστος, -ου ὁ
a false Christ or Messiah, "a pretender to the Messianic office" (Swete, Mk., 309; cf. also Tr., Syn., § xxx): Mat.24:24, Mrk.13:22 (cf. ἀντίχριστος).†
(AS)

G5581.d:
ψευδώνυμος, -ον
(ψευδής, ὄνομα)
under a false name, falsely called: 1Ti.6:20 (Æsch., Plut., a1.).†
(AS)

G5582.d:
ψεῦσμα, -τος, τό
(ψεύδω), [in Aq., Th.: Job.34:6, Pro.23:3; in Sm.: Job.13:4, al. ;]
a lie, falsehood: Rom.3:7 (Plat., Plut. al.).†
(AS)

G5584.d:
ψηλαφάω, -ῶ
(ψάω, to touch), [in LXX for מוּשׁ, מָשַׁשׁ pi., etc. ;]
__1. to feel or grope about; with accusative, to feel about for, search after: metaphorically, of seeking God, Act.17:27.
__2. to feel, touch, handle: with accusative of person(s), Luk.24:39, 1Jn.1:1; προσεληλύθατε ψηλαφωμένῳ (ὄρει ?), Heb.12:18 (R, txt., a mount that might be touched; mg., a palpable and kindled fire; see Westc., in l).†
(AS)
G5584.s: to manipulate, i.e. verify by contact; figuratively, to search for
G5584.o: from the base of G5567 (ψάλλω) (compare G5586 (ψῆφος));

G5585.d:
ψηφίζω
(ψῆφος), [in LXX: 3Ki.3:8 8:5 A (סָפַר ni..) * ;]
to count (prop., with pebbles), reckon, calculate: τ. δαπάνην, Luk.14:28; τ. ἀριθμόν (i.e. calculate the number's meaning), Rev.13:18 (in cl. chiefly mid., to vote by casting a pebble; cf. συγ-κατα-, συμ-φηφίζω).†
(AS)
G5585.s: to use pebbles in enumeration, i.e. (generally) to compute

G5586G.d:
ψῆφος, -ου, ἡ
(ψάω, to rub) [in LXX: Exo.4:25 (צֹר), La 3:16 (חָצָץ), Ecc.7:26 (25) (צֹר), 4Ki.12:4 (5) A, Sir.18:10, 4Ma.15:26 * ;]
__1. a small smooth stone, a pebble: ψ. λευκή (for suggestions as to the meaning, see Swete, in l), Rev.2:17.
__2. From the use of pebbles in voting, a vote: Act.26:10.†
(AS)
G5586G.s: a pebble (as worn smooth by handling), i.e. (by implication, of use as a counter or ballot) a verdict (of acquittal) or ticket (of admission); a vote

G5586H.d:
ψῆφος, -ου, ἡ
(ψάω, to rub) [in LXX: Exo.4:25 (צֹר), La 3:16 (חָצָץ), Ecc.7:26 (25) (צֹר), 4Ki.12:4 (5) A, Sir.18:10, 4Ma.15:26 * ;]
__1. a small smooth stone, a pebble: ψ. λευκή (for suggestions as to the meaning, see Swete, in l), Rev.2:17.
__2. From the use of pebbles in voting, a vote: Act.26:10.†
(AS)
G5586H.s: a pebble (as worn smooth by handling), i.e. (by implication, of use as a counter or ballot) a verdict (of acquittal) or ticket (of admission); a vote

G5587.d:
ψιθυρισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(ψιθυρίζω, to whisper), [in LXX: Ecc.10:11 (לַחַשׁ) * ;]
a whispering;
__(a) of secret slander, 2Co.12:20 (Plut.);
__(b) of a murmured enchantment, Ec, l.with†
(AS)
G5587.s: by implication, a slander; probably akin to G5574 (ψεύδομαι)); whispering, i.e. secret detraction

G5588.d:
ψιθυριστής, -οῦ, ὁ
(see supr.),
a whisperer (as epithet of Hermes, Dem., 1358, 6): in bad sense, Rom.1:30.†
Syn.: καταλάλος, q.v
(AS)

G5589.d:
ψιχίον, -ου, τό
dimin. of ψίξ,
a crumb: Mat.15:27, Mrk.7:28.†
(AS)
G5589.o: diminutive from a derivative of the base of G5567 (ψάλλω) (meaning a crumb);

G5590G.d:
ψυχή, -ῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX very frequently for נֶפֶשׁ, sometimes for לֵבַב ,לֵב, etc. ;]
__1. breath (Lat. anima), breath of life, life (Hom., al.; in Arist., of the vital principle): Mat.6:25, Mrk.3:4 10:45, Luk.12:22, Jhn.10:11, Act.20:10, 24 2Co.1:23, Php.2:30, 1Th.2:8, al.
__2. the soul,
__(a) as the seat of the will, desires and affections: Mat.26:38, Mrk.12:30" (LXX) 14:34, Luk.1:46, Jhn.10:24, Act.14:2, Php.1:27, al.; ἐκ ψυχῆς, from the heart, heartily: Eph.6:6, Col.3:23;
__(b) as a periphrasis for person or self (frequently in translation from Semitic originals, see M, Pr., 87; Robinson,…
G5590G.s: breath, i.e. (by implication) spirit, abstractly or concretely (the animal sentient principle only; thus distinguished on the one hand from G4151 (πνεῦμα), which is the rational and immortal soul; and on the other from G2222 (ζωή), which is mere vitality, even of plants: these terms thus exactly correspond respectively to the Hebrew H05315, H07307 and H02416)
G5590G.k: heart (+ -ily), life, mind, soul, + us, + you

G5590H.d:
ψυχή, -ῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX very frequently for נֶפֶשׁ, sometimes for לֵבַב ,לֵב, etc. ;]
__1. breath (Lat. anima), breath of life, life (Hom., al.; in Arist., of the vital principle): Mat.6:25, Mrk.3:4 10:45, Luk.12:22, Jhn.10:11, Act.20:10, 24 2Co.1:23, Php.2:30, 1Th.2:8, al.
__2. the soul,
__(a) as the seat of the will, desires and affections: Mat.26:38, Mrk.12:30" (LXX) 14:34, Luk.1:46, Jhn.10:24, Act.14:2, Php.1:27, al.; ἐκ ψυχῆς, from the heart, heartily: Eph.6:6, Col.3:23;
__(b) as a periphrasis for person or self (frequently in translation from Semitic originals, see M, Pr., 87; Robinson,…

G5590H.k: heart (+ -ily), life, mind, soul, + us, + you

ψυχή, -ῆς, ἡ,

G5591.d:
ψυχικός, -ή, -όν
(ψυχή) [in LXX: 4Ma.1:32 * ;]
of the ψυχή (as the lower part of the immaterial in man), EV, natural: opposite to πνευματικός, 1Co.2:14 15:44 15:46; πνεῦμα μὴ ἔχοντες (EV, sensual; R, mg., natural or animal; better perhaps, of the mind; see infr.), Ju 19; with ἐπίγειος, δαιμονιώδης, opposite to ἄνωθεν κατερχομένη (σοψία), of the mind (Hort, in l), Jas.3:15†
(AS)
G5591.s: sensitive, i.e. animate (in distinction on the one hand from G4152 (πνευματικός), which is the higher or renovated nature; and on the other from G5446 (φυσικός), which is the lower or bestial nature)

G5592.d:
ψύχος (LT, ψῦ-, as in cl.), -εος (-ους), τό
(ψύχω), [in LXX: Gen.8:22 (קֹר), Job.37:9, Psa.147:17 (קָרָה), Zec.14:6, Dan LXX TH 3:67,69 * ;]
cold: Jhn.18:18, Act.28:2, 2Co.11:27.†
(AS)

G5593.d:
ψυχρός, -ά, -όν
(ψύχω), [in LXX: Pro.25:25 (קַר), Sir.43:20, 4Ma.11:26 * ;]
cold: sc. ὕδωρ (cf. Theogn., 263; Hdt., ii, 37), Mat.10:42; metaphorically, of indifferent persons, Rev.3:15-16 †
(AS)

G5594.d:
ψύχω
[in LXX for קוּר, שָׁטַח ;]
to breathe, blow; hence, to make cool. Pass., to grow cool: metaphorically, Mat.24:12.†
(AS)
G5594.s: to breathe (voluntarily but gently, thus differing on the one hand from G4154 (πνέω), which denotes properly a forcible respiration; and on the other from the base of G109 (ἀήρ), which refers properly to an inanimate breeze), i.e. (by implication, of reduction of temperature by evaporation) to chill (figuratively)

G5595.d:
ψωμίζω
(ψωμός, a morsel), [in LXX chiefly for אָכַל hi. ;]
to feed with morsels (as children or the sick; Hippocr.), hence, generally, in late writers, to feed, nourish: with accusative of person(s), Rom.12:20 (LXX); with accusative of thing(s), to give out for food, 1Co.13:3 (cf. WM, § 32, 4an; for dupl. accusative, cf. Num.11:4, Sir.15:3, al.).†
(AS)
G5595.s: to supply with bits, i.e. (generally) to nourish

G5596.d:
ψωμίον, -ου, τό
dimin. of ψωμός, a fragment, morsel: Jhn.13:26-27, 30.†
(AS)
G5596.s: a crumb or morsel (as if rubbed off), i.e. a mouthful
G5596.o: diminutive from a derivative of the base of G5597 (ψώχω);

G5597.d:
ψώχω
(ψώω, collat. form of ψάω, to rub)
to rub: Luk.6:1.†
(AS)
G5597.s: to triturate, i.e. (by analogy) to rub out (kernels from husks with the fingers or hand)
G5597.o: prolongation from the same base as G5567 (ψάλλω);

G5598.d:
Ω, ω, ὦ μέγα (cf. ὂ μικρόν),
omega, ô, the twenty-fourth and last letter. As a numeral, ω᾽ = 800, ω, = 800,000. As a symbol of the last (= τὸ τέλος), τὸ Ὦ (Rec. Ω, L, ὦ, T, ω), the Omega: Rev.1:8 21:6 22:13 (cf. Ἄλφα).†
(AS)
G5598.s: the last letter of the Greek alphabet, i.e. (figuratively) the finality

G5599.d:
ὦ
interj., with vocat.,
O;
__(a) in simple address (less frequently than in cl.; M, Pr., 71); Act.1:1 18:14 27:21, Rom.2:1, 3 9:20, 1Ti.6:20; expressing reproof, Jas.2:20;
__(b) in exclamations of surprise, etc.: Mat.15:28, Luk.24:25, Act.13:10, Rom.11:33, Gal.3:1; with nom. (Bl., § 33, 4), Mat.17:17, Mrk.9:19, Luk.9:41.†
(AS)
G5599.s: as a sign of the vocative case, O; as a note of exclamation, oh

G5600.d:
εἰμί,
with various uses and significations, like the English verb to be.
__I. As substantive verb.
__1. Of persons and things, to be, exist: Act.17:28, Jhn.1:1, 8:58, 17:5, al; ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἦν (for past ptcp.), Rev.1:4, 8, 4:8, 11:17, 16:5 (see Swete, Ap., 5; M, Pr., 228); τὰ (μὴ) ὄντα, Rom.4:17, 1Co.1:28.
__2. Of times, events, etc., to be, happen, take place: Mat.24:3, Mrk.14:2, 15:42, Luk.21:23, Jhn.4:6, 23, 5:10, al.
__3. to be present, be in a place, have come: Mat.2:13, 15, Mrk.1:45, 5:21, 15:40, Luk.1:80, 5:29, Jhn.7:30, al.; before εἰς, Mrk.2:1; before ἐκ, (ἐξ), Mat.1:20, 21:25, Mrk.11:30, Jhn.3:31, al.…
G5600.s: (may, might, can, could, would, should, must, etc.; also with G1487 (εἰ) and its comparative, as well as with other particles) be
G5600.k: + appear, are, (may, might, should) be, X have, is, + pass the flower of her age, should stand, were

G5601.d:
Ἰωβήδ (WH, -βήλ, Lk, l.with; Rec., RV, Ὠβήδ), ὁ, indecl.,
Jo bed (Obed): Mat.1:5, Luk.3:32.†
(AS)

G5602.d:
ὧδε, adv.,
[in LXX for חֲלֹם ,פֹּה ,הִנֶּה, etc. ;]
__1. prop., of manner, so (Hom., al.).
__2. In poets (rarely) and late writers, of place,
__(a) hither (BL, §25, 2): Mat.8:29, Mrk.11:3, Luk.9:41, Jhn.6:25, al.; ἕως ὧδε, Luk.23:5;
__(b) here: Mat.12:6, Mrk.9:1, Luk.9:33, Jhn.6:9, al.; τὰ ὧδε, Col.4:9; opposite to ἐκεῖ, Heb.7:8; ὧδε . . . ἢ ὧδε (ἐκεῖ), Mat.24:23, Mrk.13:21; metaphorically, here (i.e. in this circumstance or connection), 1Co.4:2, Rev.13:10, 18 14:12 17:9.
(AS)
G5602.s: in this same spot, i.e. here or hither
G5602.o: from an adverb form of G3592 (ὅδε);

G5603.d:
ᾠδή, -ῆς, ή
[in LXX chiefly for שִׁיר ;]
a song, ode, whether sad or joyful; in LXX and NT always in praise of God or Christ: Rev.5:9 14:3 15:3; ᾠ πνευματικαί Eph.5:19, Col.3:16.†
(AS)
G5603.s: a chant or "ode" (the general term for any words sung; while G5215 (ὕμνος) denotes especially a religious metrical composition, and G5568 (ψαλμός) still more specially, a Hebrew cantillation)

G5604.d:
ὠδίν
(late form of ὠδίς), -ῖνος, ἡ [in LXX for חֵבֶל חֶבֶל (and wrongly for חֶבֶל חֶבֶל, cf. Ac, l.with), חִיל, etc. ;]
a birth pang, travail pain: 1Th.5:3; metaphorically, of extreme suffering, Mat.24:8, Mrk.13:8; ὠδῖνες θανάτου (Psa.18:4 מָוֶת חֶבֶל), Act.2:24.†
(AS)
G5604.s: a pang or throe, especially of childbirth

G5605.d:
ὠδίνω
[in LXX chiefly for חוּל, also for חָבַל pi., etc. ;]
to have birthpangs, to travail: Gal.4:27 (LXX), Rev.12:2; metaphorically, Gal.4:19 (cf. συν-ωδίνω).†
(AS)
G5605.s: to experience the pains of parturition (literally or figuratively)

G5606.d:
ὦμος, οὐ, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for שְׁכֶם, כָּתֵף ;]
the shoulder: Mat.23:4, Luk.15:5.†
(AS)
G5606.s: the shoulder (as that on which burdens are borne)
G5606.o: perhaps from the alternate of G5342 (φέρω);

G5607.d:
εἰμί,
with various uses and significations, like the English verb to be.
__I. As substantive verb.
